children.text: śrīrāmajayam
children.translated_text: Victory to Śrī <s>Rāma</s>!

children.text: paribhāṣendu śekharaḥ//
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣenduśekhara</s> (The Crest-Jewel of Interpretive Rules)

children.text: / anubanda catuṣṭaya nirūpaṇam/
natvāsāmbaṃ śivaṃ bramha nāgeśaḥ kurute sudhīḥ/
children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Śiva</s> together with <s>Ambā</s>, and to <s>Brahmā</s>, the wise <s>Nāgeśa</s> composes

children.text: bālānāṃ sukhabodhāya paribhaṣendu śekharam//
children.translated_text: the <s>Paribhāṣenduśekhara</s> for the easy understanding of beginners.

children.text: prācīna vyakaraṇa tantre vācanikānyatra pāṇinīyatantre jñapakanyāyasiddāni bhaṣyavārtikayorupanibaddāni yāni paribhaṣārūpaṇi tāni vyākhyāsyante/
children.translated_text: In the earlier grammatical system, [the <s>paribhāṣās</s> (interpretive rules)] are explicitly stated (<s>vācanika</s>); but in this <s>Pāṇinīya</s> system, those interpretive principles (<s>paribhāṣā</s>) that are established through the method of inference from indicators (<s>jñāpaka-nyāya</s>) and embedded in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) and <s>Vārtika</s> (supplementary notes) — those shall be explained.

children.text: / śāstratva sampādanoddeśaprakaraṇ /
children.translated_text: Section on establishing the validity of the science (<s>śāstratva-sampādana</s>)

children.text: nanu laṇ-aiuṇ sūtrayorṇakāradvayasyaivopādānenāṇiṇgrahaṇeṣu sandehādanirṇayo 'ta āha -
children.translated_text: Now, since in the <s>laṇ</s> and <s>aiuṇ</s> <s>sūtras</s>, only two <s>ṇakāras</s> (ṇ-sounds) are employed, there arises doubt regarding the interpretation of <s>āṇ</s> and <s>iṇ</s> — and thus there is no definite conclusion. Therefore [the author] states:
Examination of the four <s>anubandhas</s> (indicatory markers)

children.text: vyākhyānato viśeṣapratipattirnahi sandehādalakṣaṇam || 1 ||
children.translated_text: Specific understanding is obtained from the commentary (<s>vyākhyāna</s>); for that which [produces] doubt is not a valid rule (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 1]

children.text: viśeṣasyānyatarādyartharūpasya vyākhyānāt śiṣṭakṛtāt pratipattiḥ niśchayo yataḥ sandehācchāstramalakṣaṇamananuṣṭāpakaṃ lakṣaṇamalakṣaṇaṃ tathā na, śāstrasya nirṇayajanakatvaucityādityarthaḥ/ asandigdhānuṣṭhānasidyarthe 'tra śāstre sandigdhoccāraṇarūpācāryavyavahāreṇasandehanivṛttervyākhyānātiriktanimittānapekṣatvaṃ bodyata iti yāvat // . tenāṇuditsavarṇasyetatparihārāya pūrveṇāṇ grahaṇam, pareṇeṇ grahaṇamiti laṇ sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam // .1 //
children.translated_text: From the commentary (<s>vyākhyāna</s>), made by the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>), there is the ascertainment — i.e. certainty — of the specific meaning (<s>viśeṣa</s>), which takes the form of one [of the possible] meanings; because from doubt, the science [becomes] non-prescriptive — a non-rule (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>) — that is, it fails to produce compliance. A rule (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is not a non-rule (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>) in that way, because it is fitting that the science should produce definitive understanding — that is the meaning. In this science, for the purpose of establishing unambiguous compliance, one should understand that there is no need for any basis other than the commentary (<s>vyākhyāna</s>) for the removal of doubt, [which is removed] through the teacher's practice (<s>ācārya-vyavahāra</s>) in the form of unambiguous pronunciation — this much [is the import]. Therefore, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>laṇ sūtra</s>, it is clear that the first <s>ṇ</s> is for the inclusion of <s>āṇ</s>, to resolve this [doubt], and the latter <s>ṇ</s> is for the inclusion of <s>iṇ</s>. [1]

children.text: tatra saṃjñā paribhāṣā viṣaye pakṣadvayamāha -
children.translated_text: Regarding the scope of <s>saṃjñā</s> (technical designation) and <s>paribhāṣā</s> (interpretive rule), two views are stated:

children.text: yathoddeśaṃ saṃjñā paribhāṣam / kārya kālaṃ saṃjñā paribhāṣam || 2 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃjñā</s> and <s>paribhāṣā</s> apply at the point of their statement (<s>yathoddeśa</s>). / <s>Saṃjñā</s> and <s>paribhāṣā</s> apply at the time of [their relevant] operation (<s>kāryakāla</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 2]

children.text:
uddesamanatikramya yatoddeśam / uddeśa upadeśa deśaḥ / adhikaraṇa sādhanaścāyam / yatra deśe upadiśyate taddeśa eva vākyārtabodhena gṛhīta śaktyā gṛhītaparibhāṣārthena ca sarvatra śāstre vyavahāraḥ/ deśaścoccāraṇakāla evātra vyavahriyate/ tattadvākyārthabodhe jāte ' bhaviṣyati kiñcidanena prayojanam ' iti jñānamātreṇa santuṣyad yathāśrutagrāhipratipatrapekṣo 'yaṃ pakṣa īdūdetsūtre kaiyaṭaḥ/
kecittu - paribhaṣāviṣaye tasminnityādi vākyārthabodhe saptamīnirdeśādikveti paryālocanāyāṃ sakalatattadvidyupasthitau sakalatattasaṃskārāya guṇabhedaṃ parikalpyaikavākyatayaiva niyamaḥ/ kāryakālapakṣetu tripādyamapyupasthiriti viśeṣaḥ/ etadevābhipretya 'adhikāronāma triprakāraḥ, kaścidekadeśasthaḥ sarvaṃ śāsramabhijvalayati, yathā - 'pradīpaḥ suprajvalitaḥ sarvaṃ veśmābhijvalayati' iti 'ṣaṣṭīsthane' iti sūtre bhāṣya uktam/ adhikāraśabdena pārārthyātparibhāṣāpyucyate/ kaścitparibhāṣārūpa iti kaiyaṭaḥ/ dīpo yathā - prabhādvārā sarvagṛhaprakāśaka evametatsvabuddhijananadvārā sarvaśāstropakārakamiti tattātparyam/ etacca pakṣadvaya sādhāraṇaṃ bhāṣyam, pakṣadvaye 'pi pradeśaikavākyatayā itaḥ pratīteḥ//
children.translated_text: 'At the point of statement' (<s>yathoddeśa</s>) means without transgressing the [original] place of statement (<s>uddeśa</s>). '<s>Uddeśa</s>' means '<s>upadeśa</s>' (instruction), i.e., the location [of the rule]; and this is an <s>adhikaraṇa-sādhana</s> (locative instrumental). At the very place where [the rule] is taught, by the power apprehended through understanding the sentence-meaning at that place, and with the purport of the <s>paribhāṣā</s> thus grasped, it operates throughout the entire science. And 'place' here refers to the time of utterance. This view — which is satisfied merely by the awareness that 'this will have some purpose in the future' once the sentence-meaning has been understood, and which requires only the literal-meaning comprehension — is [that of] <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>īdūdet sūtra</s>. Some, however, [hold]: regarding the scope of the <s>paribhāṣā</s>, when in the understanding of sentence-meanings such as 'in that' (<s>tasmāt</s>) etc., upon considering what the saptamī (locative) designation etc. refer to, [one arrives at] the understanding of all relevant instances — for the purpose of modifying all those instances, a distinction of subordinate elements is postulated, and the restriction operates through the unity of a single sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>). In the <s>kāryakāla</s> view, however, the special feature is that even the last three-quarters (<s>tripādī</s>) [of the <s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s>] is operative. It is with this in mind that in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>ṣaṣṭhīsthāne</s>' it is stated: '<s>Adhikāra</s> is of three kinds; one, situated in one place, illuminates the entire science — just as a well-lit lamp illuminates the entire house.' By the word '<s>adhikāra</s>', <s>paribhāṣā</s> too is meant, due to its serving others — this is <s>Kaiyaṭa</s>'s [view]. Some [adhikāras] are of the nature of <s>paribhāṣās</s>. Just as a lamp, through the medium of its light, illuminates the entire house — so this [paribhāṣā], through the medium of generating understanding (<s>buddhi</s>), assists the entire science — that is the purport. And this <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage is common to both views, since in both views the understanding arises through unity of sentence (<s>ekavākyatā</s>) with [specific] passages.

children.text: tatraitāvān viśeṣaḥ - yatoddeśe parbhāṣādeśe sarvavidhisūtrabuddhāvātmabhedaṃ parikalpya tairekavākyatayā paribhāṣāṇām/ taduktam - 'kiṅiti ca' iti sūtre kaiyaṭe/ 'yatoddeśe pradhānānyātmasaṃskārāya sannidhīyamānāni guṇabhedaṃ prayuñjata'iti/ kāryakāle tu tattadvidhipradeśe paribhāṣābuddhyaikavākyateti/ atra ekadeśastha ityanena tatra tatra buddhāvapi taddeśasthatvaṃ vārayati, yathā - vyavaharttṝṇāṃ kāryārthamanekadeśagamane 'pi na tattaddeśīyatvavyavahāraḥ, kintvabhijanadeśīyatva vyavahāra eva, tadvanniṣedhavākyānāmapi niṣedhyaviśeṣākāṅkṣatvādvidhyekavākyatayaivānvaya iti paribhāṣāsādṛśyātparibhāṣātvena vyavahāraḥ 'kiṅiti ca' ityatra bhāṣye/ tatraikavākyatā paryudāsena prasajya pratiṣedhe 'pi tena saha vākyārthabodhamātreṇaikavākyatā vyavahāraḥ//
children.translated_text: Therein the distinction is as follows: in the <s>yathoddeśa</s> [view], at the place of the <s>paribhāṣā</s>, by postulating a distinction of the self (i.e. the paribhāṣā being the principal element) in the awareness of all prescriptive <s>sūtras</s>, the <s>paribhāṣās</s> [operate] through unity of sentence with those [sūtras]. This is stated by <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>kiṅiti ca</s>': 'In the <s>yathoddeśa</s> [view], the principal [sūtras], being proximate for their own modification, employ a subordinate distinction.' In the <s>kāryakāla</s> [view], however, [there is] unity of sentence with the <s>paribhāṣā</s>-awareness at each prescriptive passage. Here, by [the phrase] 'situated in one place,' even when [the paribhāṣā] is [brought to] awareness elsewhere, it prevents [being considered as] situated at those other places — just as for persons who travel to many places for business purposes, there is no designation as belonging to each of those places, but only the designation of belonging to one's birthplace. Similarly, prohibitive statements too, because they require a specification of what is prohibited, are construed in unity with the prescriptive statement alone — and due to their similarity to <s>paribhāṣās</s>, they are treated as <s>paribhāṣās</s>: [this is stated] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>kiṅiti ca</s>.' Therein, the unity of sentence operates even in the case of exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) and categorical prohibition (<s>prasajya-pratiṣedha</s>) — the usage of unity of sentence [applies] merely by the understanding of sentence-meaning together with that [prohibitive rule].

children.text:
saṃjñāśāstrasya tu kāryakālapakṣe na pṛthakvākyārthabodhaḥ, kintu pradeśavākyena sahaiva/ ata evāṇo 'pragṛhyasyetyetadekavākyatāpannādasomādityetatprati na mutvādyasiddham, asiddhatvasya kāryārthatayā kāryajñānottarameva tatpravṛttiḥ, kāryajñānaṃ ca pradeśa eveti taddeśasthāsiddhatvātpūrvagrahaṇenāgrahāt/ evaṃ tadbodhottarameva virodhapratisandhānañceti tatratyaparatvena vipratiṣedhasūtrapravṛttau bījam/ ata eva kāryakālapakṣe"ayādibhyaḥ paraiva pragṛhya saṃjñā"iti 'adasomāt'
iti sūtre bhāṣya uktam//
children.translated_text: In the <s>kāryakāla</s> view, however, the <s>saṃjñā</s>-rule does not produce a separate sentence-meaning understanding, but [operates] only together with the passage-sentence. For this very reason, '[the saṃjñā] <s>aṇaḥ pragṛhyasya</s>' — this, being incorporated into a single sentence [with the prescriptive rule] — with respect to the [rule about] '<s>adasomāt</s>,' the [principle of] <s>asiddhatva</s> (not-yet-established-ness) does not [apply], since <s>asiddhatva</s>, being purpose-oriented, comes into effect only after the knowledge of the operation; and the knowledge of the operation [arises] only at the passage [where it applies] — hence, since the <s>asiddhatva</s> is situated at that place, [the saṃjñā] is not captured by the [rule of] prior inclusion. Similarly, the reconciliation of contradiction too [occurs] only after that understanding — and therein lies the basis for the application of the <s>vipratiṣedha</s> (conflict-resolution) <s>sūtra</s> based on the posteriority at that [passage]. For this very reason, in the <s>kāryakāla</s> view, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>adasomāt</s>,' it is stated: 'The <s>pragṛhya</s> designation is applicable only after [the rule] <s>ayādibhyaḥ</s>.'

children.text:
ākaḍārādhikārasthabhapadasaṃjñāviśaye tu yathoddeśapakṣa eveti tatratyaparatvenaiva bādhyabhādhakabhāvaḥ/ padādisaṃjñanāṃ tatra
jātaśaktigrahaṇeva tripādyamapi vyavahāraḥ/ ata eva pūrvatrāsiddhamiti sūtre paribhāṣāṇāmevatripādyāmapravṛttimāśaṅkya, kāryakālapakṣāśrayeṇa samāhitamityāhuḥ/ yathoddeśapakṣaḥ pragṛhyasaṃjñāprakaraṇe bhāṣye//
children.translated_text: Regarding the scope of the <s>bha</s>-designation which is situated within the section from <s>ākaḍārā</s>, only the <s>yathoddeśa</s> view applies — and the relationship of superseding and being superseded is [determined] only by the posteriority at that [location]. For the <s>pada</s> and other designations, once their denotative power has been grasped at that [location], they operate even in the last three-quarters (<s>tripādī</s>). For this very reason, on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>pūrvatrāsiddham</s>' — having raised the doubt that the <s>paribhāṣās</s> should not operate in the <s>tripādī</s> — [the commentators] say this is resolved by recourse to the <s>kāryakāla</s> view. The <s>yathoddeśa</s> view [is applicable] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the section on the <s>pragṛhya</s> designation.

children.text:
kāryakālamityasya ca kāryeṇa kālyate svasannidhiṃ prāpyata ityarthaḥ/ kāryeṇa svasaṃskārāya svavṛttiliṅgacinhitaparibhāṣāṇāmākṣepa iti yāvat/
ata eva 'pūrvatrāsiddham' iti sūtre bhāṣye tripādyā asiddhatvāttatra sapādasaptādyāyīstha paribhāṣāṇāṃ apravṛttimāśaṅkya yadyapīdaṃ tatrāsiddhaṃ tatviha siddhamityuktvā, tāvatāpyasiddhirityabhiprāyake kathamiti praśne-'kāryakālaṃ saṃjñāparibhāṣam' yatra kāryaṃ tatropasthitaṃ draṣṭavyamityuktam/
na ca kāryakāla pakṣe 'ṅamo hrasvāt' ityadau ' tasmādityuttarasya' 'tasminnitinirdiṣṭe pūrvasya' iti paribhāṣādvayopasthitau paratvāt 'ubhayanirdeśe pañcamīnirdeśo balīyān' iti tasminniti sūtrasthabhāṣyāsaṅgatiḥ, ubhayorekadeśasthatvena paratvādityasyāsaṅgatyāratteḥ, spaṣṭaṃ cedam 'ikoguṇa' ityatra kaiyaṭa iti vācyam ;
vipratiṣedhasūtre 'ṣṭādhyāyīsthapāṭhakṛtaparatvasya''śrayaṇenādoṣāt/ nahi kāryakālapakṣa ityetāvatā tadapaiti/ pakṣadvaye 'pi pradeśeṣu svabuddhijananenāviśeṣāt/ nahi tatpakṣe 'pyacetanasya śāstrasya svadeśaṃ vihāya taddeśagamanaṃ sambhavati/ nāpyasmadādibuddhijananena svadeśatyāgo bhavati/ ata eva bhāṣye tasminniti sūtre kaiyaṭaḥ - sūtra pāṭhāpekṣayā paratvasya vyavasathāpakatvamiti/ ikoguṇeti sūtrastha kaiyaṭastu tintya eva ; anyathā sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ prayogārthatvena prayogarūpaikadeśastvena kvāpi paratvaṃ nasyāt/ kiñca kiṅiti ceti sūtrastha kaiyaṭarītyā vidhisūtrāṇāṃ yathoddeśa pakṣe paribhāṣādeśe sannidhānena teṣāṃ paratvaṃ vyāhanyeta/ evañca vṛkṣebhya ityatra supicetyataḥ paratvāt 'bahuvacane jhalyet' ityetvamityādyucchidyeta, ityalam//
children.translated_text: And the meaning of '<s>kāryakāla</s>' is: 'called forth by the operation' (<s>kāryeṇa kālyate</s>), i.e., brought to its own proximity — that is the meaning. The operation calls forth the <s>paribhāṣās</s> that are marked by the signs of their [relevant] application for its own modification — this much [is meant]. For this very reason, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>pūrvatrāsiddham</s>' — having raised the doubt that, because of the <s>asiddhatva</s> (non-establishment) of the <s>tripādī</s>, the <s>paribhāṣās</s> located within the seven-and-a-half chapters should not operate there — having stated 'although this is not-yet-established there, it is established here,' and when in response to the objection 'even so there is non-establishment' the question 'how?' is raised — it is answered: '<s>Saṃjñā</s> and <s>paribhāṣā</s> [apply] at the time of operation (<s>kāryakāla</s>)' — wherever the operation [occurs], it should be seen as operative there. Nor is there inconsistency with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tasmāt</s>' in the <s>kāryakāla</s> view — [namely the objection that] in the sūtra '<s>aṅgamo hrasvāt</s>' etc., when both <s>paribhāṣās</s> '<s>tasmādityuttarasya</s>' and '<s>tasminnitinirdiṣṭe pūrvasya</s>' are present, [the selection should be] by posteriority, [and the principle] 'when both nominative and ablative are used, the ablative is stronger' [should apply] — because this is not inconsistent, since the posteriority [is determined] by both being situated at one place. And this is clear from <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on '<s>ikoguṇa</s>.' Rather, it should be said: in the <s>vipratiṣedha sūtra</s>, posteriority as determined by the sequential position in the <s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> is relied upon, so there is no fault. For the <s>kāryakāla</s> view does not thereby depart from that [principle]. In both views, since [the paribhāṣā] generates understanding at the [relevant] passages, there is no difference. For even in that view, an unconscious (<s>acetana</s>) science cannot itself leave its own place and travel to another place. Nor does the generation of understanding in us cause [the rule] to abandon its own place. For this very reason, <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tasmāt</s>' states: 'The posteriority is determined with reference to the sequential ordering of the <s>sūtra</s> text.' But <s>Kaiyaṭa</s>'s [statement] on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ikoguṇa</s>' is only a tentative [position]; otherwise, since all sciences have practical application as their purpose, and being situated at one place [only] in the form of practice, nowhere would there be posteriority. Moreover, following <s>Kaiyaṭa</s>'s method on '<s>kiṅiti ca</s>,' in the <s>yathoddeśa</s> view the posteriority of prescriptive <s>sūtras</s> would be impeded by the proximity of the <s>paribhāṣā</s> at its own place. And thus in '<s>vṛkṣebhyaḥ</s>' etc., the <s>etva</s> (substitution of e) prescribed by '<s>bahuvacane jhalyet</s>' would be blocked because of the posteriority from '<s>supica</s>' — and so enough [of this discussion].

children.text: itsaṃjñakā anubandhāḥ, teṣvavayavānavayavatvasandeha āha-
children.translated_text: The <s>anubandhas</s> (indicatory markers) are designated by <s>it</s>. Regarding the doubt whether they are parts or non-parts [of the elements they mark], [the author] states:

children.text: anekāntāḥ anubandhāḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>anubandhas</s> (indicatory markers) have multiple determinations (<s>anekānta</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 3]

children.text: anekāntā anavayavāḥ ityarthaḥ/ yo hyanavayava sa kadācittatropalabhyata eva, ayaṃ tu na tathā, tadarthabhūte vidheye kadāpyadarśanāt/ śitkidityādau samīpe 'vayavatvāropeṇa samāso bodhyaḥ/ 'vuṇchaṇkaṭh' ityādau ṇitvaprayuktaṃ kāryaṃ pūrvasayaivetyādi tu vyākhyānate nirṇeyam/ 'halantyam' ityatrāntya śabdaḥ parasamīpa bodhakaḥ//
children.translated_text: '<s>Anekānta</s>' means 'non-parts' (<s>anavayava</s>) — that is the meaning. For that which is truly a non-part is sometimes found in that [context]. But this [anubandha] is not like that, because in some cases it is never seen in the prescribed result (<s>vidheya</s>) for which it serves. In [forms like] '<s>śit</s>,' '<s>kit</s>' etc., a compound (<s>samāsa</s>) [is to be understood] by attributing part-hood [to the it-marker] due to proximity. In [sūtras like] '<s>vuṇchaṇkaṭh</s>' etc., however — [the principle that] the operation caused by the <s>ṇit</s> designation belongs to the preceding [element] — this is to be determined from the commentary (<s>vyākhyāna</s>). In '<s>halantyam</s>,' the word '<s>antya</s>' denotes proximity to the following [element].

children.text: vastutasttu-
children.translated_text: But in reality —

children.text: ekāntāḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: [The <s>anubandhas</s>] have a single determination (<s>ekānta</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 4]

children.text: ityeva nyāyyam, śāstre tatropalambhādanyatrānupalambhācca/ anavayavo hi kākādirekajātīyasambandhena gṛhavṛkṣādiṣūpalabhyate/ naivamayam/ evaṃ hi bahuvrīhirapi nyāyata evopapannaḥ, antyādi śabde lakṣaṇā ca na//
children.translated_text: This alone is proper, because [the <s>anubandha</s>] is found in that [context] in the science, and is not found elsewhere. For a non-part — like a crow and such — is found in houses, trees, etc. by virtue of its connection with one class [of things]. But this [anubandha] is not like that. For in this way, even a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) is properly established by logical reasoning, and there is no figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) of the word '<s>antya</s>' (final) etc.

children.text: kiñca anavayavatve ṇaśakapratyādau ṇāderitvānāpattiḥ, pratyayāditvābhāvāt, dadhnacaścakārasya vaiyyarthyāpattiśca/ idañca 'tasyalopaḥ' ityatra bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ tatra hyuktam,"ekāntāḥ anubandhāḥ"ityeva nyāyyamiti dik//
children.translated_text: Moreover, if [the <s>anubandha</s> is] not a component part, in the <s>ṇa</s>-<s>śak</s>-<s>pratyaya</s> and similar cases, the <s>ṇ</s>-ness etc. would not apply, because of the absence of being at the beginning of a suffix; and the redundancy of the <s>ca</s>-particle in '<s>dadhnac</s>' would follow. And this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>tasya lopaḥ</s>' (P. 1.3.9). For there it is said: 'It is proper that <s>anubandhas</s> are invariably [what they are designated to be]' — this is the direction [of the argument].

children.text: nanvekāntatve 'nekāltvādeva auśādīnāṃ sarvādeśatva siddhyā 'anekāl' sūtre śidgrahaṇaṃ vyarthamata āha -
children.translated_text: Objection: If [<s>anubandhas</s>] are invariably [separate], then since the <s>anekāltva</s> (being of more than one sound) of <s>auś</s> etc. would be established merely from being <s>anekāl</s> (multi-phonemic), the mention of <s>śit</s> in the <s>anekāl</s> <s>sūtra</s> (P. 1.1.55) would be purposeless. Therefore [<s>Nāgeśa</s>] states —

children.text: nānubandhakṛtamanekāltvam || 5 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>anekāltva</s> (multi-phonemic nature) caused by an <s>anubandha</s> is not [counted]. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 5 //

children.text: śidgrahaṇamevaitadjñāpakam, tena 'arvaṇastṛ' ityāderna sarvādeśatvam/ ḍādi viṣaye tu sarvādeśatvaṃ vinānubandhatvasyaivābhāvena''nupūrvyātsiddham//
children.translated_text: The mention of <s>śit</s> itself is the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. Therefore, in '<s>arvaṇas tṛ</s>' (P. 7.4.12) etc., the <s>sarvādeśatva</s> (whole-replacement status) does not apply. But in the domain of <s>ḍā</s> etc., since the absence of <s>anubandhatva</s> alone [is sufficient] without <s>sarvādeśatva</s>, [the result] is established from the regular order.

children.text: nanvevamapi 'avadātaṃ mukham' ityatra palopottaramātve kṛte 'dābiti ghusaṃjñāpratiṣedho na syāt, daipaḥ pakārasatve 'nejantatvāprāptyā palopottaraṃ pakārābhāvenāsya dāptvābhāvādata āha -
children.translated_text: Objection: Even so, in '<s>avadātaṃ mukham</s>,' when <s>ātva</s> is applied after the <s>pa</s>-<s>lopa</s> (deletion of <s>pa</s>), the prohibition of the <s>ghu</s>-designation by '<s>dā</s> etc.' would not apply, because if the <s>pa</s>-sound is present in <s>daip</s>, then since <s>anejanta</s>-ness (ending in a non-vowel) would not be obtained, and since after <s>pa</s>-deletion there would be no <s>pa</s>-sound, its <s>dāptva</s> (status as <s>dāp</s>) would not exist. Therefore [<s>Nāgeśa</s>] states —

children.text: nānubandhakṛtamanejamtatvam || 6 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>anejanta</s>-ness (ending in a non-vowel) caused by an <s>anubandha</s> is not [counted]. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 6 //

children.text: 'udīcāmāṅaḥ' iti nirdeśo 'syā jñāpakaḥ/ 'ādeca upajeśe' iti sūtreṇopadiśyamānasyaijantasyātvaṃ kriyate, ṅakārasatvetvejantatvābhāvādātvāprāptestasyāsaṅgatiḥ//
children.translated_text: The statement '<s>udīcām āṅaḥ</s>' is the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. By the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ādeca upajeśe</s>' (P. 6.1.45), the <s>ātva</s> (substitution of <s>a</s>) is applied to what is taught as ending in <s>ai</s>; but if the <s>ṅa</s>-sound is present, then because of the absence of <s>ejanta</s>-ness (ending in <s>e</s>/<s>ai</s>), <s>ātva</s> would not be obtained — hence the inconsistency [would arise].

children.text: na cāsyāmavasthāyāṃ tasya dhātutvābhāvātkathamātvam, tatra dhātorityasya nivṛtterityanyatra vistaraḥ/ spaṣṭañcedam"dādhāghvadāp"iti sūtre bhāṣye//
children.translated_text: And [the objection] 'How can <s>ātva</s> apply in this state, since it lacks <s>dhātu</s>-status, because of the non-application of the rule "<s>dhātoḥ</s>" (P. 3.1.91)?' — the elaboration of this is elsewhere. And this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>dādhāghvadāp</s>' (P. 1.1.20).

children.text: nanvevamapi 'vāsarūpa' sūtreṇa kaviṣaye 'ṇopyāpattirityata āha-
children.translated_text: Objection: Even so, in the domain of <s>ka</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>vāsarūpa</s>' (P. 1.1.10) would lead to the undesired application of <s>ṇa</s>. Therefore [<s>Nāgeśa</s>] states —

children.text: nānubandhakṛtamasārūpyam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>asārūpya</s> (non-homogeneity) caused by an <s>anubandha</s> is not [counted]. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 7 //

children.text: 'dadātidadhātyorvibhāṣā' iti ṇabādhakaśasya vikalpavidhāyakamasyāṃ jñāpakam, tena 'godaḥ' ityādau nāṇiti 'vāsarūpa' sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam//
children.translated_text: The [rule] '<s>dadāti-dadhātyoḥ vibhāṣā</s>' — [the fact that] <s>śa</s>, which blocks <s>ṇa</s>, [only] optionally ordains [the substitution] — is the indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. Therefore, in '<s>godaḥ</s>' etc., <s>ṇa</s> does not [apply]. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>vāsarūpa</s>' <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text:
nanu saṃkhyāgrahaṇe bahvādīnāmeva grahaṇaṃ syāt, prakaraṇasyābhidhāniyāmakatvasiddhāt 'kṛtrimākṛtrimayoḥ kṛtrime
kāryasampratyayaḥ' iti nyāyāt/ asti ca prakṛte bahvādīnāṃ saṅkhyāsaṃjñākṛteti jñānarūpaṃ prakaraṇam, natu lokaprasiddhaikadvyādīnāmityata āha -
children.translated_text: Objection: When a numerical term is used, only <s>bahu</s> (many) etc. would be taken [as referents], since it is established that the topic (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) determines [the meaning of] the expression, according to the maxim 'Between the artificial (<s>kṛtrima</s>) and the natural (<s>akṛtrima</s>), the operation applies to the artificial.' And in the present context, there is the topic in the form of the knowledge that <s>bahu</s> etc. have the <s>saṅkhyā</s>-designation, but not the commonly known [numbers] <s>eka</s>, <s>dvi</s>, etc. Therefore [<s>Nāgeśa</s>] states —

children.text: ubhayagatiriha bhavati || 8 ||
children.translated_text: In this [grammar], both interpretations apply. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 8 //

children.text:
ihauśāstre/ 'saṅkhyāyāḥ atiśadantāyāḥ' iti niṣedho 'syā jñāpakaḥ/ na hi kṛtrimā saṅkhyā tyantā śadantā vāsti, tena 'kartari kartarikarmavyatihāre' 'kaṇvameghebhyaḥ karaṇe' 'vipratiṣiddhaṃ cānadhikaraṇe' ityādau laukikakriyādravyādyavagatiḥ/ tatra kvobhaya gatiḥ, kvākṛtrimasyaiva, kva kṛtrimasyaivetyatra lakṣyānusāri vyākhyānameva śaraṇam/ ata eva āmreḍita śabdena kṛtrimasyaiva grahaṇaṃ na tu dvistrirghuṣṭamātrasya/ spaṣṭañcedaṃ saṅkhyā saṃjñā sūtre bhāṣye/
yattu - saṃjñāśāstrāṇāṃ macchāstre 'nena śabdenaita eveti niyamārthatvaṃ kṛtrimākṛtrima nyāyabījamiti/ tanna ; teṣāmagṛhītaśaktigrāhakatvena vidhitve sambhavati, niyamatvāyogāt/ 'sarve sarvārtha vācakāḥ' ityabhyupagamo 'pi yogidṛṣṭyā, natvasmaddṛṣṭyā, viśiṣya sarvaśabdārthajñanasyāśakyatvāt/ sāmāmyajñānaṃ tubhodhopayogītyanyatra nirūpitam//
children.translated_text: 'In this' means 'in this grammatical treatise.' The prohibition '<s>saṅkhyāyāḥ atiśadantāyāḥ</s>' is the indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. For there is no artificial <s>saṅkhyā</s> (number designation) that is <s>tyanta</s> (ending in <s>ti</s>) or <s>śadanta</s> (ending in <s>śat</s>). Therefore, in '<s>kartari kartari-karma-vyatihāre</s>' (P. 1.3.14), '<s>Kaṇva-Meghebhyaḥ karaṇe</s>' etc., and '<s>vipratiṣiddhaṃ cānadhikaraṇe</s>' etc., there is apprehension of worldly actions, substances, and the like. Where both interpretations apply, where only the non-artificial, and where only the artificial [applies] — in this matter, only commentary guided by actual usage (<s>lakṣyānusāri</s>) is the refuge. For this very reason, the word <s>āmreḍita</s> (repeated) takes only the technical [meaning], not mere repetition such as 'twice' or 'thrice spoken.' And this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>saṅkhyā-saṃjñā</s> <s>sūtra</s>. As for [the view] that the designation-<s>sūtras</s> have the purpose of restricting [meaning] in this grammar to 'by this word, only these [are meant],' and that this is the basis of the artificial/non-artificial maxim — that is not correct; since their function as teaching unlearned <s>śakti</s> (denotative power) is possible, restriction would be unwarranted. The claim 'all [words] denote all meanings' is also from the perspective of a <s>yogin</s>, not from our perspective, since it is impossible to know the meanings of all words distinctly. However, general knowledge is useful for understanding — this has been examined elsewhere.

children.text: nanu 'adhyetā' 'śayitā' ityādāviṅśīṅorṅitvād guṇaniṣedhaḥ syādata āha -
children.translated_text: Objection: Even so, in '<s>adhyetā</s>,' '<s>śayitā</s>,' etc., since <s>iṅ</s> and <s>śīṅ</s> have <s>ṅ</s> [as <s>anubandha</s>], the prohibition of <s>guṇa</s> would follow. Therefore [<s>Nāgeśa</s>] states —

children.text: kāryamanubhavanhi kāryī nimittatayā nāśrīyate || 9 ||
children.translated_text: That which undergoes an operation is not used as a cause in its capacity as undergoing [that operation]. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 9 //

children.text:
'sthaṇḍilācchayitari' iti nirdeśaścāsyāṃ jñāpakaḥ/ 'ūrṇunaviṣati' ityādi siddhaye kāryamanubhavanniti/ atra hi 'dvirvacane 'ci' iti nu śabdasya dvitvam, anyathā 'sanyaṅoḥ' ityasya ṣaṣṭyantatvātsannantasya kāryitvena iso dvitvanimittatvābhāvāttatpravṛttirna syāt/
vastutaḥ - samavāyikāraṇa nimittakāraṇayorbhadasya sakalalokatantraprasiddhatayā tasya tatvenā'śrayaṇābhāvena naiṣā jñāpakasādhyā/ ata eva haḥ prayuktaḥ/ sa hi tatvenānāśrayaṇe hetoḥ prasiddhatvaṃ dyotayatīti tatvam/ 'dvirvacane 'ci' ityatra bhāṣye dhvanitaiṣā//
children.translated_text: The statement '<s>sthaṇḍilāc chayitari</s>' is the indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. '[That which undergoes] an operation' — this [specification] is for the establishment of '<s>ūrṇu-naviṣati</s>' and similar forms. For there, by '<s>dvirvacane 'ci</s>' (P. 6.1.1), the <s>nu</s>-sound undergoes reduplication; otherwise, since '<s>sanyaṅoḥ</s>' (P. 6.1.11) governs a sixth-case ending [possessive], and since the <s>san</s>-ending form would be the one undergoing the operation, the absence of <s>is</s> as a cause of reduplication would prevent the operation. In reality — since the distinction between the material cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) and the efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>) is well-known in all systems of thought, and since its non-employment in that capacity [is self-evident], this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] need not be established by an indicator. For this very reason, the particle '<s>hi</s>' is used, which signifies the well-known nature of the reason for non-employment in that capacity — this is the truth. This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is alluded to in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>dvirvacane 'ci</s>'.

children.text: nanu 'praṇidāpayati' ityādau dārūpasya vidhīyamānā ghusaṃjñā dāpernasyādata āha -
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>praṇidāpayati</s>' etc., the <s>ghu</s>-designation being ordained for the <s>dā</s>-form would extend to <s>dāp</s>. Therefore [<s>Nāgeśa</s>] states —

children.text: yadāgamāstadguṇībhūtāstadgrahaṇena gṛhyante || 10 ||
children.translated_text: Augments become subordinate to that [to which they are attached], and are denoted by the expression denoting that [base]. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 10 //

children.text:
yamuddiśyā'gamo vihitaḥ, sa tadguṇībhūtaḥ śāstreṇa tadavayavatvena bodhito 'tastadgrahaṇena tadgrāhakena tadbodhakena śabdhena gṛhyate bodhyata ityarthaḥ/ tatra tadguṇībhūtā ityaṃśo bījakathanam/ loke 'pi devadattasyāṅgādhikye tadviśiṣṭasyaiva devadattagrahaṇena grahaṇaṃ dṛśyate/
yamuddiśya vihita ityukteḥ 'pranidārayati' ityādau na dārityasya ghutvam/
'ānemuk' iti mugvidhānasāmarthyādeṣānityā/ anyathā 'pacamānaḥ' ityādāvakārasya muki-anayā paribhāṣayā viśiṣṭasya savarṇadīrge tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameva/ tena 'didīye' ityādau yaṇādi na, 'jahāra' ityādau 'āta au ṇalaḥ' iti ca na/
na cākārādervarṇasya varṇāntaramavayavaḥ kathamit vācyam, vacanenāvayavatvabodhanāt/ tasya cāvayavatvasādṛśye paryavasānaṃ bodhyam/
na coktajñāpakādvarṇagrahaṇe 'syā apravṛttiriti vācyam ; 'āne muk' iti sūtra bhāṣye 'kārasyāṅgāvayavasya mugityarthe 'pacamānaḥ' ityatra 'tāsyanudāttet' iti svaro ma syādityāśaṅkhyādupadeśabhaktastadgrahaṇena grāhiṣyata ityukterasaṅgatyāpatteḥ/
kiñca ṅamantapadāvayavasya hrasvātparasya ṅamo ṅamuḍityarthe 'kurvannāste' ityādau ṅamo ṅamuḍāgame ṇatvaprāptimāśaṅkya 'yadāgamāḥ' iti nyāyenādyanasyāpi padāntagrahaṇena grahaṇāt 'padāntasya' iti niṣedha ityanayā
children.translated_text: The augment that is prescribed with reference to something becomes subordinate to that — that is, taught by grammar as a component part of it — and is thus denoted, i.e., referred to, by the expression that denotes and teaches that [base] — this is the meaning. Therein, the phrase 'become subordinate to that' is the statement of the underlying principle. In ordinary usage also, when <s>Devadatta</s> has an extra limb, the apprehension of the distinguished [<s>Devadatta</s>] by the term '<s>Devadatta</s>' is observed. Because it is said 'prescribed with reference to which,' in '<s>pranidārayati</s>' etc., the <s>ghu</s>-status of <s>dā</s> [does not extend to <s>dāp</s>]. By the authority of the <s>muk</s>-prescription in '<s>ānemuk</s>' — this [augment] is impermanent. Otherwise, in '<s>pacamānaḥ</s>' etc., the redundancy of <s>savarṇadīrgha</s> (homogeneous lengthening) with respect to the <s>a</s>-sound in <s>muk</s> — [established] by this <s>paribhāṣā</s> with respect to the qualified [form] — is quite clear. Therefore, in '<s>didīye</s>' etc., <s>yaṇ</s> etc. [do] not [apply], and in '<s>jahāra</s>' etc., '<s>āta au ṇalaḥ</s>' also [does] not [apply]. Nor should it be said 'How can a phoneme other than a <s>varṇa</s> be a component of a <s>varṇa</s> like <s>ā</s>?' — because the component-hood is taught by [grammatical] statement. And it should be understood that this component-hood terminates in similarity. Nor should it be said that from the stated indicator, this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] would not apply in the apprehension of a <s>varṇa</s>; for in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>āne muk</s>' (P. 7.2.82), in the sense that the <s>ā</s>-sound is a <s>muk</s>-augment [i.e., component], in '<s>pacamānaḥ</s>,' having raised the concern that the accent by '<s>tāsya anudāttet</s>' might not apply, and [replying] that 'it will be grasped by the expression denoting the taught [form]' — inconsistency would result [from denying this <s>paribhāṣā</s>]. Moreover, in the sense that the <s>ṅam</s>-ending component of a word, being a short [vowel] followed [by a consonant], undergoes '<s>ṅamo ṅamuḍ</s>' — in '<s>kurvann āste</s>' etc., having raised the concern of <s>ṇatva</s> upon the <s>ṅamuḍ</s> augment, by the principle '<s>yadāgamāḥ</s>' (augments take on the properties of their base), since even the initial [phoneme] of this [augment] is grasped by the term '<s>padānta</s>' (word-final), the prohibition by '<s>padāntasya</s>' [applies] — by this

children.text:
paribhaṣayā 'āgamānāmāgamidharmavaiśiṣṭyamapi hodhyate' ityāśayaka 'ṅamuṭ' sūtrasthabhāṣyāsaṅgateḥ/
kiñca-guṇāde raparatve rephaviśiṣṭa guṇatvādyeṣṭavyam/ anyathā 'ṛkārasya guṇavṛddhī arārāveva' iti niyamo na syāt/ tacca 'varṇagrahaṇe' etadapravṛttau na saṅgaccate/ ata eva 'radābhyāṃ' iti sūtre bhāṣyam -"guṇo bhavati, vṛddhirbhavati,
rephaśirā guṇavṛdadhisaṃjñako 'bhinirvartate"iti/ ata eva 'neṭi' 'ṇeraniṭi' ityadi caritārtham/
'anāgamakānāṃ sāgamakāḥ ādeśāḥ' ityasya tvayamarthaḥ - ārdhadhātukasyeḍāgama ityarthe jñāte, nityeṣu śabdeṣvāgamavidhānānupatyā arthāpattimūlakavākyāntarakalpaneneḍrahitabuddhiprasaṅge seḍbuddhiḥ kartavyeti/ evañcādeśeṣvivātrāpi buddhivipariṇāma iti na nityatvahāniḥ/
sthānivatsūtre ca nedṛśādeśagrahaṇam/ sākṣādaṣṭādyāyībodhitasthānyādeśabhāve cāritārthyāt/ kiñcevaṃ sati sthānibuddhyaiva kāryapravṛtyā 'lāvasthāyāmaḍiti' siddhantāsaṅgatiḥ/ sthānivadbhāvaviṣaye 'nirdiśyamānasya' iti paribhāṣāyāḥ pravṛttau 'tisṛṇām' itiyatira paratvāttisrādeśe sthānivadbhāvena trayādeśamāśaṅkhya, 'sakṛdgati' nyāyena samādhānaparabhāṣyāsaṅgatiḥ/
'eruḥ' ityādau sthānaṣaṣṭīnārdeśāttadantaparatayā paṭhitavākyasyaiva samudāyādeśaparatvenā'deśagrahaṇasāmarthyāttasya sthānivatsūtre grahaṇena na doṣaḥ/ ānumānika sathānyādeśabhāvakalpane 'pi śrautasthānyādeśabhāvasya na tyāga iti 'acaḥ parasmin' ityādernāsaṅgatiḥ/
etena - 'yadāgamāḥ' iti paribhāṣā sthānivatsūtreṇa gatārthetyapāstham/ etatsarvam 'dādhāghvadāp' iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam//
children.translated_text: <s>paribhāṣā</s>, 'the property-distinctness of augments belonging to the base is also taught' — this is the intent of [resolving] the inconsistency in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>ṅamuṭ</s>' <s>sūtra</s>. Moreover — when <s>guṇa</s> etc. have <s>ra</s> as subordinate [i.e., as <s>repha</s>], one should accept <s>guṇa</s>-status etc. as qualified by <s>repha</s>. Otherwise, the restriction 'the <s>guṇa</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s> of <s>ṛ</s>-sound are <s>ar</s> and <s>ār</s> alone' would not hold. And this does not accord with [the view that this <s>paribhāṣā</s>] does not apply when a <s>varṇa</s>-term is used. For this very reason, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>radābhyām</s>' (P. 7.4.1) states: '<s>Guṇa</s> occurs, <s>vṛddhi</s> occurs — a <s>guṇa</s>-and-<s>vṛddhi</s>-designated [substitute] headed by <s>repha</s> is produced.' For this very reason, '<s>neṭ</s>,' '<s>ṇer aniṭi</s>' etc. are fulfilled. The [rule] '<s>anāgamakānāṃ sāgamakāḥ ādeśāḥ</s>' (substitutes of augment-less [forms] have augments) has this meaning: when the <s>iṭ</s>-augment of an <s>ārdhadhātuka</s> [suffix] is known, in the case of eternal words, since augment-prescription would not apply, by presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) one would construct an additional statement [implying] the notion of <s>iṭ</s>-lessness — [rather,] the notion of having <s>iṭ</s> should be maintained. And just as in the case of substitutes, here too the transformation of understanding [should be applied], so there is no loss of eternality. And in the <s>sthānivat</s> <s>sūtra</s> (P. 1.1.56), such substitute-apprehension [is not needed], because it is already fulfilled by the <s>sthāni</s>-<s>ādeśa</s> (original-substitute) relationship directly taught in the eighth chapter. Moreover, if so, by the operation proceeding through the notion of the original alone, the inconsistency with the established principle '<s>l-āvasthāyām aḍ iti</s>' [would arise]. When the <s>sthānivad-bhāva</s> (treatment-as-original) is in effect and the <s>paribhāṣā</s> '<s>nirdiśyamānasya</s>' (of what is being designated) applies — in '<s>tisṛṇām</s>' etc., the <s>ira</s>-substitute, having the <s>sthānivad-bhāva</s> by proximity, might be expected to receive the <s>traya</s>-substitute, and the inconsistency with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> that resolves this by the maxim '<s>sakṛdgati</s>' (single application) [would result]. In '<s>eruḥ</s>' etc., since the locative sixth-case refers to the position, and the quoted statement is read as referring to the collective substitute, by the force of the word '<s>ādeśa</s>' (substitute), its apprehension by the <s>sthānivat</s> <s>sūtra</s> causes no defect. Even when positing an inferred <s>sthāni</s>-<s>ādeśa</s> relationship, the directly taught <s>sthāni</s>-<s>ādeśa</s> relationship is not abandoned — hence no inconsistency with '<s>acaḥ parasmin</s>' etc. By this, the [view that] the <s>paribhāṣā</s> '<s>yadāgamāḥ</s>' is rendered purposeless by the <s>sthānivat</s> <s>sūtra</s> — is refuted. All this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>dādhāghvadāp</s>'.

children.text: nanvevam udasthādityādau 'udaḥsthāstambhoḥ pūrvasya' iti pūrvasavarṇāpattirata āha -
children.translated_text: Objection: Even so, in '<s>udasthāt</s>' etc., the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>udaḥ sthāstambhoḥ pūrvasya</s>' would lead to the undesired replacement with a homogeneous vowel of the preceding [vowel]. Therefore [<s>Nāgeśa</s>] states —

children.text: nirdaśyamānasyā'deśā bhavanti|| 11 ||
children.translated_text: Substitutes apply to what is being designated. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 11 //

children.text:
'ṣaṣṭīsthāne yogā' iti sūtramāvartate/ tatra dvitīyasyāyamarthaḥ - ṣaṣṭhyantaṃ nirdiśyamānamuccāryamāṇamuccāryamāṇasajātīyameva, nirdiśyamānāvayavarūpameva vā sthanena sthānanirūpitasambandhena yujyate, na tu pratīyamānamityarthaḥ/ tenedaṃ siddham/ na ca 'asyacvau' ityādau dīrgāṇāmādeśānāpattiḥ, teṣāṃ nirdiśyamānatvābhāvāditi vācyam, jātipakṣe doṣābhāvāt/ kiṅca 'na bhūsudhiyoḥ' iti niṣedhena grahaṇakaśāstragṛhītānāṃ nirdiśyamākāryabodhānna doṣaḥ/
iyaṅuvaṅorṅitvaṃ tu ivarṇovarṇāntaśnudhātubhruvāmityarthena dhātvādīnāmapi nirdiṣṭatvādantyādeśatvāya/ rīriṅorṅitvaṃ tu spaṣṭārthameva// etenedaṃ ṅitvaṃ varṇagrahaṇe nirdiśyamāna paribhāṣāyā apravṛttijñāpakamityapāstam/ 'hayavaraṭ' sūtrasthena 'ayogavahānāmupadeśe 'lontyavidhiḥ prayojanam, vṛkṣasttatra/ naitadasti prayojanam, nirdiśyamānasyetyeva siddham' - iti bhāṣyeṇa virodhāt/
anayā paribhāṣayā 'yenavidhiḥ' iti sūtrabodhitatadantasya sathānivatvābhāva bodhanam, yadāgamā iti labdhasya ca/
tena 'supadaḥ' 'udasthāt' ityādi siddhiḥ/ anayā ca svasvanimittasannidhāpitānām 'alo 'ntyasya' ityādīnāṃ samāveśa eva, na bādhyabādhaka bhāvaḥ, virodhābhāvāt/ nāpyetayoraṅgāṅgibhavaḥ, ubhayorapi parārthatvena tadayoghāt/ 'anekāl śit' iti sūtre sarvaścaitatparibhāṣābodhita eva gṛhyate/
yattu 'ādeḥ parasya' 'alontyasya' ityetāveva tadbādhakāviti tanna ; 'udaḥsthāt' iti sūtraviṣaye 'syāḥ 'pādaḥ pat' iti sūtre bhāṣye sañcāritatvāt/ nāpyetayoriyaṃ bādhikā, etayorniviṣayatvaprasaṅgāditi 'ti viṃśateḥ' iti sūtre kaiyaṭaḥ/ akajviṣaye nāyaṃ nyāyaḥ, sthānivadbhāvena tanmadhyapattanyāyena tadbudhāyaiva kāryajanakatvāt/ iyañca avayavaṣaṣṭīviṣaye 'pi/ ata eva 'tadoḥ saḥ sāviti' satvam, 'atisyaḥ' ityatropasargatakārasya na/ nirdiśyamānayuṣmadādyavayavamaparyamtasyaiva yūyādayaḥ, na tu 'atiyūyam' ityādau sopasargāvayavamaparyantasyeti bodhyam/ 'pādaḥ pat' iti sūtre 'ṣaṣṭī sthāne' iti sūtre ca bhāṣye ca spaṣṭaiṣā//
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ṣaṣṭīsthāne yogāḥ</s>' recurs [here]. There, the meaning of the second [interpretation] is this: what is denoted by a sixth-case ending — that which is being uttered, being of the same class as what is being uttered, or having the form of a constituent part of what is denoted — is connected by the relation determined by place (<s>sthāna</s>), not that which is merely understood. By this, the following is established. And in [cases like] '<s>asyacvau</s>' and so on, there is no undesired substitution of long [vowels], because of them...

children.text: nanu 'cetā' ityādau hrasvasyekārasya pramāṇata āntaryādakāro 'pi syādata āha-
children.translated_text: Objection: In [forms like] '<s>cetā</s>' and so on, because of proximity (<s>āntarya</s>) established by authoritative source (<s>pramāṇa</s>), the short <s>i</s>-vowel should also [become] <s>a</s>. To address this, he says —

children.text: yatrānekavidhamāntaryaṃ tatra sthanata āntaryaṃ balīyaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: Where proximity is of more than one kind, proximity based on place (<s>sthāna</s>) is stronger. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 12)

children.text:
anekavidhamusthānaguṇapramāṇakṛtam/ atra mānam 'ṣaṣṭī sthāne' ityata ekadeśānuvṛtyā sthāne grahaṇe 'nuvartamāne punaḥ 'sthānentaratamaḥ' iti sūtre sthāne grahaṇameva/ taddhi tṛtīyayā vipariṇamya vākyabhedena sthāninaḥ prasaṅge jāyamānaḥ sati sambhave sthānata evāntaratama ityarthakam/
tamabgrahaṇamevānekavidhāntarya sattāgamakam/ sthānataḥusthānenetyarthaḥ/ tatra sthānata āntaryam 'iko yaṇaci'
children.translated_text: 'Of more than one kind' means arising from place (<s>sthāna</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), and authoritative source (<s>pramāṇa</s>). The authority for this is as follows: from '<s>ṣaṣṭī sthāne</s>', through partial recurrence (<s>ekadeśānuvṛtti</s>), the mention of '<s>sthāne</s>' continues; and when the mention of '<s>sthāne</s>' is already continuing, the [repetition of] '<s>sthāne</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>sthānentaratamaḥ</s>' [must mean something more]. That [word], transformed into the instrumental case through sentence-division, means: when the occasion arises for [a substitute of] the original, if possible, the nearest is determined by place alone. The [use of] the superlative suffix (<s>tamab</s>)...

children.text: ityādau prasiddhameva/ arthataḥ 'paddanno' ityādau sthānyarthābhidhāna samarthasyaivā'deśateti siddhāntādyadarthābhidhānasamartho yaḥ, sa tasyādeśa iti tatsamānārthatatsamānavarṇapadādīnāṃ te, tṛjvatkroṣṭuriti ca/ guṇato 'vāgghariḥ' ityādau/ pramāṇataḥ 'adaso 'seḥ' ityādau/ 'sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ' sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭaiṣā//
children.translated_text: ...is well-known in cases like those. By meaning: in '<s>paddannaḥ</s>' and the like, since only that which is capable of denoting the meaning of the original can be its substitute — from this established doctrine, that which is capable of denoting the same meaning is the substitute — hence those of the same meaning, same sounds, same words, and so on, such as <s>te</s>, <s>tṛjvat</s>, <s>kroṣṭu</s>, and the like. By quality: in '<s>vāgghariḥ</s>' and the like. By authoritative source: in '<s>adaso 'seḥ</s>' and the like. The <s>sūtra</s> '<s>sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ</s>'...

children.text: nanu 'proḍhavān' ityatra 'prādūhoḍheti' vṛddhiḥ syādata āha-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>proḍhavān</s>', through [the rule] '<s>prādūhoḍheti</s>', <s>vṛddhi</s> would [wrongly] apply. To address this, he says —

children.text: arthavadgrahaṇe nānarthakasya || 13 ||
children.translated_text: In a meaningful designation, a meaningless [element is] not [included]. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 13)

children.text:
viśiṣṭarūpopādāne/ upasthitārthasya śabdaṃ prati viśeṣaṇatayānvayasambhave tyāge mānābhāvo 'syā mūlam/ atrārthaḥ kalpitānvayavyatirekakalpitaḥ śāstrīyo 'pi gṛhyate iti 'saṅkhyāyāḥ' iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ iyaṃ varṇa grahaṇeṣu neti 'lasya' ityatra bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ ata eva eṣā viśiṣṭarūpopādāna viṣayeti-vṛddhāḥ/ etanmūlakameva 'yena vidhiḥ' ityatra bhāṣye paṭhyate 'alaivānarthakena tadantavidhiḥ' iti/
kiñca 'svaṃ rūpam' iti śāstre svaśabdenā'tmīyavācinār'tho gṛhyate, rūpa śabdena svarūpam, evañca tadubhayaṃ śabdasya saṃjñīti tadarthaḥ/ tatrārtho na viśeṣyastatra śastrīyopakāryāsambhavāt, kintu śabdaviśeṣaṇam/ evañcārthaviśiṣṭaḥ śabdaḥ saṃjñīti phalitam/ tenaiṣā paribhāṣā siddheti bhāṣye spaṣṭam//
children.translated_text: [This applies] in the specification of a particular form (<s>viśiṣṭarūpopādāna</s>). When there is the possibility of connection as a qualifier of the word for the presented meaning, the basis [of this rule] is the absence of authority for abandoning [that connection]. Here, 'meaning' includes even that which is technical (<s>śāstrīya</s>), determined through postulated connection and disconnection — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>saṅkhyāyāḥ</s>'. This [rule] does not [apply] in letter-designations — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>lasya</s>'. Therefore this pertains only to the specification of particular forms...

children.text: nanvevamapi 'mahadbhataścandramāḥ' ityatra 'ānmahataḥ' ityātvāpattirata āha-
children.translated_text: Objection: Even so, in '<s>mahadbhataścandramāḥ</s>', the <s>ā</s>-substitution from [the rule] '<s>ānmahataḥ</s>' would wrongly apply. To address this, he says —

children.text: gauṇamukhyayormukhye kārya sampratyayaḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: Between a secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) and a primary (<s>mukhya</s>) [sense], the operation applies to the primary. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 14)

children.text:
guṇādāgato gauṇaḥ/ yathā-gośabdasya jāḍyādiguṇanimittor'tho vāhīkaḥ/ aprasiddhaśca saṃjñādirapi tadguṇāropādeva buddhyate/ mukhamiva pradhānatvāt mukhyaḥuprathama ityarthaḥ/ gauṇe hyarthe śabdaḥ prayujyamāno mukhārthāropeṇa pravarthate/ evaṃ cāprasiddhatvaṃ gauṇalākṣaṇikatvaṃ cātra gauṇatvam/ tena 'priyatrayāṇām' ityādau trayādeśo bhavatyeva, tatra triśabdārthasyetaraviśeṣaṇatve 'pyuktagauṇatvābhāvāt/ kiñcāyaṃ nyāyo na prātipadikakārye, kintūpāttaṃ viśiṣyārthopasthāpakaṃ viśiṣṭarūpaṃ yatra tādṛśapadakārya eva/ pariniṣṭitasya padāntarasambandhe hi 'gaurvāhīkaḥ' ityādau gauṇatvapratītirnatu prātipadikasamskāravelāyāmityantaraṅgatvājjātasaṃskārabādhāyogaḥ prātipadikakārye pravṛtyabhāve bījam/
śvaśurasadṛśasyāpatyamityarthake 'śvāśuriḥ' ityādāvata iñaḥ siddhaye - upāttamityādi/ na ca prātipatikapadaṃ tādṛśamiti vācyam, tena hi prātipadikapadavatvenopasthitiriti tasya viśiṣyārthopasthāpakatvābhāvāt/ nipātapadaṃ tu cāditvenaiva cādīnāmupasthāpakamiti taduddeśyakakāryanidhāyake 'ot' ityādāvetatpravṛt 'gobhavattyā' ityādau doṣo na/
'agnīṣomau māṇavakau' ityatra prasiddhadevatādvandvavācyagnīṣomapadasya tatsadṛśaparatve 'pyantaraṅgatvādītvaṣatve bhavata eva/ sadṛśalākṣaṇikāgnisomapadayordvandve tannāmakāvityarthake ca netvaṣatve, ādye gauṇalākṣaṇikatvāt, antye 'prasiddhatvāt/ ata eva 'agnisomau māṇavako' ityatra gauṇamukhyanyāyena śatvavāraṇaparam,"agneḥ stutstomasomāḥ"iti sūtrasthaṃ bhāṣyaṃ saṅgacchate/
'gāṃ pāṭhaya' ityādau mukhya gopadārthasya pāṭhanakarmatvāsambhavena nibhaktyutpattivelāyāṃ prayoktṛbhirgauṇārthatvasya pratītāvapyapadasyāprayogeṇa boddhṛbhiḥ sarvatra padasyaiva gauṇārthakatvasya graheṇa 'atvaṃ tvaṃ sampadyate, 'amahān mahānbhūtaḥ, 'tvadbhavatiṭha ityādi bhāśyaprayoge tvādyādeśadīrgādīnāṃ karaṇena cāsya nyāyasya padakāryaviṣayatvamevocitam/ anyathā vākyasaṃskāra pakṣe teṣu tadanāpattiḥ/
kiñca"śuklām' ityukte karma nirdiṣṭam kartā kriyācānirdiṣṭe"ityādyuktyā 'ihedānīṃ gāmabhyāja kṛṣṇāṃ devadattetyādau sarvaṃ nirdiṣṭam, gāmeva karma, devadatta eva karttā, abhyājaiva kriyā' ityarthakenārthavatsūtrasthabhāṣyeṇa kārakādimātraprayoge yogyasarvakriyādhyahāre prasakte niyamārthaḥ kriyāvācakādiprayoga ityetattātparyakeṇa sāmānyataḥ kriyājanyaphalāśrayatvamātravivakṣāyāṃ dvitīyādīnāṃ sādhutvānvākhyānamityarthalābhena pāṭhanakriyānvayakāle padasyaiva gauṇarthatvapratītiḥ prayokturapi/
etanmūlakaḥ"abhivyaktapadārthāḥ ye' iti ślokopi padakāryaviṣayakaḥ/ dhvanitaṃ cedam 'sarvādīni' iti sūtre saṃjñābhūtānāṃ pratiṣedhamārabhatā vārttikakṛtā,"pūrvaparā"iti sūtre 'asaṃjñāyām' iti vadatā sūtrakṛtā, anvarthasaṃjñayā tatpratyākhyānaṃ kurvatā bhāṣyakṛtā ca/
arthāśraya etadevaṃ bhavati, śabdāśraye ca vṛddhyātve-iti 'ot' sūtrastha bhāṣyasya laukikārthavatvayogyapadāśraya
children.translated_text: <s>Gauṇa</s> (secondary/figurative) is that which comes from <s>guṇa</s> (quality). For example, the meaning 'Bāhīka' (a dull person) for the word 'go' (cow) is based on qualities such as stupidity. And even an unfamiliar technical name, etc., is understood only through the imposition of that quality. Just as something is called <s>mukhya</s> (primary) because of being principal, like the mouth — the meaning being 'first.' For a word being used in a secondary sense operates through the imposition of the primary meaning. Thus, here <s>gauṇatva</s> (secondariness) means both unfamiliarity and the state of being secondary or figurative. Therefore, in forms like '<s>priyatrayāṇām</s>' and the like, the <s>traya</s>-substitute does indeed apply, since even though the meaning of the word '<s>tri</s>' is a qualifier of the other, the aforementioned type of secondariness is absent. Furthermore, this principle does not apply to operations on <s>prātipadika</s> (nominal stems), but only to those operations on words (<s>pada-kārya</s>) where a specific form, having been adopted, serves to convey a qualified meaning. For the cognition of secondariness occurs when an already-established [word] is related to another word, as in '<s>gauḥ vāhīkaḥ</s>' (the 'cow' is a Bāhīka), but not at the stage when the stem is being processed by the grammatical apparatus — hence, due to being an inner operation, there is no possibility of obstructing the operations already generated, and this is the basis for the non-application to <s>prātipadika</s> operations. For the derivation of forms like '<s>śvāśuriḥ</s>' (meaning 'the offspring of one resembling a father-in-law'), where the <s>iñ</s> affix is needed — [one says] 'having been adopted,' etc. And one should not say that a <s>prātipadika</s>-word is of such a kind, for since it presents [its meaning] as having <s>prātipadika</s> status, it lacks the function of conveying a qualified meaning. But a <s>nipāta</s> (particle) word, being a <s>cādi</s> (beginning with '<s>ca</s>'), presents the <s>cādis</s> — hence in rules like '<s>ot</s>' that determine operations targeting those, this [principle] applies, and there is no fault in cases like '<s>gobhavattyā</s>' and the like. In '<s>agnīṣomau māṇavakau</s>' (two boys named <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>), the word '<s>agnīṣoma</s>' — which denotes the well-known <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) naming the deities — even when referring to those resembling them, the <s>ī</s>-lengthening and <s>ṣatva</s> do apply due to being an inner operation. But in the <s>dvandva</s> of the figuratively-used words '<s>agni</s>' and '<s>soma</s>' referring to persons named after them, the <s>ī</s>-lengthening and <s>ṣatva</s> do not apply — in the first case because of figurative secondariness, and in the latter because of unfamiliarity. For this very reason, in '<s>agnisomau māṇavakau</s>' (without the compound changes), the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage found in the sūtra '<s>agneḥ stutstomasomāḥ</s>' is consistent, being intended to prevent <s>śatva</s> by the <s>gauṇa-mukhya</s> (secondary-primary) principle. In examples like '<s>gāṃ pāṭhaya</s>' (make the cow recite), since the primary meaning of the word '<s>go</s>' (cow) is impossible as the object of the action of teaching, even though at the point of case-ending generation the speakers cognize the secondary sense, because no non-word is used, the listeners grasp the secondariness of the word itself everywhere — hence, by the <s>Bhāṣya</s> usages like '<s>atvaṃ tvaṃ sampadyate</s>,' '<s>amahān mahān bhūtaḥ</s>,' '<s>tvadbhavatiṭha</s>' and the like, where the <s>tvā</s>-substitute, lengthening, etc., are applied, it is appropriate that this principle pertains precisely to word-level operations. Otherwise, on the view of sentential formation, those [operations] would not arise. Moreover, by the reasoning stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>arthavat-sūtra</s> — '<s>śuklām</s>' when uttered specifies the object; the agent and the action are unspecified' — in examples like '<s>iha idānīṃ gām abhyāja kṛṣṇāṃ devadatta</s>,' everything is specified: 'go' itself is the object, <s>Devadatta</s> alone the agent, '<s>abhyāja</s>' alone the action.' This <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage, being meaningful and having the purport that when only case-markers etc. are used, a restricting use of a verbal expression etc. is needed to prevent the superimposition of all possible actions by eligibility — [implies that] through deriving the validity of the second case-ending etc. as merely denoting the substratum of a result produced by action in general, the cognition of the word's secondariness at the time of connection with the teaching-action belongs to the speaker also. The verse based on this — '<s>abhivyaktapadārthāḥ ye</s>' — also pertains to word-level operations. And this is implied by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> (author of the <s>Vārttikas</s>) who begins the prohibition of technical names in the sūtra '<s>sarvādīni</s>'; by the <s>Sūtrakāra</s> (<s>Pāṇini</s>) who says '<s>asaṃjñāyām</s>' in the sūtra '<s>pūrvaparā</s>'; and by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Patañjali</s>) who rejects that [view] through a transparent technical name. This principle operates thus when the basis is meaning; but when the basis is sound-form, [the relevant rules are] <s>vṛddhi</s> and <s>ātva</s> — [as stated in] the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>ot</s>' sūtra, which pertains to words capable of bearing worldly meaning,

children.text:
eṣa nyāyaḥ, tadrahitaśabdāśraye ca te ityarthaḥ/ 'gotaḥ' iti yathāśrutasūtre viśiṣṭarūpopādānasatvenoktarītyaivatasya
bhāṣyasya vyākhyeyatvādityalam//
children.translated_text: this is the principle; and for sound-form-based [operations] lacking that [semantic basis], they [apply differently] — such is the meaning. Since in the sūtra '<s>gotaḥ</s>' as literally read, the specific form has indeed been adopted, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on it is to be explained in the same manner stated above — enough of this.

children.text: arthavadgrahaṇe-ityasyāpavādamāha :-
children.translated_text: He states the exception to the [principle of] '<s>arthavad-grahaṇa</s>' (reference to meaningful elements):

children.text: aninasmingrahaṇānyarthavatā cānarthakena ca tadantavidhiṃ prayojayanti || 15 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 15: References to a non-initial element, along with [references] by a meaningful [element] and by a meaningless one, occasion a rule concerning [forms] ending with [that element].

children.text: 'yena vidhiḥ' ityatra bhāṣye vacana rūpeṇa paṭhitaiṣā/ tena 'rājñā' 'sāmnā' ityādvallopaḥ, 'daṇḍī' 'vāgmī' ityādau 'inhan' iti niyamaḥ, 'supayāḥ' 'susrotāḥ' ityādau 'atvasantasya' iti dīrgaḥ, 'suśarmā' 'suprathimā' ityādau 'manaḥ' iti ṅībniṣedhaśca siddhaḥ/ anye tu 'parivīviṣīdhvam' ityatra ḍhatvavyāvṛttaye kriyamāṇāt 'iṇaḥ ṣīdhvam' ityatrāṅgagrahaṇādarthavatparibhāṣānityā, tanmūlakamidamityāhuḥ/ 'vibhāṣeṭaḥ' ityatrānarthakasyaiva ṣīdhvamaḥ sambhavādatrāpi tasyaiva grahaṇamiti bhramavāraṇāya 'aṅgāt' iti pare//
children.translated_text: This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is read in the form of a statement in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on [the sūtra] '<s>yena vidhiḥ</s>.' Through it, the <s>lopa</s> (elision) in forms like '<s>rājñā</s>,' '<s>sāmnā</s>' is established; the restriction by '<s>inhan</s>' in forms like '<s>daṇḍī</s>,' '<s>vāgmī</s>' is established; the lengthening by '<s>atvasantasya</s>' in forms like '<s>supayāḥ</s>,' '<s>susrotāḥ</s>' is established; and the prohibition of <s>ṅīp</s> by '<s>manaḥ</s>' in forms like '<s>suśarmā</s>,' '<s>suprathimā</s>' is also established. Others, however, say that the <s>arthavatparibhāṣā</s> is non-eternal, based on the stem-reference in '<s>iṇaḥ ṣīdhvam</s>' which is made to exclude <s>ḍhatva</s> in '<s>parivīviṣīdhvam</s>' — and this [<s>paribhāṣā</s> 15] is founded on that. Others [add] '<s>aṅgāt</s>' to prevent confusion, since in '<s>vibhāṣeṭaḥ</s>' only the meaningless <s>ṣīdhvam</s> is possible and hence only that is referenced.

children.text: nanu 'uśca' ityatra 'liṅsicau' ityataḥ 'ātmanepadeṣu' ityeva sambadhyeta, anantaratvādata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In [the sūtra] '<s>uś ca</s>,' [the phrase] '<s>ātmanepadeṣu</s>' alone should be connected from '<s>liṅsicau</s>,' because it is immediately adjacent. Therefore he states:

children.text: ekayoganirdiṣṭānāṃ saha vā pravṛttiḥ saha vā nivṛttiḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 16: For items stated in a single rule (<s>ekayoga</s>), there is either joint application or joint non-application.

children.text: vā-śabda evārthe/ parasparānvitārthakapadānām-sahaivānuvṛttinivṛttī ityarthaḥ/ ekakārya niyuktānāṃ bahūnāṃ loke tathaiva darśanāditi bhāvaḥ/ yattu-atra jñāpakam 'neḍvaśi' ityata iḍityanuvartamāne 'ārdhadhātukasyeḍ' ityatra punariḍgrahaṇam/ taddhi netyasyāsambamdhārthamiti/ tanna ; 'dīdhīvevīṭām' iti sūtre bhāṣye tatratyeḍgrahaṇapratyākhyānāyeḍ grahaṇe 'nuvartamāne punariḍgrahaṇasyeṭo guṇarūpavikārārthakatvasyoktatvena tadvirodhāt/ naño nivṛttistu 'kvacidekadeśo 'pi anuvartate' iti nyāyena siddhā/ vastu tastu 'dīdhīvevīṭām' iti sūtrastha bhāṣyamekadeśyuktiḥ, 'ārdhadhātukasya' iti sūtrastheḍgrahaṇasya 'neḍvaśi' iti sūtre bhāṣye pratyākhyānāt, tatkaraṇena gurutarayatnamāśrityaitatpratyākhyānasyāyuktatvāt//
children.translated_text: The word '<s>vā</s>' is used in the sense of 'and.' The meaning is: the continuation or discontinuation of words whose meanings are mutually connected must be together. The idea is that in common usage, many items engaged for a single purpose are indeed seen [to behave] in this way. As for the indicator here — in [the sūtra] '<s>neḍ vaśi</s>,' when '<s>iḍ</s>' is being continued, the re-statement of '<s>iḍ</s>' in '<s>ārdhadhātukasya iḍ</s>' [is the indicator]. For that [re-statement] is for the purpose of disconnecting '<s>na</s>' (the negation). This is not so, [however]; since in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>dīdhīvevīṭām</s>,' the <s>iḍ</s>-reference therein having been rejected, and the re-statement of '<s>iḍ</s>' when '<s>iḍ</s>' is already continued having been explained as being for the purpose of denoting a phonetic change of the <s>guṇa</s>-form type, [the first interpretation] contradicts that. But the discontinuation of '<s>na</s>' is established by the principle 'sometimes even a portion [of a prior sūtra] is continued.' In truth, however, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>dīdhīvevīṭām</s>' is a partial reasoning; since the <s>iḍ</s>-reference in the sūtra '<s>ārdhadhātukasya</s>' is rejected in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>neḍ vaśi</s>,' and since it would be improper to reject that [reading] by relying on a more laborious effort in making [the <s>iḍ</s>-reference] work [differently].

children.text: nanu-alugadhikraḥ prāganaṅaḥ, uttarapadādhikāraḥ prāgaṅgādhikārādityanupapannam, ekayoganirdiṣṭatvāt/ tathā 'dāmahāyanāntācca' ityādau 'saṅkhyāvyayādeḥ' ityataḥ saṅkhyāderityanuvartate 'vyayāderiti nivṛttamiti cānupapannamata āha-
children.translated_text: Objection: [The claim that] the <s>aluk</s>-domain extends up to [the section before] <s>anaṅ</s>, and the <s>uttarapada</s>-domain up to [the section before] the <s>aṅga</s>-domain, is untenable because they are stated in a single rule. Likewise, in [sūtras like] '<s>dāmahāyanāntāc ca</s>,' the objection that '<s>saṅkhyādeḥ</s>' is continued from '<s>saṅkhyāvyayādeḥ</s>' but '<s>vyayādeḥ</s>' is discontinued is also untenable. Therefore he states:

children.text: ekayoganirdiṣṭānāmedeśo 'pyanuvartate || 17 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 17: Of items stated in a single rule, even a part may be continued [into subsequent rules].

children.text: ekārthe yogaḥusambandhastena nirdiṣṭayoḥ samudāyābhidhāyidvandvanirdiṣṭayorityartha iti 'pakṣāttiḥ' iti sūtre kaiyaṭaḥ/ tāvanmātrāṃṣe svaritatvapratijñābalāllabhyamidam/ spaṣṭā ceyam 'dāmahāyanāntācca' iti sūtre 'auto 'mśasoḥ' iti sūtre ca bhāṣye pūrvā ca//
children.translated_text: '<s>Yoga</s>' means connection for a single purpose; 'stated by that' means [items] stated in a <s>dvandva</s> compound expressing a collective meaning — such is the meaning, as [explained by] <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the sūtra '<s>pakṣāt tiḥ</s>.' This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is obtained by the force of the <s>svarita</s> marking convention to that extent only. And this is clearly [stated] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtras '<s>dāmahāyanāntāc ca</s>' and '<s>auto 'mśasoḥ</s>,' and the preceding one as well.

children.text: nanu 'tyadādīnāmaḥ' itiyādinā 'imam' ityādāvanunāsikaḥ syādata āha-
children.translated_text: Objection: By [the sūtra] '<s>tyadādīnām aḥ</s>' and the like, nasalization would arise in forms like '<s>imam</s>.' Therefore he states:

children.text: bhāvyamānena savarṇānāṃ grahaṇaṃ na || 18 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 18: There is no grasping of homogeneous sounds (<s>savarṇa</s>) by [a sound] that is being produced [by the rule itself].

children.text:
aṇuditsūtre 'apratyayaḥ' ityanena sāmartyātsūtraprāptam, jātipakṣeṇaprāptam,guṇābhedakatvenaca prāptam, netyarthaḥ/ ata evāṇuditsūtre pratyayā'deśā'gameṣu savarṇagrahaṇābhāvaṃ prakārāntareṇoktvā, 'evaṃ tarhi siddhe yadapratyaya iti pratiṣedhaṃ śāsti, tajjñāpayati bhavatyeṣāparibhāṣā 'bhāvyamānena savarṇānāṃ grahaṇaṃ na' iti/ kiñca, 'jyāda īyasaḥ' ityevāntaryato dīrghe siddhe 'jyādāt' iti dīrgoccāraṇamasyā jñāpakam/ aṇuditsūtre 'jyādāt' iti sūtre ca bhāṣye spaṣṭaiṣā/
'coḥ kuḥ' ityādau bhāvyamānenāpi savarṇagrahaṇam, vidheye udiduccāraṇasāmarthyāt/ etadevābhipretya 'bhāvyamānāṇ savarṇānna
gṛṇhāti' iti navyāḥ paṭhanti//
children.translated_text: In the <s>aṇudit-sūtra</s>, this is obtained by the force of [the word] '<s>apratyayaḥ</s>' (not an affix); it is obtained by the class-view (<s>jāti-pakṣa</s>); and it is obtained by the principle that quality-non-difference [yields the same result] — the meaning is 'not [by the sound being produced].' For this very reason, in the <s>aṇudit-sūtra</s>, after stating by another method the absence of <s>savarṇa</s>-grasping in affixes, substitutes, and augments, [the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> says]: 'Since, when the matter is already established, he teaches the prohibition with "<s>apratyayaḥ</s>," that indicates this <s>paribhāṣā</s>: "There is no grasping of homogeneous sounds by a sound being produced."' Furthermore, even though the lengthening would be established simply by '<s>jyād a</s>,' the long vowel pronunciation in '<s>jyādāt</s>' [in that sūtra] is an indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>aṇudit-sūtra</s> and on the sūtra '<s>jyādāt</s>.' In [the sūtra] '<s>coḥ kuḥ</s>' and the like, there is <s>savarṇa</s>-grasping even by the sound being produced, due to the force of the <s>udit</s> (u-marked) pronunciation in the rule. Intending precisely this, the later [grammarians] read: '<s>bhāvyamānāt savarṇān na gṛhṇāti</s>' (a sound being produced does not grasp homogeneous sounds).

children.text: nanvevam 'adaso 'seḥ' ityādinā 'amū' ityādau dīrgavidhānaṃ na syādata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, the lengthening prescribed by '<s>adaso 'seḥ</s>' and the like in forms like '<s>amū</s>' would not occur. Therefore he states:

children.text: bhāvyamāno 'pyukāraḥ savarṇān gṛṇahāti || 19 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 19: Even a <s>u</s>-sound that is being produced grasps homogeneous sounds.

children.text: 'diva ut' 'ṛta ut' iti taparakaraṇamasyā jñapakam/ 'titsvaritam' iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭaiṣā//
children.translated_text: The <s>tapara</s> (t-marking) in '<s>diva ut</s>' and '<s>ṛta ut</s>' is the indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>titsvaritam</s>'.

children.text: nanu 'gave hitaṃ gohitam' ityādau pratyayalakṣaṇenāvādyādeśāpattirata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>gave hitaṃ gohitam</s>' (beneficial to the cow) and the like, there would be the unwanted application of the <s>av</s>-substitute by <s>pratyayalakṣaṇa</s> (rule based on affix-identity). Therefore he states:

children.text: varṇāśraye nāsti pratyayalakṣaṇam// Paribh_20//
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 20: There is no <s>pratyayalakṣaṇa</s> (application of affix-based rules) when the operation pertains to individual sounds (<s>varṇa</s>).

children.text: varṇaprādhānyaviṣayametat/ tatvaṃ ca 'pratyayalope' iti sūtre sthānivadityanuvṛtyaiva siddhe pratyayalakṣaṇagrahaṇaṃ pratyayetarāviśeṣaṇatvarūpaṃ yatra prādhānyaṃ tatraiva pravṛtyarthametatsiddham/ varṇaparādhānyaṃ ca varṇasyetarāviśeṣaṇatvarūpaṃ pratyayanirūpitaniśeṣyatārūpaṃ ca/ tena 'gohitam' ityādau avādi na, 'citrāyāṃ jātā citrā' ityādāvaṇyo 'kārastadantān ṅīp ca na/ iyamalvidhau sthānivatvāprāptāvapi prāptapratyayalakṣaṇavidherniṣedhiketi spaṣṭaṃ bhāṣye//
children.translated_text: This [rule] pertains to the domain where the phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>) is principal. And the proof is: in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>pratyayalope</s>' (when a suffix is elided), since the result is already achieved by the continued application of <s>sthānivat</s> (treated as if the original were present), the specific mention of '<s>pratyayalakṣaṇa</s>' (suffix-based [operation]) [indicates that] its purpose is for application only where the principality takes the form of the suffix being a qualifier of something other [than itself] — this is established. And the principality of the phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>) takes the form of the phoneme being a qualifier of something other, and the form of being qualified as determined by the suffix. Therefore, in [forms like] '<s>gohitam</s>' and the like, it does not [apply]; in [cases like] '<s>citrāyāṃ jātā citrā</s>' and the like, [the feminine suffix] <s>ṅīp</s> does not [apply] to another <s>akāra</s>-ending [word] or to words ending in that. This [rule], even when the <s>sthānivat</s> [principle] does not obtain in <s>alvidhi</s> (phoneme-based operations), is a prohibition of a suffix-based rule that does obtain — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: nanu 'ataḥ kṛkami' ityatra kami grahaṇe siddhe, kaṃsagrahaṇaṃ vyartham, ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>ataḥ kṛkami</s>,' since the mention of <s>kami</s> alone would suffice, the [additional] mention of <s>kaṃsa</s> is redundant. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: uṇādayo 'vyutpannāni prātipadikāni// Paribh_21//
children.translated_text: <s>Uṇādi</s> [formations] are underived <s>prātipadikas</s> (nominal stems). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 21]

children.text: idamevāsyā jñāpakamiti kaiyaṭādayaḥ/ kaṃsestu na, kaṃso 'nabhidhānāt/"pratyayasya luk"ityādau bhāṣye spaṣṭā/"ṇvultṛcau"ityādau bhāṣye vyutpannānītyapi/ idaṃ śākaṭāyanarītyā/ pāṇinestvavyutpattipakṣa eveti śabdendu śekhare nirūpitam/"āyaneyī"iti sūtre bhāṣye spuṭametat//
children.translated_text: This very [redundancy] is the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) of this [paribhāṣā] — so [say] <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> and others. But <s>kaṃsa</s> does not [come under the uṇādi], because [the suffix] is not expressive [of the meaning] (<s>anabhidhāna</s>). This [paribhāṣā] is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>pratyayasya luk</s>' and the like. In the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>ṇvultṛcau</s>' and the like, [the view that they are] 'derived' (<s>vyutpanna</s>) is also [stated]. This [latter view] is according to <s>Śākaṭāyana</s>'s tradition. But for <s>Pāṇini</s>, only the view that they are underived [is correct] — this is established in the <s>Śabdenduśekhara</s>. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>āyaneyī</s>.'

children.text: nanu 'devadattaccikīrṣati' ityādau devādeḥ sannantatvaprayuktadhātutvādyāpattirata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In [forms like] '<s>devadattaś cikīrṣati</s>' and the like, [the word] '<s>deva</s>' etc. would wrongly acquire the properties of a verbal root (<s>dhātu</s>) due to being part of a <s>san</s>-ending [formation]. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: pratyayagrahaṇe yasmātsa vihitastadādestadantasya grahaṇam|| 22 ||
children.translated_text: When a suffix is mentioned, that which begins with [the base] from which that [suffix] is prescribed, and that which ends in it, are [both] included. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 22]

children.text: "yasmātpratyayavidhiḥ"iti sūtre yasmātpratyayavidhistadādipratyaya iti yogo vibhajyate/ gṛhyamāṇa upatiṣṭata iti śeṣaḥ/ tena tadādyantāṃśaḥ siddhaḥ/ tadantāṃśastu"yenavidhiḥ"ityanena siddhaḥ/ sa ca śabdarūpaṃ viśeṣyamādāya viśeṣyāntarāsatve/ yattu pratyayena svaprakṛtyavayavakasamudāyākṣepāt tadviśeṣaṇatvena tadantavidhiriti/ tat, na ; 'iyān' ityādau tasya tādṛśasamudāyena vyabhicāreṇākṣepasambhavāt/ yatra pratyayo nimittatvenāśrīyate, tatra tadādītyantāṃśamātropasathitiriti"aṅgasya"iti sūtre bhāṣyakaiyaṭayoḥ//
children.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>yasmāt pratyayavidhiḥ</s>' (from which a suffix is prescribed), the construction is divided as: '<s>yasmāt pratyayavidhiḥ tadādi pratyayaḥ</s>' — [with] the remainder: 'when grasped, is understood.' By this, the <s>tadādi</s> (beginning-with-that) portion is established. The <s>tadanta</s> (ending-in-that) portion, however, is established by [the rule] '<s>yena vidhiḥ</s>' (that by which an operation [is prescribed]). And that [operates] by taking the word-form as the qualificand, when no other qualificand is available. As for the [alternative view] that because the suffix entails (<s>ākṣepa</s>) the aggregate consisting of its own base, it operates as a qualifier thereof and thus the <s>tadanta-vidhi</s> (rule applying to what ends in it) [follows] — that is not so; because in [forms like] '<s>iyān</s>' and the like, there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) [from] such an aggregate, making the entailment impossible. Where the suffix is relied upon as a cause (<s>nimitta</s>), there only the <s>tadādi</s> (beginning-with-that) portion is understood — [this is clear] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>aṅgasya</s>'.

children.text: evaṃ yatrāpi pañcamyantātparaḥ pratyaya ātrīyate, ratrāpi tadādītyantāṃśopasthitiḥ, parantu tatra pañcamyantatā/ ata eva"eṅhrasvāt"iti sūtre eṅantādityarthalābhaḥ/ asyāḥ paribhāṣāyāḥ prayojanāntaram, 'yenavidhiḥ' ityatra, bhāṣya uktam, 'paramagārgyāyaṇaḥ' iti/ paramagārgyāyaṇasyāpatyamiti vigrahe 'pi gārgyāyaṇaśabdādeva pratyayaḥ, na viśiṣṭāt/ niṣkṛṣya tāvanmātreṇaikārthībhāvābhāve 'pi vṛttirbhavatyeva/ atra cedaṃ bhāṣyameva mānamityanyatra vistaraḥ/ pratyayamātragrahaṇe eṣā, na tu, pratyayāpratyayagrahaṇa iti"ugitaśca"iti sūtre bhāṣye/ iyamaṅgasaṃjñā sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭā//
children.translated_text: Similarly, even where a suffix is taught as following an ablative-ending [term], the <s>tadādi</s> portion is understood; however, there the ablative-ending [term functions as] the boundary (<s>avadhi</s>). For this very reason, in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>eṅhrasvāt</s>,' the meaning 'after that which ends in <s>eṅ</s>' is obtained. Another purpose of this <s>paribhāṣā</s> is stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>yena vidhiḥ</s>': '<s>paramagārgyāyaṇaḥ</s>' (the supreme descendant of <s>Gārgya</s>). Even in the analysis 'the offspring of <s>Paramagārgyāyaṇa</s>,' the suffix [is applied] only from the word <s>gārgyāyaṇa</s>, not from the qualified [compound]. Even when there is no semantic unity (<s>ekārthībhāva</s>) by extracting just that much [of the stem], a <s>vṛtti</s> (derived form) is indeed possible. Here the <s>Bhāṣya</s> itself is the authority — [for] details, [see] elsewhere. This [paribhāṣā] applies to the mention of a suffix alone, not to the mention of [both] suffix and non-suffix — [this is stated] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ugitaś ca</s>.' This [paribhāṣā] is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>aṅga-saṃjñā sūtra</s>.

children.text: yena vidhiriti sūtre bhāṣya etadghaṭakatadantāṃśasyāpavādaḥ paṭhyate :-
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>yena vidhiḥ</s>,' an exception to the <s>tadanta</s> portion produced by this [paribhāṣā] is stated:

children.text: pratyayagrahaṇe cāpañcamyāḥ || 23 ||
children.translated_text: When a suffix is mentioned, [this rule does] not [apply if the mention follows] an ablative [construction]. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 23]

children.text:
yatra pañcamyantātparaḥ pratyayaḥ kāryāntaravidhānāya parigṛhyate, tatra tadantavidhirnetyarthaḥ/ yathā"radābhyāṃ niṣṭātonaḥ"ityatra/ tena dṛṣattīrṇetyādau dhātutakārasya na natvam/ tadantetyaṃśānupasthitāvapi tadādītyaṃśasyopasthitau repha-dāntātparasya niṣṭātasyetyartha iti na doṣaḥ, tadaṃśānupasthitau mānābhāvāt/ tadantāṃśopasthitau tūbhayorekaniṣayatvameva syāditi 'dṛṣattīrṇaḥ' ityādau doṣaḥ syādeva/"syatāsī ḷluṭoḥ"ityādau ḷluṭoḥ parayorityarthe niyamenāvadhisākāṅkṣatvenopasthitadhātorityasyāvadhitvena
anvayānna tadantavijhiḥ/ 'ṅyābhyaḥ' ityādau tu na doṣaḥ, tatra kasmāditi niyatāvadhyākāṅkṣāyā abhāvena pañcamyantasya pratyayaviśeṣaṇatvābhāvāt/ aṅga saṃjñā sūtre tu tadādeḥ pratyaye para ityarthe pañcamyantasya viśeṣaṇatvaṃ spaṣṭameva/ ata eva"uttamaikābhyām" ityādi nirdeśāḥ saṅgacchante//
children.translated_text: Where a suffix that follows an ablative-ending [term] is taken up for the purpose of prescribing another operation, there the <s>tadanta-vidhi</s> (rule applying to what ends in it) does not [apply] — that is the meaning. As in '<s>radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ</s>' (after <s>rad</s> and <s>ad</s>, [the <s>n</s>] of <s>niṣṭhā</s> [becomes] <s>ṇ</s>). Therefore, in [forms like] '<s>dṛṣat-tīrṇa</s>' and the like, the <s>takāra</s> of the verbal root does not undergo <s>ṇatva</s> (cerebral substitution). Even when the <s>tadanta</s> portion is not understood, if the <s>tadādi</s> portion is understood, [the meaning is:] 'of the <s>niṣṭhā</s> [suffix] that follows [a stem ending in] <s>repha-da</s>' — so there is no fault, because in the absence of the <s>tadanta</s> portion there is no authoritative basis [for the wider scope]. But if the <s>tadanta</s> portion were understood, both [the root and the suffix] would refer to the same referent — and then in '<s>dṛṣat-tīrṇaḥ</s>' and the like there would indeed be a fault. In [sūtras like] '<s>syatāsī ḷluṭoḥ</s>' and the like, [the meaning] 'of <s>ḷluṭ</s> that follows' — because the verbal root, understood as necessarily requiring a boundary (<s>avadhi</s>) by the restriction, is construed as the boundary — there is no <s>tadanta-vidhi</s>. In '<s>ṅyābhyaḥ</s>' and the like, however, there is no fault, because there is no definite boundary-expectation, and therefore the ablative-ending [term] does not qualify the suffix. But in the <s>aṅga-saṃjñā sūtra</s>, the qualification of the ablative-ending [term] in the sense 'suffix following that' is clear. For this very reason, references like '<s>uttamaikābhyām</s>' and the like are consistent.

children.text: nanvevam 'kumārī brāmhaṇīrūpā' ityādau 'gharūpa' iti hrasvāpattirata āha:-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, in '<s>kumārī brāhmaṇīrūpā</s>' and the like, there would be the undesired shortening of the vowel through [the rule] '<s>gharūpa</s>.' Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: uttarapadādhikāre pratyayagrahaṇe na tadantagrahaṇam || 24 ||
children.translated_text: In the section on the latter member (<s>uttarapada</s>), when a suffix is mentioned, there is no inclusion of what ends in it (<s>tadanta</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 24]

children.text: "hṛdayasya hṛllekhayaṇlādeśeṣu"ityatra lekhagrahaṇāt/ tatra lekheti na ghañantam, anabhighānāt/ iyaṃ ca 'hṛdayasya' iti sūtra eva bhāṣye spaṣṭā//
children.translated_text: [The indicator is] the mention of '<s>lekha</s>' in [the sūtra] '<s>hṛdayasya hṛllekhayaṇlādeśeṣu</s>.' There, '<s>lekha</s>' is not the <s>ghañ</s>-ending [form], because [the suffix] is not applicable (<s>anabhidhāna</s>). This [paribhāṣā] is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>hṛdayasya</s>' itself.

children.text: nanvevam 'paramakārīṣagandhīputraḥ' ityatreva 'atikārīṣagandhyāputraḥ' ityatra"ṣyaṅaḥ samprasāraṇaṃ putrapatyoḥ"
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, just as in '<s>paramakārīṣagandhīputraḥ</s>,' so too in '<s>atikārīṣagandhyāputraḥ</s>,' [the rule] '<s>ṣyaṅaḥ samprasāraṇaṃ putrapatyoḥ</s>'

children.text: iti syādata āha:-
children.translated_text: would [wrongly] apply. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: strīpratyaye cānupasarjane na || 25 ||
children.translated_text: When a feminine suffix is [mentioned] and is not subordinate (<s>anupasarjana</s>), [the <s>tadādi</s> restriction does] not [apply]. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 25]

children.text:
viṣayasaptamīyam/ yaḥ strīpratyayaḥ striyaṃ prādhānyenā'ha tatra tadādiniyamo na, yastvaprādhānyenā'ha tatra tadādiniyamo 'styevetyarthaḥ/ pratyāsatyā yasya samudāyastrīpratyayāntatvamāneyaṃ tadarthaṃ pratyanupasarjanatvamevaitatparibhāṣāpravṛttau nimittam/ tena 'atirājakumāriḥ' ityādau rājakumārīśabdārthasyātiśabdārthaṃ pratyupasarjanatve 'pi tadarthaṃ pratyanupasarjanatvāt tadādāniyamābhāvena hrasva siddhiḥ/ ata evātra paribhāṣāyāṃ na śāstrīyamupasarjanatvam, asambhavāt/ asyāḥ 'pratyayagrahaṇe' ityasyāpavādatvāt tadekavākyatvāpannatvāccātrāpi grahaṇapada
sambandhena strīpratyayasāmānyagrahaṇe tadviśeṣagrahaṇe ca pravṛttiḥ, na tu strīpratyayāstrīpratyayagrahaṇe/ dhvanitañcedam 'arthavat'
sūtre bhāṣye/ iyaṃ ca vācanikyeva/ 'ṣyaṅaḥ' iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭā//
