children.translated_text: This is a locative of domain (<s>viṣaya-saptamī</s>). A feminine suffix that primarily denotes the feminine — with respect to that, the <s>tadādi</s> restriction does not [apply]; but one that denotes [the feminine] secondarily — with respect to that, the <s>tadādi</s> restriction does apply — that is the meaning. Due to proximity, for one whose aggregate form ends in a feminine suffix — for the purpose of [qualifying] that [aggregate's referent], the condition of being non-subordinate (<s>anupasarjana</s>) is the basis for the application of this <s>paribhāṣā</s>. Therefore, in '<s>atirājakumāriḥ</s>' and the like, even though the referent of the word <s>rājakumārī</s> is subordinate to the referent of the word <s>ati</s>, because it is non-subordinate with respect to that [aggregate's] referent, due to the absence of the <s>tadādi</s> restriction, the shortening [of the vowel] is established. For this very reason, in this <s>paribhāṣā</s>, it is not the technical (<s>śāstrīya</s>) subordination [that is meant], because that is impossible. Since this [paribhāṣā] is an exception to [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 22] '<s>pratyayagrahaṇe</s>' (when a suffix is mentioned), and being incorporated into a single sentence with it, here too, through its connection with the word '<s>grahaṇa</s>' (mention), [this paribhāṣā] operates in the mention of a feminine suffix in general and in the mention of a specific [feminine suffix] — but not in the mention of [both] feminine suffix and non-feminine suffix. And this is implied in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>arthavat</s>.' This [paribhāṣā] is indeed explicitly stated (<s>vācanikī</s>). It is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ṣyaṅaḥ</s>.'

children.text: nanvevam"taraptamapau ghaḥ"ityādinā tarabantādeḥ saṃjñā syādata āha:-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, by [the rule] '<s>taraptamapau ghaḥ</s>' and the like, there would be a [<s>gha</s>-]designation for [the form] beginning with <s>tarap</s> and ending [in it]. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: saṃjñāvidhau pratyayagrahaṇe tadantagrahaṇaṃ nāsti || 26 ||
children.translated_text: In the domain of <s>saṃjñā</s> (technical designation), when a suffix is mentioned, there is no inclusion of what ends in it (<s>tadanta</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 26]

children.text: "sūptiṅantam"ityantagrahaṇamasyāṃ jñāpakam/ na ca pratyayayoḥ padasaṃjñāyāmapi pratyayagrahaṇaparibhāṣayā tadantagrahaṇābhāvāt jñāpite 'pi phalābhāva iti vācyam, padasaṃjñāyāḥ 'svādiṣu' iti viṣaye prakṛti niṣṭatayā padagrahaṇasya pratyayamātragrahaṇatvābhāvāt/"suptiṅantam"iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭā //
children.translated_text: The [compound] ending in '<s>anta</s>' (final) in [the sūtra] '<s>sūptiṅantam</s>' is the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) of this [paribhāṣā]. Nor should it be said that even in the <s>pada</s>-designation of [the word ending in] a suffix, since the <s>paribhāṣā</s> of '<s>pratyayagrahaṇa</s>' (when a suffix is mentioned) [would lead to] the absence of <s>tadanta</s> inclusion, there is no result even if [this rule] is indicated — [this is not valid] because the <s>pada</s>-designation, being established with reference to the base in the domain '<s>svādiṣu</s>' (before <s>sup</s> endings etc.), the mention of '<s>pada</s>' is not a mention of a suffix alone. This [paribhāṣā] is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>suptiṅantam</s>.'

children.text: nanu 'avatapte nakulasthitam' ityādau nakulasthita śabdasya ktāntatvābhāvāt samāso na syādata āha:-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>avatapte nakulasthitam</s>' and the like, since the word <s>nakulasthita</s> does not end in <s>kta</s>, the compound should not [be formed]. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: kṛdgrahaṇe gatikārakapūrvasyāpi grahaṇam|| 27 ||
children.translated_text: When a <s>kṛt</s> suffix is mentioned, [the form] even with a <s>gati</s> (preverb) or <s>kāraka</s> (case-relation element) prefixed is [also] included. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 27]

children.text:
asyāśca karmaṇi ktānta uttarapade 'nantaro gatiḥ prakṛtisvara ityarthake 'gatiranantaraḥ' iti sūtre anantara grahaṇaṃ jñāpakam/ taddhi 'abhyuddhṛtam' ityādāvativyāpti vāraṇārtham/ 'pratyayagrahaṇa' paribhāṣayoddhṛtasya ktāntatvābhāvādeva
aprāptau tadvyarthaṃ sadasyā jñāpakam/ na ca 'abhyuddhṛtam' ityādau paratvāt 'gatirgatau' ityanenābhernighāta eveti vācyam, pādādisthatvena, padātparatvābhāvena ca tadaprāpteḥ/ anantaragrahaṇe kṛtetu tatsāmartyād gatyākṣiptadhātunirūpitamevenantaryaṃ gṛhyata iti na doṣaḥ/ na ca 'abhyuddhṛtam' ityādāvabhinā samāse 'nantarasyodaḥ pūrvapadatvābhāve 'pi svarārthaṃ taditi vācyam/ 'kārakād datta' iti sūtre 'kārakāt' iti yogaṃ vibhajya tatra gati grahaṇamanuvartya kārakādeva paraṃ gatipūrvapadaṃ
ktāntamantodāttamiti niyamena thāthādisvarāprāptyā kṛtsvareṇoda udāttatvasiddheḥ/ tasmādanantaragrahaṇaṃ vyavahitanivṛtyarthameveti jñāpakameva/ yatra gatikārakasamabhivyāhṛtaṃ kṛdantaṃ tatra kṛdgrahaṇe tadviśiṣṭasyaiva grahaṇam/ 'api'
śabdāt tadasamabhivyāhṛtasya kevalasyāpīti tadarthaḥ/ anyathānayā kṛdgrahaṇaviṣaye paratvāt 'pratyayagrahaṇa' paribhāṣāyā bādha eva syādityapi grahaṇam/ ata eva 'sāṅkūṭinam' iti 'gatikārakopapadānām' iti 'kṛdgrahaṇa' iti ca paribhāṣābhyāṃ kṛdantena samāse kṛte viśiṣṭādevāṇi siddhyati, na tu 'saṅkauṭinam' iti 'puṃyogāt' iti sūtre bhāṣyoktaṃ saṅgacchate anyathā tatra kevalakūṭinnityetasyāpīnuṇantatvāttato 'ṇi pākṣikadoṣo durvāra eva syāt/ spaṣṭaṃ cedaṃ sarvam"samāse 'nañpūrve"iti sūtre bhāṣyakaiyaṭayoḥ/ 'gatiranantaraḥ' ityatra tu gateḥ pūrvapadasya ktānta uttarapade pare kāryavidhānāttatsamavadhāne 'pi kevalasya ktāntatvena grahaṇaṃ bodhyam/ iyaṃ ca kṛdviśeṣagrahaṇe kṛtsāmānyagrahaṇe ca, na tu kṛdakṛdgrahaṇa iti/ 'anupasarjanāt' iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam//
children.translated_text: And the occurrence of the word '<s>anantara</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>gatiranantaraḥ</s>' — in the sense of 'that which follows immediately after a <s>gati</s> and a <s>prakṛti</s> retains its original accent' — when a <s>kta</s>-ending [participle] with <s>karman</s> (object) is the latter member [of a compound], is an indicatory sign (<s>jñāpaka</s>). For that [word '<s>anantara</s>'] is for the purpose of preventing over-extension in [forms like] '<s>abhyuddhṛtam</s>' and so on. Since, by the <s>paribhāṣā</s> '<s>pratyayagrahaṇa</s>', the non-applicability of <s>kta</s>-ending status to '<s>uddhṛta</s>' [would already obtain], that [word] being purposeless [otherwise] serves as an indicatory sign. And [the objection that] in '<s>abhyuddhṛtam</s>'...

children.text: padāṅgādhikāre tasya ca tadantasya ca || 28 ||
children.translated_text: In the domain of <s>pada</s> (word) and <s>aṅga</s> (stem), [rules apply] to that [word] and also to that ending in it (<s>tadanta</s>). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 28)

children.text:
padamaṅgaṃ ca viśeṣyaṃ viśeṣaṇena ca tadanta vidhiḥ/ tena 'iṣṭakacitam, pakveṣṭakacitam' ityādau
"iṣṭakeṣīkāmālānāṃ cita"iti hrasvaḥ, 'mahān, paramamahān, paramātimahān' ityādau"sāntamahataḥ"iti dīrgaśca siddhaḥ/
ata eva 'taduttarapadasya' iti pāṭho 'yukta iti bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ atra padaśabdenottarapadādhikāraḥ, kevalapadādhikāraśca/
"pādasya padājyāti"ityatra na tadantagrahaṇam, lakṣyānurodhāditi sarvam,"yena vidhiḥ"ityatra bhāṣye spaṣṭam//
children.translated_text: The <s>pada</s> and the <s>aṅga</s> are the qualified [items], and the qualification operates through the <s>tadanta</s> principle (that which ends in it). Thus, in [forms like] '<s>iṣṭakacitam</s>', '<s>pakveṣṭakacitam</s>' and so on, the shortening [of the vowel] by [the rule] '<s>iṣṭakeṣīkāmālānāṃ cita</s>' is established; and in [forms like] '<s>mahān</s>', '<s>paramamahān</s>', '<s>paramātimahān</s>' and so on, the lengthening by [the rule] '<s>sāntamahataḥ</s>' is established. For this very reason, the reading '<s>taduttarapadasya</s>' is inappropriate — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. Here, the word '<s>pada</s>' [refers to] the latter member (<s>uttarapada</s>)...

children.text: nanvevam 'asyāpatyamiḥ' ityādāvadantaprātipadikābhāvādiñ na syāt, ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, in '<s>asyāpatyam iñ</s>' and the like, the <s>iñ</s> suffix would not apply due to the absence of a <s>prātipadika</s> ending in [the required element]. To address this, he says —

children.text: vyapadeśivadekasmin || 29 ||
children.translated_text: The treatment as if possessing the designation (<s>vyapadeśivad</s>) [applies] even to a single [element]. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 29)

children.text:
nimittasadbhāvāt viśiṣṭo 'padeśo mukhyo vyavahāro yasyāsti sa vyapadeśī/ yastu vyapadeśahetvabhāvādavidyamānavyapadeśo 'sahāyaḥ, sa tena tulyaṃ vartate, kāryaṃ pratītyekasminnasahāye 'pi tatkāryaṃ kartavyamityarthaḥ/ tenākārasyāpyadantatvānna kṣatiḥ/ ekasminnityukteḥ 'sabhāsannayane' ākārasya nāditvam, daridrāghātāvikārasya nāntatvam/ anyathā 'sabhāsannayane bhavaḥ' ityarthe"vṛddhācchaḥ"daridrāghāterivarṇāntalakṣaṇo 'tta syāt/ ata eva 'hariṣu' ityādau soḥ padatvaṃ na/ loke 'pi bahuputrasatve naikasmin jyeṣṭhakaniṣṭhatvādivyavahāro 'yaṃ me jyeṣṭhaḥ, kaniṣṭhaḥ, madhyama iti, kintvekaputrasatva eva/ anena aśāstrīyasyāpyatideśaḥ/ ata eva 'iyāya' ityādāvekāctvanibandhana dvitva siddhiḥ/ ata eva 'bhavati' ityādau 'bhū' ityasyāṅgatvam, 'iyān' ityādau kāryakālapakṣe taddhitāntatvanibandhanaprātipadikatvañca siddhyati/ anyathā yasmādvihitastadāditvābhāvānna syāt/
yastu yor'thavāṃstatrārthasya tyāgopādānābhyāmekājvyapadeśaḥ, yathā 'iyāya' ityādāvarthavato dhātorayaṃ varṇarūpa eko 'jiti
kaiyaṭaḥ, tanna ; tasya 'ekapadā ṛk' ityatra bhāṣyoktarītyā mukhyavyavahāra satvāt/"ekapadā ṛk' ityatrārthena yukto
vyapadeśaḥ"iti bhāṣye uktam/ ṛktvāderarthaśabdobhayavṛttitvena tasyāḥ śabdamātrarūpaṃ padameko 'vayava ityartha iti tadāśayaḥ/
tasmādekasminstattaddharmāropeṇa yugapat yathā jyeṣṭatvādivyavahāraḥ, yathā ca 'śilāputrakasya śarūram' ityādevekasminnaropitānekakāvasthābhiḥ samudāyarūpatvādyāropeṇaitasya śarūramityādivyavahāraḥ, tathātraikāctvādi vyavahāropapattiriti lokanyāyasiddheyam/
na cāsahāya evaitatpravṛttau bhavatītyatra 'bhū' ityasyāṅgatvānāpattiḥ, sasahāyatvāditi vācyam, śapamādāyāṅgatve kārye yasmādvihitastadāditvetasya sasahāyatvābhāvālloke vijātīyakanyādisatve 'pyekaputrasya tasminnevayameva jyeṣṭha ityādivyavahāravat/
na caivam 'nijau catvāra ekācaḥ' iti bhāṣyāsaṅgatiḥ, ikārasyāsahāyatvābhāvena tatraikāctvānupapādanāditi vācyam, 'ekasmin' ityasyāparyālocanayā tatpravṛtteḥ/
arthavatā vyapadeśivadbhāva ityatrārthavatpadenāpyasahāyatvamupalakṣyate/ arthabodhakena śabdena vyapadeśisadṛśo bhāvaḥ kāryaṃ labhyata iti tadarthaḥ, prāyo 'sahāya evārthavatvāt/ 'kurute' ityādau taśabdākāro 'cāmantya iti vyavahāre sa
ādiryasyeti vyavahāre cāsahāya eveti tatra vyapadeśivadbhāvena ṭisaṃjñāsiddhirityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: The one which has a primary designation — i.e., a principal usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>) — due to the presence of the qualifying condition, is called '<s>vyapadeśī</s>' (the one possessing the designation). But one which, due to the absence of the cause of designation, lacks the designation and is alone (<s>asahāya</s>) — that one behaves as equal to [the one possessing the designation] with respect to the grammatical operation. The meaning is: even to a single one without a companion, that operation must be applied. Therefore, there is no problem even with the <s>ā</s>-vowel being treated as ending in [the required element]. Because it is said 'to a single one', in '<s>sabhāsannayane</s>', the <s>ā</s>-vowel does not receive initial-element treatment (<s>āditva</s>)...

children.text: nanu gargādibhyo vihita yañ tadanta vidhinā paramagargādibhyo 'pi syāt, ata āha:-
children.translated_text: Objection: The <s>yañ</s> suffix prescribed after <s>Garga</s> and others would, by the <s>tadanta</s> principle, also apply after <s>Paramagarga</s> and others. To address this, he says —

children.text: grahaṇavatā prātipadikena tadantavidhirnāsti || 30 ||
children.translated_text: There is no <s>tadantavidhi</s> (that-ending rule) with a <s>prātipadika</s> (nominal stem) that is [itself] being designated (<s>grahaṇavat</s>). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 30)

children.text:
iyaṃ ca 'samāsapratyayavidhau pratiṣedha ugidvarṇagrahaṇavarjam' iti vārtikasthapratyayāṃśānuvādaḥ/ ata eva
'yena vidhiḥ' iti sūtra bhāṣye pratyayavidhibhinne"aptṛn"ityādau gṛhyamāṇaprātipadikenāpi tadanta vidhipratipādanam 'svasā, paramasvasā' ityādyudāharaṇañca saṅgacchate/ ata eva ca tadantavidhisūtre bhāṣye samāsetyādiniṣedhasya kathanavadasya na kathanam/ so 'pi niṣedho viśiṣya tattadrūpeṇa gṛhītaprātipadikasūtra eva/ dhvanitaṃ cedam,"asamāse niṣkādibhyaḥ"iti sūtre bhāṣye/
atra ca jñāpakam"sapūrvācca"iti sūtram/ anyathā"pūrvādiniḥ"ityatra tadantavidhinaiva siddhe kiṃ tena//
children.translated_text: And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is a restatement of the portion concerning suffixes found in the <s>vārttika</s> '<s>samāsapratyayavidhau pratiṣedha ugidvarṇagrahaṇavarjam</s>'. For this very reason, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>yena vidhiḥ</s>', the teaching of the <s>tadanta</s> principle even with a <s>prātipadika</s> that is [itself] being designated — in cases distinct from suffix-rules, such as '<s>aptṛn</s>' and the like — and the examples '<s>svasā</s>', '<s>paramasvasā</s>' and so on, are consistent. And for this very reason, the <s>tadantavidhi</s>...

children.text: nanvevam"sūtrāntāṭṭhak" "daśāntāḍḍaḥ" "ekagopūrvāt"ityādeḥ kevala sūtraśabda daśanśabdaikaśabdādiṣvapi pravṛttirvyapadeśivadbhāvāt syāt, ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, [the rules] '<s>sūtrāntāṭṭhak</s>', '<s>daśāntāḍḍaḥ</s>', '<s>ekagopūrvāt</s>' and the like would apply even to the bare words <s>sūtra</s>, <s>daśan</s>, <s>eka</s>, and so on, by virtue of the <s>vyapadeśivad</s> treatment. To address this, he says —

children.text: vyapadeśivadbhāvo 'prātipadikena || 31 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vyapadeśivad</s> treatment does not [apply] with a <s>prātipadika</s>. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 31)

children.text:
"pūrvātsapūrvādiniḥ"ityekayoga eva kartavye pṛthag yogakaraṇamasyā jñāpakam/ na ca"iṣṭādibhyaḥ"iti sūtre 'nuvṛtyarthaṃ tathā pāṭhaḥ, ata evāniṣṭītyādisiddhiriti vācyam, jñāpakaparabhāṣyaprāmāṇyenāniṣṭītyādiprarayogāṇāṃ
aniṣṭatvāt, ekayoge 'pi tāvata uttaratranuvṛttau bādhakābhavācca/
ata eva"nāntādasaṅkhyādeḥ"iti caritārtham/ anyathā 'pañcamaḥ' ityādāvapi vyapadeśivadbhāvena
saṅkhyāditvāt tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameva/
children.translated_text: The fact that [the rule] '<s>pūrvātsapūrvādiniḥ</s>' is stated as a separate <s>yoga</s> (rule), when it could have been stated in a single <s>yoga</s>, is the indicatory sign (<s>jñāpaka</s>) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. Nor should it be said that the separate statement is for the purpose of recurrence (<s>anuvṛtti</s>) in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>iṣṭādibhyaḥ</s>', and that thereby [forms like] '<s>aniṣṭī</s>' and so on are established — because, by the authority of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> which is the basis of the indicatory sign, usages like '<s>aniṣṭī</s>' are considered undesirable; and because even in a single <s>yoga</s>, when [the term] continues to [the rule] that follows, there is no overriding [objection]. For this very reason, '<s>nāntāda</s>'...

children.text:
iyaṃ ca prātipadika grahaṇe eva, na tu prātipadikāprātipadikagrahaṇe/ tena"ugitaśca"ityatra na doṣa iti tatraiva bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ iyam 'grahaṇavatā' iti ca paribhāṣā prātyayavidhiviṣayaiveti 'asamāse niṣkādibhyaḥ'iti sūtra bhāṣyakaiyaṭayoḥ/
tena 'ahan' ityādeḥ paramāhanśabde kevalāhanśabde ca pravṛttirityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text:
And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] applies only to <s>prātipadika</s> (nominal stem) designation, not to the designation of both <s>prātipadika</s> and non-<s>prātipadika</s>. Therefore, in '<s>ugitaśca</s>' and the like, there is no fault — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on that very [<s>sūtra</s>]. And this <s>paribhāṣā</s> beginning with '<s>grahaṇavatā</s>' pertains only to the domain of suffix-rules — [this is stated] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>asamāse niṣkādibhyaḥ</s>'.
Therefore, the application [of the term] <s>ahan</s> and the like to the compound-final <s>ahan</s>-word and to the bare <s>ahan</s>-word — this is elaborated elsewhere.

children.text: nanu 'vānto yi' ityādau yādau pratyaya ityarthaḥ katham? ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>vānto yi</s>' and the like, how can it mean 'a suffix beginning with <s>ya</s>'? To this he says:

children.text: yasminvidhistadādāvalgrahaṇe || 32 ||
children.translated_text: When a rule is [expressed] with a word in the locative, [it refers to what] begins with that [word], not [what] ends with it. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 32)

children.text:
tadantavidherapavāda iyam/ vācanikyeṣā"yena vidhiḥ"ityatra bhāṣye paṭhitā/ asyāśca svarūpasatī saptamī nimittam/ ata eva"neḍvaśi kṛti"ityādau vaśādeḥ kṛta ityādyarthalābhaḥ/
iyaṃ ca"ārdhadhātukasyeḍ"iti sūtre valāderityādigrahaṇasāmarthyād viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇayorubhayoḥ saptamyantatva eva pravartate/ tena"ḍaḥ si dhuṭ"ityādau sādeḥ parasyeti nārthaḥ/"tīṣasaha" "se 'sicī"ityādau yathā tāderityādyarthalābhaḥ, tathā śabdenduśakhare nirūpitam//
children.translated_text:
This is an exception to the <s>tadantavidhi</s> (that-ending rule). This is a <s>vācanika</s> (explicitly stated) [<s>paribhāṣā</s>], cited in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>yena vidhiḥ</s>'. And the locative case [in the <s>sūtra</s>] has its own form (<s>svarūpa</s>) as its basis. Hence, in '<s>neḍ vaśi kṛti</s>' and the like, the meaning obtained is '<s>kṛt</s> [suffixes] beginning with <s>vaś</s>' and so forth.
And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>], by virtue of the force of the expressions '<s>valādi</s>' etc. in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ārdhadhātukasyeḍ</s>', applies only when both the qualified and the qualifier end in the locative. Therefore, in '<s>ḍaḥ si dhuṭ</s>' and the like, the meaning is not 'that which follows <s>sa</s>'. How the meaning '<s>tādi</s>' (beginning with <s>ta</s>) etc. is obtained in '<s>tīṣasaha</s>', '<s>se 'sicī</s>' and the like — that has been explained in the <s>Śabdenduśekhara</s>.

children.text: "ghaṭapaṭam, ghaṭapaṭau"ityādi siddhaya āha :-
children.translated_text: In order to establish [forms like] '<s>ghaṭapaṭam</s>', '<s>ghaṭapaṭau</s>' and the like, he says:

children.text: sarvo dvandvo vibhāṣayaikavadbhavati || 33 ||
children.translated_text: Every <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) optionally becomes <s>ekavat</s> (singular-like). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 33)

children.text:
"dvandvaśca prāṇi"ityādiprakaraṇaviṣayaḥ sarvo dvandva ityarthaḥ/"cārthe dvandvaḥ"iti sūtreṇa samāhāretarayogayoraviśeṣeṇa dvandva vidhānāt nyāyasiddheyam/"tiṣyapunarvasvoḥ"iti sūtrasthaṃ bahuvacanasyeti grahaṇamasyā jñāpakam/ taddhīdam"tiṣyapunarvasu"ityatra tadvyāvṛtyartham/
na caivamapyatra"jātiraprāṇinām"iti nityaikavadbhāvena bahuvacanābhāvādidaṃ sūtraṃ vyarthamiti vācyam, tadvaikalpikatvasyāpyanena jñāpanāt/ na caite prāṇina iti vācyam,"āpomayaḥ prāṇaḥ"iti śruteradbhirvinā glāyamānaprāṇānāmeva prāṇitvāta/ spaṣṭam cedam"tiṣyapunarvasvoḥ"iti sūtre bhāṣye/
ata eva"dvandvaśca prāṇī"ityādeḥ prāṇyaṅgādīnāmeva samāhāra iti viparītaniyamo na //
children.translated_text:
The meaning is: every <s>dvandva</s> that falls within the domain of the section beginning with '<s>dvandvaśca prāṇi</s>' [and the like]. Since the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>cārthe dvandvaḥ</s>' prescribes <s>dvandva</s> without distinction between <s>samāhāra</s> (collective) and <s>itaretarayoga</s> (mutual association), this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is established by logical necessity (<s>nyāyasiddha</s>). The mention of the plural '<s>bahuvacana</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tiṣyapunarvasvoḥ</s>' is the <s>jñāpaka</s> (indicator) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. For this [mention of plural] is for the purpose of excluding [singular treatment] in '<s>tiṣyapunarvasu</s>'.
Nor should one say that even so, this <s>sūtra</s> is purposeless because there would be no plural due to the obligatory <s>ekavadbhāva</s> (singular treatment) by '<s>jātir aprāṇinām</s>' — for this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] itself indicates (<s>jñāpana</s>) that that [obligatory treatment] is also optional. Nor should one say that these [<s>tiṣya</s> and <s>punarvasu</s>] are not living beings (<s>prāṇin</s>), because from the <s>śruti</s> '<s>āpo mayaḥ prāṇaḥ</s>', those whose vital breaths languish without water are indeed <s>prāṇins</s>. And this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tiṣyapunarvasvoḥ</s>'.
Therefore, from '<s>dvandvaśca prāṇi</s>' and the like, the restrictive rule that only living beings, body parts, and the like take <s>samāhāra</s> — that opposite restriction does not [hold].

children.text: sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyante || 34 ||
children.translated_text: All rules are optionally applied in Vedic usage (<s>chandas</s>). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 34)

children.text: "vyatyayo bahulam"iti sūtre bhāṣye bahulamiti yogavibhāgena"ṣaṣṭhīyuktaśchandasi"iti sūtre veti yogavibhāgena caiṣā sādhitā/ tena"pratīpamanya ūrmiryudhyati"ityādi siddham/ yuddhayata iti prāpnoti//
children.translated_text: This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is established through the division of <s>yoga</s>s (rules) by [the word] '<s>bahulam</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>vyatyayo bahulam</s>' in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, and through the division of <s>yoga</s>s by [the optionality particle] '<s>vā</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ṣaṣṭhīyuktaś chandasi</s>'. Thereby, [forms like] '<s>pratīpam anya ūrmir yudhyati</s>' and the like are established — [where] '<s>yudhyata</s>' [with <s>ātmanepada</s>] would have been expected [by rule].

children.text: nanu kṣiya ityādāviyaṅ katham? ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>kṣiya</s>' and the like, how does <s>iyaṅ</s> [substitution apply]? To this he says:

children.text: prakṛtivadanukaraṇaṃ bhavati || 35 ||
children.translated_text: An imitation (<s>anukaraṇa</s>) is treated like the original (<s>prakṛti</s>). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 35)

children.text: kṣiya itīyaṅ nirdeśo 'syā jñāpakaḥ/ tatreva prātipadikatva nibandhana vibhaktikaraṇādanityā ceyamiti"kṣiyo dīrghāt"ita sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam//
children.translated_text: The citation of <s>iyaṅ</s> in '<s>kṣiya</s>' is the <s>jñāpaka</s> (indicator) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. And that this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is non-eternal (<s>anityā</s>), since in that very [context] the application of case-endings is based on <s>prātipadikatva</s> (nominal stem status) — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>kṣiyo dīrghāt</s>'.

children.text: nanu"rāmau"ityādau vṛddhau kṛtāyāṃ kāryakāla pakṣe kathaṃ padatvam? ubhayata āśrayaṇe 'ntāditvābhāvāt yasmādvahitastadāditadantatvābhāvādata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>rāmau</s>' and the like, when <s>vṛddhi</s> has been applied, how is <s>padatva</s> (word-status) [obtained] under the <s>kāryakāla</s> (operation-time) view? Because when both [the base and the suffix] are resorted to, there is absence of initial-hood and final-hood — since that which is separated [from the original] lacks the status of beginning-with-that and ending-with-that. To this he says:

children.text: ekadeśavikṛtamananyavat || 36 ||
children.translated_text: That which is modified in one part (<s>ekadeśavikṛta</s>) is treated as not different [from the original] (<s>ananyavat</s>). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 36)

children.text:
ananyavadityasyānyavannetyarthaḥ/ tatrānyasādṛśyaniṣedhe 'nyatvābhāvaḥ sutarām/ ata eva tādṛśādarthabodhaḥ, anyathā śaktatāvacchedakaimupūrvyajñānāt tato bodho na syāt/
evañca rāniti māntasya yasmād vihitastatvam, au ityasya parādivatvena suptvamiti tadāditadantatvam
ārthasamājagrastham/
chinnapucche śuni śvatvavyavacahāravanmānte tatvaṃ lokanyāya siddham/ ata eva"prāgdīvyata"iti sūtre bhāṣye
dīvyatiśabdaikadeśadīvyacśabdānukaraṇamidamityuktvā, kimarthaṃ vikṛtanirdeśaḥ? etadeva jñāpayatyācāryo bhavatyeṣā paribhāṣā"ekadeśavikṛtamananyavat"ityuktam/
etenāyaṃ nyāyaḥ śāstrīyakārya eva śāstrīvikāra evetyapāstam/ vikṛtāvayava nibandhana kārye tu nāyam,
children.translated_text:
The meaning of '<s>ananyavat</s>' is 'not like another' (<s>anyavan na</s>). When the resemblance to another is negated, the absence of otherness [follows] a fortiori. And therefore, the cognition of meaning arises from such [a form]; otherwise, since there would be no cognition of the sequence of <s>upasargas</s> (preverbs) etc. that constitute the delimiting conditions of the denotative capacity (<s>śaktatāvacchedaka</s>), cognition would not arise from it.
Thus, in '<s>rāmau</s>', the status of being that from which [the suffix] is enjoined belongs to the <s>ma</s>-final [stem], while the <s>sup</s>-status (nominal ending status) belongs to '<s>au</s>' by virtue of its being <s>parādi</s> (beginning of the latter part) — thus the status of beginning-with-that and ending-with-that
is grasped by the aggregate of meaning.
Just as in the case of a dog whose tail has been cut off, the designation 'dog' (<s>śvatva</s>) continues — so too the designation '<s>tatva</s>' (that-ness) for the <s>ma</s>-final [stem] is established by ordinary convention (<s>lokanyāya</s>). Therefore, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>prāg dīvyataḥ</s>',
having said 'this is an imitation of <s>dīvyac</s>, which is a part of the word <s>dīvyati</s>', [<s>Patañjali</s> asks:] 'What is the purpose of the modified citation?' [And answers:] 'The teacher indicates precisely this — that this <s>paribhāṣā</s> exists: "that which is modified in one part is treated as not different."'
By this, the [objection] that this principle applies only to operations that are <s>śāstrīya</s> (rule-based), only to modifications that are <s>śāstrīya</s> — that is set aside. However, in operations based on a modified component, this [principle does] not [apply],

children.text:
chinnepucche śuni pucchavatvavyavahāravat vikṛtāvayavavyavahārasya durupapādatvāt/
evamaktaparimāṇagrahaṇe 'pi nāyam, uktayukteḥ/
etat"yenavidhiḥ"ityatra bhāṣyakaiyaṭayordhvanitam/
yatra tvardhaṃ tadadhikaṃ vā vikṛtam, tatra jātivyañjakabhūyo 'vayavadarśanābhāvena tatvāpratītau kāryasidhyarthaṃ vikṛtānalrūpāvayavatvapratītyarthaṃ ca"sathānivat"sūtram/ kvacittu lakṣyānurodhānnyāyānāśrayaṇam/ tena 'ābhīyāt ityādi siddhiḥ/ spaṣṭaṃ ca kvacinnyāyāpravṛttiḥ"prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ"ityatra kaiyaṭena darśitetyanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text:
just as in the case of a dog whose tail has been cut off, the convention of 'having a tail' does not [continue] — because the convention regarding a modified component is difficult to sustain.
Likewise, this [principle] does not [apply] in the case of designation of a stated measure, for the same reason.
This is implied in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on '<s>yena vidhiḥ</s>'.
But where half or more is modified, there — since the majority of components that manifest the <s>jāti</s> (class/universal) are not perceived — when the recognition of that-ness fails, the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>sthānivat</s>' serves to establish the operation and to bring about the recognition that the component has the form of the original (<s>vikṛtānalrūpāvayavatva</s>). But in some cases, due to conformity with attested usage (<s>lakṣya</s>), this principle is not resorted to. Thereby, [forms like] '<s>ābhīyāt</s>' and the like are established. And that in some cases this principle does not apply has been shown by <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on '<s>prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ</s>' — this is elaborated elsewhere.

children.text: iti śrīnāgeśabhaṭṭaviracite paribhāṣenduśekhare śāstratvasampādanoddeśanāmakaṃ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Paribhāṣenduśekhara</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Nāgeśa Bhaṭṭa</s>, [ends] the section named 'Establishing the Status of Being a Rule' (<s>Śāstratvasampādana</s>),

children.text: prathamaṃ prakaraṇam//
children.translated_text: the first chapter.

children.text: atha bādhabījanāmakaṃ dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇam//
children.translated_text: Now begins the second chapter named 'The Basis of Supersession' (<s>Bādhabīja</s>).

children.text: pūrvaparanityāntarajṅgāpavādānāmuttarottaraṃ balīyaḥ || 37 ||
children.translated_text: Among <s>pūrva</s> (prior), <s>para</s> (subsequent), <s>nitya</s> (invariable), <s>antaraṅga</s> (internally conditioned), and <s>apavāda</s> (exception), each successive one is stronger [than the preceding]. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 37)

children.text: pūrvātparaṃ balavat, vipratiṣedha śāstrāt, pūrvasyaparaṃ bādhakamiti yāvat//
children.translated_text: The subsequent (<s>para</s>) is stronger than the prior (<s>pūrva</s>); than the rule of <s>vipratiṣedha</s> (mutual conflict) — that is to say, the subsequent supersedes (<s>bādhaka</s>) the prior.

children.text: nanvevam 'bhindhi' ityatra paratvāt tātaṅā bādhito dhirna syādata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, in '<s>bhindhi</s>', the <s>dhi</s> [ending], superseded by <s>tātaṅ</s> due to <s>paratva</s> (subsequence), should not [appear]. To this he says:

children.text: punaḥ prasaṅga vijñānāt siddham || 38 ||
children.translated_text: It is established through the understanding of <s>punaḥprasaṅga</s> (renewed applicability). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 38)

children.text: nanvevam 'tisṛṇām' ityatra paratvāt tisrādeśe punastrayādeśaḥ syādata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, in '<s>tisṛṇām</s>', due to <s>paratva</s> (subsequence), after the <s>tisṛ</s>-substitution, the <s>traya</s>-substitution should [re]apply. To this he says:

children.text: sakṛdgatau vipratiṣedhe yad bādhitaṃ tad bādhitameva || 39 ||
children.translated_text: In <s>vipratiṣedha</s> (mutual conflict) governed by <s>sakṛdgati</s> (single-application principle), what has been superseded (<s>bādhita</s>) remains superseded. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 39)

children.text:
tatra kvaciccaritārthayorekasmin yugapadubhayoḥ kāryayorasambhavena bādhakābhāvāt paryāyeṇa tṛjādivacchāstra
dvayaprasaṅge niyamārtham"vipratiṣedha"sūtramiti sakṛdgatinyāyasiddhiḥ/
yathā tulyabalayorekaḥ preṣyo bhavati/ sa tayoḥ paryāyeṇa kāryaṃ karoti, yadā tamubhau yugapat preṣayato nānādikṣu ca kārye tadobhayorna karoti, yaugapadyāsambhavāt/ tathā śāstrayorlakṣyārthayoḥ kvacillakṣye yaugapadyena pravṛtyasambhavādapratipattau praptāyāmidaṃ paravidhyartham/ tatra kṛte yadi pūrvaprāptirasti, tarhi tadapi bhavatyeveti 'punaḥ prasaṅgavijñāna' siddhiriti"vipratiṣedha"sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam/
yattu kaiyaṭādayo vyaktau padārthe pratilakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇopaplavādubhayorapi śāstrayostattallakṣyayoracaritārthyena paryāyeṇa dvayorapi prāptau parameveti niyamārthamidamiti 'sakṛdgati' nyāyasiddhiḥ/ atra pakṣe etanniyamavaśādetallakṣyaviṣayaka pūrvaśāstrānupaplava eva/
jātipakṣe tūddeśyatāvacchedakākrānte kvacillakṣye caritārthayordvayoḥ śāstrayoḥ satpratipakṣanyāyena yugadubhayāsambhavarūpavirodhasthala ubhayorapyaprāptau paravidhyarthamidamiti punaḥ prasaṅgavijñānasiddhirityāhuḥ, tanna ; vyaktipakṣe sarvaṃ lakṣyaṃ śāstraṃ vyāpnoti na jātipakṣa ityatra mānābhāvāt/
'na brāhmaṇaṃ hanyāt' ityādau jātyāśrayasakalavyaktiviṣayatvārthameva jātipakṣāśrayaṇasya bhāṣye darśanāt/ ata eva"sarūpa"sūtre bhaṣye jātau padārthe 'navayavena sākalyena vidhipravṛtteḥ"gauranubandhyaḥ"ityādau sakala gavānubandhanāsambhavāt karmaṇo vaiguṇyamuktam/ dravyavāde cāsarvadravyāvagateḥ 'gauranubandhyaḥ' ityādāvekaḥ śāstrokto 'paro 'śāstrokta ityuktam/
kiñca nahi bhāṣyokta tṛjādidṛṣṭāntasya vyaktivakṣa eva sarva viṣayatvam na dātipakṣa ityatra mānamasti/
api ca vyaktipakṣe 'pyanyavyaktirūpa viṣayalābhena caritārthayoriyaṃ vyaktivirodhāt svaviṣayakatvaṃ na
kalpayatīti vaktuṃ śakyam/ jātipakṣe 'pi tajjātyāśrayatadvyaktiviṣayakatvameva ; naitadvyaktiviṣayakatvamityatra
children.translated_text:
In this regard, in some cases, since both [rules] have fulfilled their purpose (<s>caritārtha</s>) and since in a single [locus] the simultaneous [application] of both operations is impossible — there being no superseder — the <s>sūtra</s> on '<s>vipratiṣedha</s>' serves as a restrictive rule (<s>niyamārtha</s>) [to determine which applies] when there is occasion for two rules alternately, as with <s>tṛj</s>-substitution etc. — this is the establishment of the <s>sakṛdgati</s> (single-application) principle.
Just as when two [masters] of equal authority have one servant: he serves them alternately. But when both command him simultaneously for tasks in different directions, he serves neither, because simultaneous [execution] is impossible. Similarly, when two rules — both having [legitimate] scope in attested usage (<s>lakṣya</s>) — cannot simultaneously operate on a particular attested form, when there arises non-determination, this [<s>sūtra</s>] serves the purpose of [establishing] the later rule. If, after that [later rule] has operated, there is still occasion for the earlier [rule], then that too applies — and this is the establishment of '<s>punaḥprasaṅgavijñāna</s>' (renewed-applicability principle). This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>vipratiṣedha</s>' <s>sūtra</s>.
However, <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> and others [hold that] when the meaning of a word is a particular (<s>vyakti</s>), since [the rule] pervades every instance of the attested form, and since both rules — being <s>caritārtha</s> (purpose-fulfilled) with respect to their respective attested forms — both having occasion [to apply] alternately, this [<s>sūtra</s>] serves as a restrictive rule that only the later one [applies]. This is the establishment of the <s>sakṛdgati</s> principle. Under this view, the non-disturbance of the earlier rule with respect to that particular attested form [follows] precisely from the force of this restrictive rule.
But under the <s>jāti</s> (universal) view, [they say that] when in some attested form both rules that are <s>caritārtha</s> (purpose-fulfilled) [elsewhere], by the principle of <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (having a real opponent), in the locus of conflict — where simultaneous [application] of both is impossible — both fail to apply, and this [<s>sūtra</s>] serves the purpose of [establishing] the later rule; thus the <s>punaḥprasaṅgavijñāna</s> is established. But this is not [correct]; because there is no evidence that under the <s>vyakti</s> view a rule pervades all attested forms but not under the <s>jāti</s> view.
For in '<s>na brāhmaṇaṃ hanyāt</s>' and the like, it is seen in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> that the <s>jāti</s> view is adopted precisely for the purpose of [the rule] applying to all individuals subsumed under the <s>jāti</s>. Therefore, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>sarūpa</s>' <s>sūtra</s>, under the <s>jāti</s> view of word-meaning, since the rule applies to the whole (<s>sākalya</s>) without remainder, it was stated that in '<s>gaur anubandhyaḥ</s>' and the like, since it is impossible to bind all cows, there is a deficiency in the ritual act (<s>karman</s>). And under the <s>dravya</s> (substance) view, since not all substances are apprehended, in '<s>gaur anubandhyaḥ</s>' etc., one [cow] is prescribed by rule and the other is not prescribed by rule — thus it was stated.
Moreover, there is no evidence that the illustration of <s>tṛj</s>-substitution etc. stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> applies to all cases only under the <s>vyakti</s> view and not under the <s>jāti</s> view.
Furthermore, even under the <s>vyakti</s> view, it can be said that [each rule], having obtained scope in the form of another particular (<s>vyakti</s>) and thus being <s>caritārtha</s>, does not claim as its own domain [a form] where there is conflict with [the other rule]. Under the <s>jāti</s> view too, [the scope] is precisely the particulars subsumed under that <s>jāti</s> — not the particulars of this [other <s>jāti</s>]; in this regard

children.text:
niyāmakābhāvaḥ/
tatra lakṣyānusārāt kvacicchāstrīyadṛṣaṭāntāśrayaṇam, kvacillaukikadṛṣṭāntāśrayaṇamiti bhāṣyasammata mārga eva yukta iti bodhyam/
dvayoḥ kāryayoryaugapadyenāsambhava eva vipratiṣedha śāstropayogī/ idam"iko guṇa"iti sūtre kaiyaṭe
spaṣṭam/
yathā 'śiṣṭāt' ityādau tātaṅśībhāvayoryugapatpravṛttau svasvanimittanantaryāsambhavaḥ/ yadyapi tātaṅādeḥ sthānivadbhavenāsthyeva tat, tathāpyādeśapravṛtyuttarameva saḥ, na tu tatpravṛttikāle/
evaṃ numtṛjvatvayoḥ 'priyakroṣṭūni' ityādau yugapadasambhavaḥ, yadāgamā ityasya numpravṛtyuttaraṃ pravṛttaḥ/ evam 'bhindhi' ityatra tātaṅdhibhāvayoryugapadekasthānisambandhasyāṅgarūpanimittānantaryasya cāsambhavo bodhyaḥ/ numnuṭorapi nuṭyajādivibhaktyānantaryabādhaḥ, numi hrasvantāṅgabādha ityasambhavāt vipratiṣedhaḥ/
kvacidiṣṭānurodhena pūrvaśāstre svaritatvapratijñābalāt svaritenādhikaṃ kāryamityarthāt pūrvameva bhavati/ tena sarve pūrva vipratiṣedhāḥ saṅgṛhītā iti"svaritena"iti sūtre bhāṣye/ vipratiṣedhasūtrasthaparaśabdhasyeṣṭavācitvāt tatsaṅgraha iti"vipratiṣedha" sūtre bhāṣye//
children.translated_text: There is no determining factor [to decide between the two]. In that matter, it should be understood that the approach sanctioned by the <s>Bhāṣya</s> alone is correct — sometimes relying on technical (<s>śāstrīya</s>) examples following the pattern of actual usage (<s>lakṣya</s>), and sometimes relying on ordinary (<s>laukika</s>) examples. Only when there is an actual impossibility of two operations occurring simultaneously is the [concept of] <s>vipratiṣedha</s> (conflict of rules) useful for the grammar. This is made clear in <s>Kaiyaṭa</s>'s [commentary] on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>iko guṇa</s>'...

children.text:
nanvevam 'edhate' ityādau paratvāt vikaraṇe"anudāttaṅitaḥ"ityādi niyamānupapattiḥ, tena vyavadhānāt,
ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, in [forms like] '<s>edhate</s>' and so on, the restriction [established] by [the rule] '<s>anudāttaṅitaḥ</s>' and the like would not apply to the <s>vikaraṇa</s> (verbal affix), since it is subsequent (<s>para</s>), and because of the intervening [element]. To address this, he says —

children.text: vikaraṇebhyo niyamo balīyān || 40 ||
children.translated_text: Restrictions (<s>niyama</s>) are stronger than <s>vikaraṇas</s> (verbal affixes). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 40)

children.text:
atra"vṛdbhyaḥ syasanoḥ"iti sūtreṇa sye vibhāṣātaṅvidhānaṃ jñāpakam/ anyathā svavyavadhāne niyamāpravṛttau sāmānya śāstreṇobhayasiddhau vikalpavidhānaṃ vyarthaṃ syāt/ atrārthe jñapite tu 'sya' iti tatra viṣayasaptamī bodyeti"anudāttaṅitaḥ"ityatra bhāṣyakaiyaṭayoḥ spaṣṭam/
vikaraṇavyavadhāne 'pi niyamapravṛtteridaṃ jñapakamiti"śadeḥ śitaḥ"ityatra bhāṣye dhvanitam/
vastuto 'smājjñāpakāt"anudāttaṅitaḥ"ityādiprakaraṇaṃ tibādividhyekavākyatayā vidhāyakam/ tatra"dhātoḥ"iti vihita pañcamī, tatsāmānādhikaraṇam"anudāttaṅita"ityādi vihitaviśeṣaṇameva/
evañca lāvasthāyāṃ sye 'pi tadvyavadhāne taṅsiddhiḥ/ śabādibhyastu pūrvameva niyamaḥ/
yadvā lamātrāpekṣatvādantaraṅgā ādeśāḥ, lakāraviśeṣāpekṣatvāt syādayo bahiraṅgā iti digyogalakṣaṇapañcamyāmapi na doṣaḥ/
atra pakṣe"vṛdbhyaḥ syasanoḥ"iti sūtraṃ syaviṣaya iti vyākhyayam/ ātmane pada śabdādau bhavisaṃjñā'śrayaṇīyeti tatvam/
bhinnavākyatayā sāmānya śāstravihitānāṃ niyame tu lugādineva niyamena jātinivṛttiraṅgīkāryā/"bhuktavantaṃ prati mā bhukthā iti brūyāt, kiṃ tena kṛtaṃ syāt"iti nyāyastu nātra śāstra āśrayituṃ yuktaḥ, niyamādi śāstrāṇāṃ vaiyarthyāpatteḥ/ dhvanitaṃ cedam"sthane 'ntaratamaḥ"iti sūtre bhāṣye/
śāstrānarthakyaṃ tu vṛddhisaṃjñā sūtre bhāṣyetiraskṛtam/ sāmānyaśāstreṇotpattistu sarūpasūtrasttha kaiyaṭa rītyā pradhānānurodhena guṇabhedakalpanā tāvatprakṛti kalpanayā kāryā, pratyayanivṛttau ca tatkalpitaprakṛterapi nivṛttiḥ kalpyeti gauravamityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: Here, the optionally prescribing of <s>ātaṅ</s> for <s>sya</s> by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>vṛdbhyaḥ syasanoḥ</s>' is the indicatory sign (<s>jñāpaka</s>). Otherwise, if the restriction did not operate when its own [element] intervenes, then since both [forms] would be established by the general rule, the prescribing of an option would be purposeless. When this meaning is indicated, [the locative] '<s>sya</s>' there should be understood as a domain-locative (<s>viṣayasaptamī</s>) — [this is clear] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>anudāttaṅitaḥ</s>'...

children.text: parānnityaṃ balavat || 41 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nitya</s> (invariable) is always stronger than the <s>para</s> (subsequent). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 41)

children.text: kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgitvāt/ tatrākḷptābhāvakasyābhāvakalpanāpekṣayā kḷptābhāvakasyaiva tatkalpanamucitamiti, nityasya balavatve bījam//
children.translated_text: Because of being <s>kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgin</s> (applicable whether or not the other has operated). In that case, as between one whose non-occurrence has not been established (<s>akḷptābhāvaka</s>) and one whose non-occurrence has been established (<s>kḷptābhāvaka</s>), it is more appropriate to attribute [non-occurrence] only to the latter — this is the seed of the greater strength of the <s>nitya</s>.

children.text: tadāha :-
children.translated_text: On this he says —

children.text: kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgi nityam, tadviparītamanityam || 42 ||
children.translated_text: That which applies whether or not [the other has operated] is <s>nitya</s> (invariable); the opposite of that is <s>anitya</s> (non-invariable). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 42)

children.text: ata eva 'tudati' ityādau parādapi guṇānnityatvāt śapratyayādirbhavati//
children.translated_text: For this very reason, in [forms like] '<s>tudati</s>' and so on, because of the invariability of <s>guṇa</s> [substitution] even over the subsequent [rule], the <s>śa</s>-affix and the like apply [first].

children.text:
yadvyaktisambhandhitayā pūrvaṃ pravṛttistadvyaktisambhandhitayaiva punaḥ pravṛttau
kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgitvamityāśakhayenāha :-
children.translated_text: With the intention [of stating] that when a rule first operates in relation to a certain individual [form], and then operates again in relation to that very same individual, that is <s>kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgitva</s> (applicability whether or not operated) — he says —

children.text: śabdāntarasya prāpnuvanvidhiranityo bhavati || 43 ||
children.translated_text: A rule that would produce a different word-form (<s>śabdāntara</s>) is <s>anitya</s> (non-invariable). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 43)

children.text: idaṃ 'śadeḥ śitaḥ' iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ tatra hi 'nyaviśata' ityatra vikaraṇe kṛte tadantasyāḍ, akṛte vikaraṇe dhātumātratasyetyaḍanitya ityuktam//
children.translated_text: This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>śadeḥ śitaḥ</s>'. For there, in '<s>nyaviśata</s>', it is stated that the <s>aṭ</s> augment [applies] to the [stem] ending in the <s>vikaraṇa</s> when it has been added, and to the bare root when the <s>vikaraṇa</s> has not been added — hence <s>aṭ</s> is <s>anitya</s>.

children.text: etattulyanyāyenāha :-
children.translated_text: By the same principle, he says —

children.text: śabdāntarāt prāpnuvataḥ śabdāntare prāpnuvataścānityatvam || 44 ||
children.translated_text: When [a rule] would produce from a different word-form, and when [a rule] would produce in [the context of] a different word-form — that too is <s>anitya</s> (non-invariable). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 44)

children.text: etanmūlakamevāha :-
children.translated_text: Stating what is based on this very [principle], he says —

children.text: latraṇāntareṇa prāpnuvan vidhiranityaḥ || 45 ||
children.translated_text: A rule that would produce by means of a different <s>lakāra</s>, <s>tṛṇ</s>, or the like is <s>anitya</s> (non-invariable). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 45)

children.text: atideśaviṣaye iyam"asiddhavat"sūtre kaiyaṭenoktā //
children.translated_text: In the domain of analogical extension (<s>atideśa</s>), this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] has been stated by <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>asiddhavat</s>'.

children.text: yadā tu śāstravyatirekeṇa tadvidheyakāryayoreva nityatvādi vicāro yadāpi vyaktiviśeṣāśrayaṇābhāvaḥ, tadāha :-
children.translated_text: But when, apart from the grammatical system, the determination of <s>nitya</s>-status and the like pertains only to the operations enjoined by those [rules], and when there is no recourse to particular instances — then he says —

children.text: kvacitkṛtākṛtaprasaṅgamātreṇāpi nityatā || 46 ||
children.translated_text: Sometimes, by the mere applicability whether or not [the other has operated], <s>nitya</s>-status [is established]. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 46)

children.text: kṛte dvitīye nityatvenābhimatasya punaḥ prasaṅgamātraṃ nityatvavyavahāre prayojakam, na tu bādhakābādhita phalopahita prasaṅgo 'pi tatheti bhāvaḥ//
children.translated_text: The mere further applicability of [a rule] regarded as <s>nitya</s>, after the second [rule] has operated, is the motivating factor for the designation '<s>nitya</s>' — but it is not the case that even an applicability accompanied by the result of being overridden or not overridden [counts as such]. This is the purport.

children.text: tadāha :-
children.translated_text: On this he says —

children.text: yasya ca lakṣaṇāntareṇa nimittaṃ vihanyate na tadanityam || 47 ||
children.translated_text: That whose condition (<s>nimitta</s>) is obstructed by another rule is not <s>anitya</s>. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 47)

children.text: kvacittu bādhakābādhita phalopahita prasaṅga eva gṛhyate tadāha :-
children.translated_text: But sometimes, even the applicability accompanied by the result of being overridden is accepted [as relevant]. On this he says —

children.text: yasya ca lakṣaṇāntareṇa nimittaṃ vihanyate tadapyanityam // Paribh_48/./
children.translated_text: That whose condition (<s>nimitta</s>) is obstructed by another rule is also <s>anitya</s>. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 48)

children.text:
saptame kaiyaṭenaitadupaṣṭambhakaṃ lokavyavahāradvayamudāhṛtam/ vālisugrīvayoryudhyamānayorbhagavatā vālini hate 'pi sugrīvasya vālitaḥ prābalyaṃ na vyavaharanti, bhagavatsahāyaiḥ pāṇḍavairjaye labdhepi pāṇḍavānāṃ prābalyaṃ vyavaharanti ceti
sarvaṃ cedaṃ lakṣyānurodhād vyavasthitam//
children.translated_text: In the seventh [<s>Āhnika</s>], <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> has cited two instances from common usage to support this: when <s>Vāli</s> and <s>Sugrīva</s> were fighting, even though <s>Vāli</s> was slain by the Lord [<s>Rāma</s>], people do not speak of <s>Sugrīva</s>'s superiority over <s>Vāli</s>; [yet] when the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, aided by the Lord, obtained victory, people do speak of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>' superiority. All this...

children.text: "luṭaḥ prathamasya"iti sūtre bhāṣye -
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>luṭaḥ prathamasya</s>' —

children.text: svaribhannasya prāpnuvanvidhiranityo bhavati || 49 ||
children.translated_text: A rule that would produce by means of a <s>svaribhanna</s> [substitute] is <s>anitya</s> (non-invariable). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 49)

children.text:
iti paṭhyate/ yatra tvekasyaiva kāryasya paratvaṃ nityatvaṃ ca, tatrecchayānyatarattadubhayaṃ vā tasya balavatve niyāmakamullekhyam/ ata eva tatra paratvānnityatvācceti bhāṣye ucyate/
vastutastatra paratvādityuktirekadeśinaḥ/ spaṣṭaṃ cedaṃ vipratiṣedha sūtre kaiyaṭe/"ṇaucaṅi"iti hrasvāpekṣayā nityatvāntaraṅgatvaprayuktadvitvasya prathamataḥ pravṛttau nityatvādityeva bhāṣya uktam/ evaṃ nityāntaraṅgayorbalavatvamapi yaugapadyāsambhava eveti bodyam//
children.translated_text: This is read [in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>]. But where a single operation has both <s>paratva</s> (subsequence) and <s>nityatva</s> (invariability), there, according to one's preference, either one, or both, may be adduced as determining its greater strength. For this very reason, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> there says 'by subsequence, by invariability.' In reality, the statement 'by subsequence' there is the position of a partial [proponent]. This is clearly [an instance of] <s>vipratiṣedha</s> (conflict)...

children.text: nityādapyantaraṅgaṃ balīyaḥ ; antaraṅge bahiraṅgasyāsiddhatvāt/ tadāha :-
children.translated_text: Even stronger than the <s>nitya</s> is the <s>antaraṅga</s> (internally-conditioned operation); because the <s>bahiraṅga</s> (externally-conditioned) is treated as not-yet-established (<s>asiddha</s>) when the <s>antaraṅga</s> [applies]. On this he says —

children.text: asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgamantaraṅge || 50 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>bahiraṅga</s> (externally-conditioned) is treated as <s>asiddha</s> (not-yet-established) when the <s>antaraṅga</s> (internally-conditioned) [applies]. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 50)

children.text:
antaḥumadhye, bahiraṅga śāstrīya nimittasamudāyamadhye, antarbhūtānyaṅgāni nimittāni yasya tadantaraṅgam/ evaṃ tadīyanimittasamudāyād bahirbhatāṅgakaṃ bahiraṅgam/ etacca"kharavasānoḥ"iti sūtre"asiddhavat
sūtre ca bhāṣyakaiyaṭayoḥ spaṣṭam/ atrāṅga śabdena śabdarūpaṃ nimittameva gṛhyate, śabdaśāstre tasyaiva pradhānatvāt/ tena arthanimittakasya na bahiraṅgatvam/ ata eva"na tisṛcatasṛ"iti niṣedhaścaritārthaḥ/ anyathā
strītvarūpārthanimittakatisrāpekṣayāntaraṅgatvāt trayādeśe tadasaṅgatiḥ spaṣṭaiva/
children.translated_text: The <s>antaraṅga</s> is that whose conditions (<s>aṅga</s>, <s>nimitta</s>) are contained within the aggregate of conditions for the grammatical rule — i.e., the conditions are internal to that aggregate. Similarly, the <s>bahiraṅga</s> is that whose conditions extend beyond (<s>bahirbhūta</s>) the aggregate of its own conditions. This is made clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>kharavasānoḥ</s>' and the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>asiddhavat</s>'. Here, the word '<s>aṅga</s>'...

children.text:

nanu"yenavidhistadantasya"iti sūtre bhāṣye"ikoyaṇaci"ityādāvapi tadantavidhau 'syonaḥ' ityatra
antaraṅgatvād yaṇo guṇabādhakatvamiṣyate, tanna sidhyet, ūnaśabdamāśritya yaṇādeśaḥ, na śabdhamāśritya guṇa ityantaraṅgatvād guṇa eva syādityuktam/
atra kaiyaṭaḥ/ siverbāhulakādauṇādike na pratyaye guṇavalopoṭhāṃ prasaṅge ūṭhapavādatvād valopaṃ bādhate, guṇaṃ tvantaraṅgatvād bādhate/ guṇohyaṅgasambandhinīmiglakṣaṇāṃ laghvīmupadhāmārdhadhātukaṃ cāśrayati/ ūṭh tu vakārāntamaṅgamanunāsikādiñca pratyayamityalpāpekṣatvādantaraṅgaḥ/ tatra kṛte yaṇ guṇau prapnuta iti/
evañca saṃjñāpekṣasyāpi bahiraṅgatvaṃ spaṣṭamevoktamiticet, na ; tadantavidhāvapi bahupadārthāpekṣatvarūpa bahiraṅgatvasya guṇe satvena tatra doṣakathanaparabhāṣyāsaṅgateḥ/
bahiraṅgantaraṅgaśabdābhyāṃ bahvapekṣatvālpāpekṣatvayoḥ śabdamaryādayālābhācca/ tathā satyasiddhaṃ bahvapekṣamalpāpekṣa ityeva vadet/

tvadrītyā tadapi vaktumucitam/ prathamyāt tadeva vā vaktumucitam/ mama tvantaraṅgaparibhāṣayā tadvāraṇāsambhavt tannoktam/
kiñca siddhānte nityatvād guṇātpūrvamūṭh, guṇastu yaṇā bādhitatvādanityaḥ/ ūnaśabdamāśrityetyādi bhāṣyāsaṅgatyā cintyam/
vali lope 'ntaraṅgaparibhāṣā na pravartata iti tu na yuktam/ tatsūtre bhāṣya eva vraścādiṣu lopātiprasaṅgamāśaṅkyopadeśasāmarthyānna/
naca 'vṛścati' ityādau cāritārthayam, bahiraṅgatayā samprasāraṇasyāsiddhatvena pūrvameva tatprāpteriti bhāṣyokteḥ/
yattu nalopasya ṣaṭsaṃjñāyāmasiddhatvāt 'pañca' ityatra"na ṣaṭ"iti niṣedha iti, taccincyam/
na lopasyahi padasaṃjñāsāpekṣatvena bahiraṅgatvaṃ vācyam, tacca, na ; saṃjñākṛta bahiraṅgatvasyānāśrayaṇāt/ 'pañca' ityatra
niṣedhastu striyāṃ yatprāpnoti, tanneti vyākhyānasāmarthyena bhūtapūrvaṣaṭtvamādāyeti bhodhyam/
ata eva kṛtitugrahaṇaṃ caritārtham/ 'vṛtrahabhyām' ityādau padatvanimittakatve 'pi nalopasya bahiraṅgatvābhāvāt/ bhyāmaḥ padasaṃjñānimittatve 'pi nalopasya tannimittakatvābhāvāt/ paramparayā nimittatvamādāya bahiraṅgatvāśrayaṇaṃ tu na mānam/ dhvanitaṃ cedam"nalopaḥ sup"itisūtre bhāṣya iti, tatraiva bhāṣyapradīpodyote nirūpitam/
antaraṅge kartavye jātaṃ tatkālaprāptikaṃ ca bahiraṅgamasiddhamityarthaḥ/ vraścādiṣu padasaṃskāra pakṣe samānakālatvameva dvayoriti bodhyam/
etena 'antaraṅgaṃ bahiraṅgād balīyaḥ' iti paribhāṣāntaramityapāstam/ enāmāśritya 'vipratiṣedha' sūtre bhāṣye tasyāḥ pratyākhyānācca/
antaraṅga śāstratvamasyāliṅgam/
iye ca tripādyāṃ na pravartate, tripādyā asiddhatvāt/ asyāñca"vāha ūṭh"sūtrasthamūṭh grahaṇaṃ jñāpakamityeṣā sapādasaptādyāyīsthā/ anyathā samprasāraṇamātravidhānena laghūpadhaguṇe"vṛddhi reci"iti vṛddhau 'viśvauhaḥ' ityādisiddhestadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameva/ satyāṃ hyetasyāṃ bahiraṅgasamprasāraṇasyāsiddhatvāllaghūpadhahuṇo na syāt/
na ca"puganta"iti sūtre nimittamiko viśeṣaṇam, ata eva 'bhinatti' ityādau na guṇaḥ/ evaṃ
"nājānantarye"iti niṣedhāt kathaṃ paribhāṣāpravṛttiriti vācyam, pratyayasyāṅgāṃśa utthitākāṅkṣatvena tatravānvayāt,"puganta"ityādau karmadhārayāśrayaṇena pratyayaparāṅgāvayavalaghūpadhārūpeko guṇa iti"ikoguṇavṛddhī"iti sūtra bhāṣya
sammater'the 'bhinatti' ityādāvadoṣācca/
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the <s>Bhāṣya</s>-<s>Vārttika</s> etc. on the <s>sthānivat</s> <s>sūtra</s> (P. 1.1.56), stating 'prohibition of <s>sra</s>-replacement in the <s>traya</s>-substitute,' is consistent. By this, [the objection] that in '<s>gaudheraḥ</s>,' '<s>paceran</s>' etc., the <s>val</s>-<s>lopa</s> (deletion before <s>val</s>) would not apply because of the <s>bahiraṅga</s>-ness (external-operation status) of <s>ey</s>-substitutes etc. due to their dependence on the <s>aṅga</s>-designation — is refuted. And also because of the <s>ey</s>-substitute etc. being an <s>antaraṅga</s> (internal operation) by virtue of not being a cause of a subsequent [operation]. Objection: In the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>yena vidhis tadantasya</s>' (P. 1.1.72), even in the <s>tadanta</s>-rule regarding '<s>iko yaṇ aci</s>' (P. 6.1.77) etc., in '<s>syonaḥ</s>,' it is said that the <s>yaṇ</s>-substitute overrides <s>guṇa</s> because of <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness; that would not be established, since the <s>yaṇ</s>-substitute depends on the word '<s>ūna</s>' [alone], whereas <s>guṇa</s> depends on the word [as a whole] — hence <s>guṇa</s> alone would prevail by <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness. Here <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> [explains]: when in an <s>Uṇādi</s> suffix [derived] irregularly from <s>siv</s>, on the occasion for <s>guṇa</s>, <s>val</s>-deletion, and <s>ūṭh</s>, <s>ūṭh</s> overrides <s>val</s>-deletion because of being an exception [to it], but overrides <s>guṇa</s> because of <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness. For <s>guṇa</s> depends on the <s>ik</s>-characterized light <s>upadhā</s> (penultimate) connected to the <s>aṅga</s> (stem) and the <s>ārdhadhātuka</s> [suffix]. But <s>ūṭh</s> depends on the <s>v</s>-ending <s>aṅga</s> and the suffix beginning with a nasal — hence it is <s>antaraṅga</s> due to fewer dependencies. Once that is done, <s>yaṇ</s> and <s>guṇa</s> both become applicable. If [one argues] that thus the <s>bahiraṅga</s>-ness of even a designation-dependent [operation] has been clearly stated — no; because in the <s>tadanta</s>-rule too, since the <s>bahiraṅga</s>-ness in the form of multi-item dependency exists for <s>guṇa</s>, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> that discusses the defect there [would be] inconsistent. And because the terms <s>bahiraṅga</s> and <s>antaraṅga</s> obtain the conventional meaning of 'multi-dependent' and 'few-dependent' respectively. Were it so, the established form would merely say 'the multi-dependent [is suspended before] the few-dependent.' For this very reason, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>vipratiṣedha</s> <s>sūtra</s> (P. 1.4.2), the example for 'the <s>yaṇ</s>-substitute etc. [prevails] over <s>guṇa</s> due to <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness' is '<s>syonaḥ</s>,' but it is not said that <s>ūṭh</s> [prevails] over <s>guṇa</s> due to <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness. On your view, it would be appropriate to say that too; or rather, it would be appropriate to say that first [instead]. But in my view, since it is impossible to block that by the <s>antaraṅga</s> <s>paribhāṣā</s>, it is not said. Moreover, in the established doctrine, since <s>ūṭh</s> precedes <s>guṇa</s> due to being <s>nitya</s> (invariable), and <s>guṇa</s> is <s>anitya</s> (variable) because of being overridden by <s>yaṇ</s> — the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage beginning with 'depending on the word <s>ūna</s>' is to be reflected upon. But [the claim] that the <s>antaraṅga</s> <s>paribhāṣā</s> does not operate in <s>val</s>-deletion is not correct; for in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on that very <s>sūtra</s>, having raised the concern of excessive deletion in <s>vraśc</s>-forms etc., [the resolution is] by the authority of the teaching — not [otherwise]. Nor is this rendered purposeless in '<s>vṛścati</s>' etc., because of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> statement that since <s>samprasāraṇa</s> is <s>asiddha</s> (not yet established) due to being <s>bahiraṅga</s>, that [deletion] would be obtained even earlier. As for [the claim] that since <s>na</s>-deletion is <s>asiddha</s> with respect to the <s>ṣaṭ</s>-designation, the prohibition '<s>na ṣaṭ</s>' in '<s>pañca</s>' [follows from that] — this is to be reflected upon. For the <s>bahiraṅga</s>-ness of <s>na</s>-deletion due to its dependence on the <s>pada</s>-designation should not be asserted; and that [objection] is correct, because of the non-reliance on designation-caused <s>bahiraṅga</s>-ness. The prohibition in '<s>pañca</s>' pertaining to the feminine is to be understood by the explanatory power of [the interpretation] 'that which would apply does not apply' — taking into account the prior <s>ṣaṭ</s>-status. For this very reason, the mention of <s>kṛti</s> is fulfilled. In '<s>vṛtrahabhyām</s>' etc., because of the absence of <s>bahiraṅga</s>-ness of <s>na</s>-deletion even when it is a cause of <s>pada</s>-status. [And] because even when <s>bhyām</s> etc. are the cause of the <s>pada</s>-designation, <s>na</s>-deletion is not a cause thereof. Relying on indirect (<s>paramparā</s>) causation for <s>bahiraṅga</s>-ness is not valid. And this is indicated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>nalopaḥ sup</s>' — as examined in the <s>Bhāṣya-Pradīpa-Uddyota</s> on that very passage. The meaning is: when an <s>antaraṅga</s> [operation] is to be performed, the <s>bahiraṅga</s> [operation] that arises at the same time is <s>asiddha</s> (not yet established). In <s>vraśc</s>-forms etc., in the view of <s>pada-saṃskāra</s> (word-level processing), both [operations] are understood to be simultaneous. By this, the [view that] '<s>antaraṅga</s> is stronger than <s>bahiraṅga</s>' is a separate <s>paribhāṣā</s> — is refuted. And because [<s>Nāgeśa</s>] rejects that [separate <s>paribhāṣā</s>] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>vipratiṣedha</s> <s>sūtra</s> by relying on this one. The <s>antaraṅga</s>-nature of the rule is its inferential mark. And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] does not operate in the <s>Tripādī</s> (last three chapters), because of the <s>asiddha</s>-status of the <s>Tripādī</s>. And the mention of <s>ūṭh</s> in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>vāha ūṭh</s>' is the indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] — hence it belongs to the domain from 1.1 up to 6.4. Otherwise, by merely prescribing <s>samprasāraṇa</s>, since '<s>vṛddhi reci</s>' (P. 7.2.115) would establish <s>vṛddhi</s> in the <s>laghūpadhā-guṇa</s> (light-penultimate <s>guṇa</s>), the redundancy of that [<s>ūṭh</s> prescription] in '<s>viśvauhaḥ</s>' etc. is quite clear. For if this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is in force, since the <s>bahiraṅga</s> <s>samprasāraṇa</s> would be <s>asiddha</s>, the <s>laghūpadhā-guṇa</s> would not apply. Nor is the <s>ik</s>-specification in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>puganta</s>' (P. 7.3.86) a qualifier of the cause — for this very reason, <s>guṇa</s> does not [apply] in '<s>bhinatti</s>' etc. [The objection] 'How can the <s>paribhāṣā</s> operate given the prohibition in <s>nājānantarye</s>?' should not be raised, because the suffix, having its unfulfilled expectation arising from the <s>aṅga</s> portion, is connected there. And by relying on the <s>karmadhāraya</s> [analysis] in '<s>puganta</s>' etc., the single <s>guṇa</s> in the form of the suffix-contingent <s>aṅga</s>-component light-penultimate — is consistent with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>iko guṇa-vṛddhī</s>' (P. 1.1.3) — and there is no defect in '<s>bhinatti</s>' etc.

children.translated_text: When the <s>upasarga</s> (preverb) ends in '<s>a</s>' and the <s>upapada</s> (subordinate word) ends in '<s>na</s>', [the form] '<s>vaheḥ</s>' becomes '<s>vāheḥ</s>' optionally — since the <s>ṇvi</s> and the expression-operations [on <s>vah</s>] do not [fully] apply, the <s>na</s>-ending alone remains. Forms like '<s>vāryūheḥ</s>' should be understood as [having] '<s>kvip</s>' from [the root] '<s>ūh</s>.' Due to the multiple meanings of verbal roots, there is no incongruity of meaning. Forms like '<s>prauhaḥ</s>' are simply incorrect, since <s>vṛddhi</s> does not apply. And since this '<s>ūh</s>' element would be purposeless, the rule '<s>prād ūhoṭha</s>' also does not apply. Nor can it be said that under the <s>kāryakālapakṣa</s> (time-of-operation view) the application of this [rule] in the <s>tripādī</s> (last three chapters of the <s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s>) is unavoidable — because, since the later [rule] is <s>asiddha</s> (non-established) with respect to the earlier, there is no <s>antaraṅga</s> (inner-scope) status, and since the earlier [rule] lacks the <s>bahiraṅga</s> (outer-scope) status determined by that, it is impossible for that [<s>tripādī</s> rule] to establish [the earlier one's] non-establishment. Nor can it be said that since, due to the non-establishment of the earlier [rule] by this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>], the later rule's non-establishment with respect to it cannot be stated through '<s>pūrvatra</s>' (earlier rule principle) — for in that case, since there would be no means of determination, the undesirable consequence would be the non-application of both. Moreover, since '<s>pūrvatra</s>' [as a sūtra rule] is directly perceived, it is appropriate that this inferential [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] be overridden by it. Therefore, having first taken up the <s>kāryakālapakṣa</s> and having stated the reasonings, the <s>siddhāntin</s> states in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>visarjanīya-sūtra</s>: 'Therefore this solution is inappropriate — or [it is not inappropriate] because it has the character of a <s>bahiraṅga</s> rule.' The meaning is: when the <s>antaraṅga</s> operation is to be done within the <s>tripādī</s>, the solution is not appropriate. But the intent is that one must simply resort to an explicit statement [rather than the <s>paribhāṣā</s>]. For this very reason, for the <s>la</s>-substitute in forms like '<s>nigālyate</s>,' the statement '<s>tasya doṣaḥ</s>' was explicitly introduced. Otherwise, since due to <s>antaraṅga</s> status the optional <s>la</s>-substitute [would occur] before the <s>ṇi</s>-elision, its purposelessness is quite clear. Even those who say that the inferential <s>antaraṅga paribhāṣā</s> overrides the directly established '<s>pūrvatra</s>' principle for the sake of conformity with attested forms — they too should not be heeded by those whose sole guide is grammatical rules. This is the direction [of the argument]. For this very reason, the reference to '<s>āṅ</s>' in '<s>omāṅoś ca</s>' serves a purpose. For in '<s>khaṭvā ā ūḍhaḥ</s>,' even when the <s>savarṇadīrgha</s> (homogeneous lengthening) applies later, it is overridden by the <s>antaraṅga guṇa</s> operation, and when <s>vṛddhi</s> then becomes applicable, [the '<s>āṅ</s>' reference] serves the purpose of the <s>pararūpa</s> (subsequent-form) operation. It is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>samprasāraṇāc ca</s>' that <s>guṇa</s> is <s>antaraṅga</s> because the root first connects with the <s>upasarga</s> immediately after the generation of the meaning-conveying affix, and the word '<s>khaṭvā</s>' connects with the whole [compound] only afterward. For the imitative form '<s>ehi</s>' in connection with a <s>Śivādi</s> word, however, this [rule] does not apply, since by the authority of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>samprasāraṇāc ca</s>' — which serves as an indicator — it is certain, and because, when <s>aṅga</s> status is obtained by adopting the analogical extension '<s>prakṛtivad anukaraṇam</s>' (an imitative form is like its original), this does not apply. As for the [statement] 'the root first connects with the <s>upasarga</s>, afterward with the <s>sādhana</s> (instrument/means)' — by '<s>upasarga</s>' is meant the word having that designation, and by '<s>sādhana</s>' the <s>kāraka</s> (case-role) and the operation occasioned by it. Hence in forms like '<s>anubhūyate</s>,' the derivation of the passive <s>lakāra</s> is established due to the transitivity [of the verb]. This is not [problematic], because the action is understood as something to be accomplished, and since what is to be accomplished requires instruments, only after the connection with instruments is the action determined, and only after the application of instrument-operations does the connection of the <s>upasarga</s> — which is the occasion for the action-connection — become appropriate. For this very reason, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>suṭ kāt pūrvaḥ</s>,' having stated 'the root first [connects] with the <s>upasarga</s>' and then [saying] 'this is not the essence,' it is stated — through the reasoning 'the root first connects with the <s>sādhana</s>, afterward with the <s>upasarga</s>' — that only the latter is appropriate, as [explained] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> with '<s>sādhanaṃ hi kriyāṃ nirvartayati</s>' (for the instrument accomplishes the action) and so on. Since the meaning is expressed by the root alone through the inclusion of the meaning indicated by the <s>upasarga</s>, the derivation of the passive <s>lakāra</s> etc. in the aforementioned cases is established. Afterward, the connection with the indicatory <s>upasarga</s> occurs for the comprehension of the listener. Thus, <s>suṭ</s> occasioned by the <s>upasarga</s>, being <s>antaraṅga</s> (of more internal scope), applies before <s>dvitva</s> (reduplication) etc. in the state '<s>sam-kṛtī</s>' — then <s>dvitva</s> etc. [follow]. For this very reason, the <s>ṇatva</s> (cerebral replacement) in forms like '<s>praṇidāpayati</s>' is accounted for in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> by the principle '<s>yadāgamāḥ</s>' (augments [take on the properties] of what they are attached to). Hence the derivation of '<s>pratyeti pratyayaḥ</s>' (an affix is that which comes after) etc. is established. That operation which is occasioned by the <s>upasarga</s> and depends on the <s>upasarga</s>'s meaning — since it has a specific <s>upasarga</s> as its occasion — is <s>antaraṅga</s>. But where that is not the case, only the operation occasioned by the previously connected <s>sādhana</s> is <s>antaraṅga</s>. Hence in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>na dhātu</s>,' regarding '<s>preddhaḥ</s>,' it is stated '<s>guṇo bahiraṅgaḥ</s>' (the <s>guṇa</s> is outer-scope). Furthermore, [the statement] 'when the <s>upasarga</s> connects first, the compounding of root and <s>upasarga</s> would result in the undesired consequences of single accent, etc.' — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>upapadam atiṅ</s>.' The <s>bhāvārtha-pratyaya</s> (abstract-meaning affix) also arises first. Hence the formulation '<s>ṇer adhyayane</s>' is consistent. And this is a general indicator, since even the <s>bhāva-tiṅ</s> (abstract verbal ending) arises first; otherwise compounding would [undesirably] result in that case. But for <s>tiṅ</s> (finite verbal endings), due to the prohibition '<s>atiṅ</s>' (excluding <s>tiṅ</s>), there is no fault — provided the <s>upasarga</s> connects with the <s>bhāva-tiṅ</s>. Enough of this. As for [the principle] '<s>viśeṣāpekṣāt sāmānyāpekṣam antaraṅgam</s>' (that which depends on a general [condition] is <s>antaraṅga</s> relative to that which depends on a specific [condition]) — since in a specific-condition-dependent [rule] more specific properties serve as the occasion. For example, in '<s>rudādibhyaḥ sārvadhātuke</s>,' both <s>rudādi</s> status and <s>sārvadhātuka</s> status [are needed]. There, for knowing the <s>sārvadhātuka</s>, knowledge of the base's <s>dhātu</s> status and the affix's affix-status is necessary — hence <s>yāsuṭ</s> is <s>antaraṅga</s>. By this, what <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> states regarding the sūtra '<s>anudāttaṅitaḥ</s>'

children.translated_text: The [assertion] that '<s>ti</s>-endings and the like are <s>antaraṅga</s> (inner-scope) with respect to [the general designation] <s>l</s> alone, while <s>syāt</s>-endings and the like are <s>bahiraṅga</s> (outer-scope) because they depend on a specific <s>lakāra</s>' — that is refuted; because even when there is dependence on a specific [<s>lakāra</s>], since [the specific] does not function as a cause by the general property — the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>, i.e. the specific) being such that the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>, i.e. the general) is understood through inference even when [the specific] is the cause — there is no establishment that it is caused by an additional property. And because in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> such a characterization of <s>antaraṅga</s>-<s>bahiraṅga</s> relationship is never mentioned anywhere. As for what [is discussed] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>matup</s>-<s>sūtra</s>: in '<s>pañca gāvo yasya santi, sa pañcaguḥ</s>' (he who has five cows is '<s>pañcagu</s>'), having raised the possibility of [the suffix] <s>matup</s> [applying], the <s>siddhāntin</s> (proponent) states: 'because there is no capacity in each [individual word]; because the aggregate is not a <s>prātipadika</s>; because of the compound; because it is [already] expressed by the compound.' [Then] the objector's statement in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is: 'This is not the essence; for even when [the meaning] has been expressed, a <s>taddhita</s> suffix arises from a <s>dvigu</s> compound denoting the meaning of the suffix — as in <s>pāñcanāpitiḥ</s>.' <s>Kaiyaṭa</s>'s intention [is]: because of the <s>luk</s> (elision) prescribed by '<s>dvigorluganapatye</s>,' a <s>taddhita</s> arises from a <s>dvigu</s> expressing a <s>taddhita</s> meaning; and the word <s>pañcagu</s> is a <s>dvigu</s>. Then, [arguing that] in '<s>dvaimāturaḥ</s>,' '<s>pāñcanāpitiḥ</s>,' '<s>pañcasu kapāleṣu saṃskṛtaḥ</s>' etc., the <s>dvigu</s> having scope [elsewhere] is overridden by the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> due to posteriority in the case at hand — with this intention the <s>siddhāntin</s> states: 'This is not a <s>dvigu</s>; what then? A <s>bahuvrīhi</s>.' Not knowing that scope [of the <s>dvigu</s>], the objector [argues]: 'The <s>dvigu</s> should prevail because of being an exception (<s>apavāda</s>).' <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> [explains]: Since <s>bahuvrīhi</s> is prescribed for any case-ending [word] denoting the meaning of another word, while <s>dvigu</s> is prescribed for a number [word] denoting a <s>taddhita</s> meaning — because the <s>dvigu</s> is more specifically prescribed, it should override. Then, as a partial reasoning of the <s>siddhāntin</s>, it is stated: 'The <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [prevails] because of being <s>antaraṅga</s> (inner-scope). How is it <s>antaraṅga</s>? The <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [is prescribed] for the meaning of another word; the <s>dvigu</s> for a qualified meaning of another word — and in that [qualified case], the <s>asti</s>-reference is made for the <s>taddhita</s>.' <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> [explains]: The <s>dvigu</s>, being caused by the <s>matup</s>-meaning which requires an additional <s>asti</s>-meaning, is <s>bahiraṅga</s>. This is not the <s>siddhāntin</s>'s [real] position, because even this much does not avoid [the need for] the exception status. For we see that <s>ṇ</s>, which depends on the general [vowel] <s>ac</s>, is overridden by the long vowel (<s>dīrgha</s>), which depends on the specific <s>savarṇa</s> (homogeneous vowel). Moreover, since overriding is established by posteriority following the stated method. Moreover, here the <s>bahiraṅga</s> status is only because of dependence on an additional [factor], not merely because of dependence on a specific [factor] — hence the <s>bahiraṅga</s> status of what depends on a specific [factor] is not established in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. For this very reason, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> does not say: '<s>bahuvrīhi</s> depends on the general <s>subanta</s>; <s>dvigu</s> depends on a specific [form] thereof.' Nor should it be said that this is improper because meaning-based <s>bahiraṅga</s> status is not relied upon — because there is no fault, since it is [merely] a partial reasoning. For this very reason, the <s>asti</s>-reference is not for the purpose of [establishing the] <s>matup</s>-meaning, but rather — having demonstrated that the <s>bahiraṅga</s> status you maintain for the <s>dvigu</s> does not [even] exist because the <s>asti</s>-word [in the sūtra] is for [meaning] other than <s>matup</s> — the <s>siddhāntin</s> states: 'The prohibition of <s>dvigu</s> in the sense of <s>matup</s> must be stated [as a separate rule],' and thus [the matter] is resolved by that statement. For this very reason, in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tadoḥ saḥ sāvanantyayoḥ</s>,' '<s>anantyayoḥ</s>' (of non-final [syllables]) is purposeful. Otherwise, by <s>antaraṅga</s> status due to dependence on the general suffix, the <s>atva</s> (substitution of <s>a</s>) of the final [syllable] and the <s>satva</s> (substitution of <s>s</s>) of the non-final [syllable] being [already] established, the purposelessness [of '<s>anantyayoḥ</s>'] would be quite clear. In the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>pādaḥ pat</s>' too, the absence of this <s>antaraṅga</s> status is indicated — let the discerning understand this. Objection: If so, in '<s>asusravat</s>' and the like, because of the absence of lesser-condition status, the <s>uvaṅ</s> [substitution] by '<s>laghūpadhaguṇa</s>' would not occur. Reply: No; because there [exists] the <s>antaraṅga</s> status in the form of being an internal operation (<s>antaḥkāryatva</s>). Internal operation means being caused by a previously presented cause (<s>pūrvopasthitanimitta</s>), because the word '<s>aṅga</s>' (base) refers to the cause. This <s>antaraṅga</s> status is established by everyday reasoning (<s>lokanyāya</s>) — as [in the saying]: 'A person, rising in the morning, first attends to bodily needs, then to friends', then to relatives'.' Even for meanings — genus (<s>jāti</s>), individual (<s>vyakti</s>), gender (<s>liṅga</s>), number (<s>saṅkhyā</s>), case-relation (<s>kāraka</s>) — the order of cognition is postulated by the author of the science. And the manifestation of the word expressing them is postulated in that very order — hence their operations [follow] that very order. Thus in '<s>paṭvyā</s>' and the like, because of <s>antaraṅga</s> status, the prior <s>yaṇ</s> substitution [occurs] first, and the posterior <s>yaṇ</s> substitution, being <s>bahiraṅga</s>, is [treated as] <s>asiddha</s> (not-yet-established) — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>acaḥ parasmin</s>.' That too is merely a regulator of prior application when both are simultaneously applicable. As in '<s>paṭvyā</s>' and the like, in the step-by-step derivation (<s>vibhajyānvākhyāna</s>) of the word — but it is not a regulator of <s>asiddha</s> status for a <s>bahiraṅga</s> [rule] that has already applied, in the presence of such an <s>antaraṅga</s> [rule]. This is clear in <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>vāha ūṭh</s>': 'because by the everyday principle stated earlier, the same result is obtained.' For this very reason, in '<s>vāyvoḥ</s>' and the like, the <s>valilopa</s> (elision of <s>v</s>) is prevented by the <s>sthānivat</s> status of <s>yaṇ</s> — by the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>acaḥ parasmin</s>.' In the step-by-step derivation, however — in the stated examples — the <s>antaraṅga</s> status as prior application, and the <s>asiddha</s> status of <s>bahiraṅga</s>, should be understood as non-application in the form of [the cause] not being present (<s>nimittabhāva</s>). As for the [view] that by this method, even what precedes in position (<s>pūrvasthānika</s>) would be <s>antaraṅga</s> — that is to be reconsidered, because in '<s>srajiṣṭhaḥ</s>' and the like, the effort made by the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> — in the context of refuting the purpose of the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>prakṛtyaikāc</s>' — to prevent [a certain result] by recourse to the class-view (<s>jātipakṣa</s>), and [which prevention would follow] from the <s>luk</s> [elision] of <s>vinmatos</s> [being treated as an exception overriding] the <s>ṭi</s>-<s>lopa</s> — that [effort] would be rendered futile. For by your stated method, the <s>luk</s> of <s>vinmatos</s>, being <s>bahiraṅga</s>-<s>asiddha</s>, would effortlessly prevent [the result].

children.translated_text: And because such <s>bahiraṅga</s>-<s>asiddha</s> status by this method is never relied upon anywhere [in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>]. And because in the <s>paribhāṣā</s> [itself], the word '<s>aṅga</s>' refers to the cause. And this [paribhāṣā] does not convey <s>asiddha</s> status for a <s>bahiraṅga</s> [rule] situated in the <s>uttarapada</s> (latter member) section — the objector's statement in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ica ekāco 'm</s>' is [just] that — it should not be heeded. In '<s>parantapaḥ</s>' and the like, there is no <s>asiddha</s> status for the <s>anusvāra</s> [substitution], because <s>mum</s> [augment] does not apply in the <s>tripādī</s> (last three quarters [of the <s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s>]). Even in the later view, they say that by recourse to the <s>yathoddeśa</s> view, and by giving examples that are <s>asiddha</s> on other grounds, it is necessarily [merely] a statement of that [objector's position]. In an inner-scope (<s>antaraṅga</s>) [rule] of the <s>ābhīya</s> (ā-section) type, a <s>bahiraṅga</s> [rule] of the <s>ābhīya</s> type having the same locus does not become <s>asiddha</s> by this [principle] — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>asiddhavat sūtra</s>, since the <s>antaraṅga</s> [rule itself] is <s>asiddha</s>. Similarly, the overriding of <s>vṛddhi</s> by <s>sic</s> through the <s>antaraṅga</s> [rule], based on the principle '<s>yena nāprāptiḥ</s>' (by which [the substitute] would not be applicable), has its root in <s>antaraṅga</s>-based overriding — '<s>na sicyantaraṅgam asti</s>' (there is no <s>antaraṅga</s> with respect to <s>sic</s>) — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ikoguṇa</s>.'

children.text: nanvevam 'akṣadyūḥ' ityādau bahiraṅgasyoṭho 'siddhatvādantaraṅgo yaṇ na syāt, ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, in '<s>akṣadyūḥ</s>' and the like, since the <s>bahiraṅga</s> <s>oṭh</s> [augment] would be [treated as] <s>asiddha</s>, the <s>antaraṅga</s> <s>yaṇ</s> [substitution] should not [apply]. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: nājānantarye bahiṣṭvaprakḷptiḥ || 51 ||
children.translated_text: There is no characterization as <s>bahiraṅga</s> (outer-scope) when there is no interval (<s>ājānantarya</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 51]

children.text:
atra"ṣatvatukoḥ"iti sūtrasthaṃ tuggrahaṇaṃ jñāpakam/ anyathā 'adhītya 'pretya' ityādau samāsottaraṃ lyappravṛtyā pūrvaṃ samāse jāte tatra saṃhitāyā nityatvād lyabutpattiparyantamapyasaṃhitaya'vasthānāsambhavena ekādeśe lyapi tugapekṣayā padadvayasambandhivarṇadvayāpekṣaikādeśasya bahiraṅgatayāsiddhatvena tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameva/
"padadvayasambandhivarṇadvayāpekṣaṃ bahiraṅgam"iti 'preddhaḥ' ityādau guṇo bahiraṅga iti granthena"na dhātu lopa"iti sūtre"saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ"iti sūtre ca bhāṣye spaṣṭam/
yattu ṣatvagrahaṇamapi jñāpakam, anyathā"ko 'sicat"ityādau padadvayasambandhivarṇadvayāpekṣatvena
bahiraṅgasyaikādeśasyāsiddhatvena ṣatva pravṛttau kiṃ teneti/ tanna, iṇaḥ pūrvapadasambandhitvena ṣatvasyāpi padadvaya sambandhivarṇadvayāpekṣatvenobhayoḥ samatvāt/
ekādeśasyaparāditvena 'osicat' ityasya padatvena padāditvābhāvānna"sātpadādyoḥ"ityanena niṣedhaḥ/ traipādike 'ntaraṅge kāryakālapakṣepi bahiraṅgaparibhāṣāyā apravṛtteḥ pūrvamupapāditatvācca/
paribhāṣārthastu -- aco 'nyānantaryanimittake 'ntaraṅge kartavye jātasya bahiraṅgasya bahiṣṭva prakḷptiḥ/ bahiṣpadena bahiraṅgam, tasya bhāvo bahiraṅgatvam/ tatprayuktāsiddhatvasya na prakḷptiḥ, na prāptiriti/
'asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam' ityuktvā 'nājānantarya iti vakṣyāmi' iti bhāṣyāktyā tatratyasya antaraṅga ityasyānuvṛttisūcanāt/ tena 'pacāvedam' ityādau na doṣaḥ/ antaraṅgasyācsthānika kāryasyaitvasya anyanantarya nimittakatvābhāvāt/
'jātasya bahiraṅgasya' ityuktyā 'ajaye indram' 'dhiyati' ityādau bahiraṅgadīrgha guṇāderasiddhatvaṃ siddham/
