ata eva"iṇṅiśīnāmād guṇaḥ, savarṇadīrghatvācchacaṅantasyāntaraṅgalakṣaṇatvāt"ityādi saṅgacchate/ ata eva"omāṅośca"ityāṅgrahaṇaṃ caritārtham/ taddhi 'śivaaāaiha' iti sthite paramapi savarṇadīrghaṃ bādhitvā dhātūpasargakāryatvenāntaraṅgatvād guṇe vṛddhibādhanārtham/
nanu"akṣadyūḥ"ityatra yaṇi kṛte ūṭho 'siddhatvād valilopāpattiriti vācyam, aco 'nyānantaryanimittake 'ntaraṅge kartavye kṛte ca tasminyadantaraṅgaṃ prapnoti, tatra ca kartavye nāsiddhatvamiti tadarthāt/ asiddhaparibhāṣāyā anityatvena tadvāraṇe tvasyā vaiyarthyaṃ tenaiva siddheḥ/
ata eva"na lopaḥ sup"iti sūtre kṛti tuggrahaṇaṃ caritārtham/ anyathā 'vṛtrahabhyām' ityādau bahirbhūtabhyāmnimittakapadatvāśrayatvena bahiraṅgatayā nalopasyāsiddhatvena siddhestadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameva/ mama tu
kyajānantaryasatvānna doṣaḥ/
na caivaṃ sati"hrasvasyapiti"iti sūtrasya bhāṣyavirodhaḥ/ tatra hi 'grāmaṇi putraḥ' ityatra
"ikohrasvo 'ṅyaḥ"iti hrasve kṛte tukamāśaṅkya hrasvasyabahiraṅgāsiddhatvena samāhitam/"nājānantaryā"ityasya
children.translated_text: Here, the mention of '<s>tuk</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ṣatvatukoḥ</s>' is the indicatory sign (<s>jñāpaka</s>). Otherwise, in [forms like] '<s>adhītya</s>', '<s>pretya</s>' and so on, when the compound is formed first and then the <s>lyap</s> suffix applies after compounding — since <s>saṃhitā</s> (continuous recitation) is invariable (<s>nitya</s>) in that [compound], and since there is no possibility of remaining in a non-<s>saṃhitā</s> state even until the application of <s>lyab</s> — the <s>ekādeśa</s> (single substitute), being <s>bahiraṅga</s> (externally-conditioned) in relation to <s>tuk</s> on account of depending on two phonemes belonging to two words, would be treated as <s>asiddha</s> (not-yet-established), and thereby [the mention of <s>tuk</s>] would be pointless — this is quite clear. The [principle] that '[an operation] depending on two phonemes belonging to two words is <s>bahiraṅga</s>' [applies] in '<s>preddhaḥ</s>' and the like...

children.text:
satve tatra tadaprapterasaṅgatiḥ spaṣṭameveti vācyam ; tena bhāṣyeṇāsyā anavakāśatvabodhanāt/ etajjñāpakena antaraṅgaparibhāṣāyā anityatvabodhanasyaiva nyāyyatvāt/
ata eva"acaḥ parasmin"iti sūtre bhāṣye 'paṭu ī ā' ityatra parayaṇādeśasya anayāsiddhatvāt pūrvayaṇādeśaḥ sādhitaḥ/ ata evaiṣā bhāṣye punaḥ kvāpi nollikhitā/ ata eva antaraṅgaparibhāṣāmupakramya vipratiṣedhasūtre 'syā bahūni prayojanāni santi, tadarthameṣā paribhāṣākartavyā, pratividheyaṃ
ca doṣeṣu' ityuktam,"samprasāraṇācca"iti sūtre bhāṣye/ pratividhānaṃ ca paribhāṣāviṣaye 'nityatvāśrayaṇameveti
dhvanitamityalam//
children.translated_text: It should be said that the inapplicability [of the rule] in <s>ṣatva</s> there, due to its non-arrival, is quite clear — because the <s>Bhāṣya</s> indicates by this [<s>jñāpaka</s>] that [the <s>paribhāṣā</s>] has no scope [otherwise]. Because it is proper that through this indicatory sign, the non-invariability (<s>anityatva</s>) of the <s>antaraṅga</s> <s>paribhāṣā</s> should be understood. For this very reason, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>acaḥ parasmin</s>', in [the derivation of] '<s>paṭu ī ā</s>', the prior <s>yaṇ</s>-substitution is established because the subsequent <s>yaṇ</s>-substitution is treated as <s>asiddha</s> by this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. For this very reason, this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is not mentioned again anywhere in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. For this very reason, having introduced the <s>antaraṅga</s> <s>paribhāṣā</s>, many applications of it [are given] in the <s>vipratiṣedha</s> <s>sūtra</s>...

children.text: nanvevam 'gomatpriyaḥ' ityādau padadvayanimittakasamāśritatvena bahiraṅgaṃ lukaṃ bādhitvāntaraṅgatvāddhalṅyādilope numādayaḥ syuḥ, ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, in '<s>gomatpriyaḥ</s>' and the like, <s>luk</s> (zero-substitution), being <s>bahiraṅga</s> because of depending on two-word conditions, would be overridden, and by the <s>antaraṅga</s> status [of the other rule], <s>num</s> and other [augments] would apply in the deletion of <s>hal</s>-endings and the like. To address this, he says —

children.text: antaraṅgānapi vidhīn bahiraṅgo lug bādhate || 52 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Luk</s> (zero-substitution), though <s>bahiraṅga</s>, overrides even <s>antaraṅga</s> operations. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 52)

children.text:
atra ca"pratyayottarapadayośca"iti sūtraṃ jñāpakam/ 'tvatkṛtam' ityādau lugapekṣayā antaraṅgatvād vibhaktinimittakena"tvamāvekavacane"ityanena siddha idaṃ vyarthaṃ sattajjñāpakam/
nanu 'tava putraḥ, tvatputraḥ' ityādau tavamamādibādhamārthaṃ tadāvaśyakamiti cet, evaṃ tarhyatratya
maparyantagrahaṇānuvṛttistajjñāpiketi bhāṣyakṛtaḥ/ yuṣmadādibhya ācārakvip tu na, sampūrṇa sūtrasya jñapakatāparabhāṣyaprāmāṇayāt,"hrasvanadyāpaḥ"iti nuḍvidhāyakasūtrasthapramāṇyena halantebhyaḥ ācārakvipabhāvācca/
evamevaikārthakābhyāṃ pratipādikābhyāṃ prātipadikaṇico 'pyanabhidhānaṃ bodhyam/ etena tatrā'deśārthaṃ pratyayagrahaṇaṃ caritārthamityapāstam/
nanu maparyantānuvṛttirapi sarvādeśatvavāraṇāya caritrthā/ 'na cotsargasamānādeśā apavādāḥ'
iti nyāyenāsiddhavatsūtrasthabhāṣyasammatena maparyantasyaivādeśe siddhe tadanuvṛttirvyattheti vācyam, tasya śnamakajādau vyabhitārāditi cet, na; śnami mitvena, bahuci purastādgrahaṇena, akaci prāk ṭegrahaṇena tasya bādhe 'pyatrotsargasya
tyāge mānābhāvāt/
ata eva"tasminnaṇi ca"ityanena yuṣmākādyādeśavidhānaṃ caritārtham, anyathā'kaṅādeśameva
vidadyāt/ ākaṅi tavakādyādeśayoretadapavādayoruktanyāyenāntyādeśatvāpattiḥ, atastadvidhānam, idamevaca tajjñapakam/
yadyapi virodhe bādhakatvamiti vārtikamate 'yaṃ nyāyaḥ, bhāṣyakārastu vināpi virodhaṃ satyapi sambhave bādhakatvamicchati, ityanabhihitasūtrasthakaiyaṭarītyā nāyaṃ niyamaḥ, tathāpi yuṣmakādyā'deśavidhānajñāpita utsargaḥ svīkriyata eveti prakṛte na doṣaḥ/ etad bhāṣyamapi tatsvīkāre mānam/
evañca maparyantānuvṛttiḥ 'tvatkṛtam' ityādau maparyantasyā'deśavidhānārthā/ tatra ca antaraṅgatvāt tvamāvityeva siddhe vyarthā saṃtajjñapikā/ jñāpite tvasminnetadviṣaye tavādīnāmaprāptyā tadapavādatvābhāvena maparyantasyavā'deśārthaṃ sā caritārtheti tadāśayaḥ/
yattu haradattenāntaraṅgapravṛttau pratyaya uttarapade ca maparyantāsambhavena tadanuvṛttirvyarthā satī jñapiketyuktam, tat, na; antaraṅgāṇāmapyapavādabādhyatvena tadviṣaye tadapravṛtteḥ/
vastuta idaṃ jñāpakaṃ vārtikarītyaiva, bhāṣyarītyā tu vācanika evāyamartha ityāhuḥ/
iyam"supo dhātu"iti lugviṣayaiveti kecit/"eṅhrasvātsambuddheḥ" "na yāsayoḥ"iti sūtrasthākaraprāmāṇyena lugmātra viṣayā/ ādye 'he trapu' ityādāvanena nyāyena lopaṃ bādhitvā lug bhavatīti bhāṣye
uktam/ antye 'ntaraṅgāṃśca vidhīn sarvo 'pi lugbādhate, na tu sublugeva/ ata eva"sanīsraṃsaḥ"ityādau nalopo na bhavati/ 'pañcabhiḥ khaṭvābhiḥ krītaḥ, pañcakhaṭvaḥ' ityādāvekādeśāt prāgeva ṭāpo luk/ anyathā
kṛtaikādeśasya lukyakāraśravaṇaṃ na syāditi kaiyaṭe uktam/
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>pratyayottarapadayośca</s>' is the indicatory sign (<s>jñāpaka</s>). In [forms like] '<s>tvatkṛtam</s>' and so on, since, in comparison with <s>luk</s>, the [operation] caused by the case-ending is <s>antaraṅga</s> — namely [the rule] '<s>tvamāvekavacane</s>' — the [result] would already be established [by the <s>antaraṅga</s> principle], so this [<s>sūtra</s>] would be purposeless; being so, it serves as the indicatory sign. If it be objected that in '<s>tava putraḥ</s>', '<s>tvatputraḥ</s>' and the like, it is necessary for overriding the <s>tavam</s>/<s>amā</s> [substitutes] — then in that case, the continuation of the limitation up to [the form] '<s>ma</s>' serves as the indicatory sign — [so states] the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. But the <s>ācāra</s>-<s>kvip</s> after <s>yuṣmad</s> etc. is not [affected], because the authority of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [supports] the indicatory status of the complete <s>sūtra</s>...

children.text:
etadvirodhād yat"tadrājasya"iti sūtre kaiyaṭenoktam ' aṅgānatikrānto 'tyaṅgaḥ' ityatra
supoluki bahuvacana paratvābhāvāt "tadrājasya"iti lug na syāditi śaṅkāparabhāṣyavyākhyāvasare antaraṅgānapīti nyāyenāyaṃ luk subluko bādhakaḥ syādityāśaṅkya subluka evānena balavatvaṃ bodhyata iti tatprauḍhyeti draṣṭavyam/ lugapekṣayā luko balavatvasya vaktumaśakyatvāditi tadā śaṅkā samādhānaṃ vaktuṃ yuktam/
anena nyāyenāntaraṅganimittavināśakalukastatprayojakasamāsādīnāṃ ca prābalyaṃ bodhyata ityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: In contradiction to this, what <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> says on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tadrājasya</s>' — [namely that] in '<s>aṅgānatikrānto 'tyaṅgaḥ</s>,' since after <s>sup</s>-deletion (<s>luk</s>) there is no plurality [that would give] subsequentness, the <s>luk</s> deletion by '<s>tadrājasya</s>' would not apply; and in explaining the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage raising and resolving this doubt, having suspected that by the maxim '<s>antaraṅgam api</s>,' this <s>luk</s> would override <s>sup-luk</s>, [he states] that by this [maxim] the strength of <s>sup-luk</s> alone should be understood — this should be seen as his boldness. Since the strength of <s>luk</s> over <s>lug</s> cannot be stated [on independent grounds], it is appropriate to state the doubt and resolution in that way. By this maxim, the prepotency of <s>luk</s>-deletion that destroys the cause of an <s>antaraṅga</s> [operation], and of the compounds etc. that motivate it, is to be understood — the elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text:
nanvevam saumendre 'ntaraṅgatvādādguṇe pūrvapadātparendraśabdābhāvena"nendrasyapaparasya"iti vṛddhiniṣedho vyarthaḥ/ antādivadbhāvastūbhayata āśrayaṇe niṣiddhaḥ/
kiñca vṛddhirapyatra na prāpnoti, antādivatvobhayābhāve 'pi pūrvāntavatvenaikādeśaviśiṣṭe pūrvapadatvenendraśabdasya 'ekadeśavikṛta' nyāyena 'ubhayata āśrayaṇe nāntādivat' ityasyābhāvena tadāśrayaṇena vottarapadatve 'pi tasyānackatvādekasyaikādeśena parasya nityena"yasyeti"lopenāpahārāt/
na ca parādivadbhāvenaikādeśaviśiṣṭasyottarapadatvamevāstviti tatsambhava iti vācyam; uttarapadādyacsthānikatvād vṛddhestadabhāvenāprāptestādrūpyānatideśāt/
anyathā 'khaṭvābhiḥ' ityādāvapi pūrvāntavatvenādantatve bhisa aisāpattiriti bhāṣye spaṣṭam/
ata eva 'pūrveṣukāmaśamaḥ' ityādāvantaraṅgatvād guṇe vṛddhirnasyādityāśaṅkitam/ tadekadeśamātrasya vikārābhāvācca/ taduktaṃ bhāṣye 'indredvavacau, ekaḥ"yasyeti"lopenāpahṛto 'para ekādeśena, tato 'nacka indra śabdaḥ
sampannastatra kaḥ prasaṅgo vṛddheriti/
marudādibhirindrasya dvandve indrasyaiva pūrva nipātaḥ, ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, in '<s>Saumendra</s>' (descendant of <s>Soma</s> and <s>Indra</s>), since by <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness the <s>guṇa</s> [operates first], and since after that there would be no <s>Indra</s>-word following the prior member, the prohibition of <s>vṛddhi</s> by '<s>nendrasya aparasya</s>' would be purposeless. [Reply:] But the treatment as initial-and-final (<s>antādivadbhāva</s>) is prohibited when there is reliance on both [sides]. Moreover, <s>vṛddhi</s> too would not be obtained here: even in the absence of <s>antādivat</s>-ness of both [sides], when by having the prior-end (<s>pūrvānta</s>) status the single substitute (<s>ekādeśa</s>) is qualified by the prior-member status, by the maxim '<s>ekadeśavikṛta</s>' (what is modified in one part [retains its identity]), and due to the absence of the [rule] 'not <s>antādivat</s> when relying on both,' relying on that and having even the latter-member status, since [the <s>Indra</s>-word] would lack a vowel (<s>anac</s>), by one [element] being absorbed into the single substitute and the other being deleted by the invariable deletion of '<s>yasya iti</s>' (<s>lopa</s>). Nor should it be said that by the treatment as initial-of-the-latter (<s>parādivat</s>), the latter-member status of the <s>ekādeśa</s>-qualified [form] should obtain, making <s>vṛddhi</s> possible — because <s>vṛddhi</s>, having the initial vowel of the latter member as its locus, would not be obtained in the absence thereof, and there is no extension (<s>atideśa</s>) of such a form. Otherwise, even in '<s>khaṭvābhiḥ</s>' etc., by having prior-end status and thereby <s>ad</s>-ending status, the undesired <s>ais</s>-form [from] <s>bhis</s> would follow — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. For this very reason, in '<s>pūrveṣu kāmaśamaḥ</s>' etc., the concern was raised that <s>vṛddhi</s> would not apply when <s>guṇa</s> [applies first] due to <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness. And because only a single part is modified, not [the whole]. As stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: '<s>Indra</s> has two vowels; one is removed by the deletion of <s>yasya iti</s>, the other by the single substitute; then the <s>Indra</s>-word is obtained without a vowel — what occasion is there for <s>vṛddhi</s>?' In the <s>dvandva</s> compound of <s>Indra</s> with <s>Marut</s> etc., <s>Indra</s> alone is placed first. Therefore he says —

children.text: pūrvottarapadanimittakāryāt pūrvamantaraṅge 'pyekādeśo na || 53 ||
children.translated_text: Even the <s>antaraṅga</s> single substitute (<s>ekādeśa</s>) does not [apply] prior to an operation caused by the prior or latter member. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 53 //

children.text:
atra ca"nendrasya"iti niṣedha eva jñāpaka iti"antādivacca" "vipratiṣedhe param"iti
sūtrayorbhāṣye spaṣṭam//
children.translated_text: And here, the prohibition '<s>na indrasya</s>' itself is the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtras</s> '<s>antādivac ca</s>' (P. 6.1.85) and '<s>vipratiṣedhe param</s>' (P. 1.4.2).

children.text: nanvevamapi 'pradhāya, prasthāya' ityādāvantaraṅgatvādvitvādiṣu kṛteṣu lyap syādata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: Even so, in '<s>pradhāya</s>,' '<s>prasthāya</s>' etc., since by <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness, when reduplication etc. have been done, <s>lyap</s> would [wrongly apply]. Therefore he says —

children.text: antaraṅgānapi vidhīn bahiraṅgo lyabbādhate || 54 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>bahiraṅga</s> (external) <s>lyap</s> overrides even <s>antaraṅga</s> (internal) rules. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 54 //

children.text: "ado jagdhiḥ"iti sūtre ti kitītyeva siddhe lyabgrahaṇamasyā jñapakamiti"ado jagdhiḥ"ityatra bhāṣye spaṣṭam//
children.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ado jagdhiḥ</s>' (P. 2.4.36), since [the result] would be established merely by '<s>ti kiti</s>,' the mention of <s>lyap</s> is the indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>ado jagdhiḥ</s>'.

children.text: nanvevamapi"iyāya"ityādau dvitve kṛte 'ntaraṅgatvāt savarṇadīrghatve tadasiddhirata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: Even so, in '<s>iyāya</s>' etc., when reduplication has been done and then by <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness <s>savarṇadīrgha</s> (homogeneous lengthening) [applies], that [<s>vṛddhi</s>] would not be established. Therefore he says —

children.text: vārṇādāṅgaṃ balīyo bhavati || 55 ||
children.translated_text: A rule pertaining to <s>varṇa</s> (sound) is stronger than one pertaining to <s>aṅga</s> (stem). // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 55 //

children.text:
tenāntaraṅgamapi savatṇadīrghaṃ bādhitvā vṛddhiriti tatsiddhiḥ/"abhyāsasyāsavarṇe"itīyaṅ
vidhāyaka sūtrasthamasavarṇagrahaṇamasyā jñāpakam/ taddhi 'īṣatuḥ' ityādāviyaṅādivyāvṛtyartham/ etatparibhāṣābhāve tu 'īṣatuḥ' ityādāvantaraṅgeṇa savarṇadīrgheṇa bādhāttadvyartham/ iyaṅuvaṅau hyabhyāsasambandhanimittakatvād bahiraṅgau/
na ceyaṅādirapavādaḥ, 'yenanāprāpti' nyāyena 'iyati' ityādisakalalakṣya prāpta yaṇapavādatvasyaiva nirṇayāditi prāñcaḥ/
pare tu - etatparibhāṣābhāve"abhyāsasya"iti sūtrameva vyartham/
na ca 'iyāya' 'iyeṣa' ityādau caritārtham, tayorapi pūrvapravṛttaguṇasya pūrvapravṛttavṛddheśca
"dvirvacaneci"iti rūpātideśenāpahāre dvitve kṛte punaḥ prāpte guṇavṛddhī bādhitvāntaraṅgatvāt savarṇadīrdhāpatteḥ/ na ca 'iyati' ityādau taccaritārtham, tāvanmātraprayojakatve 'uḥ' ityeva brūyāt/ yvorityanuvartate,"iṇo yaṇ"iti
sāhacaryād vyākhyānācca ṛdhātoreva grahaṇam/ ataḥ ivarṇasyeyaṅityarthaḥ/ "abhyāsasyātau"iti
children.translated_text: Therefore, overriding even the <s>antaraṅga</s> <s>savarṇadīrgha</s>, <s>vṛddhi</s> [applies] — thus that [form] is established. The mention of '<s>asavarṇa</s>' in the prescriptive <s>sūtra</s> '<s>abhyāsasya asavarṇe</s>' (P. 7.4.60) is the indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. For that [word '<s>asavarṇa</s>'] is for the purpose of excluding <s>iyaṅ</s> etc. in '<s>īṣatuḥ</s>' and the like. In the absence of this <s>paribhāṣā</s>, since in '<s>īṣatuḥ</s>' etc. the <s>savarṇadīrgha</s> being <s>antaraṅga</s> would override [<s>iyaṅ</s>], that [word '<s>asavarṇa</s>'] would be purposeless. For <s>iyaṅ</s> and <s>uvaṅ</s> are <s>bahiraṅga</s> because of being caused by the relation to the reduplicative syllable (<s>abhyāsa</s>). Nor is <s>iyaṅ</s> etc. an exception [to <s>savarṇadīrgha</s>], since by the maxim '<s>yena aprāptiḥ</s>' (where there is non-applicability), it is determined to be an exception only to <s>yaṇ</s> which is applicable in all actual instances like '<s>iyati</s>' etc. — thus the ancients [say]. But the later [grammarians say]: In the absence of this <s>paribhāṣā</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>abhyāsasya</s>' itself would be purposeless. Nor is it rendered purposeful in '<s>iyāya</s>,' '<s>iyeṣa</s>' etc., since in those cases too, when the previously applied <s>guṇa</s> and previously applied <s>vṛddhi</s> are removed by the form-extension (<s>rūpātideśa</s>) of '<s>dvirvacane aci</s>' (P. 6.1.2), and when after reduplication <s>guṇa</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s> become applicable again, <s>savarṇadīrgha</s> would result by <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness overriding them. Nor is that rendered purposeful in '<s>iyati</s>' etc., since if it were only for that much purpose, one would simply say '<s>uḥ</s>.' Since '<s>yvoḥ</s>' continues [from the prior rule], and from the association with '<s>iṇo yaṇ</s>' and from the explanation, only the <s>ṛ</s>-root is taken. Hence the meaning is: <s>iyaṅ</s> for the <s>i</s>-class vowel. '<s>Abhyāsasya ātau</s>' or

children.text:
"abhyāsasyārteḥ"iti vā gurutvānna yuktam/
na ca"e,ai,o,au"śabdebhya ācārakvibantebhyo liṭīyaṅādyarthaṃ tatsūtranāvaśyakam, tathā"uvoṇakīyiṣati"ityādyarthamāvaśyakamiti vācyam, ṣāṣṭhaprathamānhikāntastha bhāṣya prāmāṇyena teṣāmanabhidhānāt/
antye dvitīyadvirvacanasyaiva satvena tvadukta prayogasyaiva durlabhatvāt/ evañca sampūrṇa sūtrasya jñāpakatā yuktā/
yadyapi bhāṣye 'yadayamabhyāsasyāsavarṇa ityasavarṇagrahaṇaṃ karoti' iti granthenāsavarṇagrahaṇasyaiva
jñāpakatā labhyate, tathāpi 'na hyantareṇa guṇavṛddhī asavarṇaparābhyāso bhavati' iti tadupapādana granthena sampūrṇa sūtrasyaiva jñāpakatā labhyate/
agre 'pi 'naitadasti jñāpakam, atyarthametat syāt' ityanena sūtra sārthakyameva darśitam/ asavarṇagrahaṇasyaiva jñāpakatve tu tadvyāvartyapradarśanena tat sārthakyameva darśitaṃ syāt/
na ca 'akṛtavyūha' paribhāṣayā 'iyeṣa' ityādau savarṇadīrdhāprāptiḥ, yadi dīrdhonasyāt, tarhi
guṇaḥ syāditi sambhāvanāyāḥ satvena paribhāṣāpravṛtteḥ sūpapādatvāditi kathaṃ sampūrṇa sūtrasya jñāpakateti vācyam, tasyā asatvāt/ satve vaitadbhāṣyaprāmāṇyena yatrāntaraṅgakāryapravṛttiyogyakālottarameva tannimittavināśaka bahiraṅgavidheḥ praptiḥ, tatraiva tatparibhāṣāpravṛttisvīkārācca/
na cāntaraṅgatvād dīrdhopi 'iyāya' ityādau pūrvāntavatvenābhyāsatvādivarṇatvācca ṇalyasavarṇa iyaṅvidhānena sūtraṃ caritārtham/
na ca"aci śnu"ityanena siddhiḥ, vṛddhibādhanārthatvāditi vācyam/ pratyāsatyāsavarṇa padena abhyāsottarakhaṇḍasambandhyasavarṇāca eva grahaṇāt, śāstrabādhakalpanāpekṣayā paribhāṣājñāpakatvasyaivaucityāccetyāhuḥ/
sā ceyaṃ dharmigrāhakamānādāṅgavārṇayoḥ samānakāryitva eva/
yattu samānanimittakatvarūpasamānāśrayatva evaiṣeti, tat, na ; jñāpite 'pi"iyāya""iyeṣa"ityādyasiddheḥ, sūtravaiyarthyasya tadavasthātvācca/
"syonaḥ"ityatra tu vakṣyamāṇarītyāsyā anityatvādapravṛttau guṇādantaraṅgatvād yaṇādeśaḥ/
na caivamapi 'iyāya' ityādāviyaṅ durlabhaḥ, tatra kartavye vṛddhyādeḥ sthānivatvena 'asavarṇe' iti pratiṣedhāditi vācyam, sūtrārambhasāmarthyādeva stthānivatvāpravṛtteḥ/ tacca sāmānyāpekṣam/ abhyāsakārye taduttarakhaṇḍādeśasya tatkāryapratibandhakībhūtaṃ sthānivatvaṃ neti/
ata eva 'ārati' ityādau yaṇādeśasya sthānivatvādabhyāsasya"ḍhralope"iti dīrdho durlabha ityapāstam/ dīrghavidhau tanniṣedhācca/
"ariyiyāt"ityatra sthānivatveneyaṅ bhavatyeva, tasya sthānivatvasyābhyāsakārya pratibandhakatvābhāvāt/
'iyañcāṅgasambandhinyāṅga eva' iti"svarito vā"iti sūtre bhāṣye/ tatra hi 'kumāryai' ityādo yaṇuttaramāḍuktaḥ/
iyañcānityā 'chvoḥ' iti satugnirdeśāt/ anyathāntaraṅgatvāt pūrvaṃ tukaḥ śādeśe tuko 'prāptyā tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭamevetyanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: '<s>abhyāsasya ārteḥ</s>' — such [alternatives] are not appropriate due to heaviness. Nor should it be said that the <s>sūtra</s> is not necessary for the <s>iyaṅ</s> etc. purpose in the <s>Liṭ</s> after stems like <s>e</s>, <s>ai</s>, <s>o</s>, <s>au</s> — which are <s>kvib</s>-ending forms derived from <s>ācāra</s> — but is necessary for forms like '<s>uvoṇakīyiṣati</s>' etc., because those are not mentioned in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> up to the end of the sixth day's lesson. And because the second reduplication alone exists in the final [portion], the usage you describe is itself rare. Thus the indicator-status of the complete <s>sūtra</s> is appropriate. Even though from the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage 'since he makes the mention of <s>asavarṇa</s> in <s>abhyāsasya asavarṇe</s>,' the indicator-status of the <s>asavarṇa</s>-mention alone is obtained, nevertheless from the substantiating passage 'for without <s>guṇa</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s>, the reduplicative syllable cannot be <s>asavarṇa</s>,' the indicator-status of the complete <s>sūtra</s> is obtained. Further, 'this is not an indicator; that would be excessive' — by this, the meaningfulness of the <s>sūtra</s> alone is shown. If only the <s>asavarṇa</s>-mention were the indicator, then by showing what it excludes, only its meaningfulness would be shown. Nor [is there the objection that] by the <s>akṛtavyūha</s> <s>paribhāṣā</s>, <s>savarṇadīrgha</s> would not be obtained in '<s>iyeṣa</s>' etc. — [since] if the long vowel did not occur, then <s>guṇa</s> would apply, and since the <s>paribhāṣā</s> would operate because of the [mere] possibility, this is easily justified — how then can the complete <s>sūtra</s> be an indicator? [Answer:] Because that [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] does not hold. And if it did hold, by the authority of this <s>Bhāṣya</s>, this <s>paribhāṣā</s> would be accepted only where the <s>bahiraṅga</s> rule's applicability arises only after the time suitable for the <s>antaraṅga</s> operation. Nor is the <s>sūtra</s> rendered purposeful by the <s>iyaṅ</s> prescription for '<s>iyāya</s>' etc. where, by <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness, the long vowel too would have prior-end status and thus reduplicative syllable status, and being of the <s>a</s>-class <s>varṇa</s> in the <s>Ṇal</s> [suffix], it would be <s>asavarṇa</s>. Nor should it be said that the result is established by '<s>aci śnu</s>' alone since it is for the purpose of overriding <s>vṛddhi</s> — because by the word '<s>asavarṇa</s>' as read in immediate proximity, only those <s>asavarṇa</s> vowels related to the post-reduplicative segment are taken; and because the appropriateness of indicator-status is preferred over postulating an override of a grammatical rule — thus they say. And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] pertains precisely to the equal-operation-ness of <s>aṅga</s> and <s>varṇa</s> [rules] as established by the property-grasping authority. As for [the view] that this pertains to equal-locus-ness in the form of having the same cause — no; because even if indicated, '<s>iyāya</s>,' '<s>iyeṣa</s>' etc. would not be established, and the purposelessness of the <s>sūtra</s> would remain. In '<s>syonaḥ</s>' however, since this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is non-invariable as will be explained, when it does not operate, the <s>yaṇ</s>-substitute [prevails] over <s>guṇa</s> due to <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness. Nor should it be said that <s>iyaṅ</s> is difficult to derive in '<s>iyāya</s>' etc., since when the <s>vṛddhi</s> etc. that is to be performed there has <s>sthānivat</s>-ness (treatment as original), the prohibition '<s>asavarṇe</s>' [would block <s>iyaṅ</s>] — because by the very authority of the <s>sūtra</s>'s introduction, <s>sthānivat</s>-ness does not operate. And this is general. The <s>sthānivat</s>-ness that would obstruct the <s>abhyāsa</s>-operation [from applying] to the post-reduplication-segment substitute — does not [hold]. For this very reason, [the objection] that in '<s>ārati</s>' etc., due to the <s>sthānivat</s>-ness of the <s>yaṇ</s>-substitute, the lengthening of the <s>abhyāsa</s> by '<s>ḍhralope</s>' would be unattainable — is refuted. And because in the <s>dīrgha</s>-prescription, that [<s>sthānivat</s>-ness] is prohibited. In '<s>ariyiyāt</s>', <s>iyaṅ</s> does indeed occur by <s>sthānivat</s>-ness, since that <s>sthānivat</s>-ness does not obstruct the <s>abhyāsa</s>-operation. 'And <s>iyaṅ</s> [pertains] to the <s>aṅga</s> related to <s>aṅga</s> alone' — in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>svarito vā</s>'. For there, in '<s>kumāryai</s>' etc., the <s>āṭ</s> after <s>yaṇ</s> is stated. And <s>iyaṅ</s> is non-invariable, from the <s>sat</s>-designation in '<s>chvoḥ</s>.' Otherwise, by <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness, when <s>tuk</s> [augment occurs] first in the <s>śa</s>-substitute, the purposelessness of <s>tuk</s> through non-applicability would be quite clear — the elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text: nanvevam 'seduṣaḥ' ityādau kvasontaraṅgatvādiṭi, tataḥ samprasāraṇe 'pīṭaḥ śravaṇāpattiriti cet, atra kecit--
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, in '<s>seduṣaḥ</s>' etc., when <s>kvas</s>-[affix] by <s>antaraṅga</s>-ness [triggers] <s>iṭ</s>, and then upon <s>samprasāraṇa</s>, the undesired <s>īṭ</s> [lengthening] would result. To this, some say —

children.text: akṛtavyūhāḥ pāṇinīyāḥ || 56 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Pāṇinīyas</s> (Pāṇini's followers) are <s>akṛtavyūha</s> (not pre-arranged). // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 56 //

children.text:
na kṛto viśiṣṭa ūhaḥ -- niścayaḥ, śāstrapravṛttiviṣayo yairityarthaḥ/ bhāvi nimittavināśa ityadyāhāraḥ/ bahiraṅgeṇāntaraṅgasya nimittavināśe paścāt sambhāvite 'ntaraṅgaṃ neti yāvat/
atra ca - jñāpakam,"samarthānāṃ prathamāt"iti sūtre samarthānāmiti/ taddhi sūtthitādibhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Those for whom no specific deliberation has been made — no firm determination — regarding the domain of grammatical operation — this is the meaning. [The implied supplement is:] 'when the destruction of the cause [of an <s>antaraṅga</s> operation] by a <s>bahiraṅga</s> [operation] is subsequently apprehended, the <s>antaraṅga</s> [still operates first]' — this much [is to be supplied]. And here, the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) is '<s>samarthānām</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>samarthānāṃ prathamāt</s>' (P. 2.1.1). For that [word]...

children.text:
kṛtadīrghebhyaḥ pratyayotpatyartham/ anyathāntaraṅgatvād dīrdhe kṛta eva pratyayaprāptyā tadvyarthatā spaṣṭa eva/
na cātraikādeśapravṛtti samaye vṛddhyaprāptyaikādeśe kṛta ādeśe vṛddheḥ praptāvapi tannimittavināśābhāva iti vācyam, taddavāraiva tannimittavināśasatvenākṣateḥ/
na ca sautthitau bahiraṅgatayā vṛddherasiddhatvānna tannimittavināśa iti vācyam, samarthagrahaṇenaitad
viṣaye tasyā apravṛtterapi jñāpanāt/
yattu samarthagrahaṇenāntaraṅgaparibhāṣāyā anityatvameva jñāpyata iti/ tanna, asiddha paribhāṣāyā samakālaprāpta bahiraṅgasya pūrvaṃ jātabahiraṅgasya cāntaraṅge kartavye 'siddhatvaṃ bodhyate, na tu jāte 'ntaraṅge tasya tatva bodhyate, mānābhāvāt, phalābhāvācca/
evañca sūtthitāvekādeśasya paribhāṣāsādhyatvābhāvena tadanityatvajñāpanāsambhavāt/"antaraṅgānapi vidhīn"ityāderapyasyāmevāntarbhāvaḥ/
etat pravṛttau ca nimittavināśasambhāvanāpi nimittam/ ata eva 'gomaddaṇḍī' ityādau halṅyādi lopo na/
anyathā halṅyādi lopa kāle sāmāsika luko 'prāptyā taduttaraṃ cāpahāryābhāvādaprāptyā lopasyaivāpatteḥ/ asti cātrāpi 'yadi lopo na syāt, tarhi luk syāt' iti sambhāvanā/
"alloponaḥ"iti sūtrastha taparakaraṇaṃ tu paribhānityatvajñāpanenacaritārtham/ taddhi 'āna' ityādo lopavāraṇāya/ anyathā dīrīghābhāve lopasambhāvanayaitatparibhāṣābalāt dīrghāprāptau tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭamevetyāhuḥ/
"samarthānām"iti sūtre kaiyaṭastu samarthavacaneneyaṃ paribhāṣā jñāpyate"akṛtavyūhāḥ pāṇinīyāḥ"iti/ tena 'papuṣaḥ' itiyādāvantaraṅgātpūrvaṃ kṛto 'pīḍāgamo nivartata iti vadan 'na kṛto vyūhaḥ viśiṣṭastarko nimittakāraṇavināśe 'pi kāryasthitirūpo yaiḥ' ityarthamabhipraiti/ 'nimittāpāye naimittikasyāpyapāyaḥ' iti yāvat/ sūtthitādiñi vṛddhau dīrghanivṛttau sāvuttthitirmābhūditi samarthānāmiti/
lokanyāya siddhaścāyamarthaḥ/ tathā hi loke nimittaṃ dvividhaṃ dṛṣṭam--kāryasthito niyāmakaṃ tadaniyāmakaṃ ca/
ādyaṃ yathā nyāyanaye 'pekṣā buddhiḥ, tannāśe dvitvanāśābhyupagamāt/ vedānti naye prārabdhasya vikṣepasthiti niyāmakatvaṃ ca prasiddhameva/
dvitīyaṃ yathā daṇḍādi, tannāśe 'pi ghaṭanāśadarśanāt/ śāstre lakṣyānurodhād vyavasthā/
bhāvinimittavināśe pūrvamanutpattau tu na kaścinnyāyaḥnāpi sampratipanno dṛṣṭāntaḥ/ samarthānāmityasyāpi lokasiddhārthajñāpanena cartārthyasambhave lokasiddhāpūrvatādṛśārthajñapakatve mānābhāva iti tadāśaya iti bodhyam/
pare tu 'seduṣaḥ' ityādau padāvadhike 'nvākhyāne 'sed vas as' iti sthite iṭ samprasāraṇayoḥ praptau pratipadavidhitvāt pūrvaṃ samprasāraṇe valāditvābhādiṭaḥ prāptireva neti tatsiddhiriti spaṣṭam"samarthānām"iti sūtre kaiyaṭe,"asiddhavat"sūtre kaiyaṭe ca spaṣṭametat/
yadyapi pratipadavidhitvamanavakāśatve satyeva bādhakatve bījam, tathāpi pūrvapravṛttau sāvakāśatve 'pi niyāmakaṃ bhavatyeveti tadāśayaḥ/ nirūpitaṃ caitad bahuśaḥ śabdenduśekharādau/
"samarthānām"iti sūtrasthasamarthagrahaṇaṃ tu 'viṣuṇaḥ' ityādāvakṛtasandheḥ pratyayadarśanena sarvatra tathā bhramavāraṇāya nyāyasiddhārthānuvāda eva/
dhvanitaṃ cedam"vipratiṣedha"sūtre bhāṣye/ tatra hi 'vaikṣamaṇiḥ' ityantaraṅga
paribhāṣodāharaṇamuktam/
kiñca vibhajyānvākhyāne 'su utthita as i' it sthite 'vārṇādāṅgaṃ balīyaḥ' iti prāpta vṛddhi
vāraṇāya samarthagrahaṇamityatraiva kaiyaṭe spaṣṭam/
children.translated_text: [The rule '<s>kṛtadīrghebhyaḥ</s>' is stated] for the purpose of affix-generation after stems that have undergone lengthening. Otherwise, since due to <s>antaraṅga</s> (inner-scope) status the affix would be obtained only after lengthening has been applied, its purposelessness would be quite evident. Nor can it be said that at the time of the <s>ekādeśa</s> (single substitute) application, even though <s>vṛddhi</s> becomes applicable when the substitute is made in the <s>ekādeśa</s> — which itself arose when <s>vṛddhi</s> was not yet applicable — the occasion [for <s>vṛddhi</s>] is not destroyed, because [<s>vṛddhi</s>] survives through that very channel where the destruction of the occasion is real. Nor can it be said that in the <s>sūtthita</s> (well-established) [stage], due to <s>vṛddhi</s> being non-established as an outer-scope operation, there is no destruction of the occasion — because the word '<s>samartha</s>' (capable) [in '<s>samarthānām</s>'] indicates the non-application of that [<s>asiddha paribhāṣā</s>] in this domain. As for [the claim] that the word '<s>samartha</s>' indicates merely the non-eternality of the <s>antaraṅga paribhāṣā</s> — that is not so. The <s>asiddha paribhāṣā</s> conveys the non-establishment of an outer-scope [operation] that is simultaneously applicable or that has already occurred, when the inner-scope [operation] is to be performed; but it does not convey the non-establishment of [the inner-scope operation] once it has been performed, due to the absence of valid means of knowledge and the absence of any purpose. Thus, since in the <s>sūtthita</s> case the <s>ekādeśa</s> is not something to be established by the <s>paribhāṣā</s>, it is impossible to indicate its non-eternality. The [statement] '<s>antaraṅgān api vidhīn</s>' etc. is also included within this [paribhāṣā]. And the possibility of the destruction of the occasion is itself an occasion for the application [of this principle]. Hence in forms like '<s>gomaddaṇḍī</s>' and the like, the <s>halṅyādi-lopa</s> (elision by the <s>halṅyādi</s> rule) does not apply — otherwise, at the time of <s>halṅyādi-lopa</s>, since the compound-elision (<s>luk</s>) would not be applicable, and since afterward there would be nothing to supersede it, only <s>lopa</s> would undesirably result. And here too there exists the possibility: 'if <s>lopa</s> were not to occur, then <s>luk</s> would occur.' The <s>tapara</s> marking in the sūtra '<s>al-lopo naḥ</s>', however, serves its purpose through indicating the non-eternality of the <s>paribhāṣā</s>. For it is [needed] to prevent <s>lopa</s> at the beginning [of the form] '<s>āna</s>.' Otherwise, they say, in the absence of lengthening, due to the possibility of <s>lopa</s>, by the force of this <s>paribhāṣā</s> lengthening would not apply, making its purposelessness quite evident. <s>Kaiyaṭa</s>, however, on the sūtra '<s>samarthānām</s>,' [says that] by the word '<s>samartha</s>' this <s>paribhāṣā</s> is indicated — '<s>akṛtavyūhāḥ Pāṇinīyāḥ</s>' (the <s>Pāṇinīyas</s> do not make special arrangements). Thus, in saying that in forms like '<s>papuṣaḥ</s>' the <s>iṭ</s>-augment applied before the <s>antaraṅga</s> operation is reversed, he intends the meaning: 'there is no special arrangement, i.e., the distinguished reasoning that when the occasion-cause is destroyed, the effect nonetheless persists.' That is to say: 'when the occasion ceases, the occasioned also ceases.' In the <s>sūtthita</s> case, when <s>vṛddhi</s> arises upon <s>iñ</s> application and the lengthening is reversed, [the intent is] 'let the <s>sūtthiti</s> not occur' — hence '<s>samarthānām</s>.' And this meaning is established by worldly reasoning. For in the world, the occasion is seen to be of two kinds — that which governs the persistence of the effect, and that which does not. The first is like the faculty of expectation (<s>apekṣā buddhi</s>) in the <s>Nyāya</s> system, since the destruction of duality is accepted upon its destruction. And in the <s>Vedānta</s> system, the governing of the persistence of the <s>vikṣepa</s> (projection) state by <s>prārabdha</s> [karma] is well known. The second is like a stick, etc., since the pot is seen to be destroyed even when [the stick] is not destroyed. In the technical science [of grammar], the determination is made in conformity with attested forms. But for the destruction of a future occasion before the prior [effect] has even arisen, there is no principle and no accepted example. It should be understood that the import of '<s>samarthānām</s>' is this: since it serves its purpose by indicating a worldly-established meaning, there is no valid evidence for attributing to it such an unprecedented meaning. Others, however, say that in '<s>seduṣaḥ</s>' and the like, in the word-by-word analysis, when the state '<s>sed vas as</s>' is established and both <s>iṭ</s> and <s>samprasāraṇa</s> are applicable — since <s>samprasāraṇa</s>, being a word-specific rule, applies first, <s>iṭ</s> does not in fact become applicable at all due to the absence of the <s>valādi</s> condition — and thus that [form] is established. This is clear in <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the sūtra '<s>samarthānām</s>' and in <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the '<s>asiddhavat</s>' sūtra. Although the status of a word-specific rule serves as the basis for supersession only when there is no other scope, nevertheless the import is that even when there is scope for the earlier application, [the word-specific rule] still governs. And this has been discussed at length in the <s>Śabdenduśekhara</s> and elsewhere. The '<s>samartha</s>' reference in the sūtra '<s>samarthānām</s>' is simply a restatement of what is already established by principle, to prevent the misconception that because in '<s>viṣuṇaḥ</s>' and the like an affix is seen [to apply] to an unsandhi-ed form, it would be so everywhere. And this is implied in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>vipratiṣedha</s>' sūtra, where '<s>vaikṣamaṇiḥ</s>' is cited as an example of the <s>antaraṅga paribhāṣā</s>. Furthermore, in the word-by-word analysis when the state '<s>su utthita as i</s>' is established, the '<s>samartha</s>' reference is [needed] to prevent <s>vṛddhi</s> that would be applicable by the principle '<s>vārṇād āṅgaṃ balīyaḥ</s>' — this is clear in <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on that very [sūtra].

children.text:
ata eva"asiddhavat"sūtre 'vasusamprasāraṇamajvidhau siddhaṃ vaktavyam' 'papuṣaḥ' ityādau vasoḥ
samprasāraṇe kṛte āto lopo yathā syāt' iti bhāṣye uktam/ padasya vibhajyānvākhyāne pūrvoktakaiyaṭarītyā pūrvaṃ samprasāraṇe iṭoprāptāvusnimittaka evā'to lopa iti tadasaṅgatiḥ/
ata eva 'caupratyaṅgastapratiṣedhaḥ' iti vacanaṃ vārtikakṛtā'rabdham, bhāṣyakṛtā ca na pratyākhyātam/ pratyaṅgaṃ antaraṅgam/ asyāṃ paribhāṣāyāṃ satyāṃ tu tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameva/
ata eva"chvoḥ"iti sūtre 'avaśyamatra tugabhāvārtho yatnaḥ kāryaḥ' antaraṅgatvāddhi tuk prāpnoti' iti bhāṣye uktam/ etatsatve tu tuko 'prāptyā yatnāvaśyakatvakathanamasaṅgatamiti spaṣṭameva/
na caitadanityatvajñāpanārthameva taditi tadāśayaḥ, avaśyamatretyakṣarasvārasyabhaṅgāpatteḥ/
kiñcānayaiva"pratyayottarapadayośca" "ado jagdhirlyapti kiti"itiyanayoścāritārthyena tajjñāpakavaśālluglyaporantaraṅgabādhakatā bhāṣyoktā bhajyeta/
kiñcaiṣā bhāṣye na dṛśyate/ taduktam"asiddhavat"sūtre kaiyaṭena 'nimittāpāye naimittikasyāpyapāyaḥ' iti paribhāṣāyāḥ 'bhaṣyakṛtānāśrayaṇāt' iti/ padasaṃskāra pakṣe 'hariḥ' ityādau visarge kṛte
tato gacchatītyādi sambandhe 'hariḥ gacchati' ityādyeva sādhu/ tadviṣaye padasaṃskārapakṣānāśrayaṇaṃ veti dik//
children.translated_text: For this very reason, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>asiddhavat</s>' sūtra, it is stated: '<s>vasusamprāsāraṇam aj-vidhau siddhaṃ vaktavyam</s>' — 'in forms like <s>papuṣaḥ</s>, when <s>samprasāraṇa</s> of <s>vas</s> has been applied, the <s>āt-lopa</s> (elision of <s>ā</s>) should occur.' In the word-by-word analysis, by the method stated by <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> above, when <s>samprasāraṇa</s> applies first and <s>iṭ</s> is not applicable, only the <s>āt-lopa</s> occasioned by <s>us</s> [occurs] — hence that [<s>Bhāṣya</s> statement] is inconsistent [with the alternative view]. For this very reason, the statement '<s>ca upratyaṅgastapratiṣedhaḥ</s>' was introduced by the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> and not rejected by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>. '<s>Pratyaṅga</s>' means <s>antaraṅga</s>. If this <s>paribhāṣā</s> [i.e., <s>nimittāpāye</s>...] were valid, the purposelessness of that [<s>vārttika</s>] would be quite evident. For this very reason, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>chvoḥ</s>,' it is stated: 'An effort must necessarily be made here for the purpose of preventing <s>tuk</s>-augment; for <s>tuk</s> would apply due to <s>antaraṅga</s> status.' If this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] were valid, the statement of the necessity of effort due to the non-applicability of <s>tuk</s> would be inconsistent — this is quite evident. Nor should the import be [taken as saying] that [the <s>Bhāṣya</s> statement] is simply for the purpose of indicating the non-eternality of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] — for that would break the natural sense of the words '<s>avaśyam atra</s>' (necessarily here). Moreover, by this very [<s>paribhāṣā</s>], the supersession of <s>antaraṅga</s> [rules] by <s>luk</s> and <s>lyap</s>, stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> through the indicator-force of the rules '<s>pratyayottarapadayoś ca</s>' and '<s>ado jagdhir lyap ti kiti</s>,' which [otherwise] have their own scope, would be [undesirably] fragmented. Furthermore, this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is not seen in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. As stated by <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the '<s>asiddhavat</s>' sūtra: 'because the <s>paribhāṣā</s> "when the occasion ceases, the occasioned also ceases" is not relied upon by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>.' Under the <s>padasaṃskāra</s> (word-formation) view, in forms like '<s>hariḥ</s>,' when <s>visarga</s> has been applied and then the connection with '<s>gacchati</s>' etc. occurs, only '<s>hariḥ gacchati</s>' is correct. The non-adoption of the <s>padasaṃskāra</s> view in that domain is the direction [of the argument]. Enough.

children.text: "antaraṅgādapyapavādo balīyān"/--- tatra apavāda padārthamāha ---
children.translated_text: "The <s>apavāda</s> (exception) is more powerful even than <s>antaraṅga</s>." — He now explains the meaning of the word '<s>apavāda</s>':—

children.text: yena nāprāpte yo vidhirārabhyate sa tasya bādhako bhavati || 57 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 57: A rule that is initiated when [the other rule] has not [yet] applied becomes its superseder.

children.text:
prāpta iti bhāve ktaḥ, yena nāprāpta ityasya yatkartṛkāvaśyaprāptāvityarthaḥ/ nañ dvayasya prakṛtārthadārḍhyabodhakatvāt/
evañca viśeṣaśāstroddeśyaviśeṣadharmāvacchinnavṛttisāmānyadharmāvacchinnoddeśyakaśāstrasya viśeṣaśāstreṇa
bādhaḥ/
tadaprāptiyogye 'cāritārthyaṃ hyetasya bādhakatve bhījam/ ata eva"āyādayaḥ"iti sūtre 'gopāyiṣyati' ityādāvāyādīn bādhitvā paratvāt syādayaḥ prāpnuvantītyāśaṅkya"anavakāśāḥ āyādayaḥ"'gopāyati' ityādāvapi śap syādiḥ prapnoti/
na ca sati śapyasati vā na viśeṣaḥ/ anyādidānīmidamucyate--nāsti viśeṣa iti/ yaduktam"āyādīnāṃ syādibhiravyāpto 'vakāśa iti sa nāstyavakāśa"iti bhāṣye uktam/
evamatra tatpravṛtyuttaraṃ cāritārthye 'pi tadavyāpto 'vakśo nāstīti samameva/
kiñca tatpravṛtyuttaramapi cāritārthye tadbādhabodhanam/ anyathānavakāśatvenaiva bādhe siddhe etatkathanavaiyarthyāpatteḥ,"takrakauṇḍinya"nyāyapradarśanasyāpi vaiyarthyāpatteśca/ tathā prathamadvirvacanasya taduttaraṃ sāvakāśenāpi
dvitīyadvirvacanena bādhaḥ/ yathā vā'derapi pravṛtyā caritārthena 'ādeḥ parasya' ityanena 'alo 'ntyasya' ityasya bādhaḥ/
taduktam"midaco 'ntyāt"iti sūtre bhāṣye"satyapi sambhave bādhanaṃ bhavati"iti/ anyathā"brāmhaṇebhyo dadhi dīyatām, takraṃ kauṇḍinyāya"ityatra takradānena dadhidānasya bādho na syāt/ taddanottaraṃ tatpūrvaṃ vā taddanasya cāritārthyasambhavāt/ ata eva viṣayabhede 'pyapavādatvam/
ata evācirādeśena nuṭo 'pyapavādatvāt bādhamāśaṅkya 'na tisṛ' iti jñāpakena samāhitam"tṛjvat" sūtre bhāṣye/ tena viṣayabhede 'pavādatvābhāva eva bodhyata iti kaścit, tanna ; vinmatorlukā ṭilopamātrasya bādhānāpatteḥ/
children.translated_text: '<s>Prāpta</s>' is the past passive participle used in the sense of the action; the meaning of '<s>yena na prāpte</s>' is 'when the application by a certain [rule] has not necessarily obtained.' Due to the double negation conveying emphasis of the intended meaning. Thus [the principle is]: a special rule, whose domain is delimited by a specific property which also falls within the scope of a general rule delimited by a general property, supersedes that general rule. And the basis for the superseding power is the lack of independent scope [for the special rule] if it were not to supersede. Hence, on the sūtra '<s>āyādayaḥ</s>,' having raised the objection that in forms like '<s>gopāyiṣyati</s>' the <s>syādi</s> affixes would apply, superseding the <s>āyādi</s> affixes due to the <s>paratva</s> (later-rule) principle, [the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> responds]: 'The <s>āyādis</s> are without [other] scope' — [meaning] in forms like '<s>gopāyati</s>' the <s>śap</s> (general vikaraṇa) and <s>syādi</s> also apply. And there is no difference whether <s>śap</s> is present or absent. Now it is being said for a different purpose — that there is no [other] scope. As stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: 'The claim that the <s>āyādis</s> have scope not covered by the <s>syādis</s> — that [other] scope does not exist.' Similarly here, even when there is scope for the [exception] after the application of [the general rule], the situation is exactly the same. Furthermore, even when there is scope after the application [of the general rule], the supersession is indicated [by the exception]. Otherwise, since supersession would already be established by the scopelessness alone, stating this [additional principle] would be purposeless, and the demonstration of the '<s>takra-kauṇḍinya</s>' principle would also be purposeless. Similarly, the first repetition (<s>dvirvacana</s>) is superseded by the second repetition, even though the latter has [its own] scope. Just as even when '<s>ādi</s>' has applied and has its own scope, '<s>ādeḥ parasya</s>' supersedes '<s>alo 'ntyasya</s>.' As stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>midaco 'ntyāt</s>': 'Supersession occurs even when [independent] application is possible.' Otherwise, in '<s>brāhmaṇebhyo dadhi dīyatām, takraṃ kauṇḍinyāya</s>' (let curd be given to the brahmins, buttermilk to <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>), the giving of curd would not be superseded by the giving of buttermilk — since the curd-giving has scope either after or before the buttermilk-giving. Hence <s>apavāda</s> status [applies] even when the domains differ. For this very reason, having raised the concern that <s>nuṭ</s> would be superseded by the <s>acira</s>-substitute due to <s>apavāda</s> status, it was settled by the indicator '<s>na tisṛ</s>' in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>tṛjvat</s>' sūtra. If someone says this indicates the absence of <s>apavāda</s> status when domains differ — that is not so, because the undesirable consequence would be that <s>luk</s> of <s>vinmatos</s> would supersede only the <s>ṭi-lopa</s>.

children.text:
/katipayasaṃskaraṇe yadyapi"antaraṅgādapyapavādo balīyān"ityapi paribhāṣārūpeṇāṅgīkṛtam, kintu 'paranityāntaraṅgāpavādānāmuttarottaraṃ balīyaḥ' ityanena gatārthatvāt, nāgeśalekhanasvarasāt, paribhāṣāpāṭhe paṭhitatvāt,
candrikākāreṇa dhṛtatvāt, siddhānta kaunudyāṃ bhaṭṭoji dīkṣitenāpi svīkṛtatvāt, yenanāprāpte yovidhirārabhyate sa
tasya bādhako bhavati ityevātra paribhāṣārūpeṇa paṭhyate//
children.translated_text: In a certain revised version, although '<s>antaraṅgādapyapavādo balīyān</s>' ('an exception is stronger even than an <s>antaraṅga</s> [rule]') is also accepted as a <s>paribhāṣā</s>, nevertheless — because its import is already covered by [the principle] '<s>paranityāntaraṅgāpavādānāmuttarottaraṃ balīyaḥ</s>' ('among <s>para</s>, <s>nitya</s>, <s>antaraṅga</s>, and <s>apavāda</s>, each successive one is stronger'); because of the tenor of <s>Nāgeśa</s>'s own writings; because it is read in the <s>paribhāṣā</s> list; because it is upheld by the author of the <s>Candrikā</s>; and because it was also accepted by <s>Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita</s> in the <s>Siddhāntakaumudī</s> — [it is maintained]...

children.text:
yattu 'dayaterdigi' iti sūtre dvitvottaraṃ digyādeśasya cāritārthyaṃ kaiyaṭenoktam, tat prauḍhyā/
dhvanitañca tenāpi tasya tathātvaṃ taduttaragranthena/
"asambhava eva bādhakatvam, virodhasya tadbījatvāt"iti vārtikamataṃ tu bhāṣyakṛtā dūṣitatvānna lakṣyasiddhyupayogi/
"takrakauṇḍinya"nyāyopi tadaprāptiyogye 'caritārthaviṣayo vidheyaviṣaya eva ceti"taddhiteṣvacāmādeḥ" "dhātorekācaḥ"ityādi sūtreṣu bhāṣye spaṣṭam/
kvacittu sarvathānavakāśatvādeva bādhakatvam/ yathā ṅerāmo yāḍādibādhakatvam/ na hi yāḍādiṣu kṛteṣu ṅerām prapnoti, nirdiśyamānasya vyavadhānāt/ tatra svasya pūrvaṃ pravṛttirityeva teṣāṃ bādhaḥ/ tatra bādhake pravṛtte yadyutsargaprāptirbhavati tadā bhavatyeva/ yathā tatraiva yāḍāgamaḥ/ aprāptau tu na, yathā 'paceyuḥ' ityādau dīrghavādhake niravakāśa iyādeśe dīrghābhāvaḥ//
children.translated_text: Now, the fact that <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> in [his commentary on] the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>dayaterdigi</s>' states the <s>dig</s>-substitution to be purposefully applicable after reduplication — that is said out of sophistication. And even by him, its being so is implicitly conveyed through the subsequent passage. The <s>vārttika</s> view that 'overriding occurs only in case of impossibility, since contradiction is its seed' was refuted by the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, and so it is not useful for establishing attested forms. The maxim of '<s>takrakauṇḍinya</s>' also does not reach that [conclusion]...

children.text: tadetat paṭhyate --
children.translated_text: On this, the following is read —

children.text: kvacidapavādaviṣaye 'pyutsargo 'bhiniviśata iti || 58 ||
children.translated_text: In certain cases, the general rule prevails even in the domain of the exception. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 58)

children.text:
apavādaśabdo 'tra bādhakaparaḥ/ taduktam"guṇo yaṅlukoḥ"ityatra bhāṣye/ abhyāsavikāreṣvapavādā utsargānna bādhante/ 'ajīgaṇat'/ atra gaṇerītvamapavādatvāddhalādiḥśeṣaṃ bādhate/ nagaṇerītvamapavādatvāddhalādiḥśeṣaṃ bādhate/ kiṃ tarha? anavakāśatvāditi granthena gaṇarūpābhyāsāntyaṇasyetvamityarthe halādiḥśeṣa tannivṛttau tadanavakāśam, ītve tu kṛte tasya praptiḥ, antya halo 'bhāvāt/ abhyāsavikāreṣu bādhyabādhakabhāvābhāvena ca sādhitam/ tasmiṃśca sati lope kṛte sāmarthyācchiṣṭasyāntyasyetvamiti na doṣaḥ/
na ca 'yena nāprāpti' nyāyenāpavādatvamapyasya suvacam, tasya caritārthaviṣayatāyā uktatvāt/
"iko jhal"ityatra bhāṣyepi dhvanitametat/ tatra hi 'ajjhana' iti dīrdheṇa guṇottaraṃ phalābhāvenānavakāśatvād guṇo bādhite dīrghottaraṃ guṇaḥ syāt, dīrghavidhānaṃ tu minoterdīrdhe kṛte"sani mīmā"ityatra mīgrahaṇena grahaṇer'thavattatra paścāt praptaguṇabādhanārtham,"iko jhal"iti kitvamityuktam/ anyathāpavādatvena bādhe tadviṣaye utsargāpravṛtterbhāṣyasya sūtrasya cāsaṅgatiriti spaṣṭameva/
yattu kāñcanītyādāvapavādamayaḍviṣaye 'yaṇ bhavati, 'kvacidapavādaviṣaye 'pi' iti nyāyāditi tanna ;"aṇaḥ karmaṇica"iti sūtrasthabhāṣyavirodhāt/ tatra hi 'aṇaḥ punarvacanamapavādaviṣaye 'nivṛtyartham' 'godāyo vrajati' ityādyuktam/
'kāñcanī' ityādau kāñcanenanirmitetyarthe śaiṣiko 'ṇ bodhyaḥ/
atredaṃ bodhyam -- 'yenanāprapte' ityatra yenetyasya yadi svetareṇetyarthaḥ, tadā sva viṣaye svataradyadyat prāpnoti tad bādhyam, vidhyantarāprāptaviṣayābhāvāt/
iyameva bādhyasāmānyacinteti vyavahriyate/ anavakāśatvena bādhe 'pyeṣā vaktuṃ śakyā yadyudāharaṇamasti, vinigamanāvirahāt/
yadi tu yenetyasya lakṣaṇenetyarthaḥ, kāryeṇetyartho vā tadā bādhyaviśeṣacintā/ anavakāśatvena bādhe 'pyetadbādhena sārthakyam, uta tadbādhenetyevaṃ viśeṣacintā sambhavati, yadyudāharaṇamasti//
children.translated_text: The word '<s>apavāda</s>' (exception) here refers to an overriding [rule]. This is stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>guṇo yaṅlukoḥ</s>': 'In the modifications of the reduplicate, the exceptions do not override the general rules.' [In the form] '<s>ajīgaṇat</s>' — here, the <s>ī</s>-substitution of <s>gaṇ</s>, being an exception, overrides the remainder after <s>hal</s> [consonant]. But the <s>ī</s>-substitution of <s>gaṇ</s> does not override the remainder after <s>hal</s> [by virtue of] being an exception. What then? [It is] because of having no other scope — [this is the meaning of] the passage stating the <s>e</s>-substitution of the final [vowel] of the reduplicate of the root-form...

children.text: tatra kāryeṇetyarthe pararūpatvavacchinne kātya ārabhyamāṇāyā vṛddhestadbādhakatve na nirṇīte kiṃ śāstravihitasyetyevaṃ tadviśeṣacintāyāmāha --
children.translated_text: There, in the sense 'by the operation,' when the <s>vṛddhi</s> that is being undertaken starting from <s>Kātya</s> is delimited by <s>pararūpatva</s> (taking the form of the subsequent), and when its overriding [status] has not been determined — [the question arises] 'is it one prescribed by grammar?' — in this inquiry into its specifics, he says —

children.text: purastādapavādāḥ anantarān vidhīn bādhante, nottarān || 59 ||
children.translated_text: Exceptions that precede override the immediately following rules, not the later ones. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 59)

children.text: avaśyaṃ svaparasmin bādhanīye prathamopasthitānantarabādhena cāritārthye paścādupasthitasya tataḥ parasya bādhe mānābhāva ākāṅkṣāyā nivṛttervipratiṣedhaśāstrabādhe mānābhāvāccetyetasya bījam//
children.translated_text: The basis of this is: when necessarily either its own [rule] or the other must be overridden, if [the exception] is satisfied by overriding the one immediately adjacent and first presented, then there is no authority for overriding that which is subsequently presented and further removed — because the expectation [for further overriding] ceases, and because there is no authority in the absence of a <s>vipratiṣedha</s> (conflict-of-rules) teaching.

children.text:
"nāsikodarauṣṭhajaṅghādante"ityauṣṭhādyaṃśe ṅīṣniṣedhatvāvacchinnahādhakatve nirṇīte kiṃ
nihitasyetyākāṅkṣāyāmāha :--
children.translated_text: When, in the section '<s>auṣṭha</s>' etc. of [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>nāsikodarauṣṭhajaṅghādante</s>', the overriding status delimited by the prohibition of <s>ṅīṣ</s> has been determined — [the question arises] 'of what that has been established?' — in this inquiry, he says —

children.text: madye 'pavādāḥ pūrvān vidhīn bādhante, nottarān || 60 ||
children.translated_text: Exceptions in the middle override the preceding rules, not the later ones. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 60)

children.text:
tenauṣṭhādiṣu pañcasu"asaṃyogopadhāt"iti pratiṣedha eva bādhyate, na tu sahanañvidyamānalakṣaṇa iti
"nāsikodara"itytra bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ pūrvopasthita bādhena nairākāṅkṣyamasyā bījam//
children.translated_text: Therefore, among the five [items] beginning with <s>auṣṭha</s>, only the prohibition [stated in] '<s>asaṃyogopadhāt</s>' is overridden, not the characteristic of <s>halanta</s> (consonant-ending) [that is] present together with it — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>nāsikodara</s>'. The basis of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is the absence of further expectation [once the] previously presented [rule] has been overridden.

children.text: nanu"vā chandasi"ityanena"serhyapicca"ityanantarasyāpitvasyeva herapi vikalapaḥ syāt/ tathā"noṭa"iti niṣedho 'nantarahalantalakṣaṇāyā iva sicivṛddhimṛjivṛddhayorapi syāt, ata uktanyāyamūlakamevāha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: By [the rule] '<s>vā chandasi</s>', only the <s>api</s>-option immediately following '<s>serhyapicca</s>' should be optionalized, not also [the option for] <s>her</s>. Similarly, the prohibition '<s>noṭa</s>' should apply only to the immediately following <s>halanta</s> characteristic, and also to <s>vṛddhi</s> of <s>sic</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s> of <s>mṛj</s>. To address this, he states what is based on the same principle —

children.text: anantarasya vidhirvā bhavati pratiṣedho veti || 61 ||
children.translated_text: The rule or prohibition belongs to [the rule that is] immediately adjacent. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 61)

children.text:
ata eva"saṃkhyāvyayādeḥ"iti ṅībgrahaṇaṃ caritārtham/ taddhyanantasyaṅīṣovidhyabhāvāya/"na ktici"iti sūtre dīrghagrahaṇañca -- caritārtham/ taddhyanantarasyānudāttopadeśetyasyaiva niṣedhābhāvāya/
madhye 'pavādanyayāpekṣayānantarasyeti nyāyaḥ prabala iti"aṣṭābhyaḥ"iti sūtre kaiyaṭaḥ/
pratyāsattimūlako 'yam/ lakṣyānurodhātta vyavasthetyapi pakṣāntaram/ tatra tatra kvacit svaritatvapratijñānāt, sāmarthyena vā bādhyate 'yaṃ nyāyaḥ/ yathā"ṭiḍiḍhā"iti sūtreṇa ḍāpāvyavahitasyāpi ṅīpo vidhiḥ/"na ṣaṭ"ityādinā dvayorapi ṭābṅīpoḥ pratiṣedhaḥ/ iyañca"śi sarvanāmasthānam"ityādau bhāṣye spaṣṭetyanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the mention of <s>ṅīb</s> in [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>saṃkhyāvyayādeḥ</s>' is purposefully applicable — for it is to prevent the application of <s>ṅīṣ</s> to [the rule] that is immediately adjacent. And the mention of <s>dīrgha</s> (long vowel) in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>na ktici</s>' is also purposefully applicable — for it is to prevent the prohibition of only [the rule] '<s>anudāttopadeśa</s>' that is immediately adjacent. The principle 'belonging to the immediately adjacent' is stronger than the <s>madhye-apavāda</s> (middle-exception) principle — [so states] <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>aṣṭābhyaḥ</s>'. [This principle] is based on proximity...

children.text: nanu dadhatītyādāvantaraṅgatvādantādeśe 'lvidhau, sthānivatvābhāvādādeśo na syāditi tadvaiyarthyāpattiḥ, ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In [forms like] '<s>dadhati</s>' and so on, because of <s>antaraṅga</s> status, when the <s>ādeśa</s> (substitute) for the end [of the stem] is applied in the <s>al</s>-domain, and because <s>sthānivattva</s> (the principle that the substitute behaves like the original) does not apply, the substitute would not occur — leading to its purposelessness. To address this, he says —

children.text: pūrvaṃ hyapavādā abhiniviśante paścādutsargāḥ || 62 ||
children.translated_text: The exceptions take effect first; the general rules [take effect] afterwards. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 62)

children.text:
lakṣaṇaikacakṣuṣako hyapavādaviṣayaṃ paryālocya tadviṣayatvābhāvaniṣcaya utsargeṇa tattallakṣyaṃ saṃskaroti/ anyathā vikalpāpattirityarthaḥ/
abhiniviśanta ityasya buddhyārūḍhā bhavantītyarthaḥ/ 'apavādo yadyanyatra caritārthaḥ' iti nyāyasya tu nātra praptiḥ, antādeśaprāptiviṣaye cāritārthyābhāvāt//
children.translated_text: For one who takes only the grammatical rules as his guide (<s>lakṣaṇaikacakṣuṣka</s>), having first considered the domain of the exception and determined the absence of that domain, [only then] does the general rule process each attested form. Otherwise, an undesired option would result — this is the meaning. '<s>Abhiniviśante</s>' means 'they become fixed in the mind.' But the maxim '<s>apavādo yadyanyatra cāritārthaḥ</s>' ('if the exception is purposefully applicable elsewhere') does not apply here, because there is no purposeful applicability in the domain where the end-substitute applies.

children.text:
lakṣyaikacakṣuṣkastu tacchāstra paryālocanaṃ vināpyapavādaviṣayaṃ parityajyotsargeṇa lakṣyaṃ saṃskaroti,
tasyāpi śāstraprakriyāsmaraṇapūrvakaprayoga eva dharmotpatteḥ, tadāha :-
children.translated_text: But one who takes only attested usage as his guide (<s>lakṣyaikacakṣuṣka</s>), even without considering the grammatical system, sets aside the domain of the exception and processes the attested form by the general rule — because even for him, the production of correct forms depends on recollection of the grammatical procedure. On this he says —

children.text: prakalpya cāpavādaviṣayaṃ tata utsargo 'bhiniviśante || 63 ||
children.translated_text: Having first set aside the domain of the exception, then the general rules take effect. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 63)

children.text: tata ityasyāpavādaśāstraparyālocanāt prāgapītyarthaḥ/ prakalpyetyasya parityajyetyarthaḥ/ ata eva prātipadikārtha sūtre bhāṣye"idaṃ dvayapyuktvā na kadācittāvadutsargo bhavati, apavādaṃ tāvatpratīkṣate"ityarthakamuktam//
children.translated_text: '<s>Tataḥ</s>' (then) means 'even before the consideration of the exception-rule.' '<s>Prakalpya</s>' means 'having set aside.' For this very reason, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>prātipadikārtha</s> <s>sūtra</s>, it is stated with the meaning: 'Having stated both, the general rule does not operate at that time; it first awaits the exception.'

children.text: etanmūlakameva navīnāḥ paṭhanti :-
children.translated_text: Based on this very [principle], the later [grammarians] read —

children.text: upasañjaniṣyamāṇanimittopyapavāda upasañjātanimittamapyutsargaṃ bādhata iti || 64 ||
children.translated_text: An exception, even when its condition is yet to arise, overrides the general rule even when its condition has already arisen. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 64)

children.text:
yattvabhyastasaṃjñāsūtre kaiyaṭena prakalpya ceti pratīkamupādāya yathā 'na samprasāraṇa iti parasya yaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ samprasāraṇam, pūrvasya tu tannimittakaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ' ityuktam, tattu tata utsarga ityādyakṣarārthānanuguṇam/ yattvapavādavākyārthaṃ vinā notsargavākyārtha iti, tanna, 'abhiniviśate 'pavādaviṣayam' ityādipadasvārasyabhaṅgāpatteḥ/
padajanyapadārthopasthatau vākyārthabodhābhāve kāraṇabhāvācca/
yatra tvapavādo niṣiddhaḥ, tatrāpavādaviṣaye 'pyutsargaḥ pravartata eva/ yathā 'vṛkṣau' ityatra"nādici"iti pūrvasavarṇadīrghaniṣedhādapravartamānasya vṛddhibādhakatvābhāvāt vṛddhiḥ pravartate/ ata eva"tau sat' ityādi saṅgacchate/ ata eva nirdeśād bhraṣṭāvasaranyāyasyātra śāstreṇānāśrayaṇam/ dhvanitaṃ cedam"ikoguṇa"iti sūtre bhāṣya iti bhāṣyapradīpodyote nirūpitam/
atra 'devadattasya hantari hate devadattasyonmajjanaṃ na' iti nyāyasya viṣaya eva nāsti/ hate
devadatta unmajjanaṃ na devadattahananodyatasya, hanane tu bhavatyevonmajjanam/ prakṛte 'pi na pūrvasavarṇadīrgheṇa vṛddherhananam,
children.translated_text: As for what <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> says on the <s>abhyasta-saṃjñā sūtra</s>, taking the <s>pratīka</s> (citation) '<s>prakalpya ca</s>' — 'With regard to "not <s>samprasāraṇa</s>," the <s>samprasāraṇa</s> [applies] to the prior <s>yaṇ</s> [substitute] of the subsequent [element]; but for the prior [element], there is a prohibition caused by that' — that, however, does not accord with the literal meaning of the words '<s>tata utsargaḥ</s>' (thence the general rule) etc. As for [the objection] that without the sentence-meaning of the exception (<s>apavāda</s>), the sentence-meaning of the general rule (<s>utsarga</s>) [cannot arise] — that is not so, because of the undesirable consequence of disrupting the natural force (<s>svārasya</s>) of [contextual] words [such as] '<s>abhiniviśate apavādaviṣayam</s>' (it enters the domain of the exception) etc. And because the word-meaning presented by the word is the cause for the understanding of sentence-meaning [even] in the absence [of the exception-sentence]. But where the exception is prohibited, there the general rule indeed operates even in the domain of the exception. As in '<s>vṛkṣau</s>' (two trees): because the <s>pūrvasavarṇadīrgha</s> (prior-homogeneous lengthening), which does not operate due to the prohibition [from the rule] '<s>nādici</s>,' [therefore] lacks the power to override <s>vṛddhi</s> — <s>vṛddhi</s> operates. For this very reason, [the rule] '<s>tau sat</s>' etc. is consistent. For this very reason, the principle '<s>nirdeśād bhraṣṭāvasara-nyāya</s>' (the maxim of one displaced from [its] occasion by the [rule's] statement) is not relied upon here by the science. And this is implied in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ikoguṇa</s>' — as established in the <s>Bhāṣyapradīpodyota</s>. Here the maxim 'when <s>Devadatta</s>'s killer is killed, <s>Devadatta</s> does not re-emerge' has no domain [of application]. [For] when <s>Devadatta</s> is killed, there is no re-emergence for <s>Devadatta</s> [even] of the one intent on killing him; but in the act of killing, re-emergence indeed occurs. In the case at hand too, there is no 'killing' of <s>vṛddhi</s> by the <s>pūrvasavarṇadīrgha</s>,

children.text:
kintu hananodyamasajātīyaṃ prasakti mātram, prasaktasyaiva niṣedhāt/
pratipadoktatvamapi niravakāśatve satyeva bādhaprayojakam/ spaṣṭañcadam"śeṣādvibhāṣā"iti sūtre bhāṣye/ tatra hi 'śeṣagrahaṇamanarthakam, ye pratipadaṃ vidhīyante te bādhakā bhaviṣyanti' ityāśaṅkya, 'anavakāśā hi vidhayo bādhakā bhavanti samāsāntāśca kababhāve sāvakāśāḥ' ityuktam/
kvacidanavakāśatvābhāve 'pi paranityādisamavadhāne śīghropasthitikatvena pūrvapravṛttiprayajakaṃ balavatvaṃ pratipadavidhitvenāpi, paranityāntaraṅgapratipadavidhayo virodhisannipāte teṣāṃ mithaḥ parabalīyastvamiti"pratyayottarapadayośca"iti sūtre kaiyaṭena pāṭhāt/
ata eva 'rame' ityādaupratipadoktatvāt pūrvametva ākārapraśleṣāddhalṅyādilopo na prāpnotītyāśaṅkya"eṅhrasvāt"iti lopena samāhitam//
children.translated_text: but merely an applicability (<s>prasakti</s>) that is of a different kind from the effort to kill — since the prohibition is only of what is [already merely] applicable. Even being specified individually (<s>pratipadoktatva</s>) is a cause of overriding only when there is [truly] no other scope (<s>niravakāśatva</s>). And this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>śeṣād vibhāṣā</s>.' For there, having raised the doubt, 'The mention of "<s>śeṣa</s>" (remainder) is meaningless; those [rules] that are individually prescribed will be overriders,' it is stated: 'Rules that have no [other] scope are overriders; but the <s>samāsānta</s> (compound-final) [rules] have scope in the absence of <s>kap</s>.' Sometimes even in the absence of scopelessness, when [the rule is] equal to <s>para</s> (subsequent), <s>nitya</s> (invariable), etc. — the strength that causes prior application, due to being quicker to present itself, [exists even] through being an individually specified rule (<s>pratipadavidhi</s>); the principles of <s>para</s>, <s>nitya</s>, <s>antaraṅga</s>, and <s>pratipadavidhi</s> — when they conflict — their mutual superiority of the later [over the earlier] — this is stated by <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> based on the reading in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>pratyayottarapadayoś ca</s>.' For this very reason, in '<s>rame</s>' and the like, having raised the doubt that because of being individually specified, the <s>etva</s> [applies] first, and from the coalescence of the <s>ākāra</s>, the <s>halṅyādi</s>-<s>lopa</s> would not [apply] — it is resolved by the <s>lopa</s> from [the rule] '<s>eṅhrasvāt</s>.'

children.text: nanu 'ayaje indiram' ityādāvantaraṅgasyāpi guṇasyāpavādena savarṇa dīrghema bādhaḥ syāt, ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>ayaje indiram</s>' and the like, even the <s>antaraṅga</s> <s>guṇa</s> [substitution] should be overridden by the <s>savarṇadīrgha</s> (homogeneous lengthening) as its exception (<s>apavāda</s>). Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: apavādo yadyanyatra caritārthastarhyantaraṅgeṇa bādhyate || 65 ||
children.translated_text: If an exception (<s>apavāda</s>) has fulfilled its purpose (<s>caritārtha</s>) elsewhere, then it is overridden by the <s>antaraṅga</s> (inner-scope) [rule]. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 65]

children.text:
niravakāśatvarūpasya bādhakatvabījasyābhāvāt/ evañca prakṛte 'ntaraṅgeṇa guṇena savarṇadīrghaḥ samānāśraye caritārtho yaṇguṇayorapavādo 'pi bādhyate/ pūrvopasthitinimittatvarūpāntaraṅgatvaviṣaya idam/
yattvāgamādeśayorna bādhyabādhakabhāvaḥ, bhinnaphalatvāt, ata eva 'brāmhaṇebhyo dadhi dīyatām, kambalaḥ kauṇḍinyāya' ityādau kambaladānena na dadhidānabādha iti"chvoḥ"iti sūtre kaiyaṭaḥ/ tanna, 'apavādo nugdīrghatvasya' iti"dīrdho 'kitaḥ"iti sūtrabhāṣyavirodhāt//
children.translated_text: Because the seed of overriding power — namely, the character of having no [other] scope (<s>niravakāśatva</s>) — is absent. Thus in the case at hand, the <s>savarṇadīrgha</s>, being an exception that has fulfilled its purpose in [the context of] <s>yaṇ</s> and <s>guṇa</s> and having the same locus, is overridden by the <s>antaraṅga guṇa</s>. This [paribhāṣā] applies in the domain of the <s>antaraṅga</s> status [defined as] causation by a previously-presented condition. As for [the objection that] between <s>āgama</s> (augments) and <s>ādeśa</s> (substitutes) there is no supersession relationship because of different results — 'just as when [the order is] "Give curds to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and a blanket to <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>," the giving of the blanket does not override the giving of curds' — so says <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>chvoḥ</s>.' That is not so, because of the contradiction with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>dīrgho 'kitaḥ</s>': 'the exception is of <s>nug</s>-[augment and] lengthening.'

children.text: nanu 'ajīgaṇat' ityādau gaṇerītvaṃ niravakāśatvāddhalādiḥśeṣaṃ bādheta, tatrāha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>ajīgaṇat</s>' and the like, the <s>ītva</s> (long ī substitution) of <s>gaṇ</s> should override the <s>dhalādiśeṣa</s> (rest [of the rules]) because of having no [other] scope. To address this, he says:

children.text: abhyāsavikāreṣu bādhyabādhakabhāvo nāsti || 66 ||
children.translated_text: There is no supersession relationship (<s>bādhya-bādhaka-bhāva</s>) among modifications of the reduplicative syllable (<s>abhyāsa-vikāra</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 66]

children.text:
"dīrgho 'kitaḥ"ityakidgrahaṇamasyā jñāpakam/ anyathā 'yaṃyayamyate' ityatra nuki kṛte 'najantatvād dīrghāprāptyā tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameva/
iyaṃ parāntaraṅgādibādhakānāmapyabādhakatvabodhikā/ tena 'acīkarat' 'mīmāṃsate' ityādi siddham/
ādye sanvadbhāvasya paratvaddīrgheṇa bādhaḥ prāpnoti/ antye"mānbadha"iti dīrgheṇāntaraṅgatvādityasya bādhaḥ prāptaḥ/
yattu yatraikaikapravṛtyuttaramapi sarveṣāṃ pravṛttistatraivedamityataḥ"eka"iti sūtre kaiyaṭaḥ, tanna ; nuki kṛte itvāprāptyā"guṇo yaṅlukoḥ"iti sūtrasthabhāṣyoktatadudāharaṇāsaṅgateścetyanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: The mention of '<s>akit</s>' in '<s>dīrgho 'kitaḥ</s>' is the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) of this [paribhāṣā]. Otherwise, in '<s>yaṃ yayam yate</s>' and the like, after the <s>nuk</s> [augment] has been applied, since [the base] would no longer end in <s>an</s> — and thus the lengthening would not apply — the purposelessness [of the <s>akit</s> specification] would be quite clear. This [paribhāṣā] conveys the non-overriding capacity even of [rules that are] <s>para</s> (subsequent), <s>antaraṅga</s> (inner-scope), etc. Therefore '<s>acīkarat</s>,' '<s>mīmāṃsate</s>' and the like are established. In the first [example], the <s>sanvad-bhāva</s> (treatment as <s>san</s>-derivative), being subsequent (<s>para</s>), would [otherwise] override the lengthening. In the last [example], the <s>dīrgha</s> (lengthening) by '<s>mānbadha</s>,' being <s>antaraṅga</s>, would [otherwise] override. As for <s>Kaiyaṭa</s>'s [statement] on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>eka</s>': 'This applies only where even after each individual application, all [rules] still apply' — that is not so, because after the <s>nuk</s> [augment] has been applied, the <s>ītva</s> would not [apply], and because of the inconsistency with the examples stated by the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>guṇo yaṅlukoḥ</s>' — [for] details, [see] elsewhere.

children.text: nanu taccholāditṛnviṣaye ṇvulapi syāt/ na ca tṛnnapavādaḥ, asarūpāpavādasya vikalpena bādhakatvāt/ ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In the domain of <s>tācchīlika</s> (habitual action), <s>ṇvul</s> should also [apply] [besides <s>tṛn</s>]. Nor is <s>tṛn</s> an exception [to <s>ṇvul</s>], because a non-identical exception (<s>asarūpāpavāda</s>) overrides only optionally. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: tācchīlikeṣu vāsarūpavidhirnāsti || 67 ||
children.translated_text: In [suffixes denoting] habitual action (<s>tācchīlika</s>), the optional rule of identical form (<s>vā-sarūpa-vidhi</s>) does not [apply]. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 67]

children.text:
ṇvuli siddhe"nindahiṃsa"ādisūtreṇaikājbhyo vuñvidhānamatra jñāpakam/ tatra ṇvulvuñoḥ svare viśeṣābhāvāt/
tācchīlikeṣviti viṣayasaptamī/ tena tācchīlikairatācchīlikaiśca vāsarūpavidhirneti bodhyam/
nanvevam 'kamrā, kamanā' ityādyasiddhiḥ"namikampi"iti reṇa"anudāttetaśca halādeḥ"iti yuco bādhāditi cet, na ;"sūdadīpadīkṣaśca"ityanena dīperyujniṣedhenoktārthasyānityatvāt//
children.translated_text: Since [the result] is established by <s>ṇvul</s> [alone], the prescribing of <s>vuñ</s> for monosyllabic [roots] by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>nindahiṃsa</s>' etc. is the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) of this [paribhāṣā]. For there is no difference between <s>ṇvul</s> and <s>vuñ</s> in [their] vowel. '<s>Tācchīlikeṣu</s>' is a domain-locative (<s>viṣaya-saptamī</s>). Therefore it should be understood: the optional rule of identical form (<s>vā-sarūpa-vidhi</s>) does not [apply] either with <s>tācchīlikas</s> or with non-<s>tācchīlikas</s>. Objection: If so, '<s>kamrā</s>, <s>kamanā</s>' and the like would not be established — because the <s>ra</s> [suffix] from '<s>namikampi</s>' would override the <s>yuc</s> [suffix] from '<s>anudāttetaś ca halādeḥ</s>.' Reply: No — because of the non-eternality (<s>anityatva</s>) of the stated meaning, due to the prohibition of <s>yuj</s> from <s>dīp</s> by the [rule] '<s>sūdadīpadīkṣaś ca</s>.'

children.text:
nanvevam 'hasitaṃ chātrasya hasanam' ityādau ghañ, 'icchati bhoktum' ityatra liṅloṭau,
'īṣatpānaḥ somo bhavatā' ityatra khal prāpnotītyata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, in '<s>hasitaṃ chātrasya</s> = <s>hasanam</s>' and the like, <s>ghañ</s> [would wrongly apply]; in '<s>icchati bhoktum</s>' and the like, <s>liṅ</s> and <s>loṭ</s> [would wrongly apply]; in '<s>īṣatpānaḥ somo bhavatā</s>' and the like, <s>khal</s> would [wrongly] apply. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: ktalyuṭtumunkhalartheṣu vāsarūpavidhirnāsti || 68 ||
children.translated_text: In the meanings of <s>kta</s>, <s>lyuṭ</s>, <s>tumun</s>, and <s>khal</s>, the optional rule of identical form (<s>vā-sarūpa-vidhi</s>) does not [apply]. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 68]

children.text:
idañca vāsarūpavidheranityatvāt siddham/ tadanityatve jñapakaṃ ca 'arhe kṛtyatṛcaśca' iti/
tatra hi cakārasamuccitaliṅā kṛtyatṛcorbādho mā bhūditi kṛtyatṛjgrahaṇaṃ kriyata ityanyatra vistaraḥ/ "vāsarūpa"sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭā//
children.translated_text: This is established because of the non-eternality (<s>anityatva</s>) of the <s>vā-sarūpa-vidhi</s>. And the indicator for that non-eternality is '<s>arhe kṛtyatṛcaś ca</s>.' For there, since the <s>cakāra</s> (conjunction 'and') conjoins [with] <s>liṅ</s>, the mention of <s>kṛtya</s> and <s>tṛc</s> is made [specifically] so that their overriding [by the <s>vā-sarūpa-vidhi</s>] would not occur — [for] details, [see] elsewhere. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>vā-sarūpa</s>' <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: nanu"śvaḥ paktā"ityatra vāsarūpavidhinā lṝḍapi prāpnoti, kṛte ādeśe vairūpyādata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>śvaḥ paktā</s>' (he will cook tomorrow), through the <s>vā-sarūpa-vidhi</s>, <s>lṝḍ</s> also would [wrongly] apply; and after the substitution, there would be dissimilarity of form. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: lādeśeṣu vāsarūpavidhirnāsti || 69 ||
children.translated_text: In <s>l</s>-substitutes (<s>lādeśa</s>), the optional rule of identical form (<s>vā-sarūpa-vidhi</s>) does not [apply]. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 69]

children.text: ādeśakṛtavairūpyavatsu lakāreṣu sa nāstītyarthaḥ/ atra ca"haśaśvatorlaṅca"iti laṅ vidhānaṃ jñāpakam/ anyathā"parokṣe liṭ"iti liṭā laṅaḥ samāveśo 'sārūpyāt siddha iti kiṃ laṅvidhānena? śatrādibhistiṅāṃ samāveśārthaṃ śatṛvidhāyake vibhāṣāgrahaṇānuvṛttiḥ"liṭaḥ kānajvā"iti vāgrahaṇaṃ ca kṛtam/ tajjñapayati"vāsarūpa"sūtre 'pavāda ādeśatvānākrāntaḥ pratyaya eva gṛhyata iti kaiyaṭādau dhvanitam/ tatphalaṃ tu sadādibhyo bhūtasāmānye liṭaḥ kvasureva, na tu pakṣe tiṅiti bodhyam//
children.translated_text: The meaning is: in those <s>lakāras</s> (verb-tenses/moods) that have become dissimilar due to substitution, it [the <s>vā-sarūpa-vidhi</s>] does not [apply]. And here the prescribing of <s>laṅ</s> by [the sūtra] '<s>haśaśvator laṅ ca</s>' is the indicator. Otherwise, since the inclusion of <s>laṅ</s> by <s>liṭ</s> through '<s>parokṣe liṭ</s>' would [already] be established due to non-dissimilarity — what purpose would the prescribing of <s>laṅ</s> serve? The continuation of the <s>vibhāṣā</s> (option) reference in the rule prescribing <s>śatṛ</s> etc. for the inclusion of <s>tiṅ</s> endings through <s>śatṛ</s> etc., and the <s>vā</s> (optionality) reference in '<s>liṭaḥ kānajvā</s>' — these indicate that [in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>vā-sarūpa</s>'] only the suffix that is unaffected by the substitution is grasped — this is implied in <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> etc. The result of this is: from <s>sad</s>-roots etc. for general past meaning, only the <s>kvasu</s> of <s>liṭ</s> [applies], not optionally the <s>tiṅ</s> — this should be understood.

children.text: nanu"ṅamo hrasvāt"ityādau ṅamaḥ parasyāco 'ci parato ṅama iti veti sandehaḥ syāt, ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>ṅamo hrasvāt</s>' and the like, there would be a doubt: the <s>ṅam</s> [augment] of the subsequent <s>ac</s> (vowel), or the <s>ṅam</s> [augment before the vowel] following [the short vowel]. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: ubhayanirdeśe pañcamī nirdeśo balīyān || 70 ||
children.translated_text: When both [ablative and locative] references are present, the ablative reference is stronger. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 70]

children.text:
acīti saptamīnirdeśasya"mayauño"ityuttaratra cāritārthyāt pañcamīnirdeśo 'navakāśa iti"tasmādityuttarasya"ityasyaiva pravṛttiḥ/ yatra tu"ḍaḥ si dhuṭ"ityādāvubhayorapyacāritārthyam, tatra"tasmin"iti sūtrāpekṣayā"tasmādityuttarasya"ityasya paratvāt tenaiva vyavasthā/
evamubhayoścāritārthye 'pi/ yathā"āmi sarvanāmnaḥ suṭ"ityādau/ tatrā'mīti saptamī"trestrayaḥ"ityatra caritārthā/ āditi pañacamī"ājjaserasuk"ityatra caritārtheti spaṣṭam"tasminniti"iti sūtre bhāṣye kaiyaṭe ca//
children.translated_text: Because the locative reference '<s>aci</s>' has fulfilled its purpose (<s>caritārthya</s>) in '<s>mayauṇaḥ</s>' and elsewhere, the ablative reference, having no [other] scope, [causes] only the operation of '<s>tasmād ityuttarasya</s>' (that which follows the ablative). But where, as in '<s>ḍaḥ si dhuṭ</s>' and the like, neither of the two has fulfilled its purpose — there, because '<s>tasmād ityuttarasya</s>' is subsequent to the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tasmin</s>' (the locative rule), the determination is by that [subsequent rule] alone, due to posteriority (<s>paratva</s>). Similarly even when both have fulfilled their purpose — as in '<s>āmi sarvanāmnaḥ suṭ</s>' and the like. There, the locative '<s>āmi</s>' has fulfilled its purpose in '<s>treḥ trayaḥ</s>' and the like; and the ablative '<s>āt</s>' has fulfilled its purpose in '<s>āj jaser asuk</s>' and the like — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tasmin</s>'.

children.text: iti śrī nāgeśabhaṭṭaviracite paribhāṣenduśekhare
children.translated_text: Thus [concludes] the <s>Paribhāṣenduśekhara</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Nāgeśa Bhaṭṭa</s>:

children.text: bādhabījanāmakaṃ dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇam//
children.translated_text: the second chapter named '<s>Bādhabīja</s>' (The Basis of Supersession).

children.text: // atha śāstraśeṣa nāmakaṃ tṛtīyaṃ prakaraṇam //
children.translated_text: Now begins the third chapter named '<s>Śāstraśeṣa</s>' (Remainder of the Science).

children.text: nanu"ataḥ kṛkami"iti satvam 'ayaskumbhī' ityatra na syāt kumbhaśabdasyaivopādānāt, ata āha :-
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>ataḥ kṛkami</s>,' the <s>satva</s> (substitution of <s>s</s>) in '<s>ayaskumbhī</s>' would not [apply], because only the word <s>kumbha</s> is mentioned [not the feminine]. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: prātipadikagrahaṇe liṅga viśiṣṭasyāpi grahaṇam || 71 ||
children.translated_text: When a <s>prātipadika</s> (nominal stem) is mentioned, a gender-qualified [form] of it is also included. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 71]

children.text:
sāmānyarūpeṇa viśeṣarūpeṇa vā prātipadikabodhakaśabdagrahaṇe sati liṅgabodhaka pratyaya viśiṣṭasyāpi tena grahaṇaṃ bodhyam/ apinā kevalasyāpītyarthaḥ/
asyāśca jñāpakaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇādhikārasthe"kumāra śramaṇādibhiḥ"iti sūtre strīliṅgaśramaṇādiśabdapāṭhaḥ/ strīpratyayaviśiṣṭaśramaṇādibhiśca kumārīśabdasyaiva sāmānādhikaraṇyam, na tu kumāraśabdasyeti tadetajjñāpakam/
iyañca"dviṣatparayoḥ"ityādyupapadavidhau, samāsāntavidhau, mahadātve, ñnitsvare, rājasvare brāmhaṇakumārayoḥ"bahornañvaduttarapadabhūmni"ityādau, samāsasaṅghātagrahaṇeṣu ca na pravartata iti ṅyāp sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam/
vibhaktinimittakakārye ca netyapi tatraiva/
children.translated_text: When a word denoting a <s>prātipadika</s> (nominal stem) is employed, whether in its general form or specific form, even that which is qualified by a <s>pratyaya</s> (suffix) denoting gender should be understood as being apprehended by it. The word 'api' indicates 'even of the bare stem alone.' The indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) for this is the listing of the word <s>śramaṇa</s> etc. with feminine gender in the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>kumāra</s>-<s>śramaṇādibhiḥ</s>" which falls under the section on <s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s> (co-referentiality). For the co-referentiality of the word <s>kumārī</s> is only with <s>śramaṇa</s> etc. qualified by the feminine suffix, not with the word <s>kumāra</s> — and this serves as that indicator. And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] does not apply in <s>upapada</s> (subordinate word) rules such as "<s>dviṣatparayoḥ</s>," in <s>samāsānta</s> (compound-final) rules, in <s>mahadātva</s>, in <s>ñit</s> accent, in the accent rule for <s>rāja</s>-<s>brāhmaṇa</s>-<s>kumāra</s> "<s>bahornañvaduttarapadabhūmni</s>" and the like, and in cases of apprehension of the compound as a whole — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>ṅyāp</s> <s>sūtra</s>.
