And it does not apply in operations occasioned by case-endings either — this too is stated there.

children.text:
tatra samāsāntavidhāvayavagrahaṇa eva na, samāsasaṅghātagrahaṇe tu pravartata eva, svaravidhāveva samāsasaṅghātagrahaṇe tatra doṣokteḥ,"bahuvrīherūdhasaḥ"iti sūtrastha bhāṣyācca, 'etāvatsvevānityatvādapravṛttiḥ, doṣāḥ khalvapi sākalyena parigaṇitāḥ' iti bhāṣyokteḥ/
nanvevam"bahuvrīherūdhasoṅīṣ"iti sūtrastha bhāṣyāsaṅgatiḥ/ tatra hi 'kuṇḍodhnī' ityatra"nadyṛtaśca"iti kabāpādito nadyantabahuvrīherityarthāt, nadyantasya bahuvrīhitvābhāvāt tadasaṅgatiḥ/ nadyantānāṃ yaḥ samāsa ityarthena ca parihṛtam/
nadyantaprakṛtikasubantottarapadakaḥ samāsa iti cet, na ; anayā paribhāṣayā strīpratyaya samabhivyāhāre tadrahite dṛṣṭānāṃ prātipadikatva tadvyāpya dharmāṇāṃ viśiṣṭe 'pi paryāptatvamatidiśyata ityāśayāt//
children.translated_text: Regarding that: in <s>samāsānta</s> (compound-final) rules, [this <s>paribhāṣā</s>] indeed does not apply to the apprehension of a component, but in the apprehension of the compound as a whole it does indeed apply — [since its non-application is stated] only in the apprehension of compound-wholes in accent rules, because defects are pointed out [only] there; and because of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>bahuvrīherūdhasaḥ</s>," [which states] 'non-application due to the <s>anityatva</s> (non-permanence) is only in these cases; indeed the defects have been enumerated exhaustively.' Now, if so, there would be inconsistency with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>bahuvrīherūdhasaḥ ṅīṣ</s>." For there, in the case of '<s>kuṇḍodhnī</s>,' by "<s>nadyṛtaśca</s>" from the <s>kap</s> etc. [section], [it is argued that <s>ṅīṣ</s> comes] after a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> ending in a <s>nadī</s>-stem — that is the meaning; and since a <s>nadī</s>-ending [stem] does not have the status of being a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, there is that inconsistency. It is resolved by [taking the meaning as:] 'a compound whose latter member is a <s>subanta</s> (inflected nominal) having a <s>nadī</s>-ending stem as its base' — if so proposed, no; because the intent of this <s>paribhāṣā</s> is that even for the qualified [stem with feminine suffix], the sufficiency of <s>prātipadika</s>-hood and properties pervading it, which are observed in [stems] devoid of the feminine suffix when the feminine suffix is co-expressed, is extended.

children.text:
nanvevam 'yūnaḥ paśya' ityatreva 'yuvatiḥ paśya' ityatrāpi"śvayuvonām"iti samprasāraṇaṃ syāt,
ata āha --
children.translated_text: Now, if so, just as in '<s>yūnaḥ</s> <s>paśya</s>' (see the young one), in '<s>yuvatiḥ</s> <s>paśya</s>' (see the young woman) also, the <s>samprasāraṇa</s> by "<s>śvayuvonām</s>" would apply. Therefore he states —

children.text: vibhaktau liṅgaviśiṣṭāgrahaṇam || 72 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 72: In [rules concerning] <s>vibhakti</s> (case-endings), there is no apprehension [of a stem] as qualified by gender.

children.text: spaṣṭā ceyam"yuvoranākau"ityatra bhāṣye/ ghaṭaghaṭīgrahaṇena liṅgaviśiṣṭaparibhāṣayā anityatvāt tanmūlaiṣetyanye//
children.translated_text: And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on "<s>yuvoranākau</s>." Others [say] that because of the <s>anityatva</s> (non-permanence) of the <s>paribhāṣā</s> on gender-qualified [apprehension] through the mention of <s>ghaṭa</s>-<s>ghaṭī</s>, this [result] is rooted in that.

children.text: nanu"tasyāpatyam"ityekavacananapuṃsakābhyāṃ nirdeśāt 'gārgāyo gārgyau' ityādyuktam, ata āha-
children.translated_text: Now, since in "<s>tasyāpatyam</s>" (his offspring) the statement is made with singular number and neuter gender, '<s>Gārgāyaḥ</s>, <s>Gārgyau</s>' and so on would [not] be possible. Therefore he states —

children.text: sūtre liṅgavacanamatantram || 73 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 73: In a <s>sūtra</s>, gender and number are not essential.

children.text:
"arddhaṃ napuṃsakam"iti napuṃsakagrahaṇamsyā jñāpakam/ nityanapuṃsakatvārthaṃ tu na tadityanyatra nirūpitam/
dhānyapalālanyāyena nāntarīyakatayā tayorupādānamiti"tasyāpatyam"ityatra bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ ata eva"ākaḍāra"sūtre eketi caritārthamityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: The mention of neuter gender in "<s>arddhaṃ napuṃsakam</s>" (half is neuter) serves as the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) for this. But [the view] that it is for the purpose of [indicating] permanent neuter gender is refuted elsewhere. That gender and number are employed [merely] as concomitants, by the principle of <s>dhānya-palāla-nyāya</s> (the grain-and-chaff maxim — where chaff comes along with grain, not independently intended), is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on "<s>tasyāpatyam</s>." For this very reason, the elaboration that '<s>eka</s>' in the "<s>ākaḍāra</s>" <s>sūtra</s> has its purpose already served is [discussed] elsewhere.

children.text: nanu"bhaśādibhyo bhuvyacveḥ"ityādau vidhīyamānaḥ kyaṅ 'kva divā bhṛśā bhavanti' ityatrāpi syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>kyaṅ</s> suffix prescribed in "<s>bhaśādibhyo bhuvyacveḥ</s>" and so on would also apply in '<s>kva divā bhṛśā bhavanti</s>' (where do they shine brightly). Therefore he states —

children.text: nañiva yuktamanyasadṛśādhikaraṇe tathā hyarthagatiḥ || 74 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 74: What is appropriate with <s>nañ</s> (the negative particle) is likewise appropriate in a substratum that is different from yet similar to [the item named]; for thus is the understanding of the meaning.

children.text:
nañyuktamiva yuktaṃ ca yat kiñcid dṛśyate tatra tasmād bhinne tatsadṛśe 'dhikaraṇe dravye kāryaṃ vijñāyate/ hi yataḥ tathārthagatirasti/ na hi 'abrahmaṇamānaya' ityukte loṣṭamānīya kṛtī bhavati/ ataścavyantabhinne cvyantasadṛśe 'bhūtatadbhāvaviṣaye kyaṅiti nokta doṣaḥ/
"oṣadheśca vibhaktāvaprathamāyām"ityādau vibhaktigrahaṇametannyāyasididhārthānuvāda eva/ etena vibhaktāvityādyasyānityatve jñāpakamiti vadantaḥ parāstāḥ, anityatve bhāṣyasammata phalābhāvāt/ ata eva 'akartari ca' iti sūtre kāraka grahaṇaṃ bhāṣye pratyākhyātamiti bodhyam/ spaṣṭā ceyam"bhṛśādibhyaḥ"iti sūtre bhāṣye/
atrānyasadṛśetyuktvā sādṛśyasya bhedāghaṭitatvaṃ sūcayati/ nirūpitaṃ caitanmañjūṣāyām//
children.translated_text: Just as what is appropriate with <s>nañ</s> (negation), so too whatever is observed — the operation is understood to apply in a substratum, a substance, that is different from that [named item] yet similar to it. 'Hi' means 'because' — because thus is the understanding of the meaning. For indeed, when one says '<s>abrāhmaṇam ānaya</s>' (bring a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>), one is not considered to have fulfilled the task by bringing a clod of earth. Therefore, [<s>kyaṅ</s> applies] in a domain similar to yet different from the <s>cvi</s>-derivative — namely in the domain of 'becoming what one was not before' — and the stated objection does not arise. In "<s>oṣadheśca vibhaktāvaprathamāyām</s>" and the like, the mention of <s>vibhakti</s> (case-ending) is merely a restatement of what is already established by this principle. By this, those who say that [the mention in] '<s>vibhaktāu</s>' etc. is an indicator of <s>anityatva</s> (non-permanence) are refuted, because there would be no result approved by the <s>Bhāṣya</s> if it were non-permanent. For this very reason, it should be understood that the mention of <s>kāraka</s> (syntactic role) in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>akartari ca</s>' is rejected in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>bhṛśādibhyaḥ</s>." Here, by saying 'different from yet similar to,' he indicates that similarity is incompatible with [complete] difference. And this is explained in the <s>Mañjūṣā</s>.

children.text: nanu 'vyāghrī, kaccapī' ityādau subantena samāsāt tato 'pyantaraṅgatvāṭṭāp adantatvābhāvājjāti lakṣaṇo ṅīṣ na syāt, ata āha --
gatikārakopapadānāṃ kṛdbhiḥ saha samāsavacanaṃ
children.translated_text: The compounding of <s>gati</s> (preverbs), <s>kāraka</s> (syntactic arguments), and <s>upapada</s> (subordinate words) with <s>kṛt</s>-suffixes

Now, in forms like '<s>vyāghrī</s>' (tigress) and '<s>kaccapī</s>' (female tortoise), after compounding with a <s>subanta</s> (inflected nominal), since [compounding] is more internally conditioned (<s>antaraṅga</s>) than that [feminine suffix], and since in the absence of <s>a</s>-ending [due to no <s>ṭāp</s>], the gender-based <s>ṅīṣ</s> would not apply. Therefore he states —

children.text: prāk subutpatteḥ || 75 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 75: [takes place] before the generation of <s>sup</s> (case-endings).

children.text:
"upapadam"iti sūtre 'tiṅgrahaṇena"kugati"ityatra tadapakarṣaṇenātiṅantaśca samāsa ityarthāt tayoḥ sūtrayoḥ supsupetyasya nivṛtyaikadeśānumatyā kārakāṃśe ca siddheyam/ tena 'aśvakrītī' iti siddhā/ anyathā pūrvaṃ ṭāpyadantatvābhāvāt"krītātkaraṇapūrvāt"iti ṅīṣ na syāt/
asyā anityatvāt kvacit subutpatyanantaramapi samāsaḥ/
yathā sā hi tasya dhanakrīteti/
children.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>upapadam</s>," by the mention of <s>tiṅ</s> (verbal endings) drawing away [the reference to <s>tiṅ</s>] from "<s>kugati</s>," [we get the meaning that] the compound is also with non-<s>tiṅ</s>-ending [stems] — from the meaning of those two <s>sūtras</s>, by partial acceptance of the cessation of '<s>sup-supa</s>' (nominal-with-nominal compounding requirement), and through the <s>kāraka</s> portion, this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is established. By this, '<s>aśvakrītī</s>' (one bought for a horse, feminine) is established. Otherwise, since <s>ṭāp</s> would not first [apply] due to the absence of <s>a</s>-ending, <s>ṅīṣ</s> by "<s>krītātkaraṇapūrvāt</s>" would not apply. Due to the <s>anityatva</s> (non-permanence) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>], sometimes compounding occurs even after the generation of <s>sup</s> (case-endings). For example: '<s>sā hi tasya dhanakrītā</s>' (for she is bought with his wealth).

children.text:
anye tvanityatve na mānam, tatrājāditvāṭṭābityāhuḥ/ ata eva 'kumbhakāraḥ' ityādau ṣaṣṭhī samāso 'pi subutpatteḥ pūrvameva/ ṣaṣṭhīsamāsābhāve copapadasamāsakṛta ekārthībhāva iti na tatra vākyamiti bhāṣye spaṣṭam/
tatra hi 'ṣaṣṭhīsamāsādupapadasamāso vipratiṣedhena' iti vārttikam/ athavā 'vibhāṣā ṣaṣṭhī samāso yadā na ṣaṣṭhīsamāsastadopapadasamāsaḥ' iti tatpratyākhyānaṃ ca/
yadyapyupapadasamāsasyāntaraṅgatvābhiprāyakam 'na vā ṣaṣṭhīsamāsābhāvādupapadasamāsaḥ' iti vārtikakṛtoktam, tathāpi tadubhayapratyākhyānaparam, 'athavā' ityādi bhāṣyaṃ paribhāṣāyāṃ sāmānyataḥ kārakopādānena kārakavibhaktyantena kṛdbhiḥ samāsamātrasya subutpatteḥ pūrvameva lābhāt/
etenaiṣā kārakatadviśeṣayorupādāna eveti parāstam/ asyā vidhyekavākyatvābhāvena vipratiṣedhādi
śāstravat kāryavyavasthāpakatvenopādāna evetyarthālābhācca//
children.translated_text: Others, however, say there is no evidence for <s>anityatva</s> (non-permanence) [of this <s>paribhāṣā</s>], and there [in '<s>vyāghrī</s>' etc.] <s>ṭāp</s> comes by belonging to the <s>ajādi</s> class. For this very reason, in '<s>kumbhakāraḥ</s>' (potter) and the like, the <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>-compound (genitive compound) also [takes place] before the generation of <s>sup</s>. And in the absence of a <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>-compound, the unity of meaning (<s>ekārthībhāva</s>) produced by <s>upapada</s>-compounding [suffices], so there is no [mere] sentence there — this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. For there the <s>vārttika</s> states: 'the <s>upapada</s>-compound [prevails] over the <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>-compound by <s>vipratiṣedha</s> (conflict resolution).' Alternatively, 'optionally, [there is] a <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>-compound; when there is no <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>-compound, then there is an <s>upapada</s>-compound' — this is the rejection of that [<s>vārttika</s>]. Although the <s>vārttikakāra</s> has stated, with the intent that <s>upapada</s>-compounding is more internally conditioned (<s>antaraṅga</s>), 'or rather, in the absence of <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>-compound, the <s>upapada</s>-compound [applies],' nevertheless, that [statement] along with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> beginning with '<s>athavā</s>' aims at rejecting both [alternatives], since by the general mention of <s>kāraka</s> in the <s>paribhāṣā</s>, compounding in general — [whether] with <s>kāraka</s> case-ending-bearing [words] and <s>kṛt</s>-suffixes — is obtained before the generation of <s>sup</s>. By this, [the view] that this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] applies only in the mention of <s>kāraka</s> and its specific types is refuted. Because the meaning cannot be obtained through this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] being a single syntactic unit with the prescriptive rule, and because it serves to determine the operation like a <s>śāstra</s> principle such as <s>vipratiṣedha</s> etc., the mention [of <s>kāraka</s>] is indeed [in a general sense].

children.text: nanu"ugidacām"ityatra dhātoścedugitkāryaṃ tarhyañcatereveti niyamenādhātoreva numi siddhe 'dhātugrahaṇaṃ vyartham, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Now, in "<s>ugidacām</s>," if the <s>ugit</s>-operation belongs to the <s>dhātu</s> (root), then by the restriction that it belongs only to <s>añcati</s>, since <s>num</s> augment would be established for [stems that are] not roots [anyway], the mention of '<s>dhātu</s>' would be purposeless. Therefore he states —

children.text: sampratikābhāve bhūtapūrvagatiḥ || 76 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 76: In the absence of a present [condition], the [rule] applies based on a former state.

children.text: tattad vacanasāmarthya nyāyasiddheyam/ tatsāmarthyādadhātubhūtapūrvasyāpītyarthena gomatyateḥ kvipi 'gomān' ityādau num siddhiḥ/"nāmi"ityādisūtreṣu bhāṣye spaṣṭā//
children.translated_text: This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is established by the principle of the interpretive force of various [grammatical] statements. By the force of that [statement], the meaning is that [the rule applies] even to what was formerly — but is no longer — a <s>dhātu</s> (root); thus, in forms like '<s>gomān</s>' from <s>gomati</s> and <s>ati</s> with the <s>kvip</s> suffix, the <s>num</s> augment is established. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on <s>sūtras</s> such as "<s>nāmi</s>" and others.

children.text: bahuvrīhau tadguṇasaṃvijñānamapi || 77 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 77: In a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (exocentric compound), there is also <s>tadguṇasaṃvijñāna</s> (identification through those constituent qualities).

children.text:
apinā atadguṇasaṃvijñānam/ teṣāṃ guṇānāmavayavapadārthānāṃ saṃvijñānaṃ viśeṣānvayitvamiti tadarthaḥ/
yatra samavāyasambandhena sambandhyanyapadārthaḥ, tatra prāyastadguṇasaṃvijñānam/ anyatra prāyo 'nyat/ 'lambakarṇacitragū' udāharaṇe/
'sarvādīni, jakṣatyādayaḥ' iti codāharaṇe/ sarvanāmasaṃjñā sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭā//
children.translated_text: The word 'api' (also) indicates <s>atadguṇasaṃvijñāna</s> (identification not through those constituent qualities) [as well]. <s>Tadguṇasaṃvijñāna</s> means: the constituent meanings (<s>avayava-padārtha</s>) — those qualities — have specific connection [with the referent]; that is its meaning. Where the related entity of the other word is connected by the relation of inherence (<s>samavāya-sambandha</s>), there generally there is <s>tadguṇasaṃvijñāna</s>. Elsewhere, generally the other [<s>atadguṇasaṃvijñāna</s> applies]. Examples: '<s>lambakarṇa</s>' (having drooping ears), '<s>citragū</s>' (having a spotted cow). And examples [of <s>atadguṇasaṃvijñāna</s>]: '<s>sarvādīni</s>' (the <s>sarva</s>-class), '<s>jakṣatyādayaḥ</s>' (the <s>jakṣati</s>-class). This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sarvanāma-saṃjñā</s> <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: nanu"vadaḥ supi kyap ca"iti cenānukṛṣṭasya yataḥ"bhuvo bhāve"ityatrāpyanuvṛttiḥ syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Now, if [the element] drawn forward by <s>ca</s> from "<s>vadaḥ supi kyap ca</s>" were to continue into "<s>bhuvo bhāve</s>" as well, [there would be an undesired result]. Therefore he states —

children.text: cānukṛṣṭaṃ nottaratra || 78 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 78: What is drawn forward by <s>ca</s> does not [continue] further [beyond its immediate next rule].

children.text:
ṇamulyanuvartamāne"avyaye 'yathābhipreta"iti sūtre punarṇamulgrahaṇanasyā jñāpakam/ anyathā 'ktvā ca' iti vadet/
taddhi uttaratrobhayoḥ sambamdhārtham/ udāharaṇāni sphuṭāni/
idamanityam/ ata eva"tṛtīyā ca hoḥ"ityatra cānukṛṣṭāyā api dvitīyāyā"antarāntareṇa"ityatra sambandhaḥ/
"luṭi ca kṛpaḥ"iti sūtrasthenānuvṛttyarthakasakalacakārapratyākhyānena viruddheyam/ vyākhyānādevānuvṛtti nivṛttyornirvāha iti tadāśayaḥ/"kulijāllukkhau ca"iti sūtrasthabhāṣyaviruddhā ca/ tatra hi"dvigoḥ ṣṭhaṃśca"iti sūtrāt ṣṭhanaḥ, tatra 'cenāpyanukṛṣṭasya kho 'nyatarasyām' ityasya cānuvṛttiṃ svīkṛtya lukkhau ceti bhāṣye pratyākhyātam//
children.translated_text: The indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) for this is the repeated mention of <s>ṇamul</s> in the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>avyaye yathābhipretam</s>" when <s>ṇamul</s> is [already] continuing [from a prior <s>sūtra</s>]. Otherwise, [the <s>sūtra</s>] would have said '<s>ktvā ca</s>.' For that [repeated mention] is for the purpose of connecting [<s>ṇamul</s>] with both of the subsequent [<s>sūtras</s>]. The examples are self-evident. This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is <s>anitya</s> (non-permanent). For this very reason, [although] the <s>dvitīyā</s> (accusative) drawn by <s>ca</s> in "<s>tṛtīyā ca hoḥ</s>," [it] nonetheless connects with "<s>antarāntareṇa</s>." This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is contradicted by the rejection of all the <s>ca</s>-particles that serve the purpose of <s>anuvṛtti</s> (continuation) found in the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>luṭi ca kṛpaḥ</s>." The resolution is that the cessation of continuation is achieved through interpretation alone — that is the intent. And it is contradicted by the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>kulijāl lukkhau ca</s>." For there, from the <s>sūtra</s> "<s>dvigoḥ ṣṭhaṃśca</s>" [the suffix] <s>ṣṭhan</s> [is obtained]; and having accepted the continuation of <s>ca</s> from '<s>cenāpyanukṛṣṭasya kho 'nyatarasyām</s>,' the [alternative reading] '<s>lukkhau ca</s>' is rejected in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: nanvanudāttāderantodāttācca yaducyate tadvyañjanādervyañjanāntācca na prāpnotītyata āha --
children.translated_text: Now, what is stated regarding [a stem] ending in <s>anudātta</s> (grave accent) and ending in <s>udātta</s> (acute accent) — that does not apply to [a stem] beginning with a consonant or ending in a consonant. Therefore he states —

children.text: svaravidhau vyañjanamavidyamānavat || 79 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 79: In accent rules, a consonant is treated as if non-existent.

children.text:
svaroddaśyake vidhāvityarthaḥ/"nottarapade 'nudāttādāvapṛthivīrudrapūṣamanthiṣu"iti sūtre pṛthivyādiparyudāsosyājñāpakaḥ/ anyathā pṛthivyādīnāmanudāttāditvābhāvādaprāptau tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameva/
dharmigrāhakamānādeva ca svaroddeśyakaviṣayamidam/ ata eva"śaturanumonadyajādī,"acaḥ kartturyaki"
ityādau aca ityādeścāritārthyam/ ata eva"rājavatī"ityādau nalopasyāsiddhatvādanvatīśabdatvāt,"anto 'vatyāḥ"iti svaro na, 'udaśvitvān' ityatra"hrasvanuḍbhyām"iti matubudāttatvaṃ ca netyākaraḥ/ spaṣṭaṃ cedam"samāsasya"iti
sūtre bhāṣye/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: in a rule that is intended for accent. The exclusion of <s>Pṛthivī</s> and others in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>nottarapade 'nudāttādāvapṛthivīrudrapūṣamanthiṣu</s>' is the indicatory sign (<s>jñāpaka</s>) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. Otherwise, since <s>Pṛthivī</s> and others do not have initial <s>anudātta</s> [accent], and [the rule] would not reach them anyway, their exclusion would be clearly pointless. And from the very authoritative source that apprehends the property-bearer (<s>dharmigrāhaka</s>), this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] has its domain in accent-intended [rules]. For this very reason, [in <s>sūtras</s> like] '<s>śaturanumo</s>', '<s>nadyajādī</s>', '<s>acaḥ kartturyaki</s>'...

children.text: "uccairudāttaḥ"iti sūtre kaiyaṭastu 'iyamanāvaśyakī, samimavyāhṛtājuparāgeṇa halo 'pyudāttādivadavabhāsāttadupapatteḥ' ityāha/ tatra bhāṣye 'pi dhvanitametat//
children.translated_text: <s>Kaiyaṭa</s>, however, in [his commentary on] the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>uccairudāttaḥ</s>', says: 'This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is not indispensable, because consonants too appear as if <s>udātta</s> etc. through contact with adjacent vowels — this accounts for [the usage].' This is hinted at in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> there as well.

children.text: nanvevamapi 'rājadṛṣat' itiyādau"samāsasya"ityantodāttatvaṃ ṣakārākārasya na syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: Even so, in [forms like] '<s>rājadṛṣat</s>' and the like, the final <s>udātta</s> accent [prescribed by] '<s>samāsasya</s>' would not apply to the <s>ṣa</s>-sound and <s>a</s>-sound. To address this, he says —

children.text: halsvaraprāptai vyañjanamavidyamānavat || 80 ||
children.translated_text: When an accent that applies to a consonant-vowel [pair] is expected, the consonant is treated as if non-existent. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 80)

children.text:
asyāśca"yatonāvaḥ"iti sūtre 'naupratiṣedho jñāpakaḥ/ 'nāvyam' ityatrādirnakāro na svarayogyaḥ, yaścākārastadyogyo nāsāvādiriti sa pratiṣedho 'narthakaḥ/
na cādireva makāra udāttaguṇaviśiṣṭāntaratamājrūpo 'stviti vācyam, tathā sati nimittabhūtadvayackatvasyavināśādupajīvyavirodhenādyudāttatvāprāpteḥ, ityanyatra vistaraḥ/ spaṣṭā ceyam"samāsasya"iti sūtre bhāṣye//
children.translated_text: The prohibition of <s>nau</s> in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>yatonāvaḥ</s>' is the indicatory sign (<s>jñāpaka</s>) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. In '<s>nāvyam</s>', the initial <s>n</s>-sound is not eligible for accent, and the <s>ā</s>-vowel that is eligible is not the initial — so that prohibition would be purposeless [without this <s>paribhāṣā</s>]. Nor should it be said that the <s>m</s>-sound itself, being initial, could be the <s>antaratama</s> (nearest substitute) qualified by the <s>udātta</s> property — because in that case, the duality that constitutes the condition would be destroyed, and through conflict with the relied-upon [principle], the initial-<s>udātta</s> status would not be reached...

children.text: nanu"pūraṇa guṇa"iti niṣedhastavyatyapi syāt"diva aut"itiyautvaṃ diveḥ kvipyapi syāt, tathā"yato 'nāvaḥ"iti svaro ṇyatyapi syāt"ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ"iti caṅyapi syāt; ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: The prohibition in '<s>pūraṇaguṇa</s>' would apply to <s>stavya</s> as well; the <s>au</s>-substitution by '<s>diva aut</s>' would apply to <s>div</s> even in <s>kvip</s>; similarly, the accent [rule] '<s>yato 'nāvaḥ</s>' would apply to <s>ṇyat</s> as well; and '<s>ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ</s>' would apply to <s>caṅ</s> as well. To address this, he says —

children.text: niranubandhaka grahaṇe na sānubandhakasya || 81 ||
children.translated_text: In a designation without an indicatory marker (<s>anubandha</s>), [there is no reference to] one with an indicatory marker. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 81)

children.text: tadanubandhaka grahaṇe nātadanubandhakasya || 82 ||
children.translated_text: In a designation with a particular indicatory marker, [there is no reference to] one without that indicatory marker. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 82)

children.text:
"vāmadevāḍḍayaḍḍyau"iti sūtre ḍyaḍḍtorḍitvamanayorajñāpakam/ taddhi"yayatoścātadarthe"
ityatra tayoragrahaṇārtham/ nañaḥ parasya yayadantasyottarapadasyānta udātta iti tadarthaḥ/ evaṃ cāvāmadevye 'vyaya
pūrvapadaprakṛtisvara eva bhavati/
tanmātrānubandhakagrahaṇe sa cānyaścānubandho yasya tadgrahaṇaṃ netyantyārthaḥ/ ete ca pratyayāpratyayasādhāraṇe, diva aut"ityādau sañcāritatvāt/
varṇagpahaṇe cānayorapravṛttiriti spaṣṭam"auṅa āpaḥ"ityatra bhāṣye/ yenānubandhena sānubandhakatvaṃ dvyanubandhakatvādi vā tadanuccāraṇe evaiṣā, dharmigrāhakamānāt/ tena"jaśśasoḥ"ityatra naiṣeti niranubandhakatvāt taddhitaśata evātra grahaṇaṃ syāditi na śaṅkyam/
evamantyānyatarānubandhoccāraṇe eva/ tena"vano raca"ityādau ṅvanipkvaniporagrahaṇasiddhiḥ/
ekānubandhakagrahaṇe sambhavatīti tvartho na bhāṣyādisammata ityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: The <s>ḍ</s>-status of <s>ḍyaḍḍ</s> in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>vāmadevāḍḍayaḍḍyau</s>' is the indicatory sign of these two [<s>paribhāṣās</s>]. For that [mention] is for the purpose of not including them in '<s>yayatoścātadarthe</s>'. The meaning is: the final of the latter member that ends in <s>yay</s> and follows <s>nañ</s> is <s>udātta</s>. And thus, in [the form] '<s>avāmadevya</s>', the <s>avyaya</s>-<s>pūrvapada</s> retains its original accent (<s>prakṛtisvara</s>). [The expression] 'designation with only that marker' [means] a designation where that and no other <s>anubandha</s> is present...

children.text: nanu 'kuṭīraḥ' ityādau svārthikatvāt svārthikānāṃ prakṛtito liṅgavatanānuvṛtternyāyaprāptatvāt puṃstvānupapattiḥ, 'apkalpam' ityatra napaṃsakaikavacanayoranupapattiścetyata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>kuṭīraḥ</s>' and the like, since [the suffix] is <s>svārthika</s> (having its own meaning), and since the non-continuation of gender and number from the base is expected by general principle for <s>svārthika</s> [suffixes], masculine gender would not be obtained. And in '<s>apkalpam</s>', neuter singular would not be obtained. To address this, he says —

children.text: kvacit svārthikāḥ prakṛtito liṅgavatanānyativartante || 83 ||
children.translated_text: Sometimes, <s>svārthika</s> suffixes deviate from the gender and number of the base. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 83)

children.text: "ṇacaḥ striyām"iti sūtre striyāmityuktirasyā jñāpikā/ anyathā"karmavyatihāre ṇac striyām"iti striyāmeva vidhānāt kiṃ tena? spaṣṭā ceyaṃ bahujvidhāyake bhāṣye//
children.translated_text: The mention of '<s>striyām</s>' (in the feminine) in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ṇacaḥ striyām</s>' is the indicatory sign (<s>jñāpikā</s>) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. Otherwise, since [the rule] '<s>karmavyatihāre ṇac striyām</s>' prescribes [the suffix] only in the feminine, what purpose would that serve? And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is clearly [stated] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> that prescribes <s>bahuvac</s> [compounds].

children.text: nanu 'supathī nagarī' iti"yuvoranākau"iti sūtrabhāṣyodāhṛte"inaḥ striyām"iti kap syāt ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>supathī nagarī</s>', cited as an example in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>yuvoranākau</s>', the <s>kap</s> suffix [prescribed by] '<s>inaḥ striyām</s>' would apply. To address this, he says —

children.text: samāsāntavidhiranityaḥ || 84 ||
children.translated_text: The rule prescribing compound-final elements (<s>samāsānta</s>) is non-invariable (<s>anitya</s>). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 84)

children.text: "prateraṃśvādayastatpuruṣe"ityantodāttatvāyāṃśvādiṣu rājame śabdapāṭho 'syā jñāpakaḥ/ anyathā ṭacaṃvāntodāttatve siddhe kiṃ tena?"dvitribhyāṃ pāddanmūrddhasu"iti svara vidhāyake bhāṣye spaṣṭam//
children.translated_text: The listing of the word '<s>rājameśa</s>' among the <s>aṃśvādi</s> group in [the rule] '<s>prateraṃśvādayastatpuruṣe</s>' for final-<s>udātta</s> accent is the indicatory sign (<s>jñāpaka</s>) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. Otherwise, since the final-<s>udātta</s> accent would already be established by the <s>ṭac</s> [suffix], what purpose would it serve? This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> that prescribes accent in '<s>dvitribhyāṃ pāddanmūrddhasu</s>'.

children.text:
nanu 'śatāni' ityādau numi kṛte ṣaṭsaṃjñā prāpnoti, tataśca luk syāt, tathā 'upādāsta'
ityatrātve kṛte"sthaghvoricca"itītvaṃ prāpnotītyata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>śatāni</s>' and the like, after the insertion of <s>num</s>, the <s>ṣaṭ</s>-designation would apply, and consequently <s>luk</s> (deletion) would occur. Similarly, in '<s>upādāsta</s>', after <s>ā</s>-substitution is applied, the <s>i</s>-substitution by '<s>sthaghvoricca</s>' would be expected. To address this, he says —

children.text: sannipātalakṣaṇo vidhiranimittaṃ tadvighātasya || 85 ||
children.translated_text: A rule whose condition arises from a conjunction [of elements] is not the cause of the destruction of that [very conjunction]. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 85)

children.text:
sannipātaḥudvayoḥ sambandhaḥ, tannimitto vidhistaṃ sannipātaṃ yo vihanti, tasyānimittam/
upajīvyavirodhasyāyuktatvamiti nyāyamūlaiṣā/
ata evātra sannipātaśabdena na pūrvaparayoḥ sambandha eva, kintu viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇa sannipāto 'pi gṛhyate/ ata eva 'grāmaṇi kulam' ityādau napuṃsakahrasvatve 'pi"piti kṛti"iti tuk na/ prātipadikājantatvasannipātena jātasya hrasvasya tadavidhāyakatvāt/ tukyajantatvavighātaḥ spaṣṭa eva/
na cārthāśrayatvena hrasvasya bahiraṅgatayāsiddhatvam, arthakṛtabahiraṅgatvānāśrayaṇasyoktatvāt/ kiñca"ṣatvatukorasiddhaḥ"ityetadbalāt kṛtituggrahaṇācca tugvidhau bahiraṅgaparibhāṣāyā apravṛtteḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Sannipāta</s> (conjunction) means the connection of two [elements]; a rule conditioned by that [conjunction] does not destroy that conjunction — it is not the cause [of its destruction]. The basis of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is the principle that conflict with that which is relied upon is improper. For this very reason, the word '<s>sannipāta</s>' here [refers] not only to the connection of prior and subsequent [elements], but also to the conjunction of qualified and qualifier. For this very reason, in '<s>grāmaṇikulam</s>' and the like, even with the neuter short-vowel [substitution], [the rule] '<s>piti kṛ</s>'...

children.text:
sarvavidhasannipātagrahaṇādeva 'varṇāśrayaḥ pratyayo varṇavicālasyānimittaṃ syāt' ityetatparibhāṣā
doṣanirūpaṇāvasare vārtikakṛtoktam, -- 'na hi pratyayaḥ pūrva para sannipāta nimittakaḥ, sa eva ca sannipāta śabdena gṛhyata iti matvā na pratyayaḥ sannipātanimittakaḥ iti śaṅkāyāṃ tadabhyupetyaivāṅgasaṃjñā tarhyanimittaṃ syādityekadeśinoktam' iti na tadbhāṣyavirodhaḥ/
kiñcaivaṃ 'śaivaḥ, gārgāyaḥ, vainateyaḥ' ityādāvapyaṅgasaṃjñāyā lopanimittatvānāpatyā varṇāśraya ityasya vaiyarthayam/
'grāmaṇi kulam' 'grāmaṇiputraḥ' ityādāvuttarapadanimittake hrasvatve yathākathañcid bahiraṅgaparibhāṣayāpi vāraṇaṃ sambhavatīti"kṛnmejantaḥ"ityatra"hrasvasya piti"iti sūtrecaikadeśinā tayā paribhāṣāyā tug
vārito bhāṣye/
ata eva paribhāṣāphalatvenedamuktam"kṛnmejantaḥ"iti sūtre vārtikakṛteti kecit/
sannipātalakṣaṇavidhitvamasyā liṅgam/ svapravṛtteḥ prāk svanimittabhūto yaḥ sannipātaḥ, tadvighātasya svātiriktaśāstrasya svayamanimittamiti phalati/
nanvevam 'rāmāya' ityādau"supi ca"iti dīrghānāpattiḥ, adantāṅgasannipātena jātasya yādeśasya tadvighātakatvāt/
na ca yañāditvasāpekṣadīrghasya bahiraṅgatayāsiddhatvānnātra sannipātavighāta iti vācyam, āropitāsiddhatve 'pi vastutastadvighātasya jāyamānatvenaitatpravṛtteḥ/
kiñcāntaraṅge kartavye bahiraṅgasyāsiddhatve 'pi tatra kṛte tasyāsiddhatve mānābhāḥ/
kiñcātideśikasannipātavighātābhāvamādāyaitadapravṛttau 'gauri' ityādau sambuddhilope 'pi sthānivatvena hrasvanimittasannipātavighātābhāvāt, tatraitasyātivyāptipara"kṛnmejantaḥ"iti sūtrasthabhāṣyāsaṅgatiḥ/
sannipātasyāśāstrīyatvānnātra sthānivatvamiti cet, tarhyatrāsiddhatvamapi kathamiti vibhāvya, 'aśāstrīye 'siddhatvāpravṛtteḥ'"īdūdet"iti sūtre kaiyaṭena spaṣṭamuktatvāt/
evañca pūrvatrāsiddhīye 'pi kārya etatparibhāṣāpravṛttirbhavatyeveti cet, na; 'kaṣṭāya' iti nirdeśenaitasyā anityatvāt/
yayoḥ sannipātasya vighātakaṃ śāstram, tayoḥ sannipātanimittakavidhāvupādānamapekṣitamiti tu nāgrahaḥ/ ata eva 'dākṣiḥ' ityatrākārāntaprakṛtīñsannipātanimittāṅgasaṃjñānayā paribhāṣayāllopasya nimittaṃ na syādityāśaṅkyānityatvena samāhitam,"kṛnmejantaḥ"iti sūtre bhāṣye; 'na hyaṅgasaṃjñāyāmadantasyāṅgasaṃjñā' ityuktamasti/
na ca 'kumbhakārebhyaḥ, ādhaye' ityādāvavyayasaṃjñāyā anayā paribhāṣayā vāraṇaparabhāṣyāsaṅga
tiḥ/ anayā paribhāṣayā lug mābhūt, avyayatvaṃ tu syādeva/ lukā hi tadīyasannipātasya vighātaḥ, nāvyayasaṃjñayā/ saṃjñāphalaṃ tvakac syāditi vācyam, etadudāharaṇaparabhāṣyaprāmāṇyena sākṣātparamparayā vā svanimittasannipātavighātakasya svayamanimityamityarthenādoṣāt/ etenātrākac syādityapāstam/
na ca kāryakālapakṣe lugekavākyatāpannasaṃjñābādhe 'pyakajekavākyatāpannāsyāditi vācyam, antaraṅgāyāṃ tadekavākyatāpannasaṃjñāyāṃ bahiraṅgaguṇāderasiddhatvāt, lugekavākyatāpannā tu na guṇādito 'ntaraṅgā, ubhayorapi śabdataḥ subāśrayatvāt/
"nayāsayoḥ"iti nirdeśāścaiṣānityā/ tena nātiprasaṅgaḥ/ spaṣṭā ceyaṃ"kṛnmejantaḥ"iti sūtre bhāṣye/ asyā anityatve phalāni bhāṣye parigaṇitāni - varṇāśrayaḥ, pratyayaḥ varṇavicālasyānimittam,
'dākṣiḥ'/ ātvaṃ pugvidheḥ - krāpayati/ pughrasvasya - adītapat/ tyadādyakāraṣṭābvidheḥ - yā seti/ iḍvidhirākāralopasya - papivān/"hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup" "antodāttāduttarapadāt"iti matubvibhaktyudāttatvaṃ pūrvanighātasya - agnimān, paramavācā/ nadīhrasvatvaṃ sambuddhilopasya - 'nadi, kumāri' ityādi/ yādeśo dīrghatvasya -
children.translated_text:
Because of the comprehension of all types of <s>sannipāta</s> (conjunction), the <s>paribhāṣā</s> 'a <s>pratyaya</s> (suffix) that is dependent on a <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme) should not be the cause of the displacement of that <s>varṇa</s>' — this was stated by the <s>Vārtikakāra</s> at the occasion of examining the fault: 'Since the <s>pratyaya</s> is not caused by the conjunction of preceding and following [elements], and since it is understood by the word <s>sannipāta</s> itself, therefore when the doubt arises that the <s>pratyaya</s> is not caused by <s>sannipāta</s>, accepting that very [position], the <s>aṅga</s>-designation would then be without cause — thus was stated by the <s>Ekadeśin</s>.' Therefore there is no contradiction with the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.
Moreover, in forms like '<s>Śaivaḥ</s>, <s>Gārgāyaḥ</s>, <s>Vainateyaḥ</s>' and so on, since the <s>aṅga</s>-designation is the cause of <s>lopa</s> (elision), not the patronymic [suffix], the [expression] '<s>varṇāśraya</s>' (phoneme-dependent) would become purposeless.
In [examples like] '<s>grāmaṇi kulam</s>' and '<s>grāmaṇiputraḥ</s>' and so on, where the shortening is caused by the subsequent member [of a compound], since prevention is somehow possible even through the <s>bahiraṅga-paribhāṣā</s> (rule of external operations), in [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>kṛnmejantaḥ</s>,' the <s>Ekadeśin</s> used that <s>paribhāṣā</s> to block <s>tuk</s>-augment in [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>hrasvasya piti</s>' in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.
For this very reason, some [scholars say] that this was stated in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>kṛnmejantaḥ</s>' by the <s>Vārtikakāra</s> as a result of the <s>paribhāṣā</s>.
The indication [for this <s>paribhāṣā</s>] is that it functions as a rule whose operation is characterized by <s>sannipāta</s>. The <s>sannipāta</s> that constitutes the basis of its own application prior [to the rule's operation] — the disruption of that [<s>sannipāta</s>] by a rule other than itself is not the cause of [the rule] itself. This is the result [of the <s>paribhāṣā</s>].
Objection: If so, in [forms like] '<s>Rāmāya</s>' and so on, the lengthening by [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>supi ca</s>' would fail to apply, because the <s>ya</s>-substitute produced by the conjunction of the <s>a</s>-ending <s>aṅga</s> would disrupt that [conjunction].
Nor can it be said that there is no disruption of <s>sannipāta</s> here because the lengthening, which depends on the <s>ya</s>-initial status, is <s>asiddha</s> (not yet established) due to being <s>bahiraṅga</s> (external); for even when there is attributed <s>asiddhatva</s>, since in reality the disruption [of the conjunction] does occur, this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] would apply.
Moreover, even when the <s>bahiraṅga</s> [operation] is <s>asiddha</s> while the <s>antaraṅga</s> (internal operation) is to be performed, once the latter is performed, there is no valid means of proof for the <s>asiddhatva</s> of the former.
Furthermore, if this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] does not apply by accepting that there is no disruption of conjunction through <s>atideśa</s> (extension), then even in [forms like] '<s>Gauri</s>' and so on, in the <s>sambuddhi</s>-elision also, since by <s>sthānivattva</s> (the substitute being treated as the original) there is no disruption of the conjunction that causes shortening, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>kṛnmejantaḥ</s>' — which addresses the over-application of this [rule] in that case — would be inconsistent.
If it be said that <s>sthānivattva</s> does not apply here because the <s>sannipāta</s> is non-grammatical (<s>aśāstrīya</s>), then how can <s>asiddhatva</s> apply here either? This should be considered, since <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> has clearly stated in [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>īdūdet</s>' that '<s>asiddhatva</s> does not apply to what is non-grammatical.'
And if it be said that even in the domain of <s>pūrvatrāsiddha</s> (what is not yet established with respect to the preceding), this <s>paribhāṣā</s> does apply — no; because of its occasional nature (<s>anityatva</s>), as indicated by the designation '<s>kaṣṭāya</s>.'
That the rule which disrupts the <s>sannipāta</s> of two [elements] requires the specification [of those elements] in the injunction that is caused by the <s>sannipāta</s> — this is not a [valid] objection. For this very reason, in [the form] '<s>Dākṣiḥ</s>,' having raised the doubt that the <s>l-lopa</s> (elision of <s>l</s>) would not be caused [since] the <s>aṅga</s>-designation based on the <s>ā</s>-ending stem is caused by <s>sannipāta</s> [and would be blocked] by this <s>paribhāṣā</s>, this was resolved through occasional application (<s>anityatva</s>) in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>kṛnmejantaḥ</s>'; it is not stated [in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>] that 'in the <s>aṅga</s>-designation, that which ends in <s>a</s> does not receive the <s>aṅga</s>-designation.'
Nor is there inconsistency with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> that uses this <s>paribhāṣā</s> to block [something] in [forms like] '<s>kumbhakārebhyaḥ</s>, <s>ādhaye</s>' and so on regarding the <s>avyaya</s>-designation (indeclinable designation). By this <s>paribhāṣā</s>, let <s>luk</s>-elision not occur, but the <s>avyaya</s>-status would still obtain. For the disruption of the conjunction in question is by <s>luk</s>, not by the <s>avyaya</s>-designation. However, it should be said that the result of the designation — namely <s>akac</s> — would [also not] apply. [But] by the authority of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> pertaining to this example, through the meaning that what directly or indirectly disrupts the conjunction that is its own cause is not the cause of [the rule] itself, there is no fault. By this, the [objection] that <s>akac</s> would apply here is also set aside.
Nor should it be said that in the <s>kāryakālapakṣa</s> (the view that operations apply at the time of the effect), even though the designation subsumed under the single-statement of <s>luk</s> is overridden, [the designation] subsumed under the single-statement of <s>akac</s> would still apply — because the designation subsumed under the single-statement of the <s>antaraṅga</s> [rule] renders the <s>bahiraṅga</s> <s>guṇa</s>-substitute and the like <s>asiddha</s>; whereas the [designation] subsumed under the single-statement of <s>luk</s> is not more <s>antaraṅga</s> than <s>guṇa</s>-substitute etc., since both are equally dependent on <s>sub</s> (nominal endings) in their literal form.
This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is occasional, as indicated by the designation '<s>nayāsayoḥ</s>.' Therefore there is no over-extension. And this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>kṛnmejantaḥ</s>.' The results of its occasional application are enumerated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>: <s>varṇāśraya</s>; the <s>pratyaya</s> is not the cause of <s>varṇa</s>-displacement;
'<s>Dākṣiḥ</s>'; the <s>ā</s>-substitution of the <s>puk</s>-augment rule — <s>krāpayati</s>; the shortening of <s>puk</s> — <s>adītapat</s>; the <s>ṣṭāb</s>-suffix rule for <s>tyad</s>-initial <s>a</s>-sounds — '<s>yā sā</s>' and so on; the <s>iṭ</s>-augment rule [not causing] <s>ā</s>-elision — <s>papivān</s>; the <s>matup</s>-suffix [rule] '<s>hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup</s>' and the <s>udātta</s>-accent of the <s>vibhakti</s> (case-ending) from [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>antodāttād uttarapadāt</s>' [not being blocked by] the prior <s>nighāta</s> (accent-depression) — <s>Agnimān</s>, <s>Paramavācā</s>; the shortening in <s>nadī</s>-stems [not being blocked by] <s>sambuddhi</s>-elision — '<s>Nadi</s>, <s>Kumāri</s>' and so on; the <s>ya</s>-substitute [not being blocked by] lengthening —

children.text: kaṣṭāya/ ito 'nyatra pravṛttireva, 'doṣāḥ khalvapi sākalyena parigaṇtāḥ' iti bhāṣyokteranyatravistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: '<s>kaṣṭāya</s>.' In cases other than these, [the <s>paribhāṣā</s>] does apply, because the <s>Bhāṣya</s> states 'the faults have indeed been enumerated in their entirety by <s>Sākalya</s>.' The elaboration of other [cases] is [discussed] elsewhere.

children.text: nanu 'pañcendrāṇyo devatā asya pañcendraḥ' ityādau"dvigorluk"ityaṇo luki"lukstaddhita" iti strīpratyayalukyānukaḥ śravaṇāpattiḥ, ata āha -
children.translated_text: Objection: In [forms like] '<s>Pañcendrāṇyaḥ</s>' — '[she] whose deity is the five <s>Indras</s>, [she is] <s>Pañcendraḥ</s>' — and so on, when <s>aṇ</s> undergoes <s>luk</s>-elision by [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>dvigor luk</s>,' the undesirable consequence would arise that the <s>ānuk</s> (augment) would be heard [in the surface form] due to [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>luk taddhita</s>' [causing] the <s>luk</s>-elision of the feminine suffix. Therefore he states —

children.text: sanniyogaśiṣṭānāmanyatarāpāya ubhayorapyapāyaḥ || 86 ||
children.translated_text: When one of two elements that are taught together [in a <s>sanniyoga</s> (conjunction)] is removed, both are removed. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 86)

children.text:
atra ca"bilvakādibhyaśchasya luk"iti sūtrasthaṃ chagrahaṇaṃ jñāpakam/ taddhi chamātrasya lugbodhana dvārā kuko 'nivṛttiryathā syādityartham/ kṛta kugāgamānaḍādyantargatā bilvādaya eva tatra nirdiṣṭā bilvakādiśabdena/
nacaivamapi chagrahaṇaṃ vyartham, kṛta kugāgamānuvādasāmarthyādeva tadanivṛttisiddheḥ, anyathā"bilvādibhyaḥ"ityeva vadet/ lakṣaṇapratipadoktaparibhāṣayā bilvādipuraskāreṇa vihitapratyayasyaiva lugvidhānānnātiprasaṅga iti vācyam, tato 'pi pratipadoktatvena"bilvādibhyoṇ"iti vikārādyarthasya lugāpattivāraṇārthaṃ kuganuvādacāritārthyāt/ samuccayārthakacaśabdayoge tu vidheyayorekakālikatvaikadeśatvaniyamānnyāyasiddhapīyam/
yattu"ṇāviṣṭavat"ityanena puṃvatvavidhānametadanityatvajñāpanārtham/ anyathā 'etayati' ityādau
ṭilopenaiva ṅīpi nivṛtte 'sanniyogaśiṣṭa' paribhāṣayā tasyāpi nivṛtyā 'etayati' ityādisiddhau puṃvatvavaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameveti"ṭeḥ"iti sūtre kaiyaṭaḥ, tat, na; 'iḍabiḍamācaṣṭa aiḍabiḍayati' ityādau puṃvatvasyāvaśyakatvāt/ 'aineyaḥ śyaineyaḥ' ityādi tu sthānivatvena siddhamityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text:
And here, the mention of <s>cha</s> in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>bilvakādibhyaś chasya luk</s>' serves as an indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>). For that [mention] is intended so that by conveying <s>luk</s>-elision of <s>cha</s> alone, the non-removal of <s>kuk</s>-augment would follow. The <s>Bilvādi</s> [words] that are included within [the scope of] <s>aṇ</s> and other [suffixes], having received the <s>kuk</s>-augment, are designated there by the word '<s>bilvakādi</s>.'
Nor is the mention of <s>cha</s> purposeless even so, since the non-removal [of <s>kuk</s>] is already established merely by the force of the mention of <s>kuk</s>-augment [being implied]; otherwise one would simply say '<s>bilvādibhyaḥ</s>.' [It cannot be said that] by the <s>paribhāṣā</s> of '<s>lakṣaṇapratipadokta</s>' (specifically taught [forms] override general rules), since <s>luk</s>-elision is ordained only for the <s>pratyaya</s> prescribed in conjunction with the <s>Bilvādi</s> [words], there would be no over-extension — [this cannot be said] because even from that [perspective], since [<s>cha</s>] is <s>pratipadokta</s> (specifically taught), the <s>luk</s>-elision of [suffixes] like <s>ṇ</s> in the sense of <s>vikāra</s> (modification) etc. with '<s>bilvādibhyo ṇ</s>' would [undesirably] follow, and [so] the mention of <s>kuk</s>-augment serves its purpose in preventing that. However, when there is conjunction with the <s>ca</s>-particle having the sense of aggregation, since there is a rule-based restriction of simultaneity and partial identity of the two things to be enjoined, this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is also established by convention.
As for what <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> [says] in [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>ṭeḥ</s>' — that the ordaining of <s>puṃvattva</s> (masculine-form treatment) by [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>ṇāviṣṭavat</s>' serves to indicate the occasional nature (<s>anityatva</s>) of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]; otherwise, in [forms like] '<s>etayati</s>' and so on, since <s>ṅīp</s> would already be prevented by the elision of <s>ṭi</s> alone, and by the '<s>sanniyogaśiṣṭa</s>' <s>paribhāṣā</s> that [<s>ṅīp</s>] too would be removed, thus achieving '<s>etayati</s>' and so on, the purposelessness of <s>puṃvattva</s> would be evident — that is not [correct]; because <s>puṃvattva</s> is necessarily required in [forms like] '<s>iḍabiḍam ācaṣṭa — aiḍabiḍayati</s>' and so on. And [forms like] '<s>Aineyaḥ</s>, <s>Śyaineyaḥ</s>' and so on are established through <s>sthānivattva</s> (the substitute being treated as the original) — the elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text:
nanu 'curā śīlamasyāḥ sā caurī'ityādau śīlam"chatrādibhyo ṇaḥ"iti ṇe ṅīp na prāpnotītyata
āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In [derivations like] '<s>curā śīlam asyāḥ sā Caurī</s>' (she whose nature is thieving, she is <s>Caurī</s>) and so on, when <s>ṇa</s> [is applied] by [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>chatrādibhyo ṇaḥ</s>,' the feminine suffix <s>ṅīp</s> would fail to apply in the sense of habitual disposition (<s>śīla</s>). Therefore he states —

children.text: tācchīlike ṇe 'ṇkṛtāni bhavanti || 87 ||
children.translated_text: In the case of <s>ṇa</s>-suffix denoting habitual disposition (<s>tācchīlya</s>), [the derivatives] behave like <s>kṛt</s>-formations. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 87)

children.text:
"an"ityaṇi vihitaprakṛtibhāvabādhanārtham"kārmastācchīlye"iti nipātanamasyā jñāpakam/
tācchīlikaṇāntāt"aṇodvyacaḥ"iti phiñsiddhirapyasyāḥ prayojanamiti navyāḥ/ tācchīlika ityukteḥ"tadasyāṃ
praharaṇam"iti ṇe 'dāṇḍā' ityeva/"kārmaḥ"iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭā//
children.translated_text:
The <s>nipātana</s> (irregular listing) '<s>kārmas tācchīlye</s>' — which serves to override the <s>prakṛtibhāva</s> (retention of base form) ordained in [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>an</s>' for the <s>aṇ</s> [suffix] — is the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) for this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>].
The later grammarians [say] that the derivation of <s>phiñ</s> by [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>aṇo dvyacaḥ</s>' from a <s>tācchīlika</s> (habitual-disposition) <s>ṇa</s>-ending [stem] is also a purpose of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. Because [the <s>paribhāṣā</s>] says '<s>tācchīlika</s>,' in [the application of] <s>ṇa</s> by [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>tad asyāṃ praharaṇam</s>,' the result is simply '<s>dāṇḍā</s>.' This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>kārmaḥ</s>.'

children.text: nanu"kasaparimṛḍbhyām"ityādau"mṛjervṛddhiḥ"durivārā, ityata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>kasaparimṛḍbhyām</s>' and so on, the <s>vṛddhi</s> [prescribed by] '<s>mṛjer vṛddhiḥ</s>' is difficult to prevent. Therefore he states —

children.text: dhātoḥ kāryamucyamānaṃ tatpratyaye bhavati || 88 ||
children.translated_text: An operation stated with reference to a <s>dhātu</s> (verbal root) takes effect [only] when the <s>pratyaya</s> (suffix) pertaining to that [<s>dhātu</s>] is present. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 88)

children.text:
bhrauṇahatye tatvanipātanamasyā jñāpakam/
'dhātoḥ svarūpagrahaṇe tatpratyaye kāryavijñānam' iti pāṭhastu 'prasṛḍbhiḥ' ityādau"anudāttasya cardupadhasya"ityāmāpādanena bhāṣye dūṣitaḥ/
yatkāryaṃ pratyayanimittaṃ tatreyaṃ vyavasthāpikā/ tena padāntatvanibandhanam"naśervā"iti kutvam 'praṇagbhyām' ityādau bhavatyeva/ iyaṅādividhau tu naiṣā,"na bhūsudhiyoḥ"iti niṣedhenānityatvāt/ "mṛjervṛddhiḥ"ityatra bhāṣye spaṣṭā//
children.translated_text:
The <s>nipātana</s> (irregular listing) of the <s>tatva</s> (retroflex <s>t</s>) in [the form] '<s>bhrauṇahatya</s>' is the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) for this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>].
However, the alternative reading '<s>dhātoḥ svarūpagrahaṇe tatpratyaye kāryavijñānam</s>' (when there is mention of the root's own form, the operation is understood as applying in the presence of its suffix) has been refuted in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> by demonstrating [its inadequacy] in [forms like] '<s>prasṛḍbhiḥ</s>' and so on through [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>anudāttasya car dupadhasya</s>.'
This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is a delimiting rule (<s>vyavasthāpikā</s>) for operations that are caused by a <s>pratyaya</s>. Therefore, the <s>ku</s>-substitution [prescribed by] '<s>naśer vā</s>,' which is contingent on word-finality (<s>padāntatva</s>), does apply in [forms like] '<s>praṇagbhyām</s>' and so on. But this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] does not apply in the domain of <s>iyaṅ</s>-substitute and similar rules, because of its occasional nature (<s>anityatva</s>) as indicated by the prohibition '<s>na bhūsudhiyoḥ</s>.' This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>mṛjer vṛddhiḥ</s>.'

children.text: nanu 'sarvake, iccakaiḥ' ityādau sarvanāvyayasaṃjñe na syātām, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In [forms like] '<s>sarvake</s>, <s>iccakaiḥ</s>' and so on, the <s>sarvanāman</s> (pronominal) and <s>avyaya</s> (indeclinable) designations would fail to apply. Therefore he states —

children.text: tanmadhyapatitastadgrahaṇena gṛhyate || 89 ||
children.translated_text: That which has fallen within the middle of [an expression denoted by] a [particular] term is comprehended by that term. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 89)

children.text: "nedamadasorakoḥ"iti sūtre 'akoḥ' iti niṣedho 'syā jñāpakaḥ/ 'tadekadeśabhūtaṃ tadgrahaṇena gṛhyate' iti"yena vidhiḥ"iti sūtre bhāṣye pāṭhaḥ//
children.translated_text: The prohibition '<s>akoḥ</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ned amad asor akoḥ</s>' is the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) for this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. The reading [of this <s>paribhāṣā</s>] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>yena vidhiḥ</s>' is: 'that which has become a part of [an expression denoted by a] term is comprehended by that term.'

children.text: nanu"gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ"iti sico luk 'apāsīta' ityādau pāterapi syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: The <s>luk</s>-elision of <s>sic</s> by [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ</s>' would also apply to [the root] <s>pā</s> in [forms like] '<s>apāsīta</s>' and so on. Therefore he states —

children.text: lugvikaraṇālugvikaraṇayoralugvikaraṇasya || 90 ||
children.translated_text: Between [a form with] <s>luk</s>-elision of the <s>vikaraṇa</s> (class-affix) and [a form with] non-<s>luk</s>-elision of the <s>vikaraṇa</s>, [the rule applies to] the one with non-<s>luk</s>-elision of the <s>vikaraṇa</s>. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 90)

children.text: asyāñca jñāpakaḥ"svarati sūti"iti sūtre sūṅiti vaktavye sūtisūyatyoḥ pṛthaṅnirdeśa iti
children.translated_text: And the indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is the separate mention of '<s>sūti</s>' and '<s>sūyati</s>' in the sūtra '<s>svarati sūti</s>,' where '<s>sūṅ</s>' alone could have been said — so states

children.text:
kaiyaṭaḥ/ tanna, sāhacaryādalugvikaraṇasyaiva grahaṇe prāpte pṛthaṅnirdeśasya tajjñāpakatvāsambhavāt/
dhvanitā ceyaṃ paribhāṣā"yasya vibhāṣā"ityatra bhāṣye/ tatra hi 'viditaḥ' iti prayoge niṣedhamāśaṅkya 'yadupādervibhāṣā, tadupāderniṣedhaḥ"vibhāṣā gamahanavidaviśām"iti sūtre 'śavikaraṇasya gpahaṇaṃ lugvikaraṇaścāyam' ityuktam/ tatra co hetau, yato 'yaṃlugvikaraṇaḥ, ato viśisāhacaryācchavikaraṇasya grahaṇam, na tu hanisāhacaryādasyāpi, etatparibhāṣāvirodhāditi tadāśayaḥ/
ata eva paribhāṣāyāṃ lugvikaraṇasyaiveti noktam/ kaṇṭhatastu bhāṣye eṣā kvāpi na paṭhitā/ 'gātisthā' iti sūtre 'pibatergrahaṇam kartavyam' iti vārtikakṛtā 'sarvatraiva pāgrahaṇe 'lugvikaraṇasya gpahaṇam' iti bhāṣyakṛtā coktam/ "svarati sūti"iti sūtre kaiyaṭena ca spaṣṭamuktā//
children.translated_text: <s>Kaiyaṭa</s>. That is not so, since when the reference to the non-<s>luk-vikaraṇa</s> form alone is already obtainable through co-occurrence, the separate mention cannot serve as an indicator of that. This <s>paribhāṣā</s> is also implied in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>yasya vibhāṣā</s>.' There, having raised the doubt that there would be prohibition in the usage '<s>viditaḥ</s>,' [the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> says]: 'For whichever root the option applies, for that root the prohibition applies' — in the sūtra '<s>vibhāṣā gamahanavidaviśām</s>,' it is stated that 'the reference is to the <s>śa-vikaraṇa</s> [form], and this is a <s>luk-vikaraṇa</s> [form].' The '<s>ca</s>' there is used in the causal sense: since this is a <s>luk-vikaraṇa</s> form, the reference is to the <s>śa-vikaraṇa</s> form due to co-occurrence with '<s>viś</s>,' but not due to co-occurrence with '<s>han</s>' for this [form] as well — the intent being that this would contradict this <s>paribhāṣā</s>. For this very reason, the <s>paribhāṣā</s> does not say 'only of the <s>luk-vikaraṇa</s> [form].' Explicitly, however, this is not read anywhere in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. In the sūtra '<s>gātisthā</s>,' the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> states 'the reference to <s>pā</s> must be made,' and the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> says 'in every reference to <s>pā</s>, the <s>luk-vikaraṇa</s> form is referenced.' And by <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on the sūtra '<s>svarati sūti</s>' this is clearly stated.

children.text: nanu 'prajighāyayiṣati' ityādau"heracaṅi"iti vidhīyamānaṃ kutvaṃ na syāt ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In forms like '<s>prajighāyayiṣati</s>' and the like, the <s>kutva</s> (guttural replacement) prescribed by '<s>her acaṅi</s>' would not apply. Therefore he states:

children.text: prakṛtigrahaṇe ṇyadhikasyāpi grahaṇam || 91 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 91: When the base form (<s>prakṛti</s>) is referenced, [forms] with additional <s>ṇyat</s> etc. are also included.

children.text:
acaṅīti pratiṣedha evāsyā jñāpakaḥ/ iyaṃ ca kutva viṣayaiva/"heracaṅi"iti sūtre bhāṣye
spaṣṭeyam//
children.translated_text: The prohibition '<s>acaṅi</s>' (not before <s>caṅ</s>) is itself the indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. And this pertains only to the domain of <s>kutva</s>. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>her acaṅi</s>.'

children.text: nanu 'yuṣmabhyam' ityādau 'bhyasaḥ' ityatra bhyamiti cchede bhyaso bhyami kṛte 'ntyalope etvaṃ syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In forms like '<s>yuṣmabhyam</s>' and the like, in [the sūtra] '<s>bhyasaḥ</s>,' if the analysis is '<s>bhyam</s>,' and when '<s>bhyas</s>' is replaced by '<s>bhyam</s>' and the final is elided, <s>e-tva</s> (substitution of '<s>e</s>') would apply. Therefore he states:

children.text: aṅga vṛtte punarvṛttāvavidhiḥ || 92 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 92: When an operation on a stem has been performed, there is no [repeated] application upon a subsequent stem-operation.

children.text:
aṅge 'ṅgādhikāre vṛttamuniṣpannaṃ yatkāryam, tasmin sati punaranyasyāṅgakāryasya vṛttau pravṛttāvavidhānaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ/
eṣā ca"jyādādīyasaḥ"ityādvidhānena jñāpitā/ anyathekāralopena"akṛsārva"iti dīrgheṇa ca siddhe tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameva/ ata eva"jñājanorjā" "jyādādīyasaḥ"iti sūtrayorenāṃ jñāpayitvā kiṃ prayojanamiti praśne pibaterguṇapratiṣedha uktaḥ, sa na vaktavyaḥ, ityeva prayojanamuktam, na tu lakṣyasiddhirūpam/ taduktam"bhyaso bhyam"ityatra 'abhyam' iti cchedaḥ,"śeṣe lopaḥ"cāntyalopa eva"ato guṇe"iti pararūpeṇa siddham 'yuṣmabhyam' ityanyatra nirūpitam/
evañca sūtradvayasthametajjñāpanaparaṃ bhāṣyam"bhyaso bhyam"iti sūtrasthaṃ ca bhāṣyamekadeśyuktirityāhuḥ//
children.translated_text: The meaning is: when an operation on the stem has been performed and completed within the stem-domain, upon the subsequent application of another stem-operation, there is no re-application [of the first]. This is indicated by the prescription in '<s>jyād ād īyasaḥ</s>' etc. Otherwise, since the result would be established by <s>i</s>-elision and by the lengthening from '<s>akṛtsārva</s>,' its purposelessness would be quite evident. For this very reason, in the sūtras '<s>jñā janor jā</s>' and '<s>jyād ād īyasaḥ</s>,' when asked what purpose is served by indicating these [<s>paribhāṣās</s>], the prohibition of <s>guṇa</s> for [the root] '<s>pā</s>' (to drink) is cited — [the answer being] 'that need not be stated' — this alone is stated as the purpose, not the establishment of attested forms. As stated [elsewhere]: in '<s>bhyaso bhyam</s>,' the analysis is '<s>abhyam</s>,' and the final elision by '<s>śeṣe lopaḥ</s>' is accounted for by <s>pararūpa</s> (subsequent-form substitution) through '<s>ato guṇe</s>' — '<s>yuṣmabhyam</s>' is established; this is demonstrated elsewhere. Thus, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage on the two sūtras that serves to indicate this, and the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>bhyaso bhyam</s>,' are [each] partial reasonings, they say.

children.text: yattu 'orot' iti vācye"orguṇaḥ"iti guṇagrahaṇāt --
children.translated_text: As for the argument that where '<s>or ot</s>' could have been said, the reference to <s>guṇa</s> in '<s>or guṇaḥ</s>' [indicates] —

children.text: saṃjñāpūrvakavidheranityatvam || 93 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 93: A rule preceded by a technical designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>) is non-eternal.

children.text: idañca vidheyakoṭau saṃjñāpūrvakatva eva/ 'tena svāyambhuvam' ityādi siddham//
children.translated_text: And this [non-eternality] applies only when the technical designation is on the side of the prescribed element. [Hence] forms like '<s>tena svāyambhuvam</s>' are established.

children.text: tathā niloḍityeva siddhe ānigrahaṇāt --
children.translated_text: Similarly, since [the form] would be established simply as '<s>niloḍ</s>,' [but] because of the reference to '<s>āni</s>' —

children.text: āgamaśāstramanityam || 94 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 94: The teaching of augments (<s>āgama-śāstra</s>) is non-eternal.

children.text: tena sāgaraṃ tarttukāmasyetyādi siddham//
children.translated_text: Through this, forms like '<s>sāgaraṃ tarttukāmasya</s>' etc. are established.

children.text: tathā tanādipāṭhādeva siddhe"tanādikṛñbhyaḥ"iti sūtre kṛñ grahaṇāt --
children.translated_text: Similarly, since [the form] would be established simply by the listing in the <s>tanādi</s> class, [but] because of the reference to '<s>kṛñ</s>' in the sūtra '<s>tanādikṛñbhyaḥ</s>' —

children.text: gaṇakāryamanityam || 95 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 95: Class-based operations (<s>gaṇa-kārya</s>) are non-eternal.

children.text: tena 'na viśvasedaviśvastam' ityādi siddham//
children.translated_text: Through this, forms like '<s>na viśvased aviśvastam</s>' etc. are established.

children.text: tathā cakṣiṅo ṅitkaraṇāt --
children.translated_text: Similarly, from the <s>ṅit</s>-marking of '<s>cakṣiṅ</s>' —

children.text: anudāttettvalakṣaṇamātmanepadamanityam || 96 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 96: <s>Ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) prescribed on the basis of <s>anudāttet</s> (having an <s>anudātta</s> marker) status is non-eternal.

children.text: tena 'sphāyannirmokaḥ' ityādi siddham//
children.translated_text: Through this, forms like '<s>sphāyan nirmokaḥ</s>' etc. are established.

children.text: tathā vinārtha nañā samāsena"anudāttam padamanekam"ityeva siddhe varjagrahaṇāt --
children.translated_text: Similarly, since [the result] would be established by compound with the negative particle '<s>nañ</s>' having the sense of exclusion through '<s>anudāttaṃ padam anekam</s>' alone, [but] because of the reference to '<s>varja</s>' (exclusion) —

children.text: nañghaṭitamanityam || 97 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 97: [Rules about forms] constructed with '<s>nañ</s>' (negative particle) are non-eternal.

children.text:
tena"neyaṅuvaṅ"ityasyānityatvāt 'he subhru' iti siddhamiti, tat, na; bhāṣye 'darśanāt, bhāṣyānuktajñāpitārthasya sādhutāniyāmakatve mānābhāvāt, bhāṣyāvicāritaprayojanānāṃ sautrākṣarāṇāṃ pārāyaṇādāvadṛṣṭamātrārthakatvakalpanāyā evaucityāt/
kiñca jñāpite 'pyānītyasya na sārthakyam, āḍāgamaśūnyaprayogasyāprasiddheḥ/
āḍgrahaṇaṃ tu loḍgrahaṇavaditi bodhyam/ ata eva"ghorlopo liṭi vā"it sūtre veti pratyākhyātam/ lope 'pyāṭpakṣe āṭaḥ śravaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati -- 'dadhāt' iti, aṭi 'dadhat' iti/ āgamaśāstrasyānityatve tvāṭyasati 'dadhāt' ityasiddhyā vāgrahaṇasyāvaśyakatvena tatpratyākhyānāsaṅgatiḥ spaṣṭaiva/
etena yatkaiyaṭena kecidityādināsyaiva vāgrahaṇasya tadanityatvatrāpakatoktā, sāpi cintyā,pratyākhyānaparabhāṣyavirodhāt, tanādi sūtre kṛñgrahaṇasya bhāṣye pratyākhyānācca/ cakṣiṅo ṅakārasyānteditvābhāvasampādanena cāritārthyācca//
children.translated_text: If by the non-eternality of '<s>ne yaṅ uvaṅ</s>,' the form '<s>he subhru</s>' is said to be established — that is not so; because it is seen in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [to be otherwise], and because there is no valid means of knowledge for an indicated meaning not stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> to determine correctness, and because for sūtra-letters whose purpose is not discussed in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, the supposition that they serve only some unseen purpose in ritual recitation is more appropriate. Furthermore, even if [this non-eternality] is indicated, the '<s>ānī</s>' [in the sūtra] would have no purpose, since a usage devoid of the '<s>āṭ</s>' augment is not attested. The '<s>āṭ</s>'-reference should be understood as similar to the '<s>loṭ</s>'-reference. For this very reason, in the sūtra '<s>ghor lopo liṭi vā</s>,' the '<s>vā</s>' (optionality) is rejected. Even in the <s>lopa</s>-option, in the <s>āṭ</s>-sub-option the <s>āṭ</s> will be heard — as in '<s>dadhāt</s>'; in the <s>aṭ</s>-[sub-option], '<s>dadhat</s>.' But if the <s>āgama-śāstra</s> is non-eternal and <s>āṭ</s> is absent, since '<s>dadhāt</s>' would not be derivable, the necessity of '<s>vā</s>' and the inconsistency of its rejection is quite evident. By this, what <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> states through '<s>kecit</s>' etc. — that even this '<s>vā</s>'-reference serves as an indicator of that non-eternality — that too is questionable, due to contradiction with the <s>Bhāṣya</s> which rejects [the '<s>vā</s>'], and due to the rejection of the '<s>kṛñ</s>'-reference in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>tanādi</s> sūtra, and because the '<s>ṅ</s>'-marking of '<s>cakṣiṅ</s>' serves its purpose by ensuring the absence of <s>anteditva</s> (final <s>it</s> status).

children.text: evameva --
children.translated_text: Similarly —

children.text: ātideśikamanityam || 98 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 98: [Rules involving] analogical extension (<s>atideśa</s>) are non-eternal.

children.text: sarvavidhibhyo lopavidhiriḍvidhiśca balavān || 99 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 99: The rule of elision and the rule of <s>iṭ</s>-augment are more powerful than all other rules.

children.text: ityādi bhāṣyānuktaṃ bodhyam/ 'svāyamabhuvam' ityādi loke 'sādhveva, ityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: These and other [<s>paribhāṣās</s>] not stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> should be understood [accordingly]. Forms like '<s>svāyambhuvam</s>' etc. are indeed correct in common usage. The elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text: yadapi -- nanu hanterayaṅlukyāśīrliṅi vadhādeśo na syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Also — objection: for [the root] '<s>han</s>,' in the <s>yaṅ-luk</s> (intensive without affix) [form] in <s>āśīrliṅ</s> (benedictive mood), the '<s>vadha</s>'-substitute would not apply. Therefore he states:

children.text: prakṛtigrahaṇe yaṅlugantasyāpi grahaṇam || 100 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 100: When the base form (<s>prakṛti</s>) is referenced, [forms] ending in the <s>yaṅ-luk</s> (frequentative without affix) are also included.

children.text:
ṣāṣṭadvitvasya dviḥprayogasiddhāntena prayogadvayarūpe samudāye prakṛtirūpatvabodhanenedaṃ nyāyasiddham/
ata eva juhudhītyadau dvitve kṛte dhitvasiddhiriti/ tadapi na, bhāṣye 'darśanāt/ kiñca tena siddhantena pratyekaṃ dvayostatvabodhane 'pi samudāyasya tatvabodhane mānābhāvaḥ/
ata eva"dayaderdigi"iti sūtre 'steḥ paratvād dvitve kṛte parasyāsterbhūbhāve pūrvasya śravaṇaṃ prāpnotītyāśaṅkya viṣayasapmyāśrayaṇena parihṛtaṃ bhāṣye/
anyathā tvaduktarītyā 'ekājdvirvacana' nyāyena samudāyasyaivādeśāpattau tadasaṅgatiḥ spaṣṭaiva/
tasmāduttarakhaṇḍamādāyaiva yathāyogaṃ tattatkāryapravṛttirbodhyā/
"bhūsuvoḥ"ityasya tadantāṅgasyetyarthāt prāptasya guṇaniṣedhasya bobhūtviti niyama iti na tadvirodhaḥ/ tasmāddhanteryaṅluki 'vadhyāt' ityādi mādhavādyudāhṛtaṃ cintyamevetyanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: This is established by principle through the <s>ṣāṣṭha-dvitva</s> (genitive-reduplication) doctrine: since in the aggregate consisting of two usages, the understanding of the base-form nature [includes the aggregate]. Hence in forms like '<s>juhudhī</s>' etc., when reduplication has been applied, the <s>dhi</s> form is established. But even that is not so, because it is seen [otherwise] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. Moreover, even if that doctrine conveys the nature of each of the two individually, there is no valid means for conveying the nature of the aggregate. Hence in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>dayed er digi</s>,' having raised the doubt that when reduplication is applied by the <s>paratva</s> (later-rule priority) of '<s>steḥ</s>,' the later '<s>ster</s>' becoming '<s>bhū</s>' would result in the hearing of the earlier [portion] — this is resolved in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> by resorting to domain-equality. Otherwise, by the method you propose, since by the '<s>ekāj dvirvacana</s>' principle only the aggregate would undergo substitution, the inconsistency with that [<s>Bhāṣya</s> passage] is quite evident. Therefore it should be understood that operations apply to the respective latter portions as appropriate. The prohibition of <s>guṇa</s> that is applicable to the stem ending in [the form from] '<s>bhūsuvoḥ</s>' is restricted to '<s>bobhūtva</s>' — hence there is no contradiction. Therefore, examples like '<s>vadhyāt</s>' cited by <s>Mādhava</s> and others for [the root] '<s>han</s>' in <s>yaṅ-luk</s> are indeed questionable — the elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text: yadapi nanu"vṛddhiryasyācāmādiḥ"ityatrekparibhāṣopasthitau śālīyādyasiddhiḥ, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Also — objection: in '<s>vṛddhir yasyācām ādiḥ</s>,' when the <s>eka-paribhāṣā</s> (single-element principle) is applicable, the derivation of '<s>śālīya</s>' etc. would fail. Therefore he states:

children.text: vidhau paribhāṣopatiṣṭate nānuvāde || 101 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 101: A <s>paribhāṣā</s> (interpretive principle) is applicable in a prescriptive rule (<s>vidhi</s>), not in a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>).

children.text:
anūdyamāna viśeṣaṇeṣu tanniyāmikā paribhāṣā nopatiṣṭata ati tadarthaḥ/
vidhyaṅgabhūtānāṃ paribhāṣāṇāṃ vidheyenāsiddhatayā sambandhāsambhave 'pi tadviśeṣeṇavyavasthāpakatvena
caritārthānāṃ tadviśeṣeṇavyavasthāpakatve mānābhāva iti tarkamūleyam/
kiñca"udīcāmātaḥ sthāne"iti sūtre sthāne grahaṇamasyā liṅgam/ anyathā"ṣaṣṭī sthāne"
iti paribhāṣayaiva tallābhe tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameveti, tat, na;"udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ"ityādau"ṣyaṅaḥ samprasāraṇam"iti sūtrabhāṣyoktarītyā"allopo 'naḥ"ityādau caitasyā vyabhicaritatvāt, bhāṣyānuktatvācca/ sthāna sambandho na
children.translated_text: The meaning is: a <s>paribhāṣā</s> that governs [the interpretation of] qualifiers does not apply to qualifiers that are being restated. The reasoning behind this is: although the <s>paribhāṣās</s> that are auxiliary to prescriptive rules cannot be related to [the rule] since the prescribed element is not [yet] established, [these <s>paribhāṣās</s>] serve their purpose by determining [the scope through] the qualifiers of that [prescribed element]; and there is no valid means for their determining [the scope] through qualifiers of the restated [element]. Moreover, the reference to '<s>sthāne</s>' in the sūtra '<s>udīcām ātaḥ sthāne</s>' is the indicator of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>]. Otherwise, since that [result] would be obtainable through the <s>paribhāṣā</s> '<s>ṣaṣṭhī sthāne yogā</s>' alone, its purposelessness would be quite evident — but that is not so; because in '<s>udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ</s>' etc., by the method stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>ṣyaṅaḥ samprasāraṇam</s>' and in '<s>al-lopo 'naḥ</s>' etc., this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is shown to be inconsistent, and because it is not stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. The [genitive] relationship with the substitution-locus is not

children.text:
paribhāṣālabhya ityarthasya"ṣaṣṭī sthāne"iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭamuktatvena tvaduktajñapakāvambhavācca/ tatra sthānegrahaṇaṃ tu spaṣṭārthameva/
kiñca"vidhauparibhāṣā"iti pravādaḥ"ikoguṇavṛddhī""acaśca"ityanayorvidhīyata ityadhyāhāramūlakaḥ, anyatra tu nāsyā phalamityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: obtainable through a <s>paribhāṣā</s> — this meaning is clearly stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the sūtra '<s>ṣaṣṭhī sthāne yogā</s>,' making the indicator you cite impossible. The '<s>sthāne</s>'-reference there simply serves to make the meaning explicit. Furthermore, the maxim '<s>vidhau paribhāṣā</s>' (a <s>paribhāṣā</s> applies in a prescriptive rule) is based on the implied complement 'what is being prescribed' in the sūtras '<s>iko guṇavṛddhī</s>' and '<s>acaś ca</s>'; elsewhere, however, this [principle] has no result — the elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text: nanu 'namaskaroti devān' 'namasyati devān' ityādau"namaḥ svasti"it caturthī durvārā, ityata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In forms like '<s>namaskaroti devān</s>' and '<s>namasyati devān</s>,' the fourth case (<s>caturthī</s>) prescribed by '<s>namaḥ svasti</s>' would be impossible to prevent. Therefore he states:

children.text: upapadavibhakteḥ kārakavibhaktirbalīyasī || 102 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 102: The case-ending based on <s>kāraka</s> (syntactic role) is more powerful than the case-ending based on <s>upapada</s> (governing word).

children.text:
kārakavibhaktitvañca kriyājanakārthakavibhaktitvam/ tacca prathamāyā apyastīti sāpi kārakavibhaktiriti"sahayukte"ityādisūtreṣu bhāṣye dhvanitam/
iyaṃ ca vācanikyeva/ ata eva"yasyaca bhāvena"iti saptamyapekṣayādhikaraṇasaptamyā balavatvamanena nyāyena,"tatra ca dīyate"iti sūtre bhāṣye dhvanitam, kaiyaṭena ca spaṣṭamuktam/ etena 'kriyānvayitvaṃ kārakatvam' ityapāstam, "yasyaca bhāvena"iti saptamyā api kriyānvayitvāt/
ye tu pradhānībhūtakriyāsambandhanimittakāryatvena kārakavibhaktīnāṃ balavatvaṃ vadanti; teṣāmubhayorapi kriyāsambandhanimittakatvena tadasaṅgatiḥ spaṣṭaiva/"namo variva"itisūtre 'namasyati devān' ityādau caturthī vāraṇāya bhāṣye upanyāsasyāsaṅgateśca//
children.translated_text: And the status of being a <s>kāraka</s>-case-ending (<s>kārakavibhaktitva</s>) means being a case-ending that expresses an action-generating meaning. And since the nominative (<s>prathamā</s>) too has this [status], it too is a <s>kāraka</s>-case-ending — this is hinted at in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on <s>sūtras</s> like '<s>sahayukte</s>' etc. And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is merely conventional (<s>vācanikī</s>). For this very reason, the greater strength of the locative of substratum (<s>adhikaraṇasaptamī</s>) over the locative [required] by '<s>yasyaca bhāvena</s>' [is established] by this principle — [as stated] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tatra ca dīyate</s>'...

children.text:
etena 'kriyākārakasambandhontaraṅgaḥ' iti tannimittā vibhaktirantaraṅgā, upapadārthena tu yatkiñcit ktiyākārakamūlakaḥ sambandha iti tannimittā vibhaktirbahiraṅgetyapāstam, 'namasyati' ityatra namaḥ padārthe 'pi kriyākārakābhāve naivānvayāt/ atra ca namaḥ padārthasyāpi kriyātvaṃ muṇḍayatau muṇḍasyeva/
"sahayukte"ityādau ca pradhāne prathamā sādhanārthamiyaṃ bhāṣya upanyastetyanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: By this, the [objection] is refuted that 'the relation of action and <s>kāraka</s> is <s>antaraṅga</s>' and hence the case-ending caused by it is <s>antaraṅga</s>, while 'the relation through the meaning of the co-word (<s>upapada</s>) is merely some relation based on action and <s>kāraka</s>' and hence the case-ending caused by it is <s>bahiraṅga</s> — [this is refuted] because in '<s>namasyati</s>', even in the meaning of the word <s>namaḥ</s>, there is no action-<s>kāraka</s> [relation], and hence no syntactic connection [on that basis]. And here, the meaning of the word <s>namaḥ</s> too has the nature of an action...

children.text: nanu 'adamuyaṅ' ityādau pūrvasyāpi muktvāpattiḥ, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>adamuyaṅ</s>' and the like, the prior [sound] too would undergo <s>muk</s>-augmentation. To address this, he says —

children.text: anantyavikāro 'ntyasadeśasya || 103 ||
children.translated_text: A non-final modification [is a modification] of that which shares the position of the final. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 103)

children.text:
anantyasadeśānanyasadeśayorekaprayoge yugapatprāptavantyasadeśasyaveti tadarthaḥ/ anyathā dhātvādernatvasatve'netā' 'sotā' ityādāveva syātām, na tu 'namati' 'siñcati' ityādau/
antyavikāra iti ca liṅgam/
antyena samāno deśo yasya so 'ntyasadeśaḥ/ tatvaṃ cāntyavarṇatadvarṇayoritarāvyavadhānena bodhyam/
ata eva vidhdha ityādyartham"na samprasāraṇe"iti caritārtham/
"allopo 'naḥ"ityādeḥ 'anastakṣṇā'ityādāvādakārādāvapravṛttirapyasyāḥ phalam, yajādi svādiparānnantāṅgasyākārasya lopa ityarthasyaivāṅgāṃśe pratyayasyottthitākāṅkṣatayaucityādaṅgāvayava yajādisvādiparasyān ityādikrameṇānekatrānekakliṣṭakalpanāpekṣayāsyā ucitatvāt/
na caiṣā"ṣyaṅaḥ samprasāraṇam"iti sūtre bhāṣye pratyākhyāteti bhramitavyam, vārtikoktaphalānāmanekakliṣṭakalpanābhiranyathāsiddhiṃ pradarśyāpi yānyetasyāḥ paribhāṣāyāḥ prayojanāni, tadarthameṣā kartavyā pratividheyaṃ doṣeṣu, pratividhānaṃ codattanirdeśāt siddhamityupasaṃhārāt/ 'mimārjiṣati' ityarthaṃ caiṣā/ tatra vṛddheḥ pūrvamantaraṅgatvāt dvitve paratvādabhyāsakārye tato 'bhyāsekārasya vṛddhivāraṇāyāvaśyakī/ na ca vṛddhau punarabhyāsahrasvatvena
siddhiḥ, 'lakṣye lakṣaṇasya' iti nyāyena punarapravṛtteḥ/
yattu"na samprasāraṇe"iti sūtre bhāṣye 'naitasyāḥ paribhāṣāyāḥ prayojanāni' ityuktam/ tasyāyamarthaḥ --
etatsūtre prayojanānyetasyāḥ paribhāṣāyā na bhavanti, vyadhādāvanatyasamānādeśayaṇo 'bhāvāditi/ 'naitāni
etasyāḥ prayojanāni' iti pāṭho 'pi kvacid dṛśyate/
children.translated_text: The meaning is: when a modification of the final-positioned [element] and a modification of another-positioned [element] both apply in a single usage, [the rule applies] to the final-positioned one. Otherwise, the <s>n</s>-substitution (<s>natva</s>) for the initial of the root would occur only in [forms like] '<s>anetā</s>', '<s>sotā</s>' and the like, and not in '<s>namati</s>', '<s>siñcati</s>' and so on. And the [compound] '<s>antyavikāra</s>' (final-modification) is an indication [of this meaning]. '<s>Antyasadeśa</s>' means one whose position is the same as the final. And that identity [of position] is determined by the other of the two — the final sound and its class...

children.text: vācanikyevaiṣā/ spaṣṭā ca"ṣyaṅaḥ"iti sūtre"adaso 'seḥ"iti sūtre ca 'kecidantyasadeśasya' ityanena bhāṣya ityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] too is merely conventional (<s>vācanikī</s>). And it is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ṣyaṅaḥ</s>' and on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>adaso 'seḥ</s>', through [the passage beginning] '<s>kecidantyasadeśasya</s>' — details are found elsewhere.

children.text:
nanu"avyaktānukaraṇasyātaḥ"iti pararūpam, 'paṭat' iti 'paṭiti' ityadau"alontyasya"
ityantyasya prāpnotītyata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: The <s>pararūpa</s> (subsequent-form substitution) [prescribed by] '<s>avyaktānukaraṇasyātaḥ</s>' — in '<s>paṭat</s>', '<s>paṭiti</s>' and the like — would apply to the final [element] by '<s>alontyasya</s>'. To address this, he says —

children.text: nānarthake 'lo 'ntyavidhiranabhyāsavikāre || 104 ||
children.translated_text: The rule [pertaining to] the final by '<s>al</s>' does not apply in a meaningless [element] or in a modification of the reduplicate. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 104)

children.text:
anabhyāsetyukte 'vibharti' ityādau"bhṛñāmit"ityādyantyasyaiva/ abhyāso 'narthakaḥ, arthavṛtyabhāvāt, kintūttarakhaṇḍa evārthavānityanyatra nirūpitam/
eṣā"alontyāt"sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭā/ phalānāmanyathāsiddhikaraṇepratyākhyātā ceti tata evāvadhāryatām//
children.translated_text: By saying '<s>anabhyāse</s>' (not in the reduplicate), in [forms like] '<s>vibharti</s>' and the like, [the rules] '<s>bhṛñāmit</s>' and the like apply only to the final. The reduplicate is meaningless, because it does not function in conveying meaning; rather, only the latter portion is meaningful — this is established elsewhere. This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>alontyāt</s>'. And it is rejected in the derivation of results by other means — this should be ascertained from that [passage] itself.

children.text: nanu 'brāhmaṇavatsā ca brāhnaṇīvatsaśca' ityādau"pumān striyā"ityekaśeṣāpattiḥ, strītvapuṃstvātiriktakṛtaviśeṣābhāvāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In [expressions like] '<s>brāhmaṇavatsā ca brāhmaṇīvatsaśca</s>' and the like, the <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (single-remainder) [rule prescribed by] '<s>pumān striyā</s>' would apply, since there is no distinction created by anything other than feminine and masculine gender. To address this, he says —

children.text: pradhānāpradhānayoḥ pradhāne kāryasampratyayaḥ || 105 ||
children.translated_text: Between principal (<s>pradhāna</s>) and non-principal (<s>apradhāna</s>) [elements], the operation applies to the principal. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 105)

children.text:
tena pradhānastrītvapuṃstvātiriktāpradhānastrītvapuṃstvakṛtaviśeṣasyāpi satvena na doṣaḥ/ spaṣṭā ceyam"napuṃsakamanapuṃsakena"ityanayorbhāṣye/
"antaraṅgopajīvyādapi pradhānaṃ prabalam' iti"hetumati ca"ityatra bhāṣyakaiyaṭayoḥ//
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the distinction created by non-principal femininity and masculinity — apart from the principal femininity and masculinity — also exists, there is no defect [in the rule]. And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on [the <s>sūtras</s>] '<s>napuṃsakamanapuṃsakena</s>' [and related ones]. [The principle that] 'the principal is stronger even than the <s>antaraṅga</s> that is relied upon' [is found] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> and <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on '<s>hetumati ca</s>'.

children.text: nanu svasrāditvaprayukto mātṛ śabdasya ṅībniṣedhaḥ paricchettṛvācakamātṛśabde 'pi syāt,
children.translated_text: Objection: The prohibition of <s>ṅīb</s> occasioned by membership in the <s>svasrādi</s> class for the word <s>mātṛ</s> would also apply to the word <s>mātṛ</s> when it means 'one who measures',

children.text: ata āha --
children.translated_text: To address this, he says —

children.text: avayavaprasiddheḥ samudāyaprasiddhirbalīyasī || 106 ||
children.translated_text: The fame of the whole (<s>samudāya</s>) is stronger than the fame of the parts (<s>avayava</s>). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 106)

children.text:
tena śuddha rūḍhasya jananīvācakasyaiva grahaṇam, na paricchattṛvācakasya/ 'yogajabodhe tadanāliṅgitaśuddharūḍhajopasthitiḥ pratibandhikā' iti vyutpattireva tadbījam/ rathakārādhikaraṇanyāyasiddho 'yamarthaḥ/
kaścittu"dīdhīvevīṭām"ityatrānayā paribhāṣayā dīdhīvevīṅoreva grahaṇam, na dīṅdhīṅveñ
vīnāmiti, tat, na; tathā sati 'dīvedhīvīṭām' ityeva vadediteyanye//
children.translated_text: Therefore, only the pure conventional (<s>śuddharūḍha</s>) [word meaning] 'mother' is designated, not the [derived word meaning] 'one who measures.' The etymological principle that 'the presentation of a pure conventional meaning not encompassed by the compositional understanding is an obstruction [to the compositional meaning]' is the very basis of this.
