This meaning is established by the <s>rathakāra</s>-<s>adhikaraṇa</s> maxim. Some, however, [say that] by this <s>paribhāṣā</s> in '<s>dīdhīvevīṭām</s>', only <s>dīdhīṅ</s> and <s>vevīṅ</s> are designated...

children.text: nanu vātāyanārthe gavākṣe 'vaṅo vaikalpikatvāt 'gokṣaḥ' ityādyapi syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In the [compound] '<s>gavākṣa</s>' meaning 'window' (<s>vātāyana</s>), since <s>avaṅ</s> is optional, [the form] '<s>gokṣaḥ</s>' and the like would also occur. To address this, he says —

children.text: vyavasthitavibhāṣayāpi kāryāṇi kriyante || 107 ||
children.translated_text: Even with a regulated option (<s>vyavasthitavibhāṣā</s>), the operations are performed. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 107)

children.text: lakṣyānusārād vyavasthā bodhyā/"śācchoḥ"iti sūtre"laṭaḥ śatṛ"ityādi sūtreṣu ca bhāṣye spaṣṭā//
children.translated_text: The regulation should be understood from [conformity with] attested usage (<s>lakṣya</s>). This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>śācchoḥ</s>' and on <s>sūtras</s> like '<s>laṭaḥ śatṛ</s>' etc.

children.text: vidhiniyamasambhave vidhireva jyāyān || 108 ||
children.translated_text: When there is the possibility of both a prescription (<s>vidhi</s>) and a restriction (<s>niyama</s>), the prescription alone is the stronger. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 108)

children.text: niyame hyaśrutāyā anyanivṛtteḥ sāmarthyāt parikalpanamuktānuvādadoṣaśceti lāghavād vidhireveti bodhyam/"yasya halaḥ"ityatra"ijādeḥ sanumaḥ"ityādau ca bhāṣye spaṣṭeyam//
children.translated_text: It should be understood that, in the case of a restriction, since the exclusion of the other [option] is unheard [in the text] and must be constructed through implicative power, the fault of being a pointless repetition arises — therefore, by [the principle of] simplicity (<s>lāghava</s>), the prescription alone [prevails]. This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>yasya halaḥ</s>' and on '<s>ijādeḥ sanumaḥ</s>' etc.

children.text: nanu"āśaṃsāyāṃ bhūtavacca"ityanena luṅa iva laṅliṭorapyatideśaḥ syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: By [the rule] '<s>āśaṃsāyāṃ bhūtavacca</s>', the analogical extension (<s>atideśa</s>) would apply to <s>laṅ</s> and <s>liṭ</s> just as to <s>luṅ</s>. To address this, he says —

children.text: sāmānyātideśe viśeṣānatideśaḥ || 109 ||
children.translated_text: In a general analogical extension (<s>sāmānyātideśa</s>), the specific [properties] are not extended. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 109)

children.text: sāmānyopasthitikāle niyamena viśeṣopasthāpakasāmagryabhāvo 'syā bījam/ tenānadyatanabhūtarūpe viśeṣe vihitayostayornātideśaḥ/ iyamanityā,"na lyapi"iti liṅgāt/ tena sthānivatsūtreṇa viśeṣātideśo 'pi/ spaṣṭaṃ caitatsarvaṃ"sthānivat"sūtre bhāṣye//
children.translated_text: The basis of this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is: at the time when the general [meaning] is present [to the mind], the aggregate of factors that would bring to mind the specific [properties] is necessarily absent. Therefore, the analogical extension does not apply to those two [<s>laṅ</s> and <s>liṭ</s>] which are prescribed for the specific [meaning of] non-present past. This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is non-invariable (<s>anityā</s>), as indicated by [the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>na lyapi</s>'. Therefore, the extension of specific [properties] also [occurs] through the <s>sthānivat</s> <s>sūtra</s>. All this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>sthānivat</s>' <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: nanu"titsvaritam"iti svaritatvam 'cikīrṣati' ityādau syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: The <s>svarita</s> status [prescribed by] '<s>titsvaritam</s>' would apply in '<s>cikīrṣati</s>' and the like. To address this, he says —

children.text: pratyayāpratyayayoḥ pratyayasya grahaṇam || 110 ||
children.translated_text: Between a suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>) and a non-suffix (<s>apratyaya</s>), [only] the suffix is designated. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 110)

children.text:
iyaṃ ca"aṅgasya"iti sūtr bhāṣye paṭhitā/ varṇagrahaṇe ca na pravartata iti tatraiva
kaiyaṭe spaṣṭam/ ata eva"sanāṃśabhikṣa uḥ""vale"ityatra sanvalayoḥ pratyayayorgrahaṇam/
pare tu"titsvaritam"iti sūtra eṣā paribhāṣā lakṣyasaṃskārāya bhāṣye kvāpi nāśriteti kaiyaṭenoktam/"aṅgasya"iti sūtre tatpratyākhyānāyaiṣā bhāṣya ekadeśinoktā/ ata eva"titi pratyayagrahaṇaṃ
kartavyam"iti vārtikakṛtoktam uktasūtrayorvyākhyānāt pratyayoreva grahaṇamityāhuḥ//
children.translated_text: This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is read in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>aṅgasya</s>'. And that it does not operate in letter-designations (<s>varṇagrahaṇa</s>) is clear in <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> on that very [passage]. For this very reason, in '<s>sanāṃśabhikṣa uḥ</s>' and '<s>vale</s>', [only] the suffixes <s>san</s> and <s>val</s> are designated. Others, however, [say that] <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> has stated that this <s>paribhāṣā</s> [arising from] the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>titsvaritam</s>' is never relied upon in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> for the purpose of deriving attested forms. [In the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on] '<s>aṅgasya</s>'...

children.text:
nanu"viparābhyāṃ jeḥ"ityātmanepadaṃ 'parāsenā jayati' ityarthake 'parājayati senā' ityatra
prapnotītyata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: The <s>ātmanepada</s> [prescribed by] '<s>viparābhyāṃ jeḥ</s>' would apply in '<s>parājayati senām</s>' in the sense of '<s>parāsenāṃ jayati</s>' (he defeats the enemy army). To address this, he says —

children.text: sahacaritāsahacaritayoḥ sahacaritasyaiva grahaṇam || 111 ||
children.translated_text: Between that which is accompanied [by something] and that which is unaccompanied, only the accompanied one is designated. (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 111)

children.text:
tena viśabdasāhacaryādupasargasyaiva parāśabdasya grahaṇamiti tatraiva bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ sahacaraṇaṃ sadṛśayoreveti sahacaritaśabdena sādṛśyavānucyate/ 'rāmalakṣmaṇau' ityādāvapi sādṛśyameva niyāmakam/ sadṛśayoreva sahavivakṣā, tayoreva sahaprayoga ityutsargācca/ dhvanitaṃ cedam"karmapravacanīyayukterdvitīyā"iti sūtre bhāṣye/
tatra hi"pañcamyapāṅparibhiḥ"iti sūtreṇa lakṣaṇādidyotakapariyoge pañcamīmāśaṅkya 'yadyapyayaṃ parirdṛṣṭāpacāro varjane cāvarjane ca, ayaṃ khalvapaśabdo 'dṛṣṭāpacāro varjanārtha eva karmapravacanīyaḥ, tasya ko 'nyaḥ sahāyo bhavitumarhatyanyo varjanārthāt, yathāsya goḥ sahāyenārtha iti gaurevānīyate, nāśvaḥ, na gardabhaḥ' ityuktam/ tena hi sadṛśānāmeva prayoge sahāyabhāvo bādhitaḥ/
"dvistriścatuḥ"iti sūtre sāhacaryeṇaiva kṛtvor'thasya grahaṇe siddhe kṛtvorthagrahaṇādeṣānityā/ tena"dīdhīvevīṭām"ityatra dhātusāhacarye 'pyāgamasyeṭo grahaṇamityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the co-occurrence with the word '<s>vi</s>,' it is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> itself that only the <s>upasarga</s> '<s>parā</s>' is taken. Co-occurrence is [only] between similar things — thus by the word 'co-occurring,' similarity is conveyed. Even in cases like '<s>rāmalakṣmaṇau</s>' (Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa), similarity alone is the determining factor. The general principle is that only similar things are intended to be mentioned together, and only similar things are used together. And this is hinted at in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>karmapravacanīyayukterdvitīyā</s>.' For there, having raised the expectation of the fifth case-ending by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>pañcamyapāṅparibhiḥ</s>' for <s>pariyoga</s> (circumjacent use) that indicates a characteristic, [the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> says:] 'Although this <s>pari</s> is of observed deviation in both exclusion and non-exclusion, this <s>apa</s> [prefix], of unobserved deviation, is a <s>karmapravacanīya</s> with the meaning of exclusion alone. What other companion could it have besides the exclusion-meaning? Just as when one needs a companion for one's cow, only a cow is brought — not a horse, not a donkey.' By this, the companionship of dissimilar things in usage is rejected. In the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>dvistriścatuḥ</s>', since the meaning of '<s>kṛtvaḥ</s>' (times) is already obtained by co-occurrence alone, the mention of '<s>kṛtvaḥ</s>'-meaning [indicates that] these are non-eternal. Therefore, in '<s>dīdhīvevīṭām</s>', even though there is co-occurrence with roots, the augment <s>iṬ</s> is also taken — the elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text: nanu"asthi"ityanaṅ 'priyasakthanā brāhmaṇena' ityatra na syāt, aṅgasya napuṃsakatvābhāvāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: The <s>anaṅ</s> substitution for '<s>asthi</s>' (bone) would not apply in '<s>priyasakthanā brāhmaṇena</s>' (by the brahmin with beautiful thighs), because the <s>aṅga</s> (stem) does not possess neuter gender. To address this, he says —

children.text: śrutānumitayoḥ śrutasambandho balavān || 112 ||
children.translated_text: Between what is explicitly stated and what is inferred, the connection with what is explicitly stated is stronger. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 112 //

children.text:
śrutenaiva sambandhaḥ, nānumitena prakaraṇādiprāptenetyarthaḥ/ prakaraṇāditaḥ śruterbalavatvāditi bhāvaḥ/
evaṃ ca tatra liṅgamasthyādīnāmeva viśeṣaṇam, nāṅgasya śiśīlugnumvidhiṣu tu gṛhyamāṇasyābhāvāt prakaraṇaprāptaṅgasyaiva viśeṣaṇam/
ata eva"vā napuṃsakasya"iti sūtre"vā śau"iti na kṛtam/ tatra napuṃsakagrahaṇaṃ hi gṛhyamāṇasya śatrantasyaiva napuṃsakatve yathā syāt, 'bahavo dadato yeṣu tāni kulāni bahudadati' ityatra mā bhūt; 'bahūni dadanti yeṣu te bahudadantaḥ' ityatra yathā syādityevamartham/ spaṣṭaṃ cedam"svamornapuṃsakāt"ityatra bhāṣye/
kecittu"aco rahābhyaṃ dve"ityatra śrutena rephasya nimittatvena yarantarbhāvādanumitena kāryitvaṃ bādhyata ityetadudāharaṇamāhuḥ, tat, na; takrakauṇḍinyanyāyena siddherityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: The connection is with what is explicitly stated alone, not with what is inferred — that is, what is obtained through context and the like — this is the meaning. The sense is: because explicit statement is stronger than context and the like. And thus, in that case [of '<s>asthi</s>'], gender is a qualifier of <s>asthi</s> and similar [stems] alone, not of the <s>aṅga</s> — because what is actually denoted is absent in the <s>śiśu</s>-, <s>lugu</s>-, and <s>num</s>-rules, [so] it is a qualifier of only the contextually obtained <s>aṅga</s>. For this very reason, in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>vā napuṃsakasya</s>' (optionally for the neuter), the specification '<s>vā śau</s>' was not made. For the mention of '<s>napuṃsaka</s>' (neuter) there is so that it applies when the <s>śatṛ</s>-ending [word] itself is neuter — as in '<s>bahavo dadato yeṣu tāni kulāni bahudadati</s>' (the families in which many give, those families are 'much-giving') — but not in '<s>bahūni dadanti yeṣu te bahudadantaḥ</s>' (those in which many things give, they are 'much-giving') — such is the purpose. And this is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>svamornapuṃsakāt</s>.' Some, however, say that in '<s>aco rahābhyāṃ dve</s>', by the explicitly stated causality of <s>repha</s>, the inclusion of <s>ya</s>-class [sounds] is inferred, and that inferred agency is overridden — [they cite] this as an example [of the <s>paribhāṣā</s>]. But that is not so, because it is established by the <s>takra-kauṇḍinya</s> maxim — the elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text: nanu"tatpuruṣe tulyārthaḥ"iti svaraḥ 'parameṇa, kārakeṇa, paramakārakeṇa' ityādau syāt, tathā"gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ"iti luk 'pai ovai śeṣaṇe' ityataḥ kṛtātvāt parasyāpi syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: The accent [prescribed by] '<s>tatpuruṣe tulyārthaḥ</s>' would apply in forms like '<s>parameṇa</s>' (supreme), '<s>kārakeṇa</s>' (agent), '<s>paramakārakeṇa</s>' (supreme agent), etc. Similarly, the <s>luk</s> (deletion) [prescribed by] '<s>gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ</s>' would apply even to the following [suffix], since it has acquired <s>kṛt</s>-status from '<s>pai ovai śeṣaṇe</s>.' To address this, he says —

children.text: lakṣaṇa pratipadoktayoḥ pratipadoktasyaiva grahaṇam || 113 ||
children.translated_text: Between a rule-derived [form] and an explicitly listed [form], only the explicitly listed one is taken. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 113 //

children.text: tattadvibhaktiviśeṣādyanuvādena vihito hi samāsādiḥ pratipadoktaḥ, tasyaiva grahaṇam, śīgropasthitikatvāt/ dvitīyo hi vilambopasthitikaḥ/ 'pai' ityasya 'pā' iti rūpaṃ lakṣaṇānusandhānapūrvakaṃ
children.translated_text: For a compound-formation etc. that is prescribed through the specification of a particular case-ending is 'explicitly listed' (<s>pratipadokta</s>), and only that is taken, because it is quickly apprehended. The second [type, i.e., the rule-derived form,] is of slow apprehension. The form '<s>pā</s>' of '<s>pai</s>' is

children.text:
vilambopasthitikam/ pibatestu tacchīghropasthitikam/ idameva hyetat paribhāṣābījam/ iyaṃ varṇagrahaṇe 'pi"ot"sūtre bhāṣye sañcāritatvāt/
yattu varṇagrahaṇe naiṣā"ādecaḥ"ityatropadeśagrahaṇāditi, tattu tasminneva sūtre śabdenduśekhare dūṣitamiti tata eva draṣṭavyam/
anityā ceyam"bhuvaśca mahāvyāhṛteḥ"iti mahāvyahṛtigrahaṇādityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: of slow apprehension, requiring prior investigation of the grammatical rule. But '<s>pibati</s>' (he drinks) — that is of quick apprehension. This very thing is the seed of this <s>paribhāṣā</s>. And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] has currency even in <s>varṇa</s>-designation (<s>varṇagrahaṇa</s>), as it is employed in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>oṭ</s>.' As for [the objection] that in <s>varṇa</s>-designation this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] does not [apply] because of the <s>upadeśa</s>-designation in '<s>ādecaḥ</s>' — that was refuted in the <s>Śabdenduśekhara</s> on that very <s>sūtra</s>, and should be seen there. And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is non-eternal, from the designation of <s>mahāvyāhṛti</s> in '<s>bhuvaśca mahāvyāhṛteḥ</s>' — the elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text: nanvevaṃ deṅo dodhātośca kṛtātvasya ghusaṃjñā na syāt, tathā meṅa ātve 'praṇimātā' ityādau"nergadanada"iti ṇatvaṃ na syāt, tathā 'gai' ityasyātve"ghumāsthā"itītvaṃ na syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, the <s>ghu</s>-designation of the roots <s>deṅ</s> (to protect) and <s>dodhātu</s> would not obtain [since they acquire <s>kṛt</s>-status through rule-derivation]. Similarly, in '<s>apraṇimātā</s>' and the like, the <s>ṇatva</s> (retroflexion) [prescribed by] '<s>nergadanada</s>' for <s>meṅ</s> after <s>ā</s>-substitution would not apply. Likewise, for '<s>gai</s>' (to sing) after <s>ā</s>-substitution, the <s>itva</s> (short-<s>i</s> status) [prescribed by] '<s>ghumāsthā</s>' would not apply. To address this, he says —

children.text: gāmādāgrahaṇeṣvaviśeṣaḥ || 114 ||
children.translated_text: In designations involving <s>gā</s>, etc., there is no distinction. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 114 //

children.text:
atra ca jñāpakaṃ daipaḥ pitvam/ taddhi 'adāp' iti sāmānyagrahaṇārtham/ anyathā lākṣaṇikatvādeva vidhau tadgrahaṇe siddhe kiṃ niṣedhe sāmānyagrahaṇārthena pitvena? tena caikadeśānumatidvārā sampūrṇā paribhāṣā jñāpyate/ iyaṃ ca lakṣaṇapratipadoktaparibhāṣāniranubandhakaparibhāṣālugvikaraṇaparibhāṣāṇāṃ bādhikā/"dādhā ghu"iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭā/
"gātisthā"iti sūtre iṇādeśagāgrahaṇameveṣyata iti na doṣa ityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: And here, the indicatory sign (<s>jñāpaka</s>) is the <s>pit</s>-status of <s>dāp</s>. For that [<s>pit</s>-marking] is for the purpose of general designation through '<s>adāp</s>.' Otherwise, since it would be taken in prescriptive rules through its rule-derived status alone, what purpose would the <s>pit</s>-marking serve in prohibition — [which requires] general designation? And through partial acceptance [of this principle], the complete <s>paribhāṣā</s> is indicated. And this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] overrides the <s>lakṣaṇa-pratipadokta</s> <s>paribhāṣā</s>, the <s>niranubandhakagrahaṇa</s> <s>paribhāṣā</s>, and the <s>lug-vikaraṇa</s> <s>paribhāṣā</s>. [It is] clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>dādhā ghu</s>.' In the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>gātisthā</s>', only the <s>iṇ</s>-substitute <s>gā</s>-designation is intended — so there is no fault — the elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text: pratyekaṃ vākyaparisamāptiḥ || 115 ||
children.translated_text: Sentence-completion applies to each [item] individually. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 115 //

children.text: 'devadattādayo bhojyantām' ityatra bhujivat//
children.translated_text: In '<s>devadattādayo bhojyantām</s>' (let <s>Devadatta</s> and others be fed), [the completion is] like [the verb] <s>bhuj</s> (to eat/feed) [applying individually to each person].

children.text: nanvevaṃ saṃyogasaṃjñāsamāsasaṃjñābhyastasaṃjñā api pratyekaṃ syuḥ, ā āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: If so, the designations <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunct consonant), <s>samāsa</s> (compound), and <s>abhyasta</s> (reduplicated) would also apply to each [element] individually. To address this, he says —

children.text: kvacitsamudāye 'pi || 116 ||
children.translated_text: In some cases, [sentence-completion applies] to the aggregate as well. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 116 //

children.text: 'gargāḥ śataṃ daṇḍyantām, arthinaśca rājāno hiraṇyāna bhavanti' ityādau daṇḍanavat/ lakṣyānurodhena ca vyavasthā//
children.translated_text: In cases like '<s>gargāḥ śataṃ daṇḍyantām</s>' (let the <s>Gargas</s> be fined a hundred) and '<s>arthinaśca rājāno hiraṇyāna bhavanti</s>' (and kings become desirous of gold), [the completion is] like the punishment [applying to the group collectively]. The determination is made in accordance with attested usage.

children.text: nanu"yūstriyākhyau"ityatra vyaktipakṣe dīrghanirdeśādanaṇtvena grāhakasūtrāprāptyodāttādyanyatamoccāraṇe 'nyasvarakasya saṃjñā na syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>yūstriyākhyau</s>' and the like, on the view that [grammatical terms denote] individuals, since long-vowel citation excludes the non-<s>aṇ</s> [option], and since the designating <s>sūtra</s> is not reached, the designation for a [sound] with a different accent (<s>svara</s>) — whether <s>udātta</s>, etc. — would not apply. To address this, he says —

children.text: abhedakāḥ guṇāḥ || 117 ||
children.translated_text: Properties (<s>guṇas</s>) are non-differentiating. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 117 //

children.text:
asati yatne svarūpeṇoccārito guṇo na bhedakaḥ, na vivakṣita ityarthaḥ/
jātipakṣe tu nāsyopayoga iti bodhyam/ 'yū' ityādau dīrghamātravṛttijātinirdeśānna kṣatirityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: A property that is articulated merely in its own form, without [special] effort, is not differentiating — not intended [as a restriction] — this is the meaning. On the view that [grammatical terms denote] universals (<s>jāti</s>), however, this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] has no application — this should be understood. In '<s>yū</s>' etc., since the citation is of the universal that subsists only in the long [vowel], there is no problem — the elaboration is elsewhere.

children.text: nanu 'sarvanāmāni' ityatra ṇatvābhāvanipātane 'pi loke saṇatvaprayogasya sādhutvaṃ syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>sarvanāmāni</s>' (the pronouns), even with the <s>nipātana</s> (irregular listing) of the absence of <s>ṇatva</s> (retroflexion), the correctness of the usage with <s>ṇatva</s> — '<s>sarvaṇāmāni</s>' — would [undesirably] follow in ordinary speech. To address this, he says —

children.text: bādhakānyeva nipātanāni || 118 ||
children.translated_text: Irregular listings (<s>nipātanas</s>) are exclusively overriding. // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 118 //

children.text:
tattatkārye nāprāpte nipātanārambhāt/"purāṇaprokteṣu"iti nipātitapurāṇaśabdena purātana śabdasya bādhaḥ prāpto 'pi pṛṣodarāditvānneti bodhyam/
purāṇeti pṛṣotarādiḥ purātaneti cetyanye/ iyam"sarvādi"sūtra bhāṣye spaṣṭā/
na caivamasthayādīnāṃ"nabviṣayasya"ityādyudāttatayāntyādeśasyānaṅaḥ sthānyanurūpe 'nudātta evoccāraṇīya udāttoccāraṇaṃ vivakṣārthaṃ bhaviṣyatīti kathamasya jñāpatvamiti vācyam, paramāsthiśabdādābantodātta udāttaguṇakasyāpi sthānivatvena vivakṣāyāṃ mānābhāvāt/
"catasaryādyudāttanipātanaṃ kariṣayate, vadhādeśe ādyudāttanipātanaṃ kariṣayate, padādayo 'ntādāttā nipātyante, sahasya sa udātto nipātyate"ityādi bhāṣyaṃ tvekaśrutyāṣṭādhyāyīpāṭhe kvacidudāttādyu
children.translated_text: Because the <s>nipātana</s> is undertaken when [the form] is not obtainable by the relevant rule. [Regarding the form] '<s>purāṇa</s>' irregularly listed in '<s>purāṇaprokteṣu</s>' — the overriding of the word '<s>purātana</s>' by '<s>purāṇa</s>' is expected but does not occur due to its being a <s>pṛṣodarādi</s> [form] — this should be understood. [Some say] '<s>purāṇa</s>' is a <s>pṛṣodarādi</s> and '<s>purātana</s>' is [the regular form] — so say others. This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is clearly [stated] in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>sarvādi</s>' <s>sūtra</s>. Nor should it be said that for the <s>asthi</s>-class [stems], the <s>anaṅ</s> substitution — being <s>udātta</s> in articulation as an end-substitute but by <s>sthānivat</s>-ness to be articulated as <s>anudātta</s> — has its <s>udātta</s> articulation as purposeful [indication]; for, from the word '<s>paramāsthi</s>' etc. where the final is <s>udātta</s>, even with <s>sthānivat</s>-ness of the <s>udātta</s> property, there is no valid means of knowledge for the intended [distinction]. The <s>Bhāṣya</s> statements — '<s>catasaryādyudāttanipātanaṃ kariṣyate</s>' (an irregular listing with initial <s>udātta</s> will be made for <s>catasṛ</s>), '<s>vadhādeśe ādyudāttanipātanaṃ kariṣyate</s>' (an irregular listing with initial <s>udātta</s> will be made for the <s>vadha</s>-substitute), '<s>padādayo 'ntodāttā nipātyante</s>' (<s>pada</s> etc. are irregularly listed as final-<s>udātta</s>), '<s>sahasya sa udātto nipātyate</s>' (the <s>sa</s> of <s>saha</s> is irregularly listed as <s>udātta</s>)' — these are based on the view that in the single-accent recitation of the <s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s>, the occasional <s>udātta</s> etc. articulation is purposeful [indication].

children.text:
ccāraṇaṃ vivakṣārthamityāśayena/
"traisvaryeṇa pāṭhaḥ"iti pakṣe tu jñāpakaparaṃ bhāṣyāmiti kaiyaṭādayaḥ/
pare tu, nipātanaṃ nāmānyādṛśe prayoge prāpte 'nyādṛśaprayogakaraṇam, tattadrūpād yatnāt tatra tatrodāttādivivakṣā/"tisṛcatasṛ"ityatra dvandvaprayukte 'ntodātte uccāraṇīye ādyudāttoccāraṇam - anyatra
sthānyarūpe svara uccāraṇīye tattaduccāraṇaṃ vivakṣārtham/
atra vikārakṛto lakṣyabhedo neti"sici vṛddhiḥ"iti bhāṣyāt pratīyate/
atra ca"asthidadhi"ityādāvanaṅāderudāttasyaivoccāraṇena siddhe udāttagrahaṇaṃ jñāpakam/ svarūpeṇoccārita ityukteranudāttāderantodāttādityudāttādiśabdoccāraṇe vivakṣaiva/
"uña oṃ"ityatrānanunāsika evoccāraṇīye yatnādhkyenānunāsikoccāraṇād vivakṣā bodhyā/"pathimathyṛbhukṣām"ityādau sthānyanurūpatayānunāsika evoccāraṇīye niranunāsikoccāraṇāt tadvivakṣā/ etadarthamevāsati yatna ityuktam/
'abādhakānyapi nipātanāni' iti tu bhāṣyaviruddham//
children.translated_text: On the view of three-accent recitation, however, <s>Kaiyaṭa</s> and others [say] that the <s>Bhāṣya</s> follows the principle of indication (<s>jñāpaka</s>). Others, however, [say:] <s>nipātana</s> means producing a different form than what would otherwise be obtained — [and] from the effort of producing each particular form, the intention of <s>udātta</s> etc. [accent] in each case [is established]. In '<s>tisṛcatasṛ</s>', when what should be articulated as final-<s>udātta</s> in a <s>dvandva</s> compound is articulated as initial-<s>udātta</s> — and elsewhere, when what should be articulated in the form of the original is articulated differently — that articulation is purposeful [indication]. In this regard, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>sici vṛddhiḥ</s>' indicates that a modification-caused difference in the attested form does not [affect the principle]. And here, in '<s>asthidadhi</s>' etc., since the result is already achieved by the <s>udātta</s> articulation of the <s>anaṅ</s> substitute alone, the mention of '<s>udātta</s>' is the indicatory sign. Because it was said 'articulated in its own form,' for <s>anudātta</s> etc. [sounds] that are final-<s>udātta</s> etc., the articulation of '<s>udātta</s>' etc. [words] is indeed purposeful [indication]. In '<s>uña oṃ</s>', when what should be articulated as non-nasal requires extra effort to be articulated as nasal — from that, the intention [should be understood]. In '<s>pathimathyṛbhukṣām</s>' etc., when what should be articulated as nasal by <s>sthānivat</s>-ness [of the original] is articulated as non-nasal — from that, that intention [is established]. It is for this very purpose that 'without [special] effort' was said. But the view that '<s>nipātanas</s> are also non-overriding' is contrary to the <s>Bhāṣya</s>.

children.text: nanūkhadhātordvitve svata eva hrasvatvāt pūrvamabhyāsahrasvāprāptau halādiḥ śeṣe savarṇa dīrghe hrasvāpattiḥ, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: For the root <s>ūkha</s> (to dry), when reduplication [occurs], since shortening is automatic, and when <s>abhyāsa</s>-shortening is not yet applicable, in the remainder after <s>hal</s> (consonant), the <s>savarṇadīrgha</s> (homogeneous long vowel) would result in shortening [being reversed]. To address this, he says —

children.text: parjanyavallakṣaṇapravṛttiḥ || 119 ||
children.translated_text: The application of grammatical rules is like [the fall of] rain (<s>Parjanya</s>). // <s>Paribhāṣā</s> 119 //

children.text:
evaṃ ca hrasvasyāpi hrasve kṛte 'lakṣye lakṣaṇasya' iti nyāyena na punarhrasvaḥ/ taduktam
"iko jhal"iti sūtre bhāṣye -- 'kṛtakāri khalvapi śāstraṃ parjanyavat' iti/ siddhe 'pi hrasvādhikārītyarthaḥ/
na ca 'lakṣye lakṣaṇasya sakṛdeva pravṛttiḥ' ityatra na mānamiti vācyam,"samovālopameke"iti lopenaikasakārasya dvitvena dvisakārasya punardvitvena ca trisakārasya siddhau"samaḥ suṭi"iti sūtrasyaiva mānatvāt,"samprasāraṇācca" "sici vṛddhiḥ"ityadau bhāṣye spaṣṭamuktatvācca/
sampūrṇāṣṭādhyāyyācāryeṇaikaśrutyā paṭhitetyatra na mānam/ kvacitpadasyaikaśrutyāpi pāṭhaḥ, yathā dāṇḍināyanādisūtre aikṣvāketi/ yadyapyadhyetāra ekaśrutyaivāṅgāni paṭhanti brahmaṇavat, tathāpi vyākhyānato 'nunāsikatvādivadudāttanipātanādijñānamityāhuḥ/
vidheyāṇ viṣaye tu"apratyayaḥ"iti niṣedhānna guṇābhedakatvena savarṇagrahaṇam, ata eva 'ghaṭavat' ityādau matormasya nānunāsiko vakāraḥ/ ata eva"tadvānāsām"iti sūtranirdeśaḥ/ anyathā"pratyaye bhāṣāyām"iti nityamanunāsikaḥ syāt, ityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: Thus, when a short vowel [substitution is prescribed] and a short vowel already exists, by the principle '<s>lakṣye lakṣaṇasya</s>' (the rule [applies] once to the attested form), no further shortening [occurs]. This is stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>iko jhal</s>': 'The science, even when it has accomplished [its task], [continues to apply] like a rain-cloud' — meaning it has scope even when [the result is already] established. Nor should it be said that there is no authority for [the principle] '<s>lakṣye lakṣaṇasya sakṛdeva pravṛttiḥ</s>' (the rule applies only once to the attested form) — because the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>samaḥ suṭi</s>' itself is the authority, since through the <s>lopa</s> (elision) from '<s>samovālopameke</s>,' the single <s>sakāra</s> would undergo reduplication, and the resulting two <s>sakāras</s> would undergo further reduplication to yield three <s>sakāras</s>. And because this is clearly stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>samprasāraṇāc ca</s>' and '<s>sici vṛddhiḥ</s>' etc. There is no authority [for the claim] that the complete <s>Aṣṭādhyāyī</s> was recited by the master in a single tone (<s>ekaśruti</s>). Sometimes even words are recited in a single tone — as '<s>aikṣvāka</s>' in the <s>Dāṇḍināyana</s> etc. <s>sūtra</s>. Although students do recite the parts in a single tone like [reciting] the <s>Veda</s>, nevertheless, knowledge of nasalization, <s>udātta</s> accent-placement, and the like is obtained from the commentary (<s>vyākhyāna</s>) — so they say. But in the domain of a prescribed <s>aṇ</s> [vowel], due to the prohibition '<s>apratyayaḥ</s>,' there is no <s>savarṇa</s>-grasping through the non-differentiation of quality. For this very reason, in '<s>ghaṭavat</s>' and the like, the <s>va</s>-sound of <s>matup</s> is not nasalized. For this very reason, there is the reference in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>tadvān āsām</s>.' Otherwise, by '<s>pratyaye bhāṣāyām</s>,' the nasalization would be permanent — [for] details, [see] elsewhere.

children.text: nanu syandūdhātoḥ 'syantsyati' ityādāvātmanepadanimittatvābhāvanimittatvāt"na vṛdbhyaścaturbhyaḥ"iti niṣedhasya bahiraṅgatvenāntaraṅgatvādūdillakṣaṇasyeḍvikalpasyāpattiḥ, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: From the root <s>syandū</s>, in '<s>syantsyati</s>' and the like, since the prohibition '<s>na vṛdbhyaś caturbhyaḥ</s>' is <s>bahiraṅga</s> (outer-scope) — because its cause, the condition for <s>ātmanepada</s>, is itself [only] a non-cause — and since the <s>iḍ</s>-option characterized by <s>ūdit</s> [would apply] due to <s>antaraṅga</s> (inner-scope) status, there would be an unwanted consequence. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: niṣedhāśca balīyāṃsaḥ || 120 ||
children.translated_text: Prohibitions are also stronger [than <s>antaraṅga</s> and <s>upajīvya</s> rules]. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 120]

children.text:
antaraṅgādupajīvyādapi balīyāṃsa ityarthaḥ/
'caturbhyaḥ' iti tu spaṣṭārthameva/ ata eva tatpratyakhyānaṃ bhāṣyoktaṃ saṅgacchate/
ata eva savarṇasaṃjñāderniṣedhaviṣaye na vikalpaḥ/ anyathā mīmāṃsakarītyā vidherupajīvyatvena prabalyāt tasya sarvathā bādhānupapatyā durvāraḥ sa iti mañjūṣāyāṃ vistaraḥ/ ata eva"dvandve ca" "vibhāṣā jasi"iti caritārtham/
vidhyunmūlanāya pravṛttirasyā bījam/"na lumatā'"kamerṇiṅ"ityanayorbhāṣye spaṣṭaiṣā//
children.translated_text: The meaning is: [prohibitions are] stronger even than <s>antaraṅga</s> (inner-scope) and <s>upajīvya</s> (dependent-upon) [rules]. The '<s>caturbhyaḥ</s>' (from four) is self-explanatory. For this very reason, the refutation stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> is consistent. For this very reason, in the domain of prohibitions such as the <s>savarṇa</s>-designation etc., there is no option (<s>vikalpa</s>). Otherwise, following the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> method, due to the strength of the prescriptive rule being the one depended upon (<s>upajīvya</s>), since its complete overriding would be untenable, that [option] would be irresistible — [for] details, [see] the <s>Mañjūṣā</s>. For this very reason, '<s>dvandve ca</s>' and '<s>vibhāṣā jasi</s>' have fulfilled their purpose. The seed of this [paribhāṣā] is its operation toward the complete uprooting of the prescriptive rule. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on '<s>na lumatā</s>' and '<s>kamer ṇiṅ</s>'.

children.text: nanvatyantasvārthikānāmarthapratyāyakatvarūpapratyayatvānupapattiḥ, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: For suffixes that are entirely in their own meaning (<s>svārthika</s>), the status of being a suffix — defined as having the capacity to convey meaning — would be untenable. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: anirdiṣṭārthāḥ pratyayāḥ svārthe || 121 ||
children.translated_text: Suffixes whose meaning is unspecified are in their own meaning (<s>svārtha</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 121]

children.text:
yasyārthaḥ prakṛtyā pratyāyyate, so 'pi pratyaya ityasyāpyaṅgīkārāt tasya pratyayatvamiti na doṣaḥ/
svārtha ityasya svīyaprakṛtyartha ityarthaḥ/ mahāsaṃjñābalādarthākāṅkṣāyāmanyānupasthitirasyā bījam/"supi sthaḥ"ityādi sūtreṣu bhāṣye spaṣṭaiṣā//
children.translated_text: Since even [the principle] 'that by which meaning is conveyed is also a suffix' is accepted, its status as a suffix is not a fault. The meaning of '<s>svārtha</s>' is 'the meaning of its own base (<s>prakṛti</s>).' The seed of this [paribhāṣā] is: by the force of the master-designation (<s>mahāsaṃjñā</s>), when there is an expectation of meaning and no other [meaning] presents itself, [the suffix takes its own meaning]. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on <s>sūtras</s> such as '<s>supi sthaḥ</s>' etc.

children.text: yogavibhāgādiṣṭa siddhiḥ || 122 ||
children.translated_text: Desired results are achieved through rule-separation (<s>yoga-vibhāga</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 122]

children.text: iṣṭasiddhireva, na tvaniṣaṭāpādanaṃ kāryamityarthaḥ/ tattatsamānavidhikadvitīyayogena vibhaktasyānityatvajñāpanametadbījam//
children.translated_text: Only desired results [are achieved], but undesired consequences should not be produced — that is the meaning. The seed of this is the indication of non-permanence (<s>anityatva</s>) through the second rule [formed by] separation into rules with identical prescriptions.

children.text: paryāyaśabdānāṃ lāghavagauravacarcā nā'driyate || 123 ||
children.translated_text: Considerations of brevity and verbosity (<s>lāghava-gaurava</s>) regarding synonymous words are not heeded. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 123]

children.text: tatra tatrānyatarasyām"vibhāṣā vā"iti sūtranirdeśajñāpitamidam //
children.translated_text: This is indicated by the reference '<s>vibhāṣā vā</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> at various places.

children.text: jñāpakasiddhaṃ na sarvatra || 124 ||
children.translated_text: What is established by an indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>) is not [valid] everywhere. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 124]

children.text:
spaṣṭameva paṭhitavye 'numānād bodhanamasārvatrikatvārthamityarthaḥ/ tena jñāpakasiddhaparibhāṣāyāniṣṭaṃ nāpādanīyamiti tātparyam/ bhāṣye 'pi dhvanitametat"ṅyāp"sūtrādau/
jñāpaketi nyāyasyāpyupalakṣaṇam/ nyāyajñāpakasiddhānāmapi keṣāñcit kathanamanyāṣāmanityatvabodhanāyeti bhāvaḥ/ yathā 'tatsthānāpanne taddharnalābhaḥ' iti nyāyasiddhaṃ sthānivatsūtram, jñāpakasiddhaṃ ca tatra"analvidhau"iti//
children.translated_text: The meaning is: the understanding through inference, when explicit statement would have been possible, is for the purpose of [indicating] non-universality. Therefore the purport is: an undesired consequence should not be produced from a <s>paribhāṣā</s> established by <s>jñāpaka</s>. This is also implied in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the '<s>ṅyāp</s>' <s>sūtra</s> etc. '<s>Jñāpaka</s>' here is an indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for <s>nyāya</s> (logical principle) as well. The idea is: the statement of even some [rules] that are established by <s>nyāya</s> and <s>jñāpaka</s> is for the purpose of conveying the non-permanence of others. As for example: the <s>sthānivat sūtra</s> is established by the <s>nyāya</s> (principle) '<s>tatsthānāpanne taddharmalābhaḥ</s>' (what occupies that position acquires those properties); and it is also established by <s>jñāpaka</s> in '<s>analvidhau</s>.'

children.text: nanu 'drogdhā drogdhā, droḍhā droḍhā' ityādau ghatvādīnāmasiddhatvāt pūrvaṃ dvitve ekatra ghatvam, aparatra ḍhatvamityasyāpyāpattirata āga --
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>drogdhā drogdhā</s>, <s>droḍhā droḍhā</s>' and the like, due to the <s>asiddhatva</s> (non-establishment) of <s>ghatva</s> and the like, if reduplication occurs first, there would be <s>ghatva</s> in one [and] <s>ḍhatva</s> in the other. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: pūrvatrāsiddhamadvitve || 125 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrvatrāsiddham</s> (treated as not-yet-established in prior [rules]) does not [apply] in reduplication. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 125]

children.text:
dvitvabhinne pūrvatra kartavye paramasiddhamityarthaḥ/"pūrivatrāsiddham"ityadhikārabhavaṃ śāstramasyā liṅgam/
yatra ca siddhatvāsiddhatvayoḥ phale viśeṣaḥ, tatraiveyam/ 'kṛṣṇarddhiḥ' ityādau jaśtvātpūrvamanantaraṃ vā dvitve rūpe viśeṣābhāvena nāsyāḥ pravṛttirityanyatra vistaraḥ/"sarvasya dve"iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭeyam//
children.translated_text: The meaning is: what is to be done in the prior [portion] is treated as established (<s>siddha</s>) with respect to the subsequent, when it is different from reduplication. The <s>śāstra</s> (rule) that falls under the <s>adhikāra</s> (heading) '<s>pūrvatrāsiddham</s>' is the indicator of this. And this [paribhāṣā applies] only where there is a difference in result between [the rule being] established and not-yet-established. In '<s>kṛṣṇarddhiḥ</s>' and the like, since whether reduplication occurs before or immediately after <s>jaśtva</s>, there is no difference in form, this [paribhāṣā] does not apply — [for] details, [see] elsewhere. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>sarvasya dve</s>.'

children.text: nanu 'goṣvaśveṣu ca svāmī' ityādivat 'goṣvaśvānāṃ ca svāmī' ityapi syāt"svāmīśvara"iti sūtreṇa ṣaṣṭhīsapmyorvidhānāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: Like '<s>goṣv aśveṣu ca svāmī</s>' and the like, '<s>goṣv aśvānāṃ ca svāmī</s>' should also [be valid], since the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>svāmīśvara</s>' prescribes both sixth and seventh case [constructions]. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: ekasyā ākṛteścaritaḥ prayoge dvitīyasyāstṛtīyasyāśca na bhaviṣyati || 126 ||
children.translated_text: When one form (<s>ākṛti</s>) has been employed, the second and third will not apply. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 126]

children.text: yatrānyākṛtikaraṇe bhinnārthatvasambhāvanā tadviṣayo 'yaṃ nyāya ityantra vistaraḥ/"kṛñcānuprayujyate"iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭeyam//
children.translated_text: Where the use of another form [would raise] the possibility of a different meaning — that is the domain of this <s>nyāya</s> (principle) — [for] details, [see] elsewhere. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>kṛñ cānuprayujyate</s>.'

children.text: nanu 'vivyādha' ityādau paratvāddhalādiḥśeṣe vasya samprasāraṇaṃ syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Objection: In '<s>vivyādha</s>' and the like, due to posteriority (<s>paratva</s>), the <s>samprasāraṇa</s> (vowel-contraction) of <s>v</s> should [wrongly apply] by the <s>dhalādiśeṣa</s> (remainder-after-<s>dhal</s>). Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: samprasāraṇaṃ tadāśrayaṃ ca kāryaṃ balavat || 127 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Samprasāraṇa</s> (vowel-contraction) and the operation dependent on it are stronger. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 127]

children.text: tadāśrayam"samprasāraṇācca"iti pūrvarūpam/ vastutaḥ"liṭyabhyāsasya"iti sūtre 'ubhayeṣāṃ grahaṇasyobhayeṣāṃ samprasāraṇameva yathā syādityarthakatvenedaṃ siddhamityeṣā vyarthā,"liṭyabhyāsasya"iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ phalāntarānyathāsiddhirapi tatraiva bhāṣye spaṣṭā/"ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ"ityādau saṃścaṅoḥ ityādi viṣayasaptamīti tatrāpi na doṣa ityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: 'Dependent on it' means the <s>pūrvarūpa</s> (prior-form substitution) from '<s>samprasāraṇāc ca</s>.' In truth, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>liṭy abhyāsasya</s>,' this is established as having its purpose [in explaining] 'the inclusion of both is so that the <s>samprasāraṇa</s> of both should occur' — hence this [paribhāṣā] is superfluous. This is clear in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>liṭy abhyāsasya</s>.' The establishment of another result on other grounds is also clear in that very <s>Bhāṣya</s>. In '<s>ṇau ca saṃścaṅoḥ</s>' and the like, '<s>saṃścaṅoḥ</s>' etc. is a domain-locative (<s>viṣaya-saptamī</s>), so there is no fault there either — [for] details, [see] elsewhere.

children.text: yattu --
children.translated_text: And furthermore —

children.text: kvacid vikṛtiḥ prakṛtiṃ gṛhṇāti || 128 ||
children.translated_text: Sometimes a modified form (<s>vikṛti</s>) grasps the original (<s>prakṛti</s>). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 128]

children.text: tena"nisamupavibhyo hvaḥ"ityatra hvāgrahaṇena hveño grahaṇasiddhiḥ//
children.translated_text: By this, in '<s>ni-sam-upa-vibhyo hvaḥ</s>,' the grasping of <s>hveñ</s> (the root 'to call') through the mention of <s>hvā</s> (its modified form) is established.

children.text: tathā --
children.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: aupadeśikaprāyogikayoraupadeśikasya grahaṇam || 129 ||
children.translated_text: Between an instructional (<s>aupadeśika</s>) and a practical (<s>prāyogika</s>) form, the instructional one is grasped. [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 129]

children.text:
tena"dāderdhātoḥ"ityatraupadeśikadhātoreva grahaṇamiti, tat, na; tayornirmūlatvāt, bhāṣyāvyavahṛtatvācca, 'na ca vikṛtiḥ prakṛtiṃ gṛhṇāti' iti"grahijyā"iti sūtrasthabhāṣyeṇādyāyāstiraskārācca/
"nisamupavibhyo hvaḥ"ityādau hveño/ṭanukaraṇe sautraḥ prayogaḥ/
ātvaviṣaya evātmanepadam, prayogasthānāmevānukaraṇasya ghusaṃjñā sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭamuktatvādityanye/ antyāpi tatra tatropadeśagrahaṇaṃ kurvataḥ sūtrakṛtovārtikakṛtaścāsammatā/
'iha hi vyākaraṇe sarveṣveva sānubandhakagrahaṇeṣu rūpamāśrīyate -- yatrāsyaitadrūpamiti, rūpanirgrahaśca śabdasya nāntareṇa laukikaṃ prayogam, tasmiṃśca laukike prayoge sānubandhakānāṃ prayogo nāstīti kṛtvā dvitīyaḥ prayoga upāsyate, 'ka upadeśo nāma' iti ghusaṃjñāsūtrastha bhāṣyeṇa prāyogikāsambhave tadgrahaṇamityarthasya lābhena bhāṣyāsammatā ca /
bhāṣye sānubandhaketyādi prakṛtābhiprayeṇa/"dādeḥ"iti sūtre dādipadasyaupadeśikadāditvavati lakṣaṇeti na doṣa ityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: By this, in '<s>dāder dhātoḥ</s>,' only the instructional (<s>aupadeśika</s>) root is grasped. [However,] that is not so — because both [paribhāṣās 128-129] are baseless (<s>nirmūlatva</s>), because they are not used in the <s>Bhāṣya</s>, and because the first [paribhāṣā 128] is rejected by the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>grahijyā</s>': '<s>na ca vikṛtiḥ prakṛtiṃ gṛhṇāti</s>' (a modified form does not grasp the original). In '<s>ni-sam-upa-vibhyo hvaḥ</s>' and the like, the use of <s>hveñ</s> with the <s>oṭ</s>-augment is a <s>sautra</s> (irregular/traditional) usage. '<s>Ātmanepada</s> applies only in the domain of <s>ātva</s>, and the <s>ghu</s>-designation applies only to forms in actual use (<s>prayogastha</s>)' — this is clearly stated in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>ghu-saṃjñā sūtra</s> — so say others. Even the last [school of thought], while making instructional-form grasping at various points, [stands] unsupported by the <s>sūtrakāra</s> and <s>vārtikakāra</s>. For in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>ghu-saṃjñā sūtra</s>, [it is stated]: 'In this grammar, in all uses with <s>anubandhas</s> (indicatory markers), the form is relied upon — [asking] "where does this form occur?" And the determination of the form of a word is not possible without a worldly (actual) usage. And in that worldly usage, there is no use of forms with <s>anubandhas</s>; therefore a second usage is sought.' [The statement] 'What is an <s>upadeśa</s> (instruction)?' in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>ghu-saṃjñā sūtra</s> — by obtaining the meaning 'when the practical form is impossible, then [the instructional form] is grasped' — the <s>Bhāṣya</s> also does not support [this paribhāṣā]. The <s>Bhāṣya</s>'s [statement about] <s>sānubandhaka</s> (forms with markers) etc. is with the intent of the matter at hand. In the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>dādeḥ</s>,' there is no fault because the word <s>dādi</s> has <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (figurative extension) to anything possessing the <s>aupadeśika dādi</s> character — [for] details, [see] elsewhere.

children.text: yadapi nanu 'ajarghā bebhidīti' ityādau tattadiguṇaprayuktā vikaraṇā yaṅluki syuḥ, tathā yaṅluki 'bebhiditā' ityādau"ekācaḥ"itoṇ niṣedhaḥ syāt, ata āha --
children.translated_text: Also, [there is this objection]: In '<s>ajarghā bebhidīti</s>' and the like, the <s>vikaraṇas</s> (verbal affixes) caused by the respective conjugational class should [wrongly apply] in <s>yaṅluk</s> (intensive without affix). Likewise, in <s>yaṅluk</s>, '<s>bebhiditā</s>' and the like, the prohibition of <s>ṇ</s> from '<s>ekācaḥ</s>' should [wrongly apply]. Therefore [the author] states:

children.text: śtipā śapānubandhena nirdiṣṭaṃ yad gaṇena ca /
children.translated_text: That which is specified by <s>śtip</s>, by <s>śap</s> with its <s>anubandha</s>, by a statement with a <s>gaṇa</s> (class-list),

children.text: yatraikājgrahaṇaṃ caiva pañcaitāni na yaṅluki || 130 ||
children.translated_text: and where there is a monosyllabic-root reference — these five do not [apply] in <s>yaṅluk</s> (intensive without affix). [<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 130]

children.text:
anubandhanirdeśo dvidhā -- svarūpeṇa, 'ṅitaḥ'ityādipadena ca/ 'hanti, yāti, vāti,"sanīvanta"iti sūtre bhareti,"dīṅo yuḍaci" "anudātta ṅitaḥ" "divādibhyaḥ śyan""ekāca upadeśe"ityudāharaṇāni/
dvitvam"sanādyantāḥ"iti"bhūvādayaḥ"iti dhātutvaṃ ca bhavatyeva,"guṇoyaṅlukoḥ"itiyīdibhirnuṣedhānityatvakalpanāt/ tena bhaṣbhāvo 'pi 'ajarghāḥ' ityādau bhavati/ ata eva"śvoditaḥ"iti sūtre kaiyaṭe -- 'yatraikāj grahaṇaṃ kiñcit' iti pāṭhaḥ/"ekāca upadeśe/ṭanudāttāt"iti sūtra ekājgrahaṇenaikadeśānumatyaiṣā jñāpyate/ anyathopadeśe 'nkācānudāttatvasyaiva satvena tadvaiyarthyaṃ spaṣṭameveti/
tadapi na, bhāṣyānuktatvāt/ ekājgrahaṇasya vadhivyāvṛtyarthamāvaśyakatvācca/
na ca vadhissthānyupadeśa ekājeveti vācyam, sākṣādupadeśasambhavenaitadviṣaye sthānyupadeśāgrahaṇāt, upadeśātvāvacchedenaikājityarthācca/
kiñca uttarārthamekājgrahaṇam/ ata eva 'jāgaritavān' ityādāvupadeśa ugantatvamādāya"śruyukaḥ kiti"itīṇ niṣedho na/ tatropadeśe ityanuvṛttiśya 'stīrṇam' ityādāviṇ niṣedhāyetyākare spaṣṭam/
na ca bhāṣye yaṅ lopo 'bebhiditā' ityādāviṭpravṛtyarthamupadeśe 'nudāttādekācaḥ śrūyamāṇādaṅgādityarthe sanīṭpratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ, 'bibhitsati' iti doṣopanyāsavad yaṅluki doṣāṇāmupanyāsena tatreḍiṣṭaḥ/
yaṅlopetyādi bhāṣyaṃ tūpakramopasaṃhārabalena na yaṅlugviṣayam/
children.translated_text: The indication of <s>anubandhas</s> (indicatory markers) is twofold — by their own form, and by words such as '<s>ṅitaḥ</s>' etc. Examples: '<s>hanti</s>', '<s>yāti</s>', '<s>vāti</s>', '<s>bhareti</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>sanīvanta</s>', and [forms in the <s>sūtras</s>] '<s>dīṅo yuḍaci</s>', '<s>anudātta ṅitaḥ</s>', '<s>divādibhyaḥ śyan</s>', '<s>ekāca upadeśe</s>'. Reduplication [occurs] by '<s>sanādyantāḥ</s>', and verbal root status (<s>dhātutva</s>) [is established] by '<s>bhūvādayaḥ</s>' — because the non-invariability of the prohibition by <s>yī</s> and other [substitutes in the <s>sūtra</s>] '<s>guṇo yaṅlukoḥ</s>' is postulated. Therefore, <s>bhaṣbhāva</s> (voicing assimilation) too occurs in '<s>ajarghāḥ</s>' and the like.

children.text:
kiñca, tasya tadviṣayakatve yaṅlope sthānivatvasyevayaṅlukyupāyāpradarśanena nyūnatpattiriti vācyam, iḍviṣaye yaṅluko loke 'nabhidhānena chandasi sarvavidhīnāṃ vaikalpikatvena ca tatra doṣānupanyāsenādoṣāt/ anyathā 'ekājgrahaṇaṃ kimartham' iti praśnasya 'uttaratra jāgartyarthamiha vadhyartham' ityuttarasya ca bhāṣye nirālambhanatvapatteḥ/
na cārdhadhātukākṣiptadhātorekāca iti viśeṣaṇam/ evaṃ ca 'bibhitsati' ityādāvuttarakhaṇḍasya dhātorekāctvamastyeva, uttarakhaṇḍe 'stitvavat/ etacca 'dayateḥ' iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ evaṃ ca prakṛtabhāṣyāsaṅgatiriti vācyam ; ākṣepe ākṣiptasyānvaye ca mānābhāvāt/
aṅgatvaṃ tu viśiṣṭa eveti"ekāco dve"iti sūtre bhāṣye spaṣṭam/ nirūpitaṃ ca tanādiśeṣe śabdenduśekhare/ dhātutvaṃ tūttarakhaṇḍa eva/ ata eva"ekāco baśo bhaṣ"iti sūtre dhātoravayavasyaikāca iti vaiyadhikaraṇyenānvaye gardhapsiddhiḥ prayojanamuktaṃ bhāṣye, na tu prasiddham 'ajarghāḥ' iti/
'ajarghāḥ, bebhidīti' ityādau śnam śyanādayastu"carkarītaṃ ca"ityasyādādau pāṭhena
yaṅlugante gaṇāntaraprayuktavikaraṇasyāprāptyā na bhavanti/
chāndasatvādeva kāryāntarāṇāmapi chandasi dṛṣṭaprayogeṣvadṛṣṭānāmabhāvo bodhyaḥ/
bhāṣāyāṃ tu tādṛśānāmabhāva eva/ śtipśabādinirdeśāstu 'bhavateraḥ' ityādi sūtrasthatannirdeśavannārthasādhakā ityanyatra vistaraḥ//
children.translated_text: Moreover, if [<s>yaṅluk</s>] were subject to that [rule's domain], then just as in the <s>yaṅ</s>-elision the non-demonstration of a means — like <s>sthānivattva</s> (original-substitute equivalence) — [leads to] deficiency in the <s>yaṅluk</s> [domain], the same objection would arise. But there is no fault, because <s>yaṅluk</s> is not employed in ordinary language for the domain of <s>iṭ</s>, and in Vedic [usage] all rules are optional, and no fault is adduced there. Otherwise, the question in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> 'what is the purpose of the <s>ekāc</s>-designation?' and the answer 'for <s>jāgarti</s> in the subsequent [section], and here for the sense of <s>vadh</s>' would become groundless. Nor [is the objection valid that] half...

children.text: nanu 'jabho 'ci, radheśca, neṭyaliṭi' ityeva sūtryatām, kiṃ dvīradhigrahaṇenetyāha --
children.translated_text: Objection: Let it simply be stated as '<s>jabho 'ci, radheśca, neṭyaliṭi</s>' — what is the need for the double mention of <s>radh</s>? To this he says —

children.text: padagauravād yogavibhāgo garīyān || 131 ||
children.translated_text: The division of rules (<s>yogavibhāga</s>) is weightier than the heaviness of words (<s>padagaurava</s>). (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 131)

children.text: prativākyaṃ bhinnavākyārthabodhakalpanena gauravaṃ spaṣṭameva/ parantu bhāṣyāsammateyam/"ṭāṅasi"iti sūtrastha bhāṣya viruddhā ca/ tatra ca inādeśe ikārapratyākhyānaṃ yogavibhāgenaiva kṛtamiti bahavaḥ//
children.translated_text: The heaviness [of the alternative] is quite evident — the postulation of different sentence-meanings for each sentence. However, this [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is not sanctioned by the <s>Bhāṣya</s>. And it contradicts the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ṭāṅasi</s>'. And there, most [grammarians say that] the rejection of the <s>i</s>-vowel in the <s>in</s>-substitution was accomplished precisely through rule-division (<s>yogavibhāga</s>).

children.text: ardhamātrālāghavena putrotsavaṃ manyante vaiyākaraṇāḥ || 132 ||
children.translated_text: Grammarians consider even the saving of half a <s>mātrā</s> (mora) a cause for celebration, like the birth of a son! (<s>Paribhāṣā</s> 132)

children.text:
"eoṅ" "aiauc"sūtrayordhvanitaiṣā bhāṣye/
tatrānekapadaghaṭitasūtre prāyaḥ padalāghavavicāra eva, na tu mātrālāghavavicāra iti"ūkāloc,"apṛkta ekāl"ityādisūtreṣu bhāṣye dhvanitam/
tatra hi sūtre algrahaṇahalgrahaṇayorviśeṣavicāre saṃjñāyāṃ halgrahaṇam"ṇyakṣatriya"iti sūtre aṇiñoriti vācyamiti trīṇi padānyalgrahaṇe, tadekaṃ svādilope halgrahaṇam"ṇya"iti sūtre aṇiñoriti na vācyam, apṛktasyeti vācyamiti trīṇyeva padānīti nāsti lāghavakṛto viśeṣa ityuktam/
"aci śnu"iti sūtre iṇa ityeva siddhe yvoriti saṃmṛdya grahaṇānna pūrveṇeṇgrahaṇam/ tatra
vibhakti nirdeśe saṃmṛdya grahaṇe ca sārdhāstrisro mātrā iṇ grahaṇe tisro mātrā iti laṇsūtre bhāṣyokteḥ, tathā"otaḥ śyani"iti
sūtre śitīti na vaktavyam/
tatrāyamarthaḥ --"ṣṭhivuklamu"iti sūtre 'śitīti na karttavyaṃ bhavati' iti bhāṣye na kevalaṃ mātrālāghavaṃ yāvadayamapyartha iti kaiyaṭokteḥ prāyeṇeti śivam//
children.translated_text: This [<s>paribhāṣā</s>] is hinted at in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the <s>sūtras</s> '<s>eoṅ</s>' and '<s>aiauc</s>'. There, in a <s>sūtra</s> composed of multiple words, the consideration is generally of word-economy (<s>padalāghava</s>) only, not of <s>mātrā</s>-economy — this is hinted at in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on <s>sūtras</s> like '<s>ūkāloc</s>', '<s>apṛkta ekāl</s>' and so on. For there, in the specific consideration of whether to use <s>al</s>-designation or <s>hal</s>-designation in the <s>sūtra</s>, [it is noted that] with <s>hal</s>-designation in the technical term — [requiring the addition of] '<s>aṇiñoḥ</s>' as stated in the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>ṇyakṣatriya</s>' — three words [are needed] with <s>al</s>-designation, whereas only one [is needed] with <s>hal</s>-designation when the <s>su</s>-ending and the like are elided — '<s>ṇya</s>'...

children.text: iti śāstraśeṣanāmakaṃ tṛtīyaṃ prakaraṇam//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter named '<s>Śāstraśeṣa</s>' (Supplement to the Grammar).

children.text: iti śrīmanmahopādhyāyaśivabhaṭṭasutasatīgarbhajanāgojībhaṭṭakṛtaḥ paribhāṣenduśekharaḥ samāptaḥ//
children.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Paribhāṣenduśekhara</s>, composed by <s>Nāgojībhaṭṭa</s>, born from the womb of <s>Satī</s>, son of the illustrious great preceptor (<s>Mahopādhyāya</s>) <s>Śivabhaṭṭa</s>.
